```tsx
        <PopIcon trigger="mount">
          <span
            className="absolute -right-1 -top-1 flex h-4 w-4 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-red-500 text-[10px] font-bold text-white"
            aria-label={`${count} notifications`}
          >
            {count}
          </span>
        </PopIcon>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Real-world examples

### Upload success state

File upload completes and the status icon switches to a popping checkmark:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { PopIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pop"
import { CheckCircle, Upload } from "lucide-react"

export function UploadButton() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"idle" | "uploading" | "done">("idle")

  async function handleUpload() {
    setStatus("uploading")
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500))
    setStatus("done")
  }

  return (
    <button
      onClick={handleUpload}
      disabled={status === "uploading"}
      className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-lg border border-neutral-200 px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium hover:bg-neutral-50 disabled:opacity-60 dark:border-neutral-700"
    >
      {status === "done" ? (
        <div role="status" className="flex items-center gap-2 text-green-600">
          <PopIcon trigger="mount">
            <CheckCircle className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
          </PopIcon>
          <span>Uploaded</span>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <>
          <Upload className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
          {status === "uploading" ? "Uploading..." : "Upload file"}
        </>
      )}
    </button>
  )
}
```

### Gamification reward badge

A trophy icon pops when a milestone is reached:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { PopIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pop"
import { Trophy } from "lucide-react"

export function MilestoneBadge({ completed }: { completed: boolean }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-1">
      {completed ? (
        <div role="status">
          <PopIcon trigger="mount">
            <Trophy className="w-10 h-10 text-yellow-500" aria-hidden="true" />
          </PopIcon>
          <span className="sr-only">Milestone reached</span>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <Trophy className="w-10 h-10 text-neutral-300" aria-hidden="true" />
      )}
      <span className="text-xs font-medium text-neutral-600">100 tasks</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/pulse.tsx"
"use client";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import type { HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import {
  pulseVariants,
  createContinuousTransition,
} from "@/lib/animation-presets";
interface PulseIconProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "animate"> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  trigger?: "mount" | "hover" | "always";
  duration?: number;
}
export function PulseIcon({
  children,
  trigger = "always",
  duration = 0.8,
  ...props
}: PulseIconProps) {
  const animate = trigger === "always" ? "animate" : undefined;
  const whileHover = trigger === "hover" ? "animate" : undefined;
  return (
    <motion.div
      variants={pulseVariants}
      initial="initial"
      animate={animate}
      whileHover={whileHover}
      transition={createContinuousTransition(duration, "easeInOut")}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

```

```tsx
export default function Example() {
  return (
    <PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={0.8}>
      <Heart className="w-6 h-6" />
    </PulseIcon>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon element to animate |
| `trigger` | `"mount"` \| `"hover"` \| `"always"` | `"always"` | When to trigger the pulse animation |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.8` | Duration of one pulse cycle in seconds |

## Use cases

`PulseIcon` drives `scale: [1, 1.05, 1]` and `opacity: [1, 0.8, 1]` on a `repeat: Infinity` cycle using `createContinuousTransition` with `easeInOut`. The default `trigger="always"` means it pulses from the moment it mounts. `trigger="hover"` enables it only while the cursor is over the element. Good fits:

- **Live / recording indicators.** A `Radio` or `Dot` icon pulsing at 0.8 s communicates "live now" without a badge.
- **Unread notification bell.** A pulsing `Bell` on a nav bar tells the user there is something to read, with `trigger="hover"` to stop on interaction.
- **Real-time sync status.** A `RefreshCw` or `Cloud` icon pulsing while data is syncing and stopping once the sync resolves.
- **Call-to-action emphasis.** A `ChevronRight` or `ArrowRight` that gently pulses at 1.2 s to nudge the user toward the next step.
- **Hover feedback on icon buttons.** `trigger="hover"` adds a scale swell on mouseover without committing to a continuous animation.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `PulseIcon` when:**

- One icon needs to pulse to communicate an ongoing state (live, active, syncing) and the rest of the page is static.
- `trigger="hover"` is appropriate for subtle interactive feedback when you want motion on demand rather than always-on.

**Do not use `trigger="always"` when:**

- More than one icon on the screen is already using `repeat: Infinity` motion. Multiple simultaneous scale pulses compete for attention and make the interface feel unstable.
- The icon is inside a table, list, or repeated card component. A pulsing icon in every row is overwhelming. Reserve always-on pulse for a single focal element.
- The pulsing serves no informational purpose. A purely decorative icon that pulses forever trains users to ignore it, making it useless as a real attention signal later.
- A calmer visual rhythm would work. [HeartbeatIcon](/docs/animations/icons/heartbeat) with its natural double-beat pause feels less aggressive than a constant scale loop, and [BounceContinuous](/docs/animations/icons/bounce-continuous) works better for directional cues.

## Accessibility notes

- A pulsing icon alone does not communicate state to screen readers. Add a text description alongside it:

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2" role="status">
  <PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={0.8}>
    <Radio className="w-4 h-4 text-red-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  </PulseIcon>
  <span className="text-sm font-medium">Live</span>
</div>
```

- `repeat: Infinity` scale animations can cause discomfort for users with vestibular sensitivities. Always check `prefers-reduced-motion` and either stop the pulse or use a non-motion indicator (color flash via CSS, for example):

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { PulseIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pulse"
import { Radio } from "lucide-react"

export function LiveIndicator() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
      {reduced ? (
        <Radio className="w-4 h-4 text-red-500" aria-hidden="true" />
      ) : (
        <PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={1.2}>
          <Radio className="w-4 h-4 text-red-500" aria-hidden="true" />
        </PulseIcon>
      )}
      <span className="text-sm font-medium text-red-600">Live</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

- When `trigger="hover"`, the pulse only fires for pointer users. Keyboard and touch users will never see it. Do not rely on the hover pulse to communicate interactive affordance; pair it with a visible focus ring and color change.

## Performance considerations

- The animation modifies `scale` and `opacity`, both compositor-only properties. No layout recalculation or repaint.
- `repeat: Infinity` with `trigger="always"` keeps the compositor thread active indefinitely. Unmount rather than hide:

```tsx
{isSyncing && (
  <PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={0.8}>
    <RefreshCw className="w-5 h-5 text-blue-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  </PulseIcon>
)}
```

- `trigger="hover"` is significantly cheaper than `trigger="always"` because the animation only runs while the mouse is over the element. Prefer hover-based pulsing for any icon that does not need to communicate an always-on status.
- Avoid more than one `trigger="always"` `PulseIcon` mounted simultaneously. The compositor cost is low per instance, but the perceptual cost of multiple simultaneous scale loops is high.

## Customization examples

### Fast pulse for urgency

A shorter `duration` (0.5 s) reads as more alert, appropriate for a critical indicator:

```tsx
import { PulseIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pulse"
import { AlertCircle } from "lucide-react"

<PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={0.5}>
  <AlertCircle className="w-5 h-5 text-orange-500" aria-hidden="true" />
</PulseIcon>
```

### Slow pulse for ambient status

A longer `duration` (1.5 s) feels calm and unobtrusive, like a breathing indicator:

```tsx
import { PulseIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pulse"
import { Cloud } from "lucide-react"

<PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={1.5}>
  <Cloud className="w-5 h-5 text-sky-400" aria-hidden="true" />
</PulseIcon>
```

### Hover-only pulse on a nav icon

Only pulses while the user is hovering, adding tactile feel to a navigation item:

```tsx
import { PulseIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pulse"
import { Bell } from "lucide-react"

<button aria-label="Notifications" className="rounded-full p-2 hover:bg-neutral-100">
  <PulseIcon trigger="hover" duration={0.6}>
    <Bell className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
  </PulseIcon>
</button>
```

## Real-world examples

### Live broadcast badge

Shows while a stream is active and stops (unmounts) when the stream ends:

```tsx
import { PulseIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pulse"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { Radio } from "lucide-react"

export function LiveBadge({ isLive }: { isLive: boolean }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (!isLive) return null

  return (
    <div
      role="status"
      className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-full bg-red-100 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-semibold text-red-600 dark:bg-red-950 dark:text-red-400"
    >
      {reduced ? (
        <Radio className="w-3.5 h-3.5" aria-hidden="true" />
      ) : (
        <PulseIcon trigger="always" duration={1}>
          <Radio className="w-3.5 h-3.5" aria-hidden="true" />
        </PulseIcon>
      )}
      LIVE
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Sync status icon in a toolbar

Pulses while a save is in flight, then unmounts cleanly when done:

```tsx
"use client"
import { PulseIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/pulse"
import { RefreshCw, CheckCircle } from "lucide-react"

export function SyncStatus({ syncing }: { syncing: boolean }) {

            <RefreshCw className="w-4 h-4 text-blue-500" aria-hidden="true" />
          </PulseIcon>
          <span>Syncing...</span>
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <CheckCircle className="w-4 h-4 text-green-500" aria-hidden="true" />
          <span>Up to date</span>
        </>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Overview

The `RotateIcon` component creates a one-shot 360° rotation triggered by hover, tap, or mount. Perfect for refresh actions and interactive feedback.

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/rotate.tsx"
"use client";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import type { HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { rotateVariants } from "@/lib/animation-presets";
import { useState } from "react";
interface RotateIconProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "animate"> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  trigger?: "hover" | "tap" | "mount";
  direction?: "clockwise" | "counterclockwise";
}
export function RotateIcon({
  children,
  trigger = "hover",
  direction = "clockwise",
  ...props
}: RotateIconProps) {
  const [key, setKey] = useState(0);
  const rotation = direction === "clockwise" ? 360 : -360;
  const customVariants = {
    initial: { rotate: 0 },
    animate: { rotate: rotation },
  };
  const handleTrigger = () => {
    setKey((prev) => prev + 1);
  };
  return (
    <motion.div
      key={key}
      variants={customVariants}
      initial="initial"
      animate={trigger === "mount" ? "animate" : undefined}
      whileHover={trigger === "hover" ? "animate" : undefined}
      whileTap={trigger === "tap" ? "animate" : undefined}
      onTap={trigger === "tap" ? handleTrigger : undefined}
      transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" }}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

```

```tsx
import { RotateIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/rotate"
import { RefreshCw } from "lucide-react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <RotateIcon trigger="hover" direction="clockwise">
      <RefreshCw className="w-6 h-6" />
    </RotateIcon>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon element to animate |
| `trigger` | `"hover"` \| `"tap"` \| `"mount"` | `"hover"` | When to trigger the rotation animation |
| `direction` | `"clockwise"` \| `"counterclockwise"` | `"clockwise"` | Rotation direction |

## Use cases

`RotateIcon` animates `rotate` from 0 to 360 (clockwise) or 0 to -360 (counterclockwise) over 0.5 s with `easeInOut`. It is a one-shot animation: it fires on the chosen trigger and stops. A `key` increment on `tap` allows it to re-fire reliably on repeated interactions. Good use cases:

- **Refresh / reload buttons.** A `RefreshCw` that rotates 360 degrees on hover or tap directly mimics the action it represents.
- **Settings gear.** A gear icon rotating a quarter turn on hover communicates "this is configurable" without words.
- **Expand/collapse toggles.** `trigger="mount"` on a chevron that appears when a section opens, combined with rotate CSS in the collapsed state, creates a smooth open/close affordance.
- **Delete/clear actions.** A counterclockwise rotation on a close or trash icon adds a tactile sense of reversal.
- **Transition feedback.** `trigger="mount"` on a sync or loading icon that rotates once when the async process begins.

Note that `RotateIcon` rotates once and stops. If you need continuous rotation (loading spinner), use [SpinIcon](/docs/animations/icons/spin).

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `RotateIcon` when:**

- You want a precise, one-shot rotation that confirms an action without looping.
- `direction="clockwise"` pairs semantically with "forward" or "refresh" actions; `direction="counterclockwise"` pairs with "undo" or "reverse" actions.
- `trigger="hover"` provides lightweight hover feedback that does not require state management.

**Do not use it when:**

- You need continuous rotation while a process is running. Use [SpinIcon](/docs/animations/icons/spin), which sets `repeat: Infinity`.
- The rotation is used as the only signal for a state change. A gear that rotates once on click tells the user something happened but not what the new state is. Pair with a label or color change.
- The icon is in a dense list where hover triggers fire on every row as the user moves the cursor through the list. This creates a distracting sequence of rotations; prefer a color-only hover state.

## Accessibility notes

- Rotation is a purely visual effect. Add `aria-hidden="true"` to the icon when it is accompanied by a text label. When the icon is the sole interactive element, give the parent button an `aria-label`:

```tsx
<button
  aria-label="Refresh data"
  className="rounded p-2 hover:bg-neutral-100"
>
  <RotateIcon trigger="hover">
    <RefreshCw className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
  </RotateIcon>
</button>
```

- For `trigger="tap"`, the rotation fires after the `onTap` event. This is a motion/react gesture event that does not fire on keyboard activation (Enter or Space). Ensure the parent element is a proper `<button>` so keyboard users still trigger the action even without seeing the rotation.
- The 0.5 s single rotation is brief enough that most users with motion sensitivity will not be affected. For extra safety, you can reduce the rotation angle:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { RotateIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/rotate"
import { RefreshCw } from "lucide-react"

export function RefreshButton({ onClick }: { onClick: () => void }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return (
    <button onClick={onClick} aria-label="Refresh" className="rounded p-2 hover:bg-neutral-100">
      {reduced ? (
        <RefreshCw className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
      ) : (
        <RotateIcon trigger="hover">
          <RefreshCw className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
        </RotateIcon>
      )}
    </button>
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- `rotate` is a transform. The animation runs on the compositor thread with no layout recalculation or repaint.
- One-shot animation (no `repeat`). The compositor releases it after 0.5 s. No ongoing cost.
- The `key` increment on `tap` remounts the `motion.div` to restart the animation. For a single icon this is a negligible DOM operation.
- `trigger="hover"` uses `whileHover`, which transitions back to `initial` (rotate 0) when the cursor leaves. Because the element is not mid-animation at exit, the return is instantaneous (no reverse animation), which is the correct behavior for a refresh icon.

## Real-world examples

### Refresh button in a data card header

The icon rotates on each click to confirm the refresh was triggered, and is disabled while the fetch is in flight:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { RotateIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/rotate"
import { RefreshCw } from "lucide-react"

export function CardHeader({ onRefresh }: { onRefresh: () => Promise<void> }) {
  const [refreshing, setRefreshing] = useState(false)

  async function handleRefresh() {
    if (refreshing) return
    setRefreshing(true)
    try {
      await onRefresh()
    } finally {
      setRefreshing(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between border-b border-neutral-200 px-4 py-3 dark:border-neutral-800">
      <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold">Analytics</h3>
      <button
        onClick={handleRefresh}
        disabled={refreshing}
        aria-label="Refresh analytics"
        className="rounded p-1.5 hover:bg-neutral-100 disabled:opacity-50 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800"
      >
        <RotateIcon trigger="tap">
          <RefreshCw className="w-4 h-4 text-neutral-500" aria-hidden="true" />
        </RotateIcon>
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Settings dropdown with rotating gear

The gear icon rotates when the dropdown opens, adding a visual accent to the interaction:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { RotateIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/rotate"
import { Settings } from "lucide-react"

export function SettingsMenu() {

  return (
    <div className="relative">
      <button
        onClick={() => setOpen((p) => !p)}
        aria-expanded={open}
        aria-label="Settings"
        className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium hover:bg-neutral-100 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800"
      >
        <RotateIcon trigger="tap">
          <Settings className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
        </RotateIcon>
        Settings
      </button>
      {open && (
        <div className="absolute right-0 mt-1 w-40 rounded-lg border border-neutral-200 bg-white shadow-md dark:border-neutral-700 dark:bg-neutral-900">
          <button className="w-full px-4 py-2 text-left text-sm hover:bg-neutral-50 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800">
            Profile
          </button>
          <button className="w-full px-4 py-2 text-left text-sm hover:bg-neutral-50 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800">
            Billing
          </button>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

# scale-in.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/icons/scale-in.mdx

title: Scale In Icon
description: Entrance animation with scale effect for icons.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { ScaleInIcon } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/icons/scale-in';
import { Zap, Star, Sparkles, Circle, Square, Triangle, Hexagon } from 'lucide-react';

## Overview

The `ScaleInIcon` component creates a scale-in entrance animation. Perfect for revealing icons with a smooth zoom effect.

## Preview

  background="grid"
  code={`import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Zap } from "lucide-react"

<ScaleInIcon delay={0} from={0.8}>
  <Zap className="w-8 h-8 text-yellow-500" />
</ScaleInIcon>`}
  <div className="flex gap-8 items-center justify-center">
    <ScaleInIcon delay={0} from={0.8}>
      <Zap className="w-8 h-8 text-yellow-500" />
    </ScaleInIcon>
    <ScaleInIcon delay={0.2} from={0.5}>
      <Star className="w-8 h-8 text-blue-500" />
    </ScaleInIcon>
    <ScaleInIcon delay={0.4} from={0.3}>
      <Sparkles className="w-8 h-8 text-purple-500" />
    </ScaleInIcon>

    ```tsx title="lib/animation-presets.ts"
      smooth: { duration: 0.3, ease: "easeInOut" } as Transition,
      quick: { duration: 0.15, ease: "easeOut" } as Transition,
      slow: { duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" } as Transition,
      spring: { type: "spring", stiffness: 300, damping: 30 } as Transition,
      bouncy: { type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 10 } as Transition,
      continuous: (duration: number = 1) =>
        ({
          duration,
          ease: "linear",
          repeat: Infinity,
        }) as Transition,
    } as const;

    export const createContinuousTransition = (
      duration: number = 1,
      ease: Easing = "linear",
    ): Transition => ({
      duration,
      ease,
      repeat: Infinity,
    });

    export const createDelayedTransition = (
      delay: number,
      duration: number = 0.3,
    ): Transition => ({
      delay,
      duration,
      ease: "easeOut" as Easing,
    });

    export const createStaggerTransition = (
      staggerDelay: number = 0.1,
      delayChildren: number = 0,
    ): Transition => ({
      staggerChildren: staggerDelay,
      delayChildren,
    });
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/scale-in.tsx"
"use client";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import type { HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import {
  scaleInVariants,
  createDelayedTransition,
} from "@/lib/animation-presets";
interface ScaleInIconProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "animate"> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  delay?: number;
  duration?: number;
  from?: number;
}
export function ScaleInIcon({
  children,
  delay = 0,
  duration = 0.3,
  from = 0.9,
  ...props
}: ScaleInIconProps) {
  const customVariants = {
    hidden: { opacity: 0, scale: from },
    visible: { opacity: 1, scale: 1 },
  };
  return (
    <motion.div
      variants={customVariants}
      initial="hidden"
      animate="visible"
      transition={createDelayedTransition(delay, duration)}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Zap } from "lucide-react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ScaleInIcon delay={0.1} duration={0.3} from={0.8}>
      <Zap className="w-6 h-6" />
    </ScaleInIcon>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon element to animate |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Delay before animation starts in seconds |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.3` | Animation duration in seconds |
| `from` | `number` | `0.9` | Initial scale value |

## Use cases

`ScaleInIcon` animates `scale` from `from` (default `0.9`) to `1` and `opacity` from `0` to `1` using `createDelayedTransition` with `easeOut`. The animation fires once on mount. Unlike [PopIcon](/docs/animations/icons/pop), which starts from `scale: 0` with an overshoot, `ScaleInIcon` starts from a value close to the final size, producing a compact zoom-in that is noticeable but not jarring.

Good use cases:

- **Feature icon reveals.** Icon sets on landing pages or pricing tables that scale in with a slight delay cascade feel polished and intentional.
- **Newly added list items.** When an item is added to a list, its icon scales in from `0.8` to `1` to highlight the change.
- **Empty-state icons.** A large decorative icon that zooms in gently draws the eye to the message without the drama of a pop.
- **Notification icons.** An avatar or status badge that scales in alongside its parent element as part of a compound entrance.
- **Tab or step indicator icons.** As the user advances through a stepper, the active step's icon scales in to mark the current state.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ScaleInIcon` when:**

- You want more visual presence than [FadeInIcon](/docs/animations/icons/fade-in) but less drama than [PopIcon](/docs/animations/icons/pop).
- `from={0.5}` or lower creates a more noticeable entrance for standalone icons; `from={0.9}` (default) is appropriate for icons within dense content where subtlety matters.
- You need to stagger multiple icons by incrementing `delay`, as the `easeOut` curve makes staggered sequences feel natural.

**Do not use it when:**

- The icon must re-animate on user interaction. `ScaleInIcon` only fires at mount. For tap or hover responses, use [BounceIcon](/docs/animations/icons/bounce), [WiggleIcon](/docs/animations/icons/wiggle), or [PopIcon](/docs/animations/icons/pop).
- You want a celebratory or playful arrival. The `easeOut` curve without overshoot is calm. Use [PopIcon](/docs/animations/icons/pop) with its back-out bezier for a more energetic entrance.
- The `from` value is below `0.3` and `duration` is long (above 0.5 s). A slow zoom from very small to full-size crosses into territory where users wait for the icon to arrive, which feels sluggish.

## Accessibility notes

- Scale and opacity transitions run through the entrance once and leave the element fully static. Screen readers are not affected by the transition itself.
- Icons alongside text labels should carry `aria-hidden="true"`. Icons that are the sole content of an interactive element need an accessible name on the parent:

```tsx
<button aria-label="Boost post" className="rounded p-1.5 hover:bg-neutral-100">
  <ScaleInIcon delay={0} from={0.8}>
    <Zap className="w-5 h-5 text-yellow-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  </ScaleInIcon>
</button>
```

- `prefers-reduced-motion` users still see the final visible state because `ScaleInIcon` renders the element from the start; only the transition is affected. To skip the animation entirely for reduced-motion users:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Sparkles } from "lucide-react"

export function AnimatedBadge() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return (
    <ScaleInIcon delay={reduced ? 0 : 0.2} duration={reduced ? 0 : 0.3} from={reduced ? 1 : 0.8}>
      <Sparkles className="w-6 h-6 text-purple-500" aria-hidden="true" />
    </ScaleInIcon>
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- The animation modifies `scale` and `opacity`, both compositor-only properties. No layout or repaint cost.
- One-shot animation (no `repeat`). After `duration` seconds, the element is a normal static node with no ongoing animation overhead.
- Staggering many `ScaleInIcon` instances by incrementing `delay` is safe. The total animation time is `delay + duration` per item, and short non-overlapping animations are trivially cheap.
- No `will-change` is needed. Scale and opacity are already composited without hinting.

## Customization examples

### Subtle entrance for a compact icon

The default `from={0.9}` is barely perceptible at small sizes; fine for UI chrome:

```tsx
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Star } from "lucide-react"

<ScaleInIcon from={0.9} duration={0.25}>
  <Star className="w-4 h-4 text-yellow-500" aria-hidden="true" />
</ScaleInIcon>
```

### Dramatic entrance for a hero illustration icon

Starting from `0.3` with a slightly longer duration makes the arrival unmistakable:

```tsx
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Sparkles } from "lucide-react"

<ScaleInIcon from={0.3} duration={0.5} delay={0.4}>
  <Sparkles className="w-16 h-16 text-purple-500" aria-hidden="true" />
</ScaleInIcon>
```

### Staggered feature icon row with precise delays

```tsx
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Shield, Zap, Globe } from "lucide-react"

const items = [
  { icon: Shield, color: "text-blue-500",   label: "Secure" },
  { icon: Zap,    color: "text-yellow-500", label: "Fast"   },
  { icon: Globe,  color: "text-green-500",  label: "Global" },
]

export function FeatureIcons() {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-10">
      {items.map(({ icon: Icon, color, label }, i) => (
        <div key={label} className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2">
          <ScaleInIcon delay={i * 0.1} from={0.7} duration={0.3}>
            <Icon className={`w-8 h-8 ${color}`} aria-hidden="true" />
          </ScaleInIcon>
          <span className="text-sm font-medium">{label}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Real-world examples

### Newly added item in a list

The icon for a freshly inserted item scales in to signal it is new:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { CheckCircle, Plus } from "lucide-react"

type Item = { id: number; label: string; fresh: boolean }

export function TaskList() {
  const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([
    { id: 1, label: "Write documentation", fresh: false },
  ])

  function addItem() {
    setItems((prev) => [
      ...prev,
      { id: Date.now(), label: "New task", fresh: true },
    ])
  }

  return (
    <div className="space-y-2">
      {items.map((item) => (
        <div key={item.id} className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-lg border border-neutral-200 px-3 py-2 dark:border-neutral-800">
          {item.fresh ? (
            <ScaleInIcon from={0.5} duration={0.3}>
              <CheckCircle className="w-4 h-4 text-green-500" aria-hidden="true" />
            </ScaleInIcon>
          ) : (
            <CheckCircle className="w-4 h-4 text-neutral-300" aria-hidden="true" />
          )}
          <span className="text-sm">{item.label}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
      <button
        onClick={addItem}
        className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg border border-dashed border-neutral-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-neutral-500 hover:border-neutral-400 dark:border-neutral-700"
      >
        <Plus className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
        Add task
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Step progress indicator

The active step icon scales in as the user advances:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { ScaleInIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/scale-in"
import { Check } from "lucide-react"

const steps = ["Account", "Profile", "Review"]

export function StepIndicator() {
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(0)

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      {steps.map((step, i) => (
        <div key={step} className="flex items-center gap-2">
          <div className="flex h-7 w-7 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-blue-600 text-white">
            {i < current ? (
              <ScaleInIcon from={0.6} duration={0.25}>
                <Check className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
              </ScaleInIcon>
            ) : (
              <span className="text-xs font-semibold">{i + 1}</span>
            )}
          </div>
          <span className="text-sm font-medium">{step}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
      <button
        onClick={() => setCurrent((p) => Math.min(p + 1, steps.length))}
        className="ml-4 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-white hover:bg-blue-700"
      >
        Next
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

# shake.mdx

title: Shake Icon
description: One-shot shake animation (horizontal shake) for icons.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { ShakeIcon } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/icons/shake';
import { AlertTriangle, AlertCircle, Info } from 'lucide-react';

## Overview

The `ShakeIcon` component creates a horizontal shake animation. Perfect for error states, alerts, and drawing attention to warnings.

## Preview

      <AlertTriangle className="w-8 h-8 text-yellow-500" />

    <span className="text-xs text-yellow-500">Hover</span>
    <ShakeIcon trigger="tap" intensity={15}>
      <AlertCircle className="w-8 h-8 text-red-500" />
    </ShakeIcon>
    <span className="text-xs text-red-500">Tap</span>
    <ShakeIcon trigger="mount" intensity={8}>
      <Info className="w-8 h-8 text-blue-500" />

    ```tsx title="lib/animation-presets.ts"
    export const listItemScaleVariants: Variants = {
      hidden: { opacity: 0, scale: 0.8 },
      visible: { opacity: 1, scale: 1 },
    };

    export const pageFadeVariants: Variants = {
      initial: { opacity: 0 },
      animate: { opacity: 1 },
      exit: { opacity: 0 },
    };

    export const pageSlideVariants: Variants = {
      initial: { opacity: 0, x: -20 },
      animate: { opacity: 1, x: 0 },
      exit: { opacity: 0, x: 20 },
    };

    export const pageScaleVariants: Variants = {
      initial: { opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 },
      animate: { opacity: 1, scale: 1 },
      exit: { opacity: 0, scale: 1.05 },
    };

    export const transitions = {
      smooth: { duration: 0.3, ease: "easeInOut" } as Transition,
      quick: { duration: 0.15, ease: "easeOut" } as Transition,
      slow: { duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" } as Transition,
      spring: { type: "spring", stiffness: 300, damping: 30 } as Transition,
      bouncy: { type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 10 } as Transition,
      continuous: (duration: number = 1) =>
        ({
          duration,
          ease: "linear",
          repeat: Infinity,
        }) as Transition,
    } as const;

    export const createContinuousTransition = (
      duration: number = 1,
      ease: Easing = "linear",
    ): Transition => ({
      duration,
      ease,
      repeat: Infinity,
    });

    export const createDelayedTransition = (
      delay: number,
      duration: number = 0.3,
    ): Transition => ({
      delay,
      duration,
      ease: "easeOut" as Easing,
    });

    export const createStaggerTransition = (
      staggerDelay: number = 0.1,
      delayChildren: number = 0,
    ): Transition => ({
      staggerChildren: staggerDelay,
      delayChildren,
    });
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/shake.tsx"
"use client";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import type { HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { shakeVariants } from "@/lib/animation-presets";
import { useState } from "react";
interface ShakeIconProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "animate"> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  trigger?: "hover" | "tap" | "mount";
  intensity?: number;
}
export function ShakeIcon({
  children,
  trigger = "hover",
  intensity = 10,
  ...props
}: ShakeIconProps) {
  const [key, setKey] = useState(0);
  const customVariants = {
    initial: { x: 0 },
    animate: {
      x: [0, -intensity, intensity, -intensity, intensity, 0],
    },
  };
  const handleTrigger = () => {
    setKey((prev) => prev + 1);
  };
  return (
    <motion.div
      key={key}
      variants={customVariants}
      initial="initial"
      animate={trigger === "mount" ? "animate" : undefined}
      whileHover={trigger === "hover" ? "animate" : undefined}
      whileTap={trigger === "tap" ? "animate" : undefined}
      onTap={trigger === "tap" ? handleTrigger : undefined}
      transition={{ duration: 0.4, ease: "easeInOut" }}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { ShakeIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/shake"
import { AlertTriangle } from "lucide-react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ShakeIcon trigger="hover" intensity={10}>
      <AlertTriangle className="w-6 h-6" />
    </ShakeIcon>
  )
}
```

  <AlertTriangle className="w-12 h-12 text-yellow-500" />
</ShakeIcon>`}
  <ShakeIcon trigger="hover" intensity={10} className="cursor-pointer">
    <AlertTriangle className="w-12 h-12 text-yellow-500" />
  </ShakeIcon>

### Tap Trigger

  background="dots"
  code={`<ShakeIcon trigger="tap" intensity={15}>
  <AlertCircle className="w-12 h-12 text-red-500" />
</ShakeIcon>`}
  <ShakeIcon trigger="tap" intensity={15}>
    <AlertCircle className="w-12 h-12 text-red-500" />
  </ShakeIcon>

### Subtle Shake

  background="dots"
  code={`<ShakeIcon trigger="hover" intensity={5} className="cursor-pointer">
  <Info className="w-12 h-12 text-blue-500" />
</ShakeIcon>`}
  <ShakeIcon trigger="hover" intensity={5} className="cursor-pointer">
    <Info className="w-12 h-12 text-blue-500" />
    <span className="text-xs text-blue-500">Hover</span>
  </ShakeIcon>

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon element to animate |
| `trigger` | `"hover"` \| `"tap"` \| `"mount"` | `"hover"` | When to trigger the shake animation |
| `intensity` | `number` | `10` | Shake intensity (distance in pixels) |

## Use cases

`ShakeIcon` translates the element along the x-axis: `x: [0, -intensity, intensity, -intensity, intensity, 0]` over 0.4 s with `easeInOut`. The horizontal back-and-forth directly mimics the real-world "no" gesture and the familiar "wrong password" shake used in iOS and macOS. Good fits:

- **Form validation errors.** A shaking warning or X icon on a field that fails validation immediately communicates what went wrong and where.
- **Destructive action confirmation.** Hovering over a delete icon with a shake on hover signals danger without a tooltip.
- **Locked or unauthorized states.** A `Lock` icon shaking when the user tries to access a restricted area conveys "access denied."
- **Attention on critical alerts.** An `AlertTriangle` that shakes on mount when a destructive confirmation modal opens pulls focus before the user reads the text.
- **Rate-limit or quota errors.** A `CircleSlash` or `Ban` icon that shakes when the user hits a limit provides immediate non-verbal feedback.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ShakeIcon` when:**

- The shake communicates "wrong," "denied," or "error" semantically. The horizontal shake is a near-universal rejection gesture.
- `trigger="mount"` fires once when an error state appears, which is the most accessible pattern (the error is new information that needs to be noticed).
- `trigger="hover"` on a destructive action like delete or disconnect forewarns the user before they commit.

**Do not use it when:**

- The icon represents something neutral or positive. Shaking a "send" or "save" icon reads as wrong.
- You need a continuous alert signal. A shaking icon that loops would be highly distracting and cause accessibility issues. Use [PulseIcon](/docs/animations/icons/pulse) for ongoing status.
- The shake is triggered by every keystroke in a text field. A shake on every input event is far too noisy; reserve it for discrete validation moments (on blur or on submit).
- `intensity` above 20 px: values that high can shift surrounding layout if the container does not clip overflow. Test for layout shift at high intensity values.

## Accessibility notes

- A shaking icon alone does not convey the error message to screen readers. The shake is a visual reinforcement only. Always pair it with visible error text and, if the error is dynamic, a live region:

```tsx
<div role="alert" className="flex items-center gap-2 text-red-600">
  <ShakeIcon trigger="mount" intensity={10}>
    <AlertCircle className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
  </ShakeIcon>
  <span className="text-sm font-medium">Incorrect password. Try again.</span>
</div>
```

- For `trigger="hover"` on a destructive icon, keyboard users will never see the shake (there is no keyboard hover equivalent). The button must have an accessible label describing the destructive action independently of the animation.
- The 0.4 s horizontal shake is brief enough to avoid vestibular concerns for most users, but for completeness you can skip it for `prefers-reduced-motion`:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { ShakeIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/shake"
import { AlertTriangle } from "lucide-react"

export function ErrorIcon() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <AlertTriangle className="w-5 h-5 text-red-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  return (
    <ShakeIcon trigger="mount" intensity={8}>
      <AlertTriangle className="w-5 h-5 text-red-500" aria-hidden="true" />
    </ShakeIcon>
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- The animation only changes `translateX`, a transform. It runs on the compositor with no layout recalculation.
- One-shot animation (no `repeat`). The compositor releases it after 0.4 s.
- The `key` increment on `tap` remounts the element. For a single icon this is negligible. Avoid placing `trigger="tap"` inside virtualized lists where each row would add its own key-reset remount.
- High `intensity` values (above 15 px) can cause the icon to visually overlap adjacent elements if the container does not have `overflow: hidden`. Add `overflow-hidden` to the wrapper when in doubt.

## Real-world examples

### Login form with wrong password shake

The shake fires each time a failed submit response arrives:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { ShakeIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/shake"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { AlertCircle } from "lucide-react"

export function LoginForm() {
  const [errorKey, setErrorKey] = useState(0)
  const [errorMsg, setErrorMsg] = useState("")
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault()
    // Simulate a failed auth attempt.
    const ok = false
    if (!ok) {
      setErrorMsg("Incorrect email or password.")
      setErrorKey((k) => k + 1)
    }
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="space-y-4 w-72">
      <input
        type="email"
        placeholder="Email"
        className="w-full rounded-lg border border-neutral-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm"
      />
      <input
        type="password"
        placeholder="Password"
        className="w-full rounded-lg border border-neutral-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm"
      />
      {errorMsg && (
        <div role="alert" className="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm text-red-600">
          {reduced ? (
            <AlertCircle className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
          ) : (
            <ShakeIcon key={errorKey} trigger="mount" intensity={8}>
              <AlertCircle className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
            </ShakeIcon>
          )}
          {errorMsg}
        </div>
      )}
      <button
        type="submit"
        className="w-full rounded-lg bg-blue-600 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white hover:bg-blue-700"
      >
        Sign in
      </button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

### Delete confirmation with shake on hover

The trash icon shakes on hover to signal the destructive nature of the action before the user clicks:

```tsx
"use client"
import { ShakeIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/shake"
import { Trash2 } from "lucide-react"

export function DeleteButton({ onDelete }: { onDelete: () => void }) {
  return (
    <button
      onClick={onDelete}
      aria-label="Delete this item permanently"
      className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg border border-red-200 px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-red-600 hover:bg-red-50 dark:border-red-900 dark:hover:bg-red-950"
    >
      <ShakeIcon trigger="hover" intensity={10}>
        <Trash2 className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
      </ShakeIcon>
      Delete
    </button>
  )
}
```

# spin.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/icons/spin.mdx

title: Spin Icon
description: Continuous rotation animation for icons.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { SpinIcon } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/icons/spin';
import { Loader, Loader2, RefreshCw, RotateCcw } from 'lucide-react';

## Overview

The `SpinIcon` component creates a continuous rotation animation. Perfect for loading indicators, refresh buttons, and processing states.

## Preview

  background="grid"
  code={`import { SpinIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/spin"
import { Loader } from "lucide-react"

<SpinIcon duration={1} direction="clockwise">
  <Loader className="w-8 h-8 text-blue-500" />
</SpinIcon>`}

    </SpinIcon>

      <Loader2 className="w-8 h-8 text-green-500" />
    </SpinIcon>
    <SpinIcon duration={1.5} direction="counterclockwise">
      <RefreshCw className="w-8 h-8 text-purple-500" />
    </SpinIcon>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/icons-spin
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/icons-spin
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/icons-spin
        ```

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/spin.tsx"
"use client";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import type { HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
interface SpinIconProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "animate"> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  duration?: number;
  direction?: "clockwise" | "counterclockwise";
}
export function SpinIcon({
  children,
  duration = 1,
  direction = "clockwise",
  ...props
}: SpinIconProps) {
  const rotation = direction === "clockwise" ? 360 : -360;
  return (
    <motion.div
      animate={{ rotate: rotation }}
      transition={{
        duration,
        ease: "linear",
        repeat: Infinity,
      }}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { SpinIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/spin"
import { Loader } from "lucide-react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <SpinIcon duration={1} direction="clockwise">
      <Loader className="w-6 h-6" />
    </SpinIcon>
  )
}
```

</SpinIcon>`}

    <Loader className="w-12 h-12 text-blue-500" />
  </SpinIcon>

</SpinIcon>`}

  </SpinIcon>

  <RefreshCw className="w-12 h-12 text-purple-500" />
</SpinIcon>`}

    <RefreshCw className="w-12 h-12 text-purple-500" />
  </SpinIcon>

### Counterclockwise

  background="dots"
  code={`<SpinIcon duration={1.5} direction="counterclockwise">
  <RotateCcw className="w-12 h-12 text-orange-500" />
</SpinIcon>`}
  <SpinIcon duration={1.5} direction="counterclockwise">
    <RotateCcw className="w-12 h-12 text-orange-500" />

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon element to animate |
| `duration` | `number` | `1` | Duration of one rotation in seconds |
| `direction` | `"clockwise"` \| `"counterclockwise"` | `"clockwise"` | Direction of rotation |

## Use cases

`SpinIcon` animates `rotate` at `ease: "linear"` with `repeat: Infinity`. The continuous linear spin is the universal signal for "a process is running." Unlike [RotateIcon](/docs/animations/icons/rotate), which fires once and stops, `SpinIcon` keeps rotating until it is unmounted. Good fits:

- **Inline loading states.** A `Loader` or `Loader2` icon spinning inside a button or next to a section title communicates an in-progress fetch.
- **Refresh-in-progress states.** A spinning `RefreshCw` inside a sync button while a sync is running, stopped as soon as the response arrives.
- **Background task indicators.** A small spinning icon in a status bar or corner badge signals that a background process is running.
- **Upload or processing progress.** A spinning `Upload` or `Cog` icon while a file is being processed.

Note: for a full-featured indeterminate spinner as a standalone loader, the [LoaderSpinner](/docs/animations/loaders/spinner) component may be a better fit as it is purpose-built with a styled ring.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `SpinIcon` when:**

- A process is actively running and you want the icon itself to carry the "in progress" signal without a separate spinner component.
- The icon's meaning (refresh, sync, load) is semantically aligned with circular rotation.
- You need directional control: `direction="counterclockwise"` for undo or rewind contexts.

**Do not use it when:**

- The process has ended and you forgot to unmount it. `repeat: Infinity` keeps the compositor awake indefinitely. Always tie unmounting to the resolved state.
- Multiple icons are spinning simultaneously in a list or feed. Each `SpinIcon` instance schedules its own infinite animation frame. For repeated rows, use a single section-level spinner instead.
- You want the rotation to stop on user interaction. Use [RotateIcon](/docs/animations/icons/rotate) for a one-shot rotation that fires on hover or tap and then rests.
- The spinning communicates something other than "process running." A spinning `Heart` or `Star` is semantically confusing.

## Accessibility notes

- A spinning icon on its own is invisible to screen readers. Add a visible or hidden label alongside it:

```tsx
<div role="status" className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <SpinIcon duration={1}>
    <Loader2 className="w-5 h-5 text-blue-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  </SpinIcon>
  <span className="sr-only">Loading...</span>
</div>
```

- When the spinner appears inside a button while an action is in flight, disable the button to prevent double submission and update its accessible name:

```tsx
<button disabled aria-label="Saving, please wait" className="...">
  <SpinIcon duration={1}>
    <Loader2 className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
  </SpinIcon>
  Saving...
</button>
```

- Continuous rotation can affect users with vestibular sensitivities. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` by slowing or stopping the spin:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { SpinIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/spin"
import { Loader2 } from "lucide-react"

export function LoadingIcon() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return (
    <div role="status">
      <SpinIcon duration={reduced ? 4 : 1}>
        <Loader2 className="w-5 h-5 text-blue-500" aria-hidden="true" />
      </SpinIcon>
      <span className="sr-only">Loading...</span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- `rotate` is a transform. The animation runs on the compositor thread with no layout or repaint cost.
- `repeat: Infinity` with `ease: "linear"` keeps the compositor awake for as long as the component is mounted. Always conditionally render rather than hiding with CSS:

```tsx
{loading && (
  <SpinIcon duration={1}>
    <Loader2 className="w-5 h-5 text-blue-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  </SpinIcon>
)}
```

- Avoid mounting many `SpinIcon` instances at the same time. Even though each is compositor-friendly, 20 simultaneous infinite rotations in a list multiply the compositor's scheduling work.
- `ease: "linear"` is intentional. Any easing other than linear creates visible jerk at the repeat boundary. Do not change the transition ease unless you understand the visual consequence at the loop point.

### Fast spin for an urgent process

## Real-world examples

### Submit button with spinning icon while saving

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { SpinIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/spin"
import { Loader2, Save } from "lucide-react"

export function SaveButton() {
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)

  async function handleSave() {
    setSaving(true)
    try {
      await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500))
    } finally {
      setSaving(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <button
      onClick={handleSave}
      disabled={saving}
      aria-label={saving ? "Saving, please wait" : "Save changes"}
      className="inline-flex h-10 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-5 text-sm font-semibold text-white disabled:opacity-70 hover:bg-blue-700"
    >
      {saving ? (
        <>
          <div role="status">
            <SpinIcon duration={0.8}>
              <Loader2 className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
            </SpinIcon>
            <span className="sr-only">Saving...</span>
          </div>
          Saving
        </>
      ) : (
        <>
          <Save className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
          Save changes
        </>
      )}
    </button>
  )
}
```

### Sync status in a toolbar

Spins while syncing, shows a check when done, and stops cleanly on unmount:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { SpinIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/spin"
import { RefreshCw, CheckCircle } from "lucide-react"

export function SyncButton() {
  const [syncing, setSyncing] = useState(false)
  const [done, setDone] = useState(false)

  async function handleSync() {
    setSyncing(true)
    setDone(false)
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000))
    setSyncing(false)
    setDone(true)
  }

  return (
    <button
      onClick={handleSync}
      disabled={syncing}
      aria-label={syncing ? "Syncing..." : "Sync data"}
      className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-lg px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-neutral-600 hover:bg-neutral-100 disabled:opacity-60 dark:text-neutral-400 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800"
    >
      {syncing ? (
        <div role="status">
          <SpinIcon duration={1}>
            <RefreshCw className="w-4 h-4 text-blue-500" aria-hidden="true" />
          </SpinIcon>
          <span className="sr-only">Syncing...</span>
        </div>
      ) : done ? (
        <CheckCircle className="w-4 h-4 text-green-500" aria-hidden="true" />
      ) : (
        <RefreshCw className="w-4 h-4" aria-hidden="true" />
      )}
      {syncing ? "Syncing" : done ? "Synced" : "Sync"}
    </button>
  )
}
```

# stroke-draw.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/icons/stroke-draw.mdx

title: Stroke Draw Icon
description: An icon that draws itself stroke by stroke.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';
import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { StrokeDrawIcon } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/icons/stroke-draw';

## Overview

The `StrokeDrawIcon` component animates SVG paths by drawing them stroke by stroke. Built using the `useStrokeDraw` hook, perfect for revealing icons with a hand-drawn effect.

<Callout type="info">
  **Uses primitive hook:** This component uses `useStrokeDraw` internally. You can use that hook directly on any SVG path for the same effect.
</Callout>

## Preview

  background="grid"
  code={`import { StrokeDrawIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/stroke-draw"

<StrokeDrawIcon 
  pathData="M12 2L2 7l10 5 10-5-10-5zM2 17l10 5 10-5M2 12l10 5 10-5"
  viewBox="0 0 24 24"
  className="w-8 h-8"
  duration={2}
/>`}

    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the hook**

    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-stroke-draw.ts"
    import { type MotionProps, type Easing } from "motion/react";

    export interface UseStrokeDrawOptions {
      duration?: number;
      delay?: number;
      repeat?: boolean;
      ease?: Easing | Easing[];
    }

    export function useStrokeDraw(options: UseStrokeDrawOptions = {}): MotionProps {
      const {
        duration = 1.5,
        delay = 0,
        repeat = false,
        ease = "easeInOut",
      } = options;

      return {
        initial: { pathLength: 0, opacity: 0 },
        animate: { pathLength: 1, opacity: 1 },
        transition: {
          pathLength: { duration, delay, ease },
          opacity: { duration: 0.2, delay },
          repeat: repeat ? Infinity : 0,
          repeatDelay: 1,
        },
      };
    }
    ```

    **Step 3: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/stroke-draw.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import {
  useStrokeDraw,
  type UseStrokeDrawOptions,
} from "@/lib/use-stroke-draw";
export interface StrokeDrawIconProps
  extends Omit<React.SVGProps<SVGSVGElement>, "children">,
    UseStrokeDrawOptions {
  pathData: string;
  strokeColor?: string;
  strokeWidth?: number;
}
export function StrokeDrawIcon({
  pathData,
  className,
  duration,
  delay,
  repeat,
  ease,
  strokeColor = "currentColor",
  strokeWidth = 2,
  ...props
}: StrokeDrawIconProps) {
  const strokeProps = useStrokeDraw({ duration, delay, repeat, ease });
  return (
    <motion.svg
      className={cn(className)}
      fill="none"
      stroke={strokeColor}
      strokeWidth={strokeWidth}
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
      viewBox={props.viewBox || "0 0 24 24"}
      width={props.width}
      height={props.height}
    >
      <motion.path d={pathData} {...strokeProps} />
    </motion.svg>
  );
}

```

```tsx
import { StrokeDrawIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/stroke-draw"

export default function Example() {

    <StrokeDrawIcon 
      pathData="M12 2L2 7l10 5 10-5-10-5zM2 17l10 5 10-5M2 12l10 5 10-5"
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      className="w-6 h-6"
    />
  )
}
```

## Props

| `pathData` | `string` | - | SVG path data |
| `strokeColor` | `string` | `"currentColor"` | Stroke color |
| `strokeWidth` | `number` | `2` | Stroke width |
| `duration` | `number` | `1` | Animation duration in seconds |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Delay before animation starts in seconds |
| `repeat` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to repeat the animation |
| `ease` | `string` | `"easeInOut"` | Easing function |
| `viewBox` | `string` | `"0 0 24 24"` | SVG viewBox attribute |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`StrokeDrawIcon` uses the `useStrokeDraw` hook to animate `pathLength` from `0` to `1` alongside `opacity` from `0` to `1`. The `pathLength` animation directly controls how much of the SVG stroke is visible, producing a hand-drawn reveal effect. By default `repeat=false` means it draws once on mount. Setting `repeat=true` loops the draw with a `repeatDelay: 1` pause. Good use cases:

- **Success checkmarks.** A check path drawing itself from left to right is one of the most satisfying completion signals in UI.
- **Onboarding illustrations.** Icons that draw themselves as the user reads an explanation keep attention on the diagram without looping motion.
- **Signature or handwriting metaphor.** A heart, star, or logo path drawing in gives a "drawn by hand" quality to a personal or boutique product.
- **Loading splash screens.** A brand icon drawing itself as a loading sequence before the main UI appears.
- **Step completion indicators.** A circle then a checkmark drawing in sequence as each step in a wizard completes.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `StrokeDrawIcon` when:**

- Your icon is a single continuous or near-continuous SVG path. Icons with many disconnected paths will draw each segment separately, which may look choppy.
- `repeat=false` (default) is correct for entrance animations. The icon draws once and stays.
- `repeat=true` works for ambient looping illustrations where the draw-and-reset cycle adds life without demanding attention.
- The icon is medium to large (24 px and above) where the stroke draw is actually perceptible. At 16 px and below, the effect is invisible.

**Do not use it when:**

- The icon uses `fill` instead of `stroke` (e.g., a solid filled shape). `pathLength` only affects stroked paths. Filled paths will remain invisible until the opacity transition completes.
- You need the icon to appear instantly. The draw takes at least `duration` seconds. For instant icons, use a static element or [FadeInIcon](/docs/animations/icons/fade-in) with `duration={0.15}`.
- The `pathData` contains many short, disconnected subpaths (like dotted patterns). Each subpath draws simultaneously from 0 to 1, which looks like fading rather than drawing.
- `repeat=true` is used on a small-text-adjacent icon. A looping draw next to body text is distracting; reserve looping for standalone illustrations.

## Accessibility notes

- `StrokeDrawIcon` renders an `<svg>` with no title or description by default. The element is not interactive and should be treated as decorative in most cases:

```tsx
<StrokeDrawIcon
  pathData="M22 11.08V12a10 10 0 1 1-5.93-9.14M22 4L12 14.01l-3-3"
  viewBox="0 0 24 24"
  className="w-8 h-8"
  strokeColor="green"
  aria-hidden="true"
/>
```

- When the drawing effect communicates a meaningful state (e.g., a checkmark that draws in to confirm a completed action), add a live region alongside it:

```tsx
<div role="status" className="flex items-center gap-2">
  <StrokeDrawIcon
    pathData="M5 13l4 4L19 7"
    viewBox="0 0 24 24"
    className="w-6 h-6"
    strokeColor="green"
    duration={0.6}
    aria-hidden="true"
  />
  <span className="sr-only">Completed</span>
</div>
```

- The `pathLength` animation is not a transform; it modifies a path attribute. Users with `prefers-reduced-motion` should ideally see the icon already drawn (final state) rather than animating. To skip the draw for them:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { StrokeDrawIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/stroke-draw"

export function AnimatedCheck() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return (
    <StrokeDrawIcon
      pathData="M5 13l4 4L19 7"
      viewBox="0 0 24 24"
      className="w-8 h-8"
      strokeColor="green"
      duration={reduced ? 0.01 : 0.8}
      delay={reduced ? 0 : 0.2}
      aria-hidden="true"
    />
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- `pathLength` and `opacity` are animated by motion/react. `pathLength` is not a compositor-only property; it causes the browser to recalculate the stroke geometry on each frame. Keep `duration` short (0.5 to 2 s) to limit the number of frames that require path recalculation.
- `repeat=false` (default) is a one-shot animation. After `duration` seconds the element is static with no ongoing cost.
- `repeat=true` uses `repeat: Infinity` with `repeatDelay: 1`. This is more expensive than a transform-only infinite animation because of the path recalculation. Use sparingly and prefer mounting in viewport only (with an `IntersectionObserver`) when the icon is not always visible.
- Very complex paths (hundreds of SVG commands) take more time to interpolate. Test on mid-range hardware if your `pathData` is long.
- Do not place many `StrokeDrawIcon` components with `repeat=true` on the same screen. Five or more simultaneously drawing paths will produce noticeable CPU usage.

## Real-world examples

### Form submission success checkmark

The check draws in after a successful form submit, giving satisfying visual confirmation:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { StrokeDrawIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/stroke-draw"

export function ContactForm() {
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false)

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault()
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1000))
    setSubmitted(true)
  }

  if (submitted) {
    return (
      <div
        role="status"
        className="flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-green-200 bg-green-50 px-8 py-6 dark:border-green-900 dark:bg-green-950"
      >
        <StrokeDrawIcon
          pathData="M22 11.08V12a10 10 0 1 1-5.93-9.14M22 4L12 14.01l-3-3"
          viewBox="0 0 24 24"
          className="w-12 h-12"
          strokeColor="#16a34a"
          strokeWidth={2}
          duration={1}
          aria-hidden="true"
        />
        <p className="font-semibold text-green-800 dark:text-green-300">Message sent!</p>
        <span className="sr-only">Your message was sent successfully.</span>
      </div>
    )
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="space-y-3 w-64">
      <input
        type="text"
        placeholder="Name"
        className="w-full rounded-lg border border-neutral-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm"
      />
      <input
        type="email"
        placeholder="Email"
        className="w-full rounded-lg border border-neutral-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm"
      />
      <button
        type="submit"
        className="w-full rounded-lg bg-blue-600 py-2 text-sm font-semibold text-white hover:bg-blue-700"
      >
        Send
      </button>
    </form>
  )
}
```

### Onboarding step icon reveal with delay

Each step icon draws in as the user advances through the onboarding wizard:

```tsx
import { StrokeDrawIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/stroke-draw"

const steps = [
  {
    label: "Create account",
    path: "M20 21v-2a4 4 0 0 0-4-4H8a4 4 0 0 0-4 4v2M12 11a4 4 0 1 0 0-8 4 4 0 0 0 0 8z",
  },
  {
    label: "Add your team",
    path: "M17 21v-2a4 4 0 0 0-4-4H5a4 4 0 0 0-4 4v2M9 11a4 4 0 1 0 0-8 4 4 0 0 0 0 8zM23 21v-2a4 4 0 0 0-3-3.87M16 3.13a4 4 0 0 1 0 7.75",
  },
  {
    label: "Start building",
    path: "M13 2H6a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v16a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h12a2 2 0 0 0 2-2V9zM13 2v7h7",
  },
]

export function OnboardingSteps({ currentStep }: { currentStep: number }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex gap-8">
      {steps.map(({ label, path }, i) => (
        <div key={label} className="flex flex-col items-center gap-2 text-center">
          {i <= currentStep ? (
            <StrokeDrawIcon
              pathData={path}
              viewBox="0 0 24 24"
              className="w-10 h-10 text-blue-600"
              duration={0.8}
              delay={i * 0.2}
              aria-hidden="true"
            />
          ) : (
            <div className="h-10 w-10 rounded-full border-2 border-dashed border-neutral-300" />
          )}
          <span className="text-xs font-medium text-neutral-600">{label}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Using the Hook Directly

This component is built using the `useStrokeDraw()` hook. You can use the hook directly for more control:

```tsx
import { useStrokeDraw } from "@/lib/hooks/use-stroke-draw"
import { motion } from "motion/react"

export function CustomStrokeIcon() {
  const strokeProps = useStrokeDraw({ duration: 2, delay: 0.5 })
  
  return (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" className="w-12 h-12">
      <motion.path 
        d="M12 2L2 7l10 5 10-5-10-5z" 
        stroke="currentColor"
        strokeWidth={2}
        fill="none"
        {...strokeProps} 
      />
    </svg>
  )
}
```

    ```tsx title="components/animations/icons/wiggle.tsx"
"use client";
import * as motion from "framer-motion/client";
import type { HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { wiggleVariants } from "@/lib/animation-presets";
import { useState } from "react";
interface WiggleIconProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "animate"> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  trigger?: "hover" | "tap" | "mount";
  intensity?: number;
}
export function WiggleIcon({
  children,
  trigger = "hover",
  intensity = 10,
  ...props
}: WiggleIconProps) {
  const [key, setKey] = useState(0);
  const customVariants = {
    initial: { rotate: 0 },
    animate: {
      rotate: [0, -intensity, intensity, -intensity, intensity, 0],
    },
  };
  const handleTrigger = () => {
    setKey((prev) => prev + 1);
  };
  return (
    <motion.div
      key={key}
      variants={customVariants}
      initial="initial"
      animate={trigger === "mount" ? "animate" : undefined}
      whileHover={trigger === "hover" ? "animate" : undefined}
      whileTap={trigger === "tap" ? "animate" : undefined}
      onTap={trigger === "tap" ? handleTrigger : undefined}
      transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" }}
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { WiggleIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/wiggle"
import { Bell } from "lucide-react"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <WiggleIcon trigger="hover" intensity={10}>
      <Bell className="w-6 h-6" />
    </WiggleIcon>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The icon element to animate |
| `trigger` | `"hover"` \| `"tap"` \| `"mount"` | `"hover"` | When to trigger the wiggle animation |
| `intensity` | `number` | `10` | Wiggle intensity (rotation angle in degrees) |

## Use cases

`WiggleIcon` animates `rotate` through `[0, -intensity, intensity, -intensity, intensity, 0]` over 0.5 s with `easeInOut`. It is a one-shot rotation wiggle that fires and rests. The left-right shake pattern is recognizable as a bell ring, a phone vibration, or a playful "hey, look at this" gesture. Good fits:

- **Notification bells.** A bell icon that wiggles on hover or on mount when unread notifications arrive is the most natural use.
- **Phone / contact icons.** A wiggling phone conveys "ring ring" more expressively than a static icon.
- **Warning or attention icons.** A gentler alternative to [ShakeIcon](/docs/animations/icons/shake) for icons that need to draw attention without implying "wrong."
- **Waving hand or greeting icons.** A wave or hand emoji icon wiggling on mount communicates a warm welcome.
- **Interactive toolbar icons.** A light wiggle on hover for icons that perform a rotational-metaphor action (e.g., a key icon wiggling to suggest "unlock this").

The key distinction from [ShakeIcon](/docs/animations/icons/shake): shake translates horizontally (x-axis, `[0, -10, 10, ...]`) while wiggle rotates around the z-axis (`rotate: [0, -10, 10, ...]`). Shake feels "wrong/error"; wiggle feels "playful/attention."

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `WiggleIcon` when:**

- The icon represents a ringing, waving, or vibrating object where rotational oscillation is physically accurate.
- You want a one-shot playful interaction that fires on hover or tap without persisting.
- The icon is isolated and not one of many simultaneously animated elements.

**Do not use it when:**

- You want a continuous wiggle. `WiggleIcon` fires once and stops. Continuous wiggling (`repeat: Infinity`) is not built into this component by design, because a permanently wiggling icon in a nav bar would be extremely distracting. If you genuinely need persistent motion, consider [PulseIcon](/docs/animations/icons/pulse) or [HeartbeatIcon](/docs/animations/icons/heartbeat) for a subtler always-on effect.
- The icon conveys an error. The rotational wiggle reads as playful, not alarming. Use [ShakeIcon](/docs/animations/icons/shake) for error states.
- Multiple icons in a navigation bar all wiggle on hover simultaneously. A wiggling nav bar is disorienting. Apply hover-wiggle only on the single bell or notification icon in the nav.
- `intensity` above 20 degrees on a small icon: high rotation on a small element can cause visual overlap with adjacent content.

## Accessibility notes

- The wiggle is purely visual. Icons alongside labels should carry `aria-hidden="true"`. Icons used as standalone interactive elements need an accessible name on the parent button:

```tsx
<button aria-label="Notifications (3 unread)" className="relative rounded p-2 hover:bg-neutral-100">
  <WiggleIcon trigger="hover">
    <Bell className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
  </WiggleIcon>
</button>
```

- For `trigger="mount"` on a notification bell, the wiggle fires once but does not announce itself to screen readers. Pair with a live region or badge count if the notification count is new information:

```tsx
<div role="status" aria-label="3 new notifications">
  <WiggleIcon trigger="mount">
    <Bell className="w-6 h-6 text-yellow-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  </WiggleIcon>
  <span className="sr-only">3 new notifications</span>
</div>
```

- A 0.5 s rotation wiggle is brief and unlikely to cause vestibular discomfort, but for completeness honor `prefers-reduced-motion`:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { WiggleIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/wiggle"
import { Bell } from "lucide-react"

export function NotificationBell() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <Bell className="w-6 h-6 text-yellow-500" aria-hidden="true" />
  return (
    <WiggleIcon trigger="mount" intensity={8}>
      <Bell className="w-6 h-6 text-yellow-500" aria-hidden="true" />
    </WiggleIcon>
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- `rotate` is a transform. The animation runs on the compositor thread with no layout recalculation or repaint.
- One-shot animation (no `repeat`). The compositor releases it after 0.5 s. No ongoing cost.
- The `key` increment on `tap` remounts the `motion.div` cleanly to allow re-animation on each tap. This is a trivial DOM operation for a single element.
- `trigger="hover"` uses `whileHover`. Between hover events the element returns to `rotate: 0` instantly because the wiggle has already completed by the time the user exits the hover. No reverse transition artifacts.

## Real-world examples

### Notification bell badge in a nav bar

Wiggles once on mount when new notifications arrive, with a badge count and reduced-motion fallback:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useEffect, useState } from "react"
import { WiggleIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/wiggle"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { Bell } from "lucide-react"

export function NavNotificationBell({ count }: { count: number }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const [wiggleKey, setWiggleKey] = useState(0)

  useEffect(() => {
    if (count > 0) setWiggleKey((k) => k + 1)
  }, [count])

  const icon = (
    <div className="relative">
      {reduced ? (
        <Bell className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
      ) : (
        <WiggleIcon key={wiggleKey} trigger="mount" intensity={10}>
          <Bell className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
        </WiggleIcon>
      )}
      {count > 0 && (
        <span
          className="absolute -right-1 -top-1 flex h-4 w-4 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-red-500 text-[10px] font-bold text-white"
          aria-hidden="true"
        >
          {count > 9 ? "9+" : count}
        </span>
      )}
    </div>
  )

  return (
    <button
      aria-label={count > 0 ? `${count} unread notifications` : "Notifications"}
      className="rounded-full p-2 hover:bg-neutral-100 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800"
    >
      {icon}
    </button>
  )
}
```

### Incoming call button

A phone icon wiggles on mount to simulate a ringing incoming call:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { WiggleIcon } from "@/components/animations/icons/wiggle"
import { Phone, PhoneOff } from "lucide-react"

export function IncomingCall({ caller }: { caller: string }) {
  const [answered, setAnswered] = useState<boolean | null>(null)

  if (answered !== null) {
    return (
      <p className="text-sm font-medium text-neutral-600">
        {answered ? `Connected to ${caller}` : "Call declined"}
      </p>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-4 rounded-2xl border border-neutral-200 p-6 shadow-sm dark:border-neutral-800">
      <WiggleIcon trigger="mount" intensity={14}>
        <Phone className="w-10 h-10 text-green-500" aria-hidden="true" />
      </WiggleIcon>
      <p className="font-semibold">{caller}</p>
      <p className="text-sm text-neutral-500">Incoming call</p>
      <div className="flex gap-4">
        <button
          onClick={() => setAnswered(true)}
          aria-label="Answer call"
          className="flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-green-500 text-white hover:bg-green-600"
        >
          <Phone className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
        </button>
        <button
          onClick={() => setAnswered(false)}
          aria-label="Decline call"
          className="flex h-12 w-12 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-red-500 text-white hover:bg-red-600"
        >
          <PhoneOff className="w-5 h-5" aria-hidden="true" />
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Overview

The `SlideInList` component creates a staggered slide-in effect for list items. Perfect for revealing content progressively from any direction.

    ```tsx title="components/animations/lists/slide-in.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface SlideInListProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "children"> {
  children: React.ReactNode[];
  direction?: "left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom";
  staggerDelay?: number;
  duration?: number;
  distance?: number;
  as?: "div" | "ul" | "ol" | "section" | "article";
}
export function SlideInList({
  children,
  direction = "left",
  staggerDelay = 0.1,
  duration = 0.3,
  distance = 20,
  as: Component = "div",
  className,
  ...props
}: SlideInListProps) {
  const childrenArray = React.Children.toArray(children);
  const getInitialPosition = () => {
    switch (direction) {
      case "left":
        return { x: -distance, y: 0 };
      case "right":
        return { x: distance, y: 0 };
      case "top":
        return { x: 0, y: -distance };
      case "bottom":
        return { x: 0, y: distance };
    }
  };
  const MotionComponent = motion[Component as keyof typeof motion] as any;
  return (
    <MotionComponent className={cn(className)} {...props}>
      {childrenArray.map((child, index) => (
        <motion.div
          key={index}
          initial={{ ...getInitialPosition(), opacity: 0 }}
          animate={{ x: 0, y: 0, opacity: 1 }}
          transition={{
            duration,
            delay: index * staggerDelay,
            ease: "easeOut",
          }}
        >
          {child}
        </motion.div>
      ))}
    </MotionComponent>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { SlideInList } from "@/components/animations/lists/slide-in"

const items = ["Item 1", "Item 2", "Item 3"]

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <SlideInList direction="left" staggerDelay={0.1}>
      {items.map((item, index) => (
        <div key={index} className="p-4 border rounded-lg">
          {item}
        </div>
      ))}
    </SlideInList>
  )
}
```
