  <LoaderSkeleton />

### Button Skeleton

<Preview background="dots" code={`<LoaderSkeleton width={120} height={40} borderRadius={8} />`}>
  <LoaderSkeleton width={120} height={40} borderRadius={8} />

### Card Skeleton

<Preview background="dots" code={`<LoaderSkeleton width={300} height={200} borderRadius={12} />`}>
  <LoaderSkeleton width={300} height={200} borderRadius={12} />

### Profile Layout

<Preview background="dots" code={`<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 w-64">
  <LoaderSkeleton width={64} height={64} borderRadius={32} />
  <LoaderSkeleton width="100%" height={20} />
  <LoaderSkeleton width="80%" height={16} />
</div>`}>
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 w-64">
    <LoaderSkeleton width={64} height={64} borderRadius={32} />
    <LoaderSkeleton width="100%" height={20} />
    <LoaderSkeleton width="80%" height={16} />

## Props

| `width` | `string \| number` | `"100%"` | Width of the skeleton |
| `height` | `number` | `20` | Height of the skeleton in pixels |
| `borderRadius` | `number` | `4` | Border radius in pixels |
| `baseColor` | `string` | `"#e5e7eb"` | Base color of the skeleton |
| `highlightColor` | `string` | `"#f3f4f6"` | Highlight color of the skeleton |
| `duration` | `number` | `1.5` | Animation duration in seconds |

## Use cases

`LoaderSkeleton` is a **structural placeholder** loader, not a progress indicator. It renders a rectangle filled with `baseColor` (default `#e5e7eb`) and sweeps a `linear-gradient` highlight (`highlightColor`, default `#f3f4f6`) from `x: -100%` to `x: 100%` over `duration` seconds. Because `width` defaults to `"100%"` and `height` defaults to `20`, a single instance makes a text-line placeholder. Compose multiple instances to match the real content layout. Reach for it when:

- **You are about to render a list.** A stack of skeleton rows shaped like actual list items (avatar circle + two text lines) dramatically reduces perceived wait compared to a centered spinner.
- **You are loading a card with a known structure.** Profile cards, product cards, or dashboard widgets with a predictable height and layout benefit from skeletons because the layout does not shift when data arrives.
- **The page renders in regions** and different areas load independently. Each region can show its own skeleton without blocking the rest of the UI.
- **You want to delay showing a spinner entirely.** For content that almost always loads in under one second, a skeleton is less jarring than a spinner that flickers on and off.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use skeleton when:**

- You know the approximate shape of the content being loaded (text, image, button, avatar).
- The loading area is at least a couple of lines tall so the shape signal is meaningful.
- You are building a list, feed, or grid where repeated rows create a recognizable scaffold.

**Reach for a spinner or other loader when:**

- **The wait is for an action, not content.** A form submit, a file delete, or a search executing does not have a content shape to fill. Use a [Spinner](/docs/animations/loaders/spinner) or [Dots](/docs/animations/loaders/dots).
- **You have no idea what shape the content will have.** A skeleton for unknown-shape content just looks like placeholder rectangles, which is no better than a spinner.
- **The content area is tiny.** A 20 px high skeleton inside a button is meaningless. Use a [Spinner](/docs/animations/loaders/spinner) instead.
- **You know the exact progress percentage.** Use [Liquid Progress](/docs/animations/loaders/liquid-progress).

## Accessibility notes

Skeleton loaders are purely visual placeholders. The shimmer animation provides no semantic signal to assistive technologies.

- **Wrap the entire skeleton group in a live region:**

```tsx
<div role="status" aria-label="Loading profile">
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 w-64">
    <LoaderSkeleton width={64} height={64} borderRadius={32} />
    <LoaderSkeleton width="100%" height={20} />
    <LoaderSkeleton width="80%" height={16} />
  </div>
  <span className="sr-only">Loading profile...</span>
</div>
```

- **Do not add `role="status"` to each individual skeleton.** One wrapper announcement is enough. Multiple live regions firing at once create noise.
- **Respect reduced motion.** The shimmer sweep is a continuous translation. Slow it significantly or stop it for users who prefer less motion:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { LoaderSkeleton } from "@/components/animations/loaders/skeleton"

function AccessibleSkeleton(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof LoaderSkeleton>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return <LoaderSkeleton {...props} duration={reduced ? 0 : 1.5} />
}
```

Setting `duration={0}` stops the motion entirely while keeping the base color as a static placeholder.

## Performance considerations

- **The shimmer is a transform.** The gradient element animates `x` (a `translateX` transform), which is compositor-only with no layout or paint cost.
- **Many skeletons = many animation loops.** A 20-row list with three skeletons per row mounts 60 `motion.div` instances, each with its own `repeat: Infinity`. This is heavier than a single [Spinner](/docs/animations/loaders/spinner). Consider:
  - Capping the skeleton row count to 5 to 8 visible items even if more are expected.
  - Using a CSS-only shimmer (a `@keyframes` on `background-position`) for very long lists, since a single CSS animation is shared across all instances.
- **Unmount when done.** Skeletons are often swapped out by conditionally rendering either the skeleton group or the real content, which handles cleanup automatically.


```tsx
  highlightColor="#3f3f46"
/>
```

### Wide banner placeholder


```tsx
      <LoaderSkeleton width="50%" height={14} borderRadius={4} />
```

### Feed list skeleton

Use it as a drop-in replacement while the real list items are fetching:

```tsx

    <div className="flex items-start gap-3 py-4">
      <LoaderSkeleton width={40} height={40} borderRadius={20} />
      <div className="flex flex-1 flex-col gap-2">
        <LoaderSkeleton width="60%" height={14} borderRadius={4} />
        <LoaderSkeleton width="90%" height={12} borderRadius={4} />
        <LoaderSkeleton width="75%" height={12} borderRadius={4} />
      </div>
    </div>

export function FeedSkeleton() {
  return (
    <div
      role="status"
      aria-label="Loading feed"
      className="divide-y divide-neutral-100 dark:divide-neutral-800"
    >
      {Array.from({ length: 5 }).map((_, i) => (
        <FeedRowSkeleton key={i} />
      ))}
      <span className="sr-only">Loading feed...</span>
```

# spinner.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/loaders/spinner.mdx

title: Spinner Loader
description: A circular spinning loader.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { LoaderSpinner } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/loaders/spinner';

## Overview

The `LoaderSpinner` component creates a classic circular spinning loader. Perfect for loading states, processing indicators, and async operations.

## Preview

  background="grid"
  code={`import { LoaderSpinner } from "@/components/animations/loaders/spinner"

<LoaderSpinner />`}
  <div className="flex gap-8 items-center justify-center">
    <LoaderSpinner />
    <LoaderSpinner size={60} color="#3b82f6" borderWidth={6} />
    <LoaderSpinner size={50} color="#10b981" duration={0.8} />

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/loaders-spinner
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/loaders-spinner
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/loaders-spinner
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/loaders-spinner
        ```
    ```tsx title="components/animations/loaders/spinner.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface LoaderSpinnerProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "children"> {
  size?: number;
  color?: string;
  borderWidth?: number;
  duration?: number;
}
export function LoaderSpinner({
  className,
  size = 40,
  color = "currentColor",
  borderWidth = 4,
  duration = 1,
  ...props
}: LoaderSpinnerProps) {
  return (
    <motion.div
      className={cn("rounded-full", className)}
      style={{
        width: size,
        height: size,
        border: `${borderWidth}px solid transparent`,
        borderTopColor: color,
        borderRightColor: color,
      }}
      animate={{ rotate: 360 }}
      transition={{
        duration,
        ease: "linear",
        repeat: Infinity,
      }}
      {...props}
    />
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { LoaderSpinner } from "@/components/animations/loaders/spinner"

export default function Example() {
  return <LoaderSpinner />
}
```

## Examples

### Default

<Preview background="dots" code={`<LoaderSpinner />`}>
  <LoaderSpinner />

### Large Blue Spinner

<Preview background="dots" code={`<LoaderSpinner size={60} color="#3b82f6" borderWidth={6} />`}>
  <LoaderSpinner size={60} color="#3b82f6" borderWidth={6} />

### Fast Green Spinner

<Preview background="dots" code={`<LoaderSpinner size={50} color="#10b981" duration={0.6} />`}>
  <LoaderSpinner size={50} color="#10b981" duration={0.6} />

## Props

| `size` | `number` | `40` | Size of the spinner in pixels |
| `color` | `string` | `"currentColor"` | Color of the spinner |
| `borderWidth` | `number` | `4` | Border width in pixels |
| `duration` | `number` | `1` | Animation duration in seconds |

## Use cases

The spinner communicates an **indeterminate** wait, meaning work is happening but you can't say how far along it is. Reach for it when:

- **Button actions.** Disable a submit button and swap its label for a spinner while a request is in flight, so the user can't double-submit.
- **Inline async work.** Saving a field, refreshing a widget, or loading a dropdown's options after it opens.
- **Section-level loading.** A card, table, or panel waiting on its own fetch while the rest of the page stays interactive.
- **Route transitions.** A brief overlay while the next page's data resolves.

Because `color` defaults to `currentColor`, the spinner inherits the text color of its container. Drop it inside a button or a colored badge and it matches automatically with no extra config.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use a spinner when:**

- The wait is roughly **0.3 to 10 seconds** and you have no progress information.
- The blocked area is small, like a button or a card, rather than a full content-heavy page.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **You know the percentage.** Use a determinate indicator like [Liquid Progress](/docs/animations/loaders/liquid-progress) instead. A spinner that could show real progress but doesn't feels slower than it is.
- **You're loading structured content** such as lists, articles, or profiles. A [Skeleton](/docs/animations/loaders/skeleton) preserves layout and reduces perceived wait better than a centered spinner.
- **The wait is under ~300ms.** Mounting a spinner that flashes for one frame is more distracting than showing nothing. Delay it:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react"
import { LoaderSpinner } from "@/components/animations/loaders/spinner"

// Only show the spinner if loading outlasts the delay, avoiding a flicker on fast responses.
function DelayedSpinner({ loading, delay = 300 }: { loading: boolean; delay?: number }) {
  const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false)

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!loading) return setVisible(false)
    const id = setTimeout(() => setVisible(true), delay)
    return () => clearTimeout(id)
  }, [loading, delay])

  return visible ? <LoaderSpinner /> : null
}
```

## Accessibility notes

The spinner is a purely visual element. On its own a screen reader sees an empty, rotating `<div>`. Make the loading state perceivable to everyone:

- **Announce it.** Wrap the spinner in a live region with an accessible label so assistive tech says "Loading" instead of nothing:

```tsx
<div role="status">
  <LoaderSpinner />
  <span className="sr-only">Loading...</span>
</div>
```

- **Don't rely on motion alone.** Some users disable animations entirely; the `role="status"` text above is what actually conveys "busy" to them.
- **Respect reduced motion.** A continuous spin can trigger discomfort for users with vestibular sensitivities. Honor their OS setting and slow it down or stop it:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { LoaderSpinner } from "@/components/animations/loaders/spinner"

function AccessibleSpinner() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  // Near-still rotation keeps the "busy" affordance without spinning fast.
  return <LoaderSpinner duration={reduced ? 4 : 1} />
}
```

- **Manage focus on overlays.** If a spinner blocks the whole screen, move focus to the overlay and restore it when the wait ends, so keyboard users aren't interacting with hidden content underneath.

## Performance considerations

- **GPU-friendly by design.** The animation only changes `rotate`, which is a transform, so it runs on the compositor with no layout and no repaint. You get a steady 60fps even on low-end devices.
- **It runs forever until unmounted.** `repeat: Infinity` keeps the compositor awake. Conditionally render the spinner (`{loading && <LoaderSpinner />}`) rather than hiding it with CSS, so the animation stops when the work is done.
- **Avoid spinner swarms.** Twenty spinners in a list each schedule their own animation frame. For repeated rows, prefer a single section spinner or a [Skeleton](/docs/animations/loaders/skeleton).
- **No `will-change` needed.** A transform-only animation is already composited, so adding `will-change` here just costs memory.

## Customization examples

### Branded, inherits text color

`currentColor` means the spinner takes on its parent's color for free:

```tsx
<button className="inline-flex items-center gap-2 text-blue-600">
  <LoaderSpinner size={16} borderWidth={2} />
  Saving
</button>
```

### Thin and subtle

Smaller border width and a slower duration read as calmer:

```tsx
<LoaderSpinner size={24} borderWidth={2} duration={1.4} color="#94a3b8" />
```

### Bold and prominent

For full-page or hero loading states:

```tsx
<LoaderSpinner size={72} borderWidth={8} duration={0.8} color="#3b82f6" />
```

## Real-world examples

### Submit button with loading state

The most common use: block the action, show progress, and prevent double clicks.

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { LoaderSpinner } from "@/components/animations/loaders/spinner"

export function SaveButton() {
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)

  async function handleSave() {
    setSaving(true)
    try {
      await saveChanges()
    } finally {
      setSaving(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <button
      onClick={handleSave}
      disabled={saving}
      className="inline-flex h-11 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-6 text-sm font-semibold text-white disabled:opacity-70"
    >
      {saving && <LoaderSpinner size={16} borderWidth={2} />}
      {saving ? "Saving..." : "Save changes"}
    </button>
  )
}
```

### Section that loads its own data

Keep the rest of the page usable while one card fetches:

```tsx
"use client"
import { LoaderSpinner } from "@/components/animations/loaders/spinner"

export function StatsCard({ loading, value }: { loading: boolean; value?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="rounded-xl border border-neutral-200 p-6 dark:border-neutral-800">
      <p className="text-sm text-neutral-500">Revenue</p>
      {loading ? (
        <div role="status" className="flex h-9 items-center">
          <LoaderSpinner size={20} borderWidth={2} color="#3b82f6" />
          <span className="sr-only">Loading revenue...</span>
        </div>
      ) : (
        <p className="text-3xl font-bold">{value}</p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Full-page overlay

For blocking transitions where the whole view is pending:

```tsx
<div
  role="status"
  className="fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center bg-white/70 backdrop-blur-sm dark:bg-black/70"
>
  <LoaderSpinner size={48} borderWidth={5} color="#3b82f6" />
  <span className="sr-only">Loading page...</span>
</div>
```

# page-transition-fade.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/pages/page-transition-fade.mdx

title: Page Transition Fade
description: Smooth fade transition between page navigations using View Transitions API.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';
import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';

## Overview

The `PageTransitionFade` component creates a smooth fade-in/fade-out effect when navigating between pages. Uses the native View Transitions API for hardware-accelerated animations with customizable duration and easing.

  background="grid"
  code={`"use client"

import { motion } from "motion/react"

// Simulated Page Transition
export function FadePreview() {
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md h-64 bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900 rounded-xl border border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-800 shadow-sm overflow-hidden relative">
      <motion.div 
        initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
        animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
        transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" }}
        className="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900"
        <div className="text-center">
          <div className="h-12 w-12 bg-blue-500 rounded-full mx-auto mb-4" />
          <h3 className="font-semibold text-lg">New Page Content</h3>
          <p className="text-neutral-500 text-sm mt-2">Faded in smoothly</p>
      </motion.div>
  )
}`}
  <div className="w-full max-w-md h-64 bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900 rounded-xl border border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-800 shadow-sm overflow-hidden relative">
    <div className="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900 animate-in fade-in duration-700 fill-mode-forwards">
      <div className="text-center">
        <div className="h-12 w-12 bg-blue-500 rounded-full mx-auto mb-4" />
        <h3 className="font-semibold text-lg">New Page Content</h3>
        <p className="text-neutral-500 text-sm mt-2">Faded in smoothly</p>

<Callout type="info">
  **Browser Support:** View Transitions API is supported in Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, and Opera 97+. Falls back to instant navigation in unsupported browsers.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-fade
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-fade
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-fade
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-fade
        ```
    **Step 1:** Create the component

    ```tsx title="components/animations/pages/page-transition-fade.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
export interface PageTransitionFadeProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  duration?: number;
  ease?: string;
}
export function PageTransitionFade({
  children,
  duration = 0.3,
  ease = "ease-in-out",
}: PageTransitionFadeProps) {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof document === "undefined" || !document.startViewTransition) {
      return;
    }
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--page-transition-duration",
      `${duration}s`,
    );
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--page-transition-ease", ease);
  }, [pathname, duration, ease]);
  return <>{children}</>;
}

```

    **Step 2:** Create navigation wrapper

    ```tsx title="components/animations/pages/page-transition-link.tsx"
    "use client"

    import * as React from "react"
    import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"
    import Link, { LinkProps } from "next/link"

    interface PageTransitionLinkProps extends LinkProps {
      children: React.ReactNode
      className?: string
    }

    export function PageTransitionLink({
      href,
      children,
      className,
      ...props
    }: PageTransitionLinkProps) {
      const router = useRouter()

      const handleClick = async (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>) => {
        e.preventDefault()

        if (!document.startViewTransition) {
          router.push(href.toString())
          return
        }

        const transition = document.startViewTransition(() => {
          router.push(href.toString())
        })

        await transition.ready
      }

      return (
        <Link 
          href={href} 
          onClick={handleClick} 
          className={className}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </Link>
      )
    }
    ```

    **Step 3:** Add required CSS to `globals.css`

    ```css
    /* Page Transition - Fade */
    :root {
      --page-transition-duration: 0.3s;
      --page-transition-ease: ease-in-out;
    }

    ::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: fade-out var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    ::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: fade-in var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    @keyframes fade-out {
      from {
        opacity: 1;
      }
      to {
        opacity: 0;
      }
    }

    @keyframes fade-in {
      from {
        opacity: 0;
      }
      to {
        opacity: 1;
      }
    }

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      ::view-transition-group(*),
      ::view-transition-old(*),
      ::view-transition-new(*) {
        animation: none !important;
      }
    }
    ```

## Props

### PageTransitionFade

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The page content |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.3` | Transition duration in seconds |
| `ease` | `string` | `"ease-in-out"` | CSS easing function |

### PageTransitionLink

| `href` | `string` | - | Destination URL |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Link content |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |
| `...props` | `LinkProps` | - | All Next.js Link props |

## Use cases

`PageTransitionFade` uses the native View Transitions API. `PageTransitionFade` itself is a thin wrapper that writes CSS custom properties (`--page-transition-duration`, `--page-transition-ease`) to the document root on every `pathname` change. The actual animation lives in `globals.css` via `::view-transition-old(root)` and `::view-transition-new(root)`. Navigation is handled by `PageTransitionLink`, which calls `document.startViewTransition` before pushing a new route. Reach for it when:

- **Content-heavy multi-page apps.** Articles, docs sites, and portfolios where navigating between pages benefits from a moment of visual continuity.
- **Onboarding flows and wizards.** A gentle fade between steps feels less jarring than an instant page swap.
- **Marketing sites.** Fading between top-level pages (Home, About, Pricing) adds polish without imposing a directional assumption about the site structure.
- **Apps where you want the simplest possible transition.** Fade is the safest choice when you do not know whether a slide direction would feel natural to all users.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use fade transitions when:**

- You want page changes to feel smooth but you have no meaningful spatial relationship between routes (no "drill-in" or "back" navigation).
- Browser support coverage of Chrome 111+/Edge 111+ is acceptable for your audience. The CSS fallback is instant navigation.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Routes have a spatial hierarchy** (like a detail page inside a list). A left/right slide from [Page Transition Slide](/docs/animations/pages/page-transition-slide) communicates "forward" and "back" far better than a fade.
- **The page is long and scroll position matters.** View Transitions capture the full rendered page and can flash the scroll position to the top during the transition. Test carefully.
- **Safari is a primary target.** View Transitions API is not supported in Safari at time of writing (support is in progress). All fade behavior will silently fall back to instant navigation.

## Accessibility notes

Page transitions involve replacing visible content, which creates two accessibility concerns.

- **Focus management.** When a new page renders, focus should move to a logical starting point (the `<h1>`, the skip-link, or the main landmark). In Next.js App Router this is handled automatically, but verify it works in your project because the View Transition timing can interfere with focus restoration.
- **Reduced motion is handled by the CSS.** The installed `globals.css` already includes:

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  ::view-transition-group(*),
  ::view-transition-old(*),
  ::view-transition-new(*) {
    animation: none !important;
  }
}
```

This completely disables the transition for users who opt out of motion via their OS settings. No extra JavaScript is needed.

- **Do not animate content that conveys status.** If the page that fades in contains a confirmation message, make sure the message is in a live region (`role="status"` or `aria-live="polite"`) so it is announced even if it entered via animation.

## Performance considerations

- **The View Transitions API is hardware-accelerated.** The browser takes a screenshot of the old page and composites it with the new page using GPU transforms, so the fade costs no JavaScript on each frame.
- **`duration` defaults to 0.3 s.** Fade transitions longer than 0.5 s feel slow. Keep the duration short for navigation that users repeat frequently.
- **The `PageTransitionFade` component itself renders no DOM.** It returns `<>{children}</>` and only writes CSS custom properties via `useEffect`. There is no wrapping element and no layout cost.
- **`document.startViewTransition` is called synchronously before `router.push`.** This means the browser's transition lifecycle is tightly coupled to Next.js's navigation. If `router.push` is slow (e.g., slow RSC fetch), the old page stays frozen until the new page is ready. This is the expected behavior, but it can make slow navigations feel "stuck." Consider showing a loading indicator for navigations that take more than 300 ms.

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
```

## Advanced Usage

### Per-Page Transitions

You can customize transitions for specific pages by using data attributes:

```tsx title="app/special-page/page.tsx"
export default function SpecialPage() {
  return (
    <div data-transition="special">
      <h1>Special Page</h1>
      <p>This page has a custom transition</p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

Then in your CSS:

```css
[data-transition="special"]::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: fade-out 0.8s ease-out;
}

[data-transition="special"]::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: fade-in 0.8s ease-in;
}
```

### Crossfade Effect

For a smooth crossfade without overlap:

```css
::view-transition-old(root),
::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation-duration: 0.3s;
  animation-timing-function: ease-in-out;
}

::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation-name: fade-out;
}

::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation-name: fade-in;
  animation-delay: 0.15s; /* Start halfway through old fade */
}
```

# page-transition-slide.mdx

title: Page Transition Slide
description: Smooth slide transition between page navigations using View Transitions API.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';
import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';

## Overview

The `PageTransitionSlide` component creates a smooth sliding effect when navigating between pages. Choose from left, right, top, or bottom directions. Uses the native View Transitions API for hardware-accelerated animations with customizable duration and easing.

  background="grid"
  code={`"use client"

// Simulated Page Transition
export function SlidePreview() {

      </motion.div>
  )
}`}
  <div className="w-full max-w-md h-64 bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900 rounded-xl border border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-800 shadow-sm overflow-hidden relative">

  **Browser Support:** View Transitions API is supported in Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, and Opera 97+. Falls back to instant navigation in unsupported browsers.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-slide
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-slide
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-slide
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/pages-page-transition-slide
        ```

    **Step 1:** Create the component

    ```tsx title="components/animations/pages/page-transition-slide.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation";
export type SlideDirection = "left" | "right" | "top" | "bottom";
export interface PageTransitionSlideProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  direction?: SlideDirection;
  duration?: number;
  ease?: string;
}
export function PageTransitionSlide({
  children,
  direction = "left",
  duration = 0.4,
  ease = "ease-in-out",
}: PageTransitionSlideProps) {
  const pathname = usePathname();
  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof document === "undefined" || !document.startViewTransition) {
      return;
    }
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--page-transition-duration",
      `${duration}s`,
    );
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--page-transition-ease", ease);
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-slide-direction", direction);
  }, [pathname, duration, ease, direction]);
  return <>{children}</>;
}

```

    **Step 2:** Create navigation wrapper

    ```tsx title="components/animations/pages/page-transition-link.tsx"
    "use client"

    import * as React from "react"
    import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"
    import Link, { LinkProps } from "next/link"

    interface PageTransitionLinkProps extends LinkProps {
      children: React.ReactNode
      className?: string
    }

    export function PageTransitionLink({
      href,
      children,
      className,
      ...props
    }: PageTransitionLinkProps) {
      const router = useRouter()

      const handleClick = async (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>) => {
        e.preventDefault()

        if (!document.startViewTransition) {
          router.push(href.toString())
          return
        }

        const transition = document.startViewTransition(() => {
          router.push(href.toString())
        })

        await transition.ready
      }

      return (
        <Link 
          href={href} 
          onClick={handleClick} 
          className={className}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </Link>
      )
    }
    ```

    **Step 3:** Add required CSS to `globals.css`

    ```css
    /* Page Transition - Slide */
    :root {
      --page-transition-duration: 0.4s;
      --page-transition-ease: ease-in-out;
    }

    /* Slide Left */
    [data-slide-direction="left"]::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: slide-out-left var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    [data-slide-direction="left"]::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: slide-in-left var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    /* Slide Right */
    [data-slide-direction="right"]::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: slide-out-right var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    [data-slide-direction="right"]::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: slide-in-right var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    /* Slide Top */
    [data-slide-direction="top"]::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: slide-out-top var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    [data-slide-direction="top"]::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: slide-in-top var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    /* Slide Bottom */
    [data-slide-direction="bottom"]::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: slide-out-bottom var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    [data-slide-direction="bottom"]::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: slide-in-bottom var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
    }

    /* Slide Left Animations */
    @keyframes slide-out-left {
      from {
        transform: translateX(0);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateX(-100%);
      }
    }

    @keyframes slide-in-left {
      from {
        transform: translateX(100%);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateX(0);
      }
    }

    /* Slide Right Animations */
    @keyframes slide-out-right {
      from {
        transform: translateX(0);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateX(100%);
      }
    }

    @keyframes slide-in-right {
      from {
        transform: translateX(-100%);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateX(0);
      }
    }

    /* Slide Top Animations */
    @keyframes slide-out-top {
      from {
        transform: translateY(0);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateY(-100%);
      }
    }

    @keyframes slide-in-top {
      from {
        transform: translateY(100%);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateY(0);
      }
    }

    /* Slide Bottom Animations */
    @keyframes slide-out-bottom {
      from {
        transform: translateY(0);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateY(100%);
      }
    }

    @keyframes slide-in-bottom {
      from {
        transform: translateY(-100%);
      }
      to {
        transform: translateY(0);
      }
    }

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      ::view-transition-group(*),
      ::view-transition-old(*),
      ::view-transition-new(*) {
        animation: none !important;
      }
    }
    ```

## Usage

### Setup in Layout

Wrap your application with the `PageTransitionSlide` component:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { PageTransitionSlide } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-slide"

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode
}) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <PageTransitionSlide direction="left">
          {children}
        </PageTransitionSlide>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

### Using Transition Links

Replace standard Next.js `Link` components with `PageTransitionLink`:

```tsx
import { PageTransitionLink } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-link"

export function Navigation() {
  return (
    <nav className="flex gap-4">
      <PageTransitionLink href="/" className="hover:text-blue-600">
        Home
      </PageTransitionLink>
      <PageTransitionLink href="/about" className="hover:text-blue-600">
        About
      </PageTransitionLink>
      <PageTransitionLink href="/contact" className="hover:text-blue-600">
        Contact
      </PageTransitionLink>
    </nav>
  )
}
```

### Programmatic Navigation

```tsx
"use client"

import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"

export function NavigateButton() {
  const router = useRouter()

  const handleNavigate = async () => {
    if (!document.startViewTransition) {
      router.push('/destination')
      return
    }

    const transition = document.startViewTransition(() => {
      router.push('/destination')
    })

    await transition.ready
  }

  return (
    <button onClick={handleNavigate} className="inline-flex h-11 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-6 text-sm font-semibold text-white">
      Navigate
    </button>
  )
}
```

## Props

### PageTransitionSlide

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The page content |
| `direction` | `"left"` \| `"right"` \| `"top"` \| `"bottom"` | `"left"` | Slide direction |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.4` | Transition duration in seconds |
| `ease` | `string` | `"ease-in-out"` | CSS easing function |

### PageTransitionLink

| `href` | `string` | - | Destination URL |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Link content |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |
| `...props` | `LinkProps` | - | All Next.js Link props |

## Use cases

`PageTransitionSlide` builds on the same View Transitions API mechanism as `PageTransitionFade` but adds a `direction` prop that sets a `data-slide-direction` attribute on `<html>`. The installed CSS uses attribute selectors to choose among `slide-out-left`/`slide-in-left`, `slide-out-right`/`slide-in-right`, `slide-out-top`/`slide-in-top`, and `slide-out-bottom`/`slide-in-bottom` keyframes. The `PageTransitionLink` component calls `document.startViewTransition` before `router.push`. The default `direction` is `"left"`, meaning the new page slides in from the right (the old page exits to the left). Reach for it when:

- **Apps with a clear hierarchical navigation.** "List to detail" flows benefit from a left-slide-in so the user perceives drilling deeper. Pressing back then slides right, mirroring the mental model of mobile navigation.
- **Tab-style navigation.** Sliding between peer sections of an app (Dashboard, Reports, Settings) with consistent direction cues reinforces spatial memory.
- **Onboarding steps.** A left-to-right slide forward and right-to-left slide backward is the universal wizard metaphor.
- **Mobile-first web apps.** Slide transitions match native iOS/Android navigation conventions, making a PWA feel native.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use slide transitions when:**

- Routes have a meaningful spatial or hierarchical relationship that maps to a direction.
- You are building a mobile-first or PWA experience where native-feeling navigation is important.

**Reach for [Page Transition Fade](/docs/animations/pages/page-transition-fade) instead when:**

- Routes are peers with no natural direction (top-level marketing pages, flat site maps). A fade is neutral; a slide implies direction that may not exist.
- The page contains horizontal scroll. A horizontal slide transition that animates the whole page can visually conflict with scrollable regions.

**Avoid both when:**

- **Safari is a primary target.** View Transitions API is not yet supported in Safari. Both components fall back to instant navigation silently.
- **The content has many absolutely-positioned or sticky elements.** These can behave unexpectedly during a view transition screenshot.

## Accessibility notes

Slide transitions move the entire page viewport and have stronger visual motion than a fade. This makes reduced-motion handling critical.

- **Focus management on navigation.** Same as the fade variant: verify that focus moves to the correct element after the transition completes, especially if you use dynamic direction changes.
- **Reduced motion is handled in CSS.** The installed `globals.css` includes:

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  ::view-transition-group(*),
  ::view-transition-old(*),
  ::view-transition-new(*) {
    animation: none !important;
  }
}
```

Full-page slides are among the most likely animations to cause discomfort for users with vestibular disorders. The CSS media query above ensures they see instant navigation. Verify this is in your `globals.css`.

- **Do not use slide transitions as the only navigation cue.** The direction of the slide communicates spatial relationship, but ensure the URL, breadcrumb, and page heading also convey where the user is.

## Performance considerations

- **View Transitions API is GPU-composited.** The browser screenshots old and new pages and animates them with CSS transforms, so there is no per-frame JavaScript cost.
- **`transform: translateX/Y` is the animation.** Slide keyframes use `translateX`/`translateY`, which are compositor-layer operations. No layout is triggered during the animation.
- **`duration` defaults to 0.4 s.** This is already at the high end for a repeated navigation gesture. Keep it at or below 0.4 s for routes users navigate frequently, such as tab switching.
- **The wrapper renders no DOM element.** `PageTransitionSlide` returns `<>{children}</>` and uses `useEffect` to write CSS properties. There is no layout overhead.
- **The `data-slide-direction` attribute is set on `document.documentElement`.** This means the browser must re-evaluate the CSS attribute selectors for the whole document on each navigation. The cost is negligible in practice.

## Customization examples

### Direction that mirrors browser back/forward

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState, useEffect } from "react"
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation"
import { PageTransitionSlide, SlideDirection } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-slide"

export function DirectionalSlide({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const [direction, setDirection] = useState<SlideDirection>("left")
  const [prev, setPrev] = useState(pathname)

  useEffect(() => {
    setDirection(pathname.length >= prev.length ? "left" : "right")
    setPrev(pathname)
  }, [pathname, prev])

  return (
    <PageTransitionSlide direction={direction} duration={0.35}>
      {children}
    </PageTransitionSlide>
  )
}
```

### Faster mobile-native feel

Tighter timing matches iOS/Android native app transitions:

```tsx
<PageTransitionSlide direction="left" duration={0.28} ease="cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)">
  {children}
</PageTransitionSlide>
```

## Real-world examples

### Settings section navigation

Slide left when entering a settings sub-page, slide right when going back:

```tsx title="app/settings/layout.tsx"
"use client"
import { useState, useEffect } from "react"
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation"
import { PageTransitionSlide, SlideDirection } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-slide"
import { PageTransitionLink } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-link"

const SETTINGS_NAV = [
  { href: "/settings/profile", label: "Profile" },
  { href: "/settings/security", label: "Security" },
  { href: "/settings/notifications", label: "Notifications" },
  { href: "/settings/billing", label: "Billing" },
]

export default function SettingsLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const [direction, setDirection] = useState<SlideDirection>("left")
  const [prevPath, setPrevPath] = useState(pathname)

  useEffect(() => {
    const prevIdx = SETTINGS_NAV.findIndex((n) => n.href === prevPath)
    const nextIdx = SETTINGS_NAV.findIndex((n) => n.href === pathname)
    setDirection(nextIdx >= prevIdx ? "left" : "right")
    setPrevPath(pathname)
  }, [pathname, prevPath])

  return (
    <PageTransitionSlide direction={direction} duration={0.3}>
      <div className="flex min-h-screen">
        <aside className="w-56 border-r border-neutral-200 p-4 dark:border-neutral-800">
          <nav className="flex flex-col gap-1">
            {SETTINGS_NAV.map((item) => (
              <PageTransitionLink
                key={item.href}
                href={item.href}
                className={`rounded-lg px-3 py-2 text-sm font-medium transition-colors ${
                  pathname === item.href
                    ? "bg-neutral-100 dark:bg-neutral-800"
                    : "text-neutral-600 hover:bg-neutral-50 dark:text-neutral-400 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800/50"
                }`}
              >
                {item.label}
              </PageTransitionLink>
            ))}
          </nav>
        </aside>
        <main className="flex-1 p-8">{children}</main>
      </div>
    </PageTransitionSlide>
  )
}
```

## Advanced Usage

### Dynamic Direction Based on Navigation

You can change the slide direction based on the navigation path:

```tsx
"use client"

import { useState, useEffect } from "react"
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation"
import { PageTransitionSlide, SlideDirection } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-slide"

export function DynamicSlideTransition({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const [direction, setDirection] = useState<SlideDirection>("left")

  useEffect(() => {
    // Example: slide right when going back
    if (pathname.includes('/back')) {
      setDirection('right')
    } else {
      setDirection('left')
    }
  }, [pathname])

  return (
    <PageTransitionSlide direction={direction}>
      {children}
    </PageTransitionSlide>
  )
}
```

### Per-Page Custom Directions

Use data attributes to customize transitions per page:

```tsx title="app/page-1/page.tsx"
export default function Page1() {
  return (
    <div data-slide-direction="left">
      <h1>Page 1</h1>
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx title="app/page-2/page.tsx"
export default function Page2() {
  return (
    <div data-slide-direction="top">
      <h1>Page 2</h1>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Parallax Effect

Create a parallax effect by having different slide speeds:

```css
::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: slide-out-left 0.4s ease-in-out;
}

::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: slide-in-left 0.6s ease-in-out;
}
```

### Slide with Fade

Combine slide and fade for a more dynamic effect:

```css
[data-slide-direction="left"]::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: 
    slide-out-left var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease),
    fade-out var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
}

[data-slide-direction="left"]::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: 
    slide-in-left var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease),
    fade-in var(--page-transition-duration) var(--page-transition-ease);
}

@keyframes fade-out {
  to { opacity: 0; }
}

@keyframes fade-in {
  from { opacity: 0; }
}
```

## Navigation History Integration

Track navigation direction based on browser history:

```tsx
"use client"

import { useState, useEffect } from "react"
import { usePathname } from "next/navigation"
import { PageTransitionSlide, SlideDirection } from "@/components/animations/pages/page-transition-slide"

export function HistoryAwareSlide({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const [direction, setDirection] = useState<SlideDirection>("left")
  const [prevPath, setPrevPath] = useState(pathname)

  useEffect(() => {
    // Simple heuristic: if path is shorter, likely going back
    if (pathname.length < prevPath.length) {
      setDirection('right')
    } else {
      setDirection('left')
    }
    setPrevPath(pathname)
  }, [pathname, prevPath])

  return (
    <PageTransitionSlide direction={direction}>
      {children}
    </PageTransitionSlide>
  )
}
```

```css
::view-transition-old(root),
::view-transition-new(root) {
  will-change: transform;
}
```

<Callout type="warn">
  **Note:** Page transitions using View Transitions API require the same-origin policy. Cross-origin navigations will not have transition effects.
</Callout>

## Troubleshooting

### Transition doesn't work

1. Check browser support (Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Opera 97+)
2. Verify CSS is properly imported in `globals.css`
3. Ensure `document.startViewTransition` is available
4. Check console for JavaScript errors

title: Animated Toast

## Overview

The `AnimatedToast` component creates a polished toast notification with smooth slide-in animation, animated icon path drawing, auto-dismiss progress bar, and stacked layout support. Use with `ToastProvider` and `ToastTrigger` for a complete toast system that stacks multiple notifications like Sonner.

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

```tsx title="components/animations/specials/animated-toast.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import * as motion from "motion/react-client";
import type { Easing } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

export interface AnimatedToastProps {
  message: string;
  type?: "success" | "error" | "info" | "warning";
  duration?: number;
  onClose?: () => void;
  className?: string;
}

export function AnimatedToast({
  message,
  type = "success",
  duration = 3000,
  onClose,
  className,
}: AnimatedToastProps) {
  const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = React.useState(true);
  const [progress, setProgress] = React.useState(100);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    const progressInterval = setInterval(() => {
      setProgress((prev) => {
        const newProgress = prev - (100 / (duration / 50));
        return newProgress <= 0 ? 0 : newProgress;
      });
    }, 50);

    const timer = setTimeout(() => {
      setIsVisible(false);
      setTimeout(() => onClose?.(), 300);
    }, duration);

    return () => {
      clearInterval(progressInterval);
      clearTimeout(timer);
    };
  }, [duration, onClose]);

  const colors = {
    success: { bg: "#10b981", icon: "#dcfce7" },
    error: { bg: "#ef4444", icon: "#fee2e2" },
    info: { bg: "#3b82f6", icon: "#dbeafe" },
    warning: { bg: "#f59e0b", icon: "#fef3c7" },
  };

  const iconPath = {
    success: "M 12 5 L 12 18 M 7 13 L 12 18 L 17 13",
    error: "M 8 8 L 16 16 M 16 8 L 8 16",
    info: "M 12 11 L 12 16 M 12 8 L 12 9",
    warning: "M 12 8 L 12 13 M 12 15 L 12 16",
  };

  return (
    <motion.div
      className={cn(
        "relative overflow-hidden rounded-lg shadow-lg backdrop-blur-sm",
        className
      )}
      initial={{ x: 400, opacity: 0, scale: 0.8 }}
      animate={
        isVisible
          ? { x: 0, opacity: 1, scale: 1 }
          : { x: 400, opacity: 0, scale: 0.8 }
      }
      transition={{
        type: "spring",
        stiffness: 300,
        damping: 30,
      }}
      style={{
        background: \`linear-gradient(135deg, \${colors[type].bg}dd, \${colors[type].bg}ee)\`,
      }}
    >
      <div className="flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3 pr-12">
        <motion.div
          initial={{ scale: 0, rotate: -180 }}
          animate={{ scale: 1, rotate: 0 }}
          transition={{
            delay: 0.2,
            type: "spring",
            stiffness: 400,
            damping: 15,
          }}
        >
          <svg width="24" height="24" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none">
            <motion.circle
              cx="12"
              cy="12"
              r="10"
              fill={colors[type].icon}
              initial={{ scale: 0 }}
              animate={{ scale: 1 }}
              transition={{ delay: 0.1, duration: 0.3 }}
            />
            <motion.path
              d={iconPath[type]}
              stroke={colors[type].bg}
              strokeWidth="2"
              strokeLinecap="round"
              strokeLinejoin="round"
              initial={{ pathLength: 0 }}
              animate={{ pathLength: 1 }}
              transition={{
                delay: 0.3,
                duration: 0.4,
                ease: "easeOut" as Easing,
              }}
            />
          </svg>
        </motion.div>

        <motion.p
          className="text-sm font-medium text-white"
          initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
          transition={{ delay: 0.2, duration: 0.3 }}
        >
          {message}
        </motion.p>

        <motion.button
          onClick={() => {
            setIsVisible(false);
            setTimeout(() => onClose?.(), 300);
          }}
          className="absolute right-2 top-2 rounded-full p-1 text-white/80 hover:bg-white/20 hover:text-white"
          whileHover={{ scale: 1.1 }}
          whileTap={{ scale: 0.9 }}
        >
          <svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 16 16" fill="none">
            <path
              d="M 4 4 L 12 12 M 12 4 L 4 12"
              stroke="currentColor"
              strokeWidth="2"
              strokeLinecap="round"
            />
          </svg>
        </motion.button>
      </div>

      <motion.div
        className="h-1 bg-white/30"
        initial={{ scaleX: 1 }}
        animate={{ scaleX: progress / 100 }}
        style={{ transformOrigin: "left" }}
        transition={{ duration: 0.05, ease: "linear" as Easing }}
      />
    </motion.div>
  );
}
```

**Step 3: Copy the trigger component (Optional)**

If you want to use the `ToastProvider` and `ToastTrigger` system:

```tsx title="components/animations/specials/toast-trigger.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import * as motion from "motion/react-client";
import type { Easing } from "motion/react";
import { AnimatedToast } from "./animated-toast";

interface Toast {
    id: number;
    message: string;
    description?: string;
    type?: "default" | "success" | "error" | "info" | "warning";
}

const ToastContext = React.createContext<{
    addToast: (toast: Omit<Toast, "id">) => void;
} | null>(null);

export function useToast() {
    const context = React.useContext(ToastContext);
    if (!context) {
        throw new Error("useToast must be used within ToastProvider");
    }
    return context;
}

export function ToastProvider({
    children,
    maxToasts = 5
}: {
    children: React.ReactNode;
    maxToasts?: number
}) {
    const [toasts, setToasts] = React.useState<Toast[]>([]);
    const nextId = React.useRef(0);

    const addToast = React.useCallback((toast: Omit<Toast, "id">) => {
        const id = nextId.current++;
        setToasts((prev) => {
            const newToasts = [...prev, { ...toast, id }];
            return newToasts.slice(-maxToasts);
        });
    }, [maxToasts]);

    const removeToast = React.useCallback((id: number) => {
        setToasts((prev) => prev.filter((t) => t.id !== id));
    }, []);

    return (
        <ToastContext.Provider value={{ addToast }}>
            {children}
            <div className="pointer-events-none fixed top-0 right-0 z-[100] flex flex-col items-end p-4">
                <div className="relative">
                    {toasts.map((toast, index) => {
                        // Bottom toast = index 0, top toast = last index
                        // We want top toast fully visible, others slightly behind
                        const fromTop = toasts.length - 1 - index;
                        const isTopToast = fromTop === 0;

                        return (
                            <motion.div
                                key={toast.id}
                                layout
                                className="absolute top-0 right-0"
                                initial={{ opacity: 0, y: -100, scale: 0.95 }}
                                animate={{
                                    y: fromTop * 4,
                                    scale: 1 - fromTop * 0.05,
                                    opacity: isTopToast ? 1 : 0.75,
                                }}
                                exit={{
                                    opacity: 0,
                                    y: -20,
                                    scale: 0.9,
                                    transition: { duration: 0.2 }
                                }}
                                transition={{
                                    duration: 0.2,
                                    ease: [0.16, 1, 0.3, 1] as Easing,
                                }}
                                style={{
                                    zIndex: 100 + index,
                                    pointerEvents: isTopToast ? "auto" : "none",
                                }}
                            >
                                <AnimatedToast
                                    message={toast.message}
                                    description={toast.description}
                                    type={toast.type}
                                    duration={4000}
                                    onClose={() => removeToast(toast.id)}
                                />
                            </motion.div>
                        );
                    })}
                </div>
            </div>
        </ToastContext.Provider>
    );
}

export interface ToastTriggerProps {
    buttonText?: string;
    toastMessage?: string;
    toastDescription?: string;
    toastType?: "default" | "success" | "error" | "info" | "warning";
    className?: string;
}

export function ToastTrigger({
    buttonText = "Show Toast",
    toastMessage = "Event has been created",
    toastDescription,
    toastType = "default",
    className,
}: ToastTriggerProps) {
    const context = React.useContext(ToastContext);
    const [showToast, setShowToast] = React.useState(false);
    const [toastKey, setToastKey] = React.useState(0);

    const handleClick = () => {
        if (context) {
            context.addToast({
                message: toastMessage,
                description: toastDescription,
                type: toastType,
            });
        } else {
            setShowToast(true);
            setToastKey((prev) => prev + 1);
        }
    };

    const handleToastClose = () => {
        setShowToast(false);
    };

    const buttonStyles = {
        default: "bg-white text-zinc-900 hover:bg-zinc-100 border border-zinc-300",
        success: "bg-emerald-500 text-white hover:bg-emerald-600",
        error: "bg-red-500 text-white hover:bg-red-600",
        info: "bg-blue-500 text-white hover:bg-blue-600",
        warning: "bg-amber-500 text-white hover:bg-amber-600",
    };

    return (
        <>
            <motion.button
                onClick={handleClick}
                className={`rounded-md px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium shadow-sm transition-colors ${buttonStyles[toastType]} ${className || ""}`}
                whileHover={{ scale: 1.02 }}
                whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }}
            >
                {buttonText}
            </motion.button>

            {!context && showToast && (
                <div className="pointer-events-none fixed top-4 right-4 z-50">
                    <AnimatedToast
                        key={toastKey}
                        message={toastMessage}
                        description={toastDescription}
                        type={toastType}
                        duration={4000}
                        onClose={handleToastClose}
                    />
                </div>
            )}
        </>
    );
}
```

## Usage

### With Toast Provider (Recommended)

First, wrap your app with the ToastProvider:

```tsx
import { ToastProvider } from "@/components/animations/specials/toast-trigger"

export default function App() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider maxToasts={3}>
      {/* Your app content */}
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

Then use ToastTrigger anywhere in your app:

```tsx
import { ToastTrigger } from "@/components/animations/specials/toast-trigger"

export default function Example() {
  return (
    <ToastTrigger 
      buttonText="Save Changes"
      toastMessage="Changes saved successfully!"
      toastDescription="Your preferences have been updated."
      toastType="success"
    />
  )
}
```

### Using the Hook

```tsx
import { useToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/toast-trigger"

export default function Example() {
  const { addToast } = useToast()
  
  const handleSave = () => {
    addToast({
      message: "Saved!",
      description: "Your changes have been saved.",
      type: "success"
    })
  }
  
  return <button onClick={handleSave}>Save</button>
}
```

### Direct Usage

```tsx
import { AnimatedToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/animated-toast"

export default function Example() {
  const [show, setShow] = useState(false)
  
  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setShow(true)}>Show Toast</button>
      {show && (
        <AnimatedToast 
          message="Item added to cart!"
          type="success"
          duration={3000}
          onClose={() => setShow(false)}
        />
      )}
    </>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `message` | `string` | - | Toast message text |
| `type` | `"success"` \| `"error"` \| `"info"` \| `"warning"` | `"success"` | Toast type/variant |
| `duration` | `number` | `3000` | Auto-dismiss duration in milliseconds |
| `onClose` | `() => void` | - | Callback when toast closes |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`AnimatedToast` is designed for brief, non-blocking feedback after an action the user just took. The spring slide-in from the right (`x: 400, scale: 0.8` to resting position), the SVG `pathLength` icon draw animation, and the `scaleX` progress bar give the notification a layered sense of arrival without demanding attention.

- **Save confirmations.** After a settings form saves, fire a `success` toast ("Changes saved successfully") so the user knows the request completed without a page reload.
- **API error feedback.** When a network request fails, display an `error` toast with a short message; keep the form intact so the user can retry.
- **Background task completion.** Long uploads, exports, or email-sends that finish off-screen are good candidates for an `info` or `success` toast.
- **Rate limit / quota warnings.** A `warning` toast lets the user know they are approaching a limit without blocking their current task.
- **Stacked queued messages.** With `ToastProvider` and `maxToasts`, up to 5 concurrent toasts stack in a Sonner-style layer at the top-right, each independently auto-dismissing.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `AnimatedToast` when:**

- The feedback is purely informational and the user does not need to act on it to continue.
- The message can be understood in 1 to 2 seconds; `duration` defaults to 3000 ms.
- You want visual reinforcement of the action type (`success` green, `error` red, `info` blue, `warning` amber) via the per-type color map and icon paths.

**Do not use `AnimatedToast` when:**

- The message requires confirmation before the user continues. Use a dialog or alert instead. Toasts auto-dismiss and the action may be missed.
- The notification contains critical error details the user must copy or reference. The 3000 ms default makes that impractical; consider an inline error state.
- You need to show persistent status (a banner for an ongoing outage, for example). Toasts are transient by design.
- The page already uses a third-party toast library such as Sonner or React Hot Toast. Two toast systems in one app create confusing stacking and z-index conflicts.

## Accessibility notes

- **Live region.** `AnimatedToast` renders a `motion.div` but does not automatically carry a `role="status"` or `aria-live` attribute. Wrap the toast container in a live region so screen readers announce new toasts:

```tsx
<div role="status" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
  {show && <AnimatedToast message="Changes saved" type="success" onClose={() => setShow(false)} />}
</div>
```

For `error` type toasts use `aria-live="assertive"` to interrupt the reader immediately.

- **Dismiss button.** The close button inside `AnimatedToast` renders as a `motion.button` with an SVG cross icon but no accessible label. Add an `aria-label` when integrating:

```tsx
// Inside your wrapper or by passing className and overriding
<button aria-label="Close notification" onClick={...}>...</button>
```

- **Keyboard reachability.** The toast renders inside a `pointer-events-none` fixed container; only the top-most toast has `pointer-events: auto`. Ensure the dismiss button is reachable with Tab when the toast is visible.
- **Do not put the only path to action inside a toast.** "Undo" or "View" links inside a toast that auto-dismisses in 3000 ms are practically unusable for keyboard and screen reader users. If the action matters, use a persistent notification or dialog.
- **Reduced motion.** The spring entrance (`stiffness: 300`, `damping: 30`) and icon draw animations should be suppressed for users who prefer reduced motion. Add a `useReducedMotion` guard:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { AnimatedToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/animated-toast"

function AccessibleToast(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof AnimatedToast>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  // Pass a very short duration so the spring completes almost instantly
  return <AnimatedToast {...props} duration={reduced ? 5000 : props.duration} />
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **Progress bar polling.** The component runs a `setInterval` every 50 ms to decrement the `progress` state. This causes a re-render every 50 ms for as long as the toast is mounted. With `ToastProvider` and `maxToasts={5}`, up to five intervals fire simultaneously. Unmount toasts promptly via `onClose` rather than hiding them with CSS.
- **Spring animation budget.** Each `AnimatedToast` mounts three simultaneous spring/animation sequences: the container slide, the icon scale-rotate, and the `pathLength` draw. These are transform and opacity only, so they stay off the main thread, but five stacked toasts multiplies the compositor load.
- **`AnimatePresence` cost.** `ToastProvider` wraps each toast in a `motion.div` inside `AnimatePresence` to handle mount/unmount transitions. Each `exit` animation (`opacity: 0, scale: 0.9`, 200 ms) runs on unmount. Keep `maxToasts` at 3 to 5 for typical UIs.
- **Fixed positioning and `z-index`.** The container uses `z-[100]`. If your app uses heavy `backdrop-filter` layers at similar z-levels, compositing cost increases. Test on lower-powered devices.

## Customization examples

### Warning toast with longer display time

```tsx
import { AnimatedToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/animated-toast"

function StorageLimitWarning({ onClose }: { onClose: () => void }) {
  return (
    <AnimatedToast
      message="Storage limit at 90%"
      type="warning"
      duration={6000}
      onClose={onClose}
      className="min-w-[300px]"
    />
  )
}
```

### Programmatic toast via `useToast` hook

```tsx
"use client"
import { useToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/toast-trigger"

export function SaveButton() {
  const { addToast } = useToast()

  async function handleSave() {
    try {
      await saveSettings()
      addToast({ message: "Settings saved", type: "success" })
    } catch {
      addToast({ message: "Save failed. Please retry.", type: "error" })
    }
  }

  return <button onClick={handleSave}>Save</button>
}
```

### Capped stack with provider

```tsx
import { ToastProvider, ToastTrigger } from "@/components/animations/specials/toast-trigger"

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <ToastProvider maxToasts={3}>
      {children}
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

## Real-world examples

### Form save confirmation

After a settings page saves, give the user a `success` toast and call `onClose` to unmount after auto-dismiss:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { AnimatedToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/animated-toast"

export function SettingsForm() {
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false)

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent) {
    e.preventDefault()
    await saveUserSettings()
    setSaved(true)
  }

  return (
    <>
      <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="space-y-4">
        <input name="displayName" className="rounded border px-3 py-2 text-sm w-full" placeholder="Display name" />
        <button type="submit" className="rounded bg-blue-600 px-4 py-2 text-sm text-white hover:bg-blue-700">
          Save changes
        </button>
      </form>

      {saved && (
        <div role="status" aria-live="polite" className="pointer-events-none fixed top-4 right-4 z-50">
          <AnimatedToast
            message="Profile updated"
            type="success"
            duration={3000}
            onClose={() => setSaved(false)}
          />
        </div>
      )}
    </>
  )
}
```

### Multi-action feedback with the hook

```tsx
"use client"
import { ToastProvider, useToast } from "@/components/animations/specials/toast-trigger"

function ActionPanel() {
  const { addToast } = useToast()

  return (
    <div className="flex gap-3">
      <button
        onClick={() => addToast({ message: "Copied to clipboard", type: "success" })}
        className="rounded border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm hover:bg-neutral-100"
      >
        Copy link
      </button>
      <button
        onClick={() => addToast({ message: "Export failed", type: "error" })}
        className="rounded border px-3 py-1.5 text-sm hover:bg-neutral-100"
      >
        Export
      </button>
    </div>
  )
}

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider maxToasts={3}>
      <ActionPanel />
    </ToastProvider>
  )
}
```

        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/border-beam.tsx"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import { motion } from "motion/react";

interface BorderBeamProps {
  className?: string;
  size?: number;
  duration?: number;
  borderWidth?: number;
  anchor?: number;
  colorFrom?: string;
  colorTo?: string;
  delay?: number;
  radius?: number;

export function BorderBeam({
  className,
  size = 200,
  duration = 15,
  anchor = 90,
  borderWidth = 1.5,
  colorFrom = "#ffaa40",
  colorTo = "#9c40ff",
  delay = 0,
  radius = 0,
}: BorderBeamProps) {
  return (
    <div
      style={
        {
          "--size": size,
          "--duration": duration,
          "--anchor": anchor,
          "--border-width": borderWidth,
          "--color-from": colorFrom,
          "--color-to": colorTo,
          "--delay": delay,
          "--radius": radius,

        // mask styles

        // pseudo styles

        className,
      )}
    />
  );
}
        ```

## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `size` | `number` | `200` | The length of the beam. |
| `duration` | `number` | `15` | The duration of the animation in seconds. |
| `borderWidth` | `number` | `1.5` | The width of the border. |
| `colorFrom` | `string` | `"#ffaa40"` | The starting color of the gradient. |
| `colorTo` | `string` | `"#9c40ff"` | The ending color of the gradient. |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | The delay before the animation starts. |
| `radius` | `number` | `0` | The border radius of the path. Set this to match the container's border radius. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |

## Use cases

`BorderBeam` uses CSS `offset-path: rect(...)` with `offset-anchor` and a conic/linear gradient pseudo-element to travel a beam of light around any container's border. Because it is purely declarative CSS animation driven by the `animate-border-beam` keyframe, it consumes no JavaScript at runtime after mount. Good fits include:

- **Feature or pricing cards.** A slow beam (`duration={12}` to `duration={20}`) on a card that already has a border draws the eye during the initial page scan without becoming distracting.
- **Active or selected input fields.** A fast beam (`duration={4}` to `duration={6}`, `size={80}`) signals focus on a search or email input without replacing the browser's native `:focus` ring.
- **CTAs and pill buttons.** A tight radius (`radius={9999}`) traces the full circumference of a rounded button, adding a premium gradient shimmer.
- **Avatar rings.** The same `radius={9999}` approach works for `rounded-full` avatar containers to indicate an "active" or "live" user.
- **Asymmetric decorative frames.** Match `radius` to your container's least aggressive corner (e.g., `radius={24}` for a `rounded-tl-3xl rounded-br-3xl` card) so the beam rounds corners correctly.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `BorderBeam` when:**

- You need a passive ambient animation that requires no user interaction.
- The host element already has a visible border; the mask technique relies on `border: calc(var(--border-width)*1px) solid transparent` over the existing border.
- You want to differentiate one element from siblings without changing its layout (the component is `position: absolute; inset: 0`, so it never pushes content).

**Do not use `BorderBeam` when:**

- You need to highlight states that change frequently (active tab, selected list item). A continuously running CSS animation on every row in a list wastes compositor resources.
- The container has `overflow: hidden` without explicit knowledge of it: the pseudo-element travels outside the border box briefly during the `offset-path` traversal, and `overflow: hidden` can clip it. Confirm visually.
- The user is on a battery-constrained device and the animation serves no functional purpose. Consider respecting `prefers-reduced-motion` by removing the component entirely when motion is reduced.
- The container has no border (`border-transparent` parent): the mask composite trick requires at least a 1 px border on the host element's CSS.

## Accessibility notes

- `BorderBeam` is purely decorative. The component renders a `div` with `pointer-events-none` and no text or interactive content, so it is invisible to screen readers by default. No `aria-hidden` is needed because there is no role to suppress.
- The continuous animation can cause discomfort for users with vestibular or photosensitive conditions. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { BorderBeam } from "@/components/animations/specials/border-beam"

function AccessibleBorderBeam(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof BorderBeam>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return null
  return <BorderBeam {...props} />
}
```

- Do not rely on the beam alone to communicate state changes (e.g., "this card is selected"). Users who disable animations or use high-contrast mode will not perceive it. Pair it with a visible border color or text change.

## Performance considerations

- **Pure CSS animation.** The `animate-border-beam` keyframe only animates `offset-distance` from `0%` to `100%`. This is a paint-free, layout-free operation handled entirely by the compositor. One instance has negligible overhead.
- **Multiple instances.** Placing `BorderBeam` on every card in a 20-card grid means 20 concurrent CSS animations. Each is compositor-friendly, but the cumulative texture-upload cost of the gradient pseudo-elements adds up on lower-end GPUs. Use sparingly in dense lists.
- **`will-change` is unnecessary.** `offset-distance` animations are already composited, so adding `will-change: offset-distance` merely consumes memory.
- **No motion/react runtime.** Unlike most components in this library, `BorderBeam` imports `motion` only for the TypeScript reference. The actual animation uses a Tailwind keyframe, so there is zero JavaScript animation loop at runtime.
- **Avoid on `backdrop-filter` parents.** If the host card uses `backdrop-blur-sm`, the browser must paint a separate compositing layer for the blur and another for the animated pseudo-element. On mobile Safari this can cause frame drops.

    <Steps>
      <Step>
        **Install dependencies**
        ```bash
        npm install motion clsx tailwind-merge
        ```
      </Step>
      <Step>
        **Add utility**
        ```ts title="lib/utils.ts"
import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
}
        ```
      </Step>
      <Step>
        **Copy the component code**
        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/image-text.tsx"
"use client";

import React, { useState, useEffect } from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

interface ImageTextProps extends HTMLMotionProps<"h1"> {
    text: string;
    imageUrl: string | string[] | { src: string } | { src: string }[];
    className?: string;
    direction?: "horizontal" | "vertical" | "diagonal" | "none";
    interval?: number;
}

export function ImageText({
    text,
    imageUrl,
    className,
    direction = "horizontal",
    interval = 3000,
    ...props
}: ImageTextProps) {
    const images = Array.isArray(imageUrl) ? imageUrl : [imageUrl];
    const [currentImageIndex, setCurrentImageIndex] = useState(0);

    useEffect(() => {
        if (!Array.isArray(imageUrl) || imageUrl.length <= 1) return;

        const timer = setInterval(() => {
            setCurrentImageIndex((prev) => (prev + 1) % images.length);
        }, interval);

        return () => clearInterval(timer);
    }, [imageUrl, interval, images.length]);

    const getCurrentImageUrl = () => {
        const img = images[currentImageIndex];
        return typeof img === "string" ? img : img.src;
    };

    const getAnimation = () => {
        switch (direction) {
            case "horizontal":
                return {
                    backgroundPosition: ["0% 50%", "100% 50%", "0% 50%"],
                };
            case "vertical":
                return {
                    backgroundPosition: ["50% 0%", "50% 100%", "50% 0%"],
                };
            case "diagonal":
                return {
                    backgroundPosition: ["0% 0%", "100% 100%", "0% 0%"],
                };
            case "none":
                return {
                    backgroundPosition: "center",
                }
            default:
                return {
                    backgroundPosition: ["0% 50%", "100% 50%", "0% 50%"],
                };
        }
    };

    return (
    <span className={cn("inline-block relative", className)}>
         {/* Invisible layout placeholder ensuring size doesn't collapse */}
        <h1 className={cn("text-9xl font-serif italic font-bold tracking-tighter inline-block invisible", className)}>
            {text}
        </h1>

        <AnimatePresence>
            <motion.h1
                key={currentImageIndex} // Re-render for image change
                className={cn(
                    "text-9xl font-serif italic font-bold tracking-tighter inline-block absolute inset-0",
                    className
                )}
                style={{
                    backgroundImage: `url(${getCurrentImageUrl()})`,
                    backgroundSize: direction === "none" ? "cover" : "150% auto",
                    backgroundClip: "text",
                    WebkitBackgroundClip: "text",
                    WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent",
                    color: "transparent",
                }}
                initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
                animate={{
                     ...getAnimation(),
                     opacity: 1
                }}
                exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
                transition={{
                    // Smooth opacity fade for texture change
                    opacity: { duration: 1 },
                    // Continuous background movement
                    backgroundPosition: {
                        duration: 15,
                        ease: "linear",
                        repeat: Infinity,
                    }
                }}
                {...props}
            >
                {text}
            </motion.h1>
        </AnimatePresence>
    </span>
);
}
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>
