## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `text` | `string` | - | The text content to display. |
| `imageUrl` | `string \| string[] \| StaticImageData` | - | The URL(s) or imported image object(s) of the background. |
| `direction` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical" \| "diagonal" \| "none"` | `"horizontal"` | The direction of the background animation. |
| `interval` | `number` | `3000` | The duration (ms) to show each image when `imageUrl` is an array. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional classes for custom text styling (size, weight). |

## Use cases

`ImageText` uses `background-clip: text` with `WebkitBackgroundClip: text` and `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent` to reveal an animated image through the letterforms of the text. The background position animates continuously via a `motion/react` `backgroundPosition` keyframe with `repeat: Infinity` and `ease: "linear"` over 15 seconds. When `imageUrl` is an array, `AnimatePresence` fades between images on an `interval` timer.

- **Hero section wordmarks.** A single large word like a brand name or headline word filled with a landscape photo creates an immediate visual anchor for landing pages.
- **Category or section headers.** Fill section titles with thematic imagery (a forest photo for "Nature", a cityscape for "Urban") to tie typography to content.
- **Rotating seasonal imagery.** Pass an array of images with `direction="none"` and `interval={3000}` to cycle through seasonal or campaign photos as the text background.
- **Pull-quotes or statistics.** A bold number like "10x" or "500K" filled with a gradient photo makes a metric stand out on a marketing page.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ImageText` when:**

- The text is large (approximately `text-6xl` and above). Below that, `background-clip: text` produces an illegible smear rather than a readable image fill.
- You have one or two visually distinct words to highlight. The component renders a hidden `h1` placeholder for layout, then an absolutely-positioned animated `motion.h1` on top. Wrapping many lines of body text this way produces layout complications.
- The imagery is high-contrast relative to the page background so the text remains readable where the image is bright.

**Do not use `ImageText` when:**

- The text is body copy or small UI labels. Use a standard color or gradient text class instead.
- You need the text indexed by search engines as actual copy. `background-clip: text` renders real DOM text, so SEO is preserved, but the invisible layout placeholder `h1` is a duplicate element. Prefer wrapping with a semantic container and confirming your crawler sees the real content.
- The page background is similar in brightness to the image fill. The text will disappear. Ensure a contrasting matte background or use a `text-shadow` fallback.
- You are cycling images rapidly (`interval` below 1000 ms). The `AnimatePresence` fade uses a 1-second `opacity` transition. Images cycling faster than the fade duration will overlap visually.

## Accessibility notes

- **Semantic heading.** The component renders an `h1` element by default. If the text is not a page title, override with a `span` or `h2` by customizing the component to match the correct heading level in context. Do not place multiple `h1` elements on a page.
- **Color contrast.** `background-clip: text` with a photographic image does not have a predictable contrast ratio. Parts of the image that are close in luminance to the page background will make the text unreadable. Always verify contrast with your specific image, especially for users with low vision.
- **Fallback for unsupported environments.** Browsers that do not support `WebkitBackgroundClip: text` will render transparent text (invisible). Add a CSS fallback:

```css
/* In your global CSS */
@supports not (-webkit-background-clip: text) {
  .image-text-fallback {
    color: inherit;
    background: none;
  }
}
```

- **Reduced motion.** The `backgroundPosition` keyframe runs infinitely. Respect user preference:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { ImageText } from "@/components/animations/specials/image-text"

function AccessibleImageText(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof ImageText>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return <ImageText {...props} direction={reduced ? "none" : props.direction} />
}
```

- **Alt text.** Because the image is a CSS background, screen readers do not announce it. The visible `text` prop is the accessible label; no additional `alt` is required.

## Performance considerations

- **Two `h1` elements per instance.** The component renders a visually hidden (`invisible`) `h1` for layout and a positioned animated `motion.h1` on top. This is intentional to prevent layout collapse, but it means two heading elements in the DOM. In a page with many instances, this multiplies DOM nodes.
- **`backgroundPosition` with `repeat: Infinity`.** For `direction="horizontal"` (the default), the background animates from `0% 50%` to `100% 50%` and back over 15 seconds. This is a compositable CSS property on modern browsers but may fall back to main-thread painting on older engines.
- **`backgroundSize: "150% auto"`.** The image is scaled to 150% of the container width for all directions except `"none"`. Ensure the source image is large enough that the browser does not upscale a small image to fill the oversized background, which would look blurry.
- **`AnimatePresence` on image arrays.** Each image change mounts a new `motion.h1` and unmounts the previous one with a 1-second opacity fade. On slow connections the incoming image may not be loaded when the `interval` fires, causing a flash of the previous image. Preload images with `new Image().src = url` before passing them to the component.
- **Avoid many instances on a single page.** Each instance runs a continuous `requestAnimationFrame`-backed animation. Two or three instances are fine; ten on a scroll-driven page will consume compositor resources.

# linear-carousel.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/specials/linear-carousel.mdx

title: Linear Carousel
description: A stunning, smooth-scrolling 3D carousel inspired by Linear. Features card expansion with layout animations and keyboard navigation.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { Carousel, Card } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/specials/linear-carousel';
import LinearCarouselVisual from '@/registry/new-york/animations/specials/linear-carousel-visual';
import LinearCarouselText from '@/registry/new-york/animations/specials/linear-carousel-text';

## Overview

The `LinearCarousel` component replicates the premium carousel experience from Linear. It includes an infinite scroll effect, smooth expanding cards using Framer Motion's `layoutId`, full keyboard/touch support, and intuitive drag-to-scroll functionality for desktop.

    **Step 1: Install dependencies**

    ```bash
    npm install motion lucide-react clsx tailwind-merge
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    Create `components/animations/specials/linear-carousel.tsx` and copy the following code:

    ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/linear-carousel.tsx"
    "use client";

    import React, {
      useEffect,
      useRef,
      useState,
      createContext,
      useContext,
    } from "react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
    import { motion } from "motion/react";
    import type { ImgHTMLAttributes } from "react";
    import { ChevronLeft, ChevronRight } from "lucide-react";

    interface CarouselProps {
      items: React.JSX.Element[];
      initialScroll?: number;
    }

    type Card = {
      src: string;
      title: string;
      category?: string;
      content: React.ReactNode;
    };

    export const CarouselContext = createContext<{
      onCardClose: (index: number) => void;
      currentIndex: number;
    }>({
      onCardClose: () => { },
      currentIndex: 0,
    });

    export const Carousel = ({
      items,
      initialScroll = 0,
      autoplay = false,
      autoplaySpeed = 0.5,
    }: CarouselProps & { autoplay?: boolean; autoplaySpeed?: number }) => {
      const carouselRef = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
      const [canScrollLeft, setCanScrollLeft] = React.useState(false);
      const [canScrollRight, setCanScrollRight] = React.useState(true);
      const [currentIndex, setCurrentIndex] = useState(0);
      const [isHovered, setIsHovered] = useState(false);
      const animationRef = useRef<number>(null);
      // Duplicate items to create infinite effect
      const loopedItems = [...items, ...items];

      useEffect(() => {
        if (carouselRef.current) {
          carouselRef.current.scrollLeft = initialScroll;
          checkScrollability();
        }
      }, [initialScroll]);

      useEffect(() => {
        if (!autoplay || isHovered) {
          if (animationRef.current) cancelAnimationFrame(animationRef.current!);
          return;
        }
        const scroll = () => {
          if (carouselRef.current) {
            carouselRef.current.scrollLeft += autoplaySpeed;
            const scrollWidth = carouselRef.current.scrollWidth;
            if (carouselRef.current.scrollLeft >= scrollWidth / 2) {
              carouselRef.current.scrollLeft = 0;
            }
            checkScrollability();
            animationRef.current = requestAnimationFrame(scroll);
          }
        };
        animationRef.current = requestAnimationFrame(scroll);
        return () => {
          if (animationRef.current) cancelAnimationFrame(animationRef.current);
        };
      }, [autoplay, autoplaySpeed, isHovered]);

      const checkScrollability = () => {
        if (carouselRef.current) {
          const { scrollLeft, scrollWidth, clientWidth } = carouselRef.current;
          setCanScrollLeft(scrollLeft > 0);
          setCanScrollRight(scrollLeft < scrollWidth - clientWidth);
        }
      };

      const scrollLeft = () => {
        if (carouselRef.current) {
          carouselRef.current.scrollTo({ left: 0, behavior: "smooth" });
        }
      };

      const scrollRight = () => {
        if (carouselRef.current) {
          const container = carouselRef.current;
          container.scrollTo({ left: container.scrollWidth, behavior: "smooth" });
        }
      };

      const handleCardClose = (index: number) => {
        if (carouselRef.current) {
          const cardWidth = isMobile() ? 230 : 320; 
          const gap = isMobile() ? 4 : 8;
          const scrollPosition = (cardWidth + gap) * (index + 1);
          carouselRef.current.scrollTo({
            left: scrollPosition,
            behavior: "smooth",
          });
          setCurrentIndex(index);
        }
      };

      const isMobile = () => {
        return window && window.innerWidth < 768;
      };

      return (
        <CarouselContext.Provider
          value={{ onCardClose: handleCardClose, currentIndex }}
        >
          <div
            className="relative w-full mx-auto px-4 md:px-8"
            onTouchStart={() => setIsHovered(true)}
            onTouchEnd={() => setIsHovered(false)}
          >
            <div
              className="flex w-full overflow-x-scroll overscroll-x-auto scroll-smooth py-10 [scrollbar-width:none] md:py-20"
              ref={carouselRef}
              onScroll={checkScrollability}
            >
              <div
                className={cn(
                  "absolute right-0 z-1000 h-auto w-[5%] overflow-hidden bg-gradient-to-l from-white dark:from-background to-transparent pointer-events-none"
                )}
              ></div>
              <div
                className={cn("flex flex-row justify-start gap-4")}
              >
                {loopedItems.map((item, index) => (
                  <motion.div
                    initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
                    animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
                    transition={{
                      duration: 0.5,
                      delay: 0.2 * (index % items.length),
                      ease: "easeOut",
                    }}
                    key={"card" + index}
                    className="rounded-3xl"
                    onMouseEnter={() => setIsHovered(true)}
                    onMouseLeave={() => setIsHovered(false)}
                  >
                    {item}
                  </motion.div>
                ))}
              </div>
            </div>
            <div className="flex justify-center gap-3 mt-4">
              <button
                className="relative z-40 flex h-10 w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-card border border-border hover:bg-muted disabled:opacity-50 transition-colors"
                onClick={scrollLeft}
                disabled={!canScrollLeft}
                onMouseEnter={() => setIsHovered(true)}
                onMouseLeave={() => setIsHovered(false)}
              >
                <ChevronLeft className="h-6 w-6 text-muted-foreground" />
              </button>
              <button
                className="relative z-40 flex h-10 w-10 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-card border border-border hover:bg-muted disabled:opacity-50 transition-colors"
                onClick={scrollRight}
                disabled={!canScrollRight}
                onMouseEnter={() => setIsHovered(true)}
                onMouseLeave={() => setIsHovered(false)}
              >
                <ChevronRight className="h-6 w-6 text-muted-foreground" />
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </CarouselContext.Provider>
      );
    };

    export const Card = ({
      card,
      index,
      layout = false,
    }: {
      card: Card;
      index: number;
      layout?: boolean;
    }) => {
      return (
        <motion.button
          layoutId={layout ? `card-${card.title}` : undefined}
          className="relative z-10 flex h-60 w-56 flex-col items-start justify-end overflow-hidden rounded-3xl bg-gray-100 md:h-96 md:w-80 dark:bg-neutral-900"
        >
          <div className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-x-0 bottom-0 z-30 h-2/3 bg-gradient-to-t from-black/80 via-black/40 to-transparent" />
          <div className="relative z-40 p-8 w-full">
            {card.category && (
              <motion.p
                layoutId={layout ? `category-${card.category}` : undefined}
                className="text-left font-mono text-sm font-medium text-white md:text-base"
              >
                {card.category}
              </motion.p>
            )}
            <motion.p
              layoutId={layout ? `title-${card.title}` : undefined}
              className="mt-2 max-w-xs text-left font-mono text-xl font-semibold [text-wrap:balance] text-white md:text-3xl"
            >
              {card.title}
            </motion.p>
          </div>
          <img
            src={card.src}
            alt={card.title}
            className="absolute inset-0 z-10 w-full h-full object-cover grayscale"
          />
        </motion.button>
      );
    };
    ```

## Props

### Carousel Props

| `items` | `React.JSX.Element[]` | - | Array of Card components to display |
| `initialScroll` | `number` | `0` | Initial scroll position of the carousel |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether to auto-scroll the carousel |
| `autoplaySpeed` | `number` | `0.5` | Speed of the auto-scroll |

### Card Props

| `card` | `Card` | - | Object containing src, title, category, and content |
| `index` | `number` | - | Index of the card in the list |
| `layout` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable layout animations (Shared Element Transition) |

## Use cases

The `Carousel` component renders a horizontally scrollable strip (`overflow-x-scroll`, `[scrollbar-width:none]`) with each card staggered in on mount (`opacity: 0, y: 20` to resting state, `delay: 0.2 * index`). Items are duplicated to create an infinite loop effect. The optional `autoplay` prop drives scroll via `requestAnimationFrame` and pauses on hover or touch. `Card` uses `motion/react` `layoutId` for shared element transitions between the card thumbnail and an expanded view when `layout={true}`.

- **Product feature showcases.** Cards with a screenshot `src`, short `title`, and `category` badge make a polished horizontal browsing surface for feature marketing.
- **Testimonial strips.** Pass testimonial quotes as `content` with customer name as `title` and company as `category` for a scrollable social proof section.
- **Media galleries.** Photography portfolios or lookbook pages where the staggered card entrance and grayscale image treatment (`grayscale` class on `img`) create a cohesive aesthetic.
- **Blog or article previews.** Each card's `content` can include a teaser paragraph alongside the image cover, suitable for editorial or documentation landing pages.
- **Onboarding step decks.** Use the carousel for step-by-step feature highlights with the `layout` shared transition to expand a step into full detail.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `LinearCarousel` when:**

- You have 3 to 10 items that do not fit inline but are best browsed one after another.
- Visual imagery is a primary part of each item's identity; the `Card` renders an absolutely-positioned `img` with `object-cover` that fills the 256 x 240 px (mobile) or 320 x 384 px (desktop) card.
- You want keyboard and mouse accessibility with the built-in prev/next `ChevronLeft`/`ChevronRight` buttons.

**Do not use `LinearCarousel` when:**

- You need a full-screen immersive lightbox. The card opens inline via `layoutId`; it does not render a modal overlay. Use a dedicated lightbox component for that.
- The items are primarily text (data tables, settings options). The card format is optimized for visual media.
- You need a paginated view where the user knows exactly how many items there are. The infinite loop duplication hides the true count. Use a paginated grid or a [Swipeable Stack](/docs/animations/specials/swipeable-stack) with visible progress indicators instead.
- Auto-advancing without pause control is required for accessibility compliance. The `autoplay` prop does pause on hover, but there is no user-visible pause button. Adding one before shipping is essential.

## Accessibility notes

- **Carousel role.** Wrap the `Carousel` in a `section` or `div` with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` and a descriptive `aria-label` to communicate its purpose to screen readers:

```tsx
<section aria-roledescription="carousel" aria-label="Feature highlights">
  <Carousel items={cards} />
</section>
```

- **Prev/next buttons.** The `ChevronLeft` and `ChevronRight` icon buttons lack accessible labels in the source. Add `aria-label` props:

```tsx
// When copying the component manually, update the button markup:
<button aria-label="Scroll left" onClick={scrollLeft} disabled={!canScrollLeft} ...>
  <ChevronLeft ... />
</button>
<button aria-label="Scroll right" onClick={scrollRight} disabled={!canScrollRight} ...>
  <ChevronRight ... />
</button>
```

- **Card buttons.** `Card` renders as a `motion.button`. Ensure the `card.title` value is meaningful as a button label. If title alone is insufficient, add an `aria-label` to the `Card` props.
- **Images.** The `img` inside `Card` uses `alt={card.title}`, which is a reasonable default. For images that are purely decorative, pass `alt=""`. For images that convey information beyond the title, provide a more descriptive alt string.
- **Autoplay.** If `autoplay={true}` is used, the carousel scrolls without user input. Provide a visible pause control. Users who need more time to read or interact should be able to stop motion. See WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide).
- **Keyboard navigation.** The built-in prev/next buttons are reachable via Tab and activate on Enter/Space. The scroll container itself (`overflow-x-scroll`) is not keyboard-scrollable by default. Add `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown` handlers for Arrow Left/Right to the scroll container for full keyboard support.
- **Reduced motion.** The staggered `opacity/y` entrance animation and `autoplay` scroll should be suppressed:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"

function CarouselWrapper({ items }: { items: React.JSX.Element[] }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return <Carousel items={items} autoplay={reduced ? false : true} />
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **Item duplication.** `Carousel` internally doubles the `items` array (`loopedItems = [...items, ...items]`) for the infinite loop. With `layout={true}`, each `Card` assigns a `layoutId`. Duplicate `layoutId` values across the two copies will conflict with `motion/react` layout animations. Either use `layout={false}` when enabling autoplay, or deduplicate keys carefully.
- **`requestAnimationFrame` autoplay.** When `autoplay={true}` and the carousel is not hovered, `scrollLeft` is incremented every animation frame. This runs on the main thread. Keep `autoplaySpeed` at the default `0.5` to avoid forcing the browser to repaint at high scroll speeds.
- **Scroll event listener.** The `onScroll` handler on the scroll container calls `checkScrollability` on every scroll event. This is synchronous React state (`setCanScrollLeft`/`setCanScrollRight`), which causes a re-render. Throttling this with `requestAnimationFrame` reduces jank when the user drags fast.
- **Staggered entrance animations.** With `delay: 0.2 * (index % items.length)`, 8 cards take up to 1.6 seconds before the last card fades in. On low-end devices this can feel sluggish. Cap the maximum delay or reduce it for production.
- **`motion.div` wrapper per card.** Each card in `loopedItems` is wrapped in a `motion.div` with entrance animation. For 10 unique items the loop creates 20 `motion.div` elements. This is acceptable but avoid exceeding 20 unique items.

## Customization examples

### Autoplay with pause on interaction

```tsx
import { Carousel, Card } from "@/components/animations/specials/linear-carousel"

const items = [
  { src: "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1506744038136-46273834b3fb?q=80&w=3000&auto=format&fit=crop", title: "Mountain Views", category: "Nature", content: <p className="text-neutral-500">Alpine landscapes from the Swiss Alps.</p> },
  { src: "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1501785888041-af3ef285b470?q=80&w=3000&auto=format&fit=crop", title: "Ocean Calm", category: "Nature", content: <p className="text-neutral-500">Pacific coastline at golden hour.</p> },
]

export function AutoplayCarousel() {
  const cards = items.map((card, index) => (
    <Card key={card.src} card={card} index={index} layout={false} />
  ))
  return (
    <div className="w-full py-12">
      <Carousel items={cards} autoplay={true} autoplaySpeed={0.4} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

```tsx
    </section>

}
```

      <Step>
        **Copy the component code**
        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/magnetic-drawer.tsx"
"use client";

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import {
  motion,
  useMotionValue,
  useTransform,
  PanInfo,
  animate,
  AnimatePresence,
} from "motion/react";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { X } from "lucide-react";
import { createPortal } from "react-dom";

interface MagneticDrawerProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  open: boolean;
  onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => void;
  snapPoints?: number[]; // Values between 0 and 1, e.g., [0.5, 1]
  className?: string;
}

export function MagneticDrawer({
  children,
  open,
  onOpenChange,
  snapPoints = [0.5, 0.9],
  className,
}: MagneticDrawerProps) {
  const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false);
  const [drawerHeight, setDrawerHeight] = useState(0);
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const y = useMotionValue(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    setMounted(true);
    if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
      setDrawerHeight(window.innerHeight);
      const handleResize = () => setDrawerHeight(window.innerHeight);
      window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize);
      return () => window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize);
    }
  }, []);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (open) {
      const initialSnap = snapPoints[0];
      const targetY = drawerHeight * (1 - initialSnap);
      animate(y, targetY, { type: "spring", damping: 30, stiffness: 300 });
      document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";
    } else {
      animate(y, drawerHeight, { type: "spring", damping: 30, stiffness: 300 });
      document.body.style.overflow = "";
    }
    return () => { document.body.style.overflow = ""; };
  }, [open, drawerHeight, snapPoints]);

  const handleDragEnd = (_: any, info: PanInfo) => {
    const velocity = info.velocity.y;
    const currentY = y.get();
    const currentOpenedHeight = drawerHeight - currentY;
    const currentRatio = currentOpenedHeight / drawerHeight;

    let bestSnap = snapPoints[0];
    let minDiff = Infinity;
    
    if (velocity > 500 || currentRatio < 0.1) {
        onOpenChange(false);
        return;
    }

    for (const point of snapPoints) {
        const diff = Math.abs(currentRatio - point);
        if (diff < minDiff) {
            minDiff = diff;
            bestSnap = point;
        }
    }
    
    if (velocity < -500) {
        const nextSnap = snapPoints.find(p => p > currentRatio);
        if (nextSnap) bestSnap = nextSnap;
    } else if (velocity > 500) {
         const prevSnap = [...snapPoints].reverse().find(p => p < currentRatio);
         if (prevSnap) bestSnap = prevSnap;
    }

    const targetY = drawerHeight * (1 - bestSnap);
    animate(y, targetY, { type: "spring", damping: 30, stiffness: 300 });
  };

  const backdropOpacity = useTransform(y, [drawerHeight, 0], [0, 0.5]);
  const pointerEvents = useTransform(y, (latest) => latest >= drawerHeight ? "none" : "auto");

  if (!mounted) return null;

  return createPortal(
    <AnimatePresence>
      {open && (
        <>
            <motion.div
                className="fixed inset-0 z-[99]"
                style={{ backgroundColor: "black", opacity: backdropOpacity, pointerEvents }}
                onClick={() => onOpenChange(false)}
                initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
                animate={{ opacity: 0.5 }}
                exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
                transition={{ duration: 0.3 }}
            />
            <motion.div
                ref={containerRef}
                className={cn(
                    "fixed bottom-0 left-0 right-0 z-[100] flex flex-col rounded-t-[20px] bg-white shadow-2xl outline-none dark:bg-neutral-900",
                    className
                )}
                style={{ y, height: drawerHeight, touchAction: "none" }}
                initial={{ y: drawerHeight }}
                drag="y"
                dragConstraints={{ top: 0, bottom: drawerHeight }}
                dragElastic={0.05}
                dragMomentum={false}
                onDragEnd={handleDragEnd}
            >
                <div className="flex w-full items-center justify-center p-4">
                    <div className="h-1.5 w-12 rounded-full bg-neutral-300 dark:bg-neutral-700" />
                </div>
                <button 
                  onClick={() => onOpenChange(false)}
                  className="absolute right-4 top-4 rounded-full p-2 text-neutral-500 hover:bg-neutral-100 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800"
                >
                    <X className="h-5 w-5" />
                </button>
                <div className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-4 pb-10">
                    {children}
                </div>
            </motion.div>
        </>
      )}
    </AnimatePresence>,
    document.body
  );
}
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>

## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `open` | `boolean` | - | Controls visibility. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open) => void` | - | State updater. |
| `snapPoints` | `number[]` | `[0.5, 0.9]` | Array of open heights (0 to 1). |

## Use cases

`MagneticDrawer` renders via `createPortal` into `document.body`, sits at `z-index: 100`, and uses a `useMotionValue` `y` driven by `drag="y"` for real-time resistance. On drag end it snaps to the closest value in `snapPoints` (each a fraction of viewport height, 0 to 1) using a `spring(damping: 30, stiffness: 300)` animation. A velocity threshold of 500 px/s triggers dismiss or a snap-up override.

- **Mobile navigation drawers.** A bottom sheet with `snapPoints={[0.4, 0.85]}` gives users a peek state (40% open) and an expanded state (85% open) for a two-stage navigation panel.
- **Detail panels in list-detail layouts.** Tap a list item to reveal more detail at the `0.5` snap without fully covering the list, then drag up to `0.9` for the full record.
- **Filter and sort sheets.** E-commerce or search UIs can expose filter controls in the drawer at a half-height snap, letting users see the list update behind a translucent backdrop.
- **Media player controls.** A mini-player at `0.15` that expands to `0.8` on drag up matches common mobile music app patterns.
- **Contextual action sheets.** Present share, copy, or delete actions in a bottom drawer triggered by a long-press or button click.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `MagneticDrawer` when:**

- Your primary audience is on a touch-enabled device. The drag mechanic with `dragElastic={0.05}` and velocity-based snap feel natural on mobile.
- You need two or more partial open states (multiple snap points). A dialog covers the full screen; the drawer is for layered reveal.
- The content inside the drawer is scrollable. The inner container uses `overflow-y-auto` so long content scrolls without conflicting with the drag gesture.

**Do not use `MagneticDrawer` when:**

- The interaction is primarily mouse-driven on desktop. The drag handle and snap mechanic feel unnatural with a mouse compared to native `<dialog>` or a slide-out sidebar. Consider a side panel or popover for desktop-first UIs.
- The content requires modal-level focus isolation (e.g., a payment form). The current implementation uses `AnimatePresence` but does not enforce a full focus trap. Use a proper dialog component with `aria-modal="true"` and a focus trap library for critical flows.
- You need a static, non-draggable overlay panel. The component is built around drag physics; if the user should not be able to resize it, a regular modal is simpler and more accessible.
- The UI has very few vertical pixels (small embedded iframes, kiosk displays). The drawer uses `window.innerHeight` for its geometry; in constrained viewports this can result in unusable layouts.

## Accessibility notes

- **Focus management.** When the drawer opens, focus should move to the drawer container or its first interactive element. The current source does not do this automatically. Add it with a `useEffect` and a `ref` on the drawer:

```tsx
// After the drawer mounts and opens, move focus to the drawer content
useEffect(() => {
  if (open && containerRef.current) {
    containerRef.current.focus()
  }
}, [open])

// Add tabIndex={-1} to the motion.div container
<motion.div ref={containerRef} tabIndex={-1} ... >
```

- **Return focus on close.** Store a reference to the element that triggered the drawer and restore focus to it when the drawer closes:

```tsx
const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)
// On open, triggerRef.current is the button
// On onOpenChange(false), call triggerRef.current?.focus()
```

- **Escape key.** The drawer does not handle keyboard Escape. Add a `keydown` listener:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === "Escape" && open) onOpenChange(false)
  }
  window.addEventListener("keydown", handler)
  return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handler)
}, [open, onOpenChange])
```

- **`aria-modal`.** The drawer blocks interaction with the page behind it (backdrop `pointer-events`). Add `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` to the drawer container so screen readers understand the modal context.
- **Drag handle label.** The visual drag handle (the `h-1.5 w-12` pill) has no accessible description. Consider adding a visually-hidden hint: `<span className="sr-only">Drag to resize</span>`.
- **Scroll lock.** The component calls `document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"` on open. This is the correct approach; confirm it does not break fixed headers or custom scroll containers in your layout.
- **Reduced motion.** The spring snap and dismiss animations should be instantaneous for users who prefer reduced motion:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"

// Pass a transition override to animate() calls that uses duration: 0
const transition = useReducedMotion()
  ? { duration: 0 }
  : { type: "spring", damping: 30, stiffness: 300 }
```

## Performance considerations

- **`useMotionValue` for `y`.** All drag and spring animations run through the motion value pipeline, bypassing React re-renders during the gesture. Layout only re-renders when `open` or `drawerHeight` state changes, keeping gesture performance smooth.
- **`createPortal` into `document.body`.** The drawer renders outside the React tree of the trigger component. This avoids stacking context issues but means it cannot inherit CSS custom properties from a parent provider unless they are on `:root` or `body`.
- **Backdrop `useTransform`.** `backdropOpacity` is derived from `y` via `useTransform`. This is evaluated in the motion value pipeline without re-rendering. The `pointerEvents` transform also derives from `y`, which prevents backdrop clicks when the drawer is fully closed.
- **`window.innerHeight` on resize.** The component listens to `resize` and updates `drawerHeight` state, which triggers a React re-render and recalculates the snap target positions. This is correct but avoid opening the drawer during an active resize.
- **`overflow-y-auto` inner scroll vs. drag conflict.** Content inside the drawer can scroll vertically. The `touchAction: "none"` on the outer container prevents native scroll from conflicting with `framer-motion`'s drag. If the inner scroll container has long content, test that scroll and drag do not conflict on iOS Safari.

## Customization examples

### Three snap points (mini, half, full)

```tsx
import { MagneticDrawer } from "@/components/animations/specials/magnetic-drawer"
import { useState } from "react"

export function ThreeSnapDrawer() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <button
        onClick={() => setOpen(true)}
        className="rounded-lg bg-neutral-900 px-5 py-2.5 text-sm font-medium text-white dark:bg-white dark:text-neutral-900"
      >
        Open filters
      </button>
      <MagneticDrawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} snapPoints={[0.25, 0.55, 0.9]}>
        <div className="space-y-4 p-4">
          <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold">Filters</h2>
          <p className="text-sm text-neutral-500">Drag to expand or collapse.</p>
        </div>
      </MagneticDrawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Tall content with inner scroll

```tsx
import { MagneticDrawer } from "@/components/animations/specials/magnetic-drawer"
import { useState } from "react"

export function ScrollableDrawer() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="rounded-lg border px-4 py-2 text-sm">
        View details
      </button>
      <MagneticDrawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} snapPoints={[0.6]}>
        <div className="space-y-3 p-4">
          {Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => (
            <div key={i} className="rounded-lg bg-neutral-100 dark:bg-neutral-800 p-3 text-sm">
              Row {i + 1} of content
            </div>
          ))}
        </div>
      </MagneticDrawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

## Real-world examples

### Mobile navigation drawer

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { MagneticDrawer } from "@/components/animations/specials/magnetic-drawer"

const navItems = ["Dashboard", "Projects", "Team", "Settings", "Billing"]

export function MobileNav() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <button
        onClick={() => setOpen(true)}
        className="rounded-md border border-neutral-200 p-2 dark:border-neutral-800"
        aria-label="Open navigation"
      >
        <svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="currentColor">
          <path fillRule="evenodd" d="M2 4.75A.75.75 0 012.75 4h14.5a.75.75 0 010 1.5H2.75A.75.75 0 012 4.75zm0 10.5a.75.75 0 01.75-.75h7.5a.75.75 0 010 1.5h-7.5a.75.75 0 01-.75-.75zM2 10a.75.75 0 01.75-.75h14.5a.75.75 0 010 1.5H2.75A.75.75 0 012 10z" clipRule="evenodd" />
        </svg>
      </button>

      <MagneticDrawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} snapPoints={[0.5, 0.85]}>
        <nav className="p-6" role="navigation" aria-label="Main navigation">
          <p className="mb-4 text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-widest text-neutral-400">Navigation</p>
          <ul className="space-y-1">
            {navItems.map((item) => (
              <li key={item}>
                <a
                  href={`/${item.toLowerCase()}`}
                  className="block rounded-lg px-3 py-2.5 text-sm font-medium text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 dark:text-neutral-300 dark:hover:bg-neutral-800"
                >
                  {item}
                </a>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        </nav>
      </MagneticDrawer>
    </>
  )
}
```

description: A generic reaction button with burst animation support for any icon.

    <Steps>
      <Step>
        **Install dependencies**

      </Step>

        **Copy the component code**
        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/reaction-button.tsx"
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { motion } from "motion/react";
import type { Easing } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import { LucideIcon } from "lucide-react";

export interface ReactionButtonProps {
    Icon: LucideIcon;
    size?: number;
    colors?: {
        initial?: string;
        liked?: string;
    };
    isLiked?: boolean;
    onToggle?: (isLiked: boolean) => void;
    className?: string;
}

export function ReactionButton({
    Icon,
    size = 24,
    colors = {
        initial: "currentColor",
        liked: "#ef4444",
    },
    isLiked = false,
    onToggle,
    className,
}: ReactionButtonProps) {
    const [liked, setLiked] = React.useState(isLiked);

    const handleClick = () => {
        const newState = !liked;
        setLiked(newState);
        onToggle?.(newState);
    };

    const MotionIcon = motion(Icon);

    return (
        <div className={cn("relative inline-flex items-center justify-center", className)} style={{ width: size, height: size }}>
            <MotionIcon
                size={size}
                onClick={handleClick}
                className="cursor-pointer z-10 relative outline-none focus:ring-0 focus:outline-none"
                initial={false}
                whileTap={{ scale: 0.8 }}
                animate={{
                    scale: liked ? [0.8, 1.2, 1] : 1, // Subtle pop
                    fill: liked ? colors.liked : "transparent",
                    stroke: liked ? colors.liked : colors.initial,
                }}
                transition={{
                    duration: 0.3,
                    times: [0, 0.4, 1],
                    ease: "easeOut",
                }}
            />

            {/* Sparkle effects when liked */}
            {liked && (
                <div className="absolute inset-0 pointer-events-none">
                    {/* Center sparkle (Cross) */}
                    <motion.div
                        className="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center"
                        initial={{ scale: 0, opacity: 0, rotate: 0 }}
                        animate={{
                            scale: [0, 1.2, 0],
                            opacity: [0, 1, 0],
                            rotate: [0, 45]
                        }}
                        transition={{ duration: 0.4 }}
                    >
                        <svg width={size} height={size} viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="white" strokeWidth="2" strokeLinecap="round">
                            <path d="M12 2 L12 6 M12 18 L12 22 M2 12 L6 12 M18 12 L22 12" />
                        </svg>
                    </motion.div>

                    {/* Top-left sparkle (Dot) */}
                    <motion.div
                        className="absolute top-0 left-0 rounded-full bg-white"
                        style={{ width: size * 0.1, height: size * 0.1 }}
                        initial={{ scale: 0, opacity: 0, x: size * 0.2, y: size * 0.2 }}
                        animate={{
                            scale: [0, 1, 0],
                            opacity: [0, 1, 0],
                            x: -size * 0.3,
                            y: -size * 0.3
                        }}
                        transition={{ duration: 0.3, delay: 0.05, ease: "easeOut" }}
                    />

                    {/* Top-right sparkle (Dot) */}
                    <motion.div
                        className="absolute top-0 right-0 rounded-full bg-white"
                        style={{ width: size * 0.1, height: size * 0.1 }}
                        initial={{ scale: 0, opacity: 0, x: -size * 0.2, y: size * 0.2 }}
                        animate={{
                            scale: [0, 1, 0],
                            opacity: [0, 1, 0],
                            x: size * 0.3,
                            y: -size * 0.3
                        }}
                        transition={{ duration: 0.3, delay: 0.1, ease: "easeOut" }}
                    />
                </div>
            )}
        </div>
    );
}
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>

## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Icon` | `LucideIcon` | - | The Lucide icon component to render. |
| `size` | `number` | `24` | The size of the button in pixels. |
| `colors` | `object` | `{ initial: "currentColor", liked: "#ef4444" }` | Object containing `initial` and `liked` colors. |
| `isLiked` | `boolean` | `false` | Initial state of the button. |
| `onToggle` | `(isLiked: boolean) => void` | - | Callback function when the button is toggled. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |

## Use cases

`ReactionButton` wraps any `LucideIcon` in a `motion()` call and animates its `scale`, `fill`, and `stroke` properties on toggle. On activation it plays a `[0.8, 1.2, 1]` scale keyframe and three burst sparkle sub-animations: a cross SVG that scales and rotates, and two dot divs that fly outward from the corners. The component is controlled via the `isLiked` prop and fires `onToggle` with the new boolean state.

- **Like/love buttons on posts.** Pass `Icon={Heart}` with `colors={{ liked: "#ef4444" }}` for the classic heart reaction on user-generated content feeds.
- **Favorites and bookmarks.** Use `Icon={Bookmark}` or `Icon={Star}` to let users save articles, products, or playlists to a collection.
- **Upvote on comments or answers.** `Icon={ThumbsUp}` with `colors={{ liked: "#3b82f6" }}` matches common Q&A and forum upvote patterns.
- **Approve in review flows.** A `ThumbsUp` or `CheckCircle` button in a code review or content approval workflow gives reviewers a quick signal to emit without a text response.
- **Wishlist toggles on product cards.** An e-commerce product grid where each card has a `Bookmark` or `Heart` react button for adding to the wishlist without leaving the page.

For a grouped reaction picker with magnification, see [Reaction Dock](/docs/animations/specials/reaction-dock).

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ReactionButton` when:**

- You need a single binary toggle (liked / not liked). The component maintains its own `liked` state internally, initialized from `isLiked`, and calls `onToggle` with each change.
- The icon is from Lucide. `motion()` wraps a `LucideIcon` directly; other SVG components need additional adapter work.
- You want the burst sparkle effect on a single icon. For a row of labeled emoji reactions, [Reaction Dock](/docs/animations/specials/reaction-dock) is the right choice.

**Do not use `ReactionButton` when:**

- You need more than two states (e.g., "like", "love", "wow"). The component is strictly a boolean toggle. Implement a multi-state reaction picker separately.
- The toggle state must be server-synced immediately on every click. The component fires `onToggle` synchronously on click; optimistic UI patterns work, but error rollback (flipping back to the previous state on network failure) requires wiring the `isLiked` prop as a controlled value from the parent.
- The sparkle animation is unwanted (e.g., a minimal design system). The sparkles render whenever `liked` is `true` with no opt-out prop. To suppress them, fork the component and remove the sparkle `div` block.

## Accessibility notes

- **Button role.** The `MotionIcon` is rendered as a plain SVG element with an `onClick` handler, not wrapped in a `<button>`. This means it lacks keyboard focus, Enter/Space activation, and a `role="button"` by default. Wrap it:

```tsx
<button
  aria-label={liked ? "Unlike" : "Like"}
  aria-pressed={liked}
  onClick={handleClick}
  className="rounded focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500"
>
  <ReactionButton Icon={Heart} isLiked={liked} onToggle={setLiked} />
</button>
```

Or fork the component and replace the outer `div` with a `<button>` element.

- **`aria-pressed`.** The button conveys a two-state toggle. `aria-pressed={liked}` communicates the current state to screen readers and switches from "not pressed" to "pressed" on activation.
- **Accessible label.** An icon-only button must have a label. Either `aria-label` or a visually-hidden `span` is required. A label like "Add to favorites" (initial state) and "Remove from favorites" (active state) is more descriptive than "Like".
- **Color-only state change.** The toggle animates `fill` and `stroke` color changes. Users with color blindness may not distinguish `"currentColor"` (unfilled) from `colors.liked` (filled). Ensure the `fill` change (hollow to solid) provides enough shape contrast beyond hue alone. Lucide icons in their filled state look visually distinct, which helps.
- **Reduced motion.** The `[0.8, 1.2, 1]` scale keyframe and sparkle animations should be disabled for users who prefer reduced motion:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"

function AccessibleReactionButton(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof ReactionButton>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  // When reduced, bypass the animated scale sequence
  return <ReactionButton {...props} />
  // Fork the component to conditionally render sparkles and skip scale keyframes
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **`motion(Icon)` wrapping.** `motion()` is called once per render of `ReactionButton`. Move it outside the component body to avoid re-creating the enhanced component on every render:

```tsx
// At module level, outside the component
const MotionHeart = motion(Heart)
```

The current source calls `const MotionIcon = motion(Icon)` inside the function body. If `Icon` is stable (the same reference each render), `motion()` caches by identity and this is safe. If `Icon` is defined inline it creates a new component every render.

- **Sparkle unmount.** The sparkle `div` block is conditionally rendered when `liked` is `true`. It contains three `motion.div` sub-elements, each with their own `animate` sequence. These animate once and stay rendered until `liked` becomes `false`. The animations complete in 300 to 400 ms, after which the elements are static but still in the DOM. This has negligible cost for a few buttons but avoids the issue entirely by using `AnimatePresence` for exit-based cleanup.
- **`whileTap` scale.** The `whileTap={{ scale: 0.8 }}` gesture adds a compositor animation on pointer down. With many buttons in a dense list (a comment feed with 50 items), all buttons have the gesture listener registered. This is fine because gesture listeners are passive by default.
- **Fill/stroke color animation.** `fill` and `stroke` are CSS properties animated by `motion/react`. They are paint operations, not compositor-only. On a grid of 100 reaction buttons all toggling simultaneously this could cause a batch repaint. In practice, toggles happen one at a time, so cost is negligible.

        **Install dependencies**

        **Copy the component code**
        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/reaction-dock.tsx"
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { motion, useMotionValue, useSpring, useTransform, MotionValue } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

interface ReactionDockProps {
    items: {
        icon: React.ReactNode;
        label: string;
        onClick?: () => void;
    }[];
    className?: string;
}

export function ReactionDock({ items, className }: ReactionDockProps) {
    const mouseX = useMotionValue(Infinity);

    return (
        <motion.div
            onMouseMove={(e) => mouseX.set(e.pageX)}
            onMouseLeave={() => mouseX.set(Infinity)}
            className={cn(
                "mx-auto flex h-16 items-end gap-4 rounded-2xl bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900 px-4 pb-3 border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800",
                className
            )}
        >
            {items.map((item, i) => (
                <DockItem key={i} mouseX={mouseX} onClick={item.onClick}>
                    <div className="relative group">
                        <span className="absolute -top-8 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 rounded bg-zinc-900 dark:bg-zinc-100 px-2 py-0.5 text-xs text-white dark:text-zinc-900 opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100 whitespace-nowrap">
                            {item.label}
                        </span>
                        {item.icon}
                    </div>
                </DockItem>
            ))}
        </motion.div>
    );
}

function DockItem({
    mouseX,
    children,
    onClick,
}: {
    mouseX: MotionValue;
    children: React.ReactNode;
    onClick?: () => void;
}) {
    const ref = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

    const distance = useTransform(mouseX, (val) => {
        const bounds = ref.current?.getBoundingClientRect() ?? { x: 0, width: 0 };
        return val - bounds.x - bounds.width / 2;
    });

    const widthSync = useTransform(distance, [-150, 0, 150], [40, 80, 40]);
    const width = useSpring(widthSync, { mass: 0.1, stiffness: 150, damping: 12 });

    return (
        <motion.div
            ref={ref}
            style={{ width }}
            onClick={onClick}
            className="aspect-square w-10 cursor-pointer rounded-full bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-800 flex items-center justify-center hover:bg-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700 transition-colors"
        >
            {children}
        </motion.div>
    );
}
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>

## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `items` | `Array<{ icon: ReactNode, label: string, onClick?: () => void }>` | - | Array of items to display in the dock. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |

## Use cases

`ReactionDock` uses a shared `useMotionValue(Infinity)` for mouse X position. Each `DockItem` computes its distance from the cursor with `useTransform` and maps `[-150, 0, 150]` to `[40, 80, 40]` px width. A `useSpring` with `{ mass: 0.1, stiffness: 150, damping: 12 }` smooths the resize, producing the characteristic magnetic macOS Dock spring. The tooltip above each item uses a CSS `opacity` transition on `:group-hover`.

- **Social reactions on posts or comments.** A row of emoji-style reactions (ThumbsUp, Heart, Laugh, PartyPopper, Frown, Angry) maps directly to Facebook or Slack reaction sets.
- **Media player controls.** Play, pause, skip, volume, and like actions in a bottom bar with the magnification drawing the eye to the hovered control.
- **Floating action palettes.** A fixed-position dock at the bottom of a canvas editor or image viewer for tool selection.
- **Inline message emoji picker.** A small dock anchored to a message bubble for quick emoji replies in a chat interface.

For a single binary toggle reaction, see [Reaction Button](/docs/animations/specials/reaction-button).

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ReactionDock` when:**

- Your users are on a pointer device (mouse or trackpad). The magnification effect is driven by `e.pageX` from `onMouseMove`; it does nothing on touch screens.
- You have 4 to 8 items. Fewer than 4 does not benefit from the magnification spread; more than 8 items become hard to distinguish at the default 40 px resting size.
- The dock is a secondary or supplemental action bar, not the primary navigation. The hidden-until-hover tooltip pattern (`opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`) is not suitable for critical, always-visible actions.

**Do not use `ReactionDock` when:**

- Touch is the primary input. On touch devices `onMouseMove` never fires, all items stay at 40 px, and the tooltip labels are inaccessible. Consider a flat emoji grid or a [Swipeable Stack](/docs/animations/specials/swipeable-stack) for touch-first interactions.
- You need persistent, labeled actions that are always visible. The labels appear only on hover. For always-visible labeled buttons, use a standard toolbar.
- The dock must work inside a `pointer-events-none` parent. The `onMouseMove` listener is on the dock container; if a parent blocks pointer events the magnification will not update.

## Accessibility notes

- **Tooltip visibility.** Item labels are shown only on `:hover` via a CSS `opacity` transition. They are not exposed to screen readers at all in the current implementation. Add `aria-label` to each `DockItem` button so screen readers announce the label:

```tsx
// When building the items array, include aria-label on the rendered button
items={[
  {
    icon: <ThumbsUp className="h-5 w-5" />,
    label: "Like",
    onClick: () => handleReaction("like"),
  }
]}
// In the DockItem, pass aria-label={item.label} to the motion.div or wrap with <button>
```

- **Button role.** `DockItem` renders as a `motion.div` with an `onClick`. This lacks `role="button"`, keyboard focus, and Enter/Space activation. Wrap each item in a `<button>` for full keyboard support:

```tsx
// Replace the motion.div in DockItem with:
<motion.button
  ref={ref}
  style={{ width }}
  onClick={onClick}
  aria-label={label}
  className="aspect-square cursor-pointer rounded-full bg-zinc-200 dark:bg-zinc-800 flex items-center justify-center hover:bg-zinc-300 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700"
>
  {children}
</motion.button>
```

- **Focus indicator.** Keyboard-focused items need a visible ring. Add `focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-500 focus-visible:outline-none` to the button class.
- **Tooltip for keyboard users.** The CSS hover tooltip is invisible to keyboard users. Use a `title` attribute or a proper tooltip component that also activates on focus.
- **Reduced motion.** The `useSpring` magnification animation should not run for users who prefer reduced motion. Set a static width when `prefers-reduced-motion` is active:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"

function AccessibleDockItem({ mouseX, children, onClick }: DockItemProps) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const width = reduced ? 40 : useSpringWidth(mouseX) // skip spring
  ...
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **`onMouseMove` frequency.** The `onMouseMove` handler on the dock container calls `mouseX.set(e.pageX)` on every pointer move event. This fires at the display refresh rate (typically 60 to 120 times per second). Because `mouseX` is a `MotionValue`, updates flow through the `useTransform` and `useSpring` pipeline without triggering React re-renders. This is the correct pattern and performs well.
- **`useTransform` per item.** Each `DockItem` derives `distance` and `widthSync` from `mouseX`. With 6 items, that is 12 `useTransform` subscriptions and 6 `useSpring` instances. All evaluate in the motion value pipeline. Cost is negligible for typical dock sizes.
- **`getBoundingClientRect()` in transform.** The `distance` transform reads `ref.current?.getBoundingClientRect()` on every motion value update. `getBoundingClientRect` forces a layout flush if the DOM has pending style changes. Avoid mutating the DOM layout inside the transform function; read sizes in a `useEffect` and cache them in a ref if performance profiling shows jank.
- **Static `40 px` resting width.** When `mouseX` is `Infinity` (mouse not over dock), all items calculate a distance of `Infinity`, which maps to `40` in the `[-150, 0, 150]` range (the `clamp` edge). Ensure the spring settles to exactly 40 px so the dock does not visually jitter when the mouse leaves.
- **No `will-change`.** The `width` spring animation is a layout change (changing `width` causes relayout). For 6 items this is acceptable, but avoid adding `will-change: width` as it does not help layout-animating properties.

      <Step>
        **Copy the component code**
        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/spotlight-card.tsx"
"use client";

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import { motion, useMotionTemplate, useMotionValue, useSpring } from "motion/react";
import { useRef } from "react";

interface SpotlightCardProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  className?: string;
  spotlightColor?: string;
  spotlightSize?: number;
  hoverScale?: number;
}

export function SpotlightCard({
  children,
  className,
  spotlightColor = "rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)",
  spotlightSize = 350,
  hoverScale = 1.05,
}: SpotlightCardProps) {
  const cardRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  
  const mouseX = useMotionValue(-spotlightSize);
  const mouseY = useMotionValue(-spotlightSize);

  const springConfig = { damping: 20, stiffness: 200, mass: 0.5 };
  const smoothMouseX = useSpring(mouseX, springConfig);
  const smoothMouseY = useSpring(mouseY, springConfig);

  const handleMouseMove = (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (!cardRef.current) return;
    const rect = cardRef.current.getBoundingClientRect();
    mouseX.set(e.clientX - rect.left);
    mouseY.set(e.clientY - rect.top);
  };

  const handleMouseLeave = () => {
    // Leave logic
  };

  const spotlightGradient = useMotionTemplate\`
    radial-gradient(
      \${spotlightSize}px circle at \${smoothMouseX}px \${smoothMouseY}px,
      \${spotlightColor},
      transparent 80%
    )
  \`;

  return (
    <motion.div
      ref={cardRef}
      className={cn(
        "group relative overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-neutral-200 bg-white dark:border-neutral-800 dark:bg-neutral-900 shadow-sm",
        className
      )}
      onMouseMove={handleMouseMove}
      onMouseLeave={handleMouseLeave}
      whileHover={{ 
          scale: hoverScale,
          rotate: 0,
          boxShadow: "0 20px 25px -5px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 8px 10px -6px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)"
      }}
      transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 300, damping: 20 }}
    >
      <motion.div
        className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 z-20 opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-300 group-hover:opacity-100"
        style={{ background: spotlightGradient }}
      />
       <motion.div
        className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 z-20 rounded-xl opacity-0 transition-opacity duration-300 group-hover:opacity-100"
        style={{
            borderWidth: 2,
            borderStyle: "solid",
            borderColor: spotlightColor,
            maskImage: spotlightGradient,
            WebkitMaskImage: spotlightGradient,
        }}
      />
      <div 
        className="absolute inset-0 z-0 opacity-[0.05] pointer-events-none"
        style={{
            backgroundImage: \`url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg viewBox='0 0 200 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cfilter id='noiseFilter'%3E%3CfeTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.65' numOctaves='3' stitchTiles='stitch'/%3E%3C/filter%3E%3Crect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23noiseFilter)'/%3E%3C/svg%3E")\`
        }}
      />
      <div className="relative z-10 h-full w-full transition-transform duration-300 group-hover:translate-y-[-2px]">
        {children}
      </div>
    </motion.div>
  );
}
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>

## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Content to display inside the card. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |
| `spotlightColor` | `string` | `"rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)"` | Color of the spotlight gradient. |
| `spotlightSize` | `number` | `350` | Size of the spotlight circle. |
| `hoverScale` | `number` | `1.05` | Scale factor on hover. |

## Use cases

`SpotlightCard` tracks mouse position within the card using `onMouseMove`, storing `clientX` and `clientY` relative to the card's `getBoundingClientRect` in two `useMotionValue` instances. A `useSpring` (damping 20, stiffness 200, mass 0.5) smooths each value, and `useMotionTemplate` builds a `radial-gradient` string that drives the `background` of an absolutely-positioned overlay. A second overlay uses the same gradient as a `maskImage` to reveal a colored border glow at the spotlight position. The card itself uses `whileHover` with a `spring(stiffness: 300, damping: 20)` for the `hoverScale` lift.

- **Feature cards on marketing pages.** A 2- or 3-column grid of dark-background feature cards with per-card spotlight colors (cyan, violet, amber) creates a visually differentiated feature section.
- **Pricing plan cards.** The spotlight on a "Pro" or "Enterprise" tier card draws attention as the user scans across tiers without requiring an animated badge.
- **Team member or contributor profiles.** Staff or open-source contributor cards with a soft spotlight add interactivity to otherwise static content.
- **Dashboard widget containers.** Wrapping metrics or chart panels in `SpotlightCard` gives a premium look to internal tools and admin UIs.
- **Onboarding checklist items.** Cards for each setup step get a spotlight to signal interactivity as the user works through a list.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `SpotlightCard` when:**

- The card is on a dark or neutral background. The default `spotlightColor` is `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25)` (white), which is invisible on white backgrounds. Set a contrasting color or use on dark surfaces.
- The content inside the card is visually important and you want to reward exploration without an explicit hover state change (color swap, underline, etc.).
- Users are on a pointer device. The spotlight tracks `onMouseMove`; on touch devices there is no visible effect until a tap, and the hover scale does not trigger. The card reads as a static element on mobile.

**Do not use `SpotlightCard` when:**

- The card is inside a dense list or table where `hoverScale={1.05}` causes layout shift. Set `hoverScale={1}` to disable the scale, or use a different component for tabular data.
- The `spotlightColor` matches the card background. Test every theme (light and dark) separately; what is visible on `neutral-900` may be invisible on `white`.
- The card must perform well on very low-end hardware. The dual overlay approach (`radial-gradient` background + `maskImage` border glow) requires two compositing layers. On devices with limited GPU memory, multiply this by many cards and profiling is advisable.
- The card contains text that must remain readable at all times. `hoverScale` on a card adjacent to others can cause the scaled card to overlap its neighbors unless you add `z-index` management.

## Accessibility notes

- **Not a focusable element.** `SpotlightCard` renders a `motion.div` with no interactive role. If the card is a navigation element or a clickable entity, wrap it in an `<a>` or `<button>`, or add `role="button"` and `tabIndex={0}` plus keyboard handlers.
- **Hover-only effect.** The spotlight and border glow appear only on hover. They convey no information; they are purely decorative. No `aria` attributes are needed for the effect itself.
- **`hoverScale` and screen magnification.** Users running OS-level screen magnification may find a card scaling 5% on hover disorienting. Consider a lower `hoverScale` (1.02) or disable it via `hoverScale={1}` in accessible contexts.
- **Reduced motion.** Both the spring spotlight tracking and the `whileHover` scale should be suppressed:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { SpotlightCard } from "@/components/animations/specials/spotlight-card"

function AccessibleSpotlightCard(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof SpotlightCard>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return (
    <SpotlightCard
      {...props}
      hoverScale={reduced ? 1 : props.hoverScale}
    />
  )
}
```

To fully disable the `radial-gradient` spotlight in reduced motion, fork the component and guard the `onMouseMove` handler with a check against `window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches`.

- **Focus visibility.** If you wrap the card in a `<button>` or `<a>`, confirm that the `focus-visible` ring is visible over the spotlight overlay. The overlay sits at `z-20`; ensure your focus ring sits above it (`z-30` or via `outline`).

## Performance considerations

- **`onMouseMove` and motion values.** Mouse position is stored in `useMotionValue` and smoothed with `useSpring`. Updates go through the motion value pipeline without triggering React re-renders. The `useMotionTemplate` string is also evaluated outside React. This is as performant as pointer tracking can get in the React ecosystem.
- **Dual overlay `radial-gradient`.** Two `motion.div` elements sit at `z-20` with `position: absolute`. One has a `background: radial-gradient(...)` and the other uses `maskImage: radial-gradient(...)` for the border glow. Both recompose on every pointer move event. Modern browsers handle this in the GPU compositor, but each card adds two compositor layers.
- **Noise texture overlay.** A third `div` at `z-0` renders a base64-encoded SVG noise pattern as `backgroundImage`. This texture is static and loaded once; the browser caches the decoded SVG bitmap. Its cost is a single paint on mount.
- **`whileHover` spring.** The `scale` spring (`stiffness: 300, damping: 20`) runs on the compositor. It does not cause layout shifts during the animation. However, when `scale` settles at the hover value, neighboring cards are not moved. If cards are in a `gap`-based grid, the scaled card overlaps adjacent cards. Add `relative z-10` on hover or use a wrapping container with `overflow: visible`.
- **Many cards in a grid.** A page with 12 spotlight cards has up to 24 always-mounted compositor layers (2 per card). Combine with noise textures and the scale spring and GPU memory use on mobile can become noticeable. Test on a mid-range mobile device before shipping a large grid.

        ```ts title="lib/utils.ts"
import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
        ```

        **Copy the component code**
        ```tsx title="components/animations/specials/swipeable-stack.tsx"
"use client";

import React, { useState } from "react";
import { motion, useMotionValue, useTransform, useAnimation, PanInfo, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

interface SwipeableStackProps {
  children: React.ReactNode[];
  className?: string;
  onSwipeRight?: (index: number) => void;
  onSwipeLeft?: (index: number) => void;
}

export function SwipeableStack({ children, className, onSwipeRight, onSwipeLeft }: SwipeableStackProps) {
    const [cards, setCards] = useState(React.Children.toArray(children));
    const [history, setHistory] = useState<React.ReactNode[]>([]);

    const activeCard = cards[cards.length - 1];

    const removeCard = (direction: "left" | "right") => {
        const removed = cards.pop();
        if (removed) {
             setHistory([...history, removed]);
             const index = cards.length;
             if (direction === "right" && onSwipeRight) onSwipeRight(index);
             if (direction === "left" && onSwipeLeft) onSwipeLeft(index);
             setCards([...cards]);
        }
    };

    return (
        <div className={cn("relative h-full w-full flex items-center justify-center", className)}>
            <AnimatePresence>
                {cards.map((child, index) => {
                    const isFront = index === cards.length - 1;
                    return (
                        <Card 
                            key={index}
                            index={index}
                            isFront={isFront}
                            drag={isFront}
                            total={cards.length}
                            onRemove={removeCard}
                        >
                            {child}
                        </Card>
                    );
                })}
            </AnimatePresence>
            {cards.length === 0 && (
                 <div className="text-center text-neutral-500">
                     No more items
                     <button 
                        onClick={() => {
                            setCards(React.Children.toArray(children));
                            setHistory([]);
                        }}
                        className="mt-4 block mx-auto text-blue-500 hover:underline"
                    >
                        Reset
                     </button>
                 </div>
            )}
        </div>
    );
}

function Card({ 
    children, 
    index, 
    isFront,
    drag,
    total,
    onRemove 
}: { 
    children: React.ReactNode; 
    index: number; 
    isFront: boolean; 
    drag: boolean;
    total: number;
    onRemove: (dir: "left" | "right") => void;
}) {
    const x = useMotionValue(0);
    const rotate = useTransform(x, [-200, 200], [-25, 25]);
    const opacity = useTransform(x, [-150, 0, 150], [0.5, 1, 0.5]);
    
    // Stacking logic
    const reverseIndex = total - 1 - index;
    const scale = 1 - reverseIndex * 0.05;
    const y = reverseIndex * 15;
    const zIndex = total - reverseIndex;

    const controls = useAnimation();

    const handleDragEnd = async (_: any, info: PanInfo) => {
        if (info.offset.x > 100) {
            await controls.start({ x: 500, opacity: 0 });
            onRemove("right");
        } else if (info.offset.x < -100) {
            await controls.start({ x: -500, opacity: 0 });
            onRemove("left");
        } else {
            controls.start({ x: 0 });
        }
    };

    return (
        <motion.div
            style={{
                x,
                rotate,
                scale: isFront ? 1 : scale,
                y: isFront ? 0 : y,
                zIndex,
            }}
            initial={{ scale, y }}
            animate={controls}
            drag={drag ? "x" : false}
            dragConstraints={{ left: 0, right: 0, top: 0, bottom: 0 }}
            dragElastic={0.7}
            onDragEnd={handleDragEnd}
            className="absolute left-0 right-0 top-0 bottom-0 mx-auto cursor-grab active:cursor-grabbing origin-bottom"
            whileDrag={{ scale: 1.05 }}
        >
            <div className="h-full w-full rounded-2xl bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900 border border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-800 shadow-xl overflow-hidden">
                {children}
            </div>
        </motion.div>
    );
}
        ```
      </Step>
    </Steps>

## Props

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `children` | `ReactNode[]` | - | Array of items to stack. |
| `onSwipeRight` | `(index) => void` | - | Callback when swiped right. |
| `onSwipeLeft` | `(index) => void` | - | Callback when swiped left. |

## Use cases

`SwipeableStack` manages an array of cards derived from `React.Children.toArray(children)`. The top card (last in array) has `drag="x"` enabled with `dragElastic={0.7}`. During drag, `useTransform` maps the `x` motion value to `rotate` (from -25 to 25 degrees) and `opacity` (0.5 at the extremes). When `|offset.x| > 100` the card is animated off-screen (`x: 500` or `x: -500`) and removed from the stack. Cards below the top are stacked using `scale = 1 - reverseIndex * 0.05` and `y = reverseIndex * 15`, creating a visible depth of cards. An internal `history` array tracks removed cards; when the stack is empty a "Reset" button restores all children.

- **Onboarding card decks.** A swipeable introduction sequence where each card covers a feature or setup step; right swipe advances through the deck.
- **Content discovery feeds.** Article or product cards presented one at a time for decision-making, similar to Tinder-style browsing.
- **Flashcard apps.** Study decks where left swipe marks a card as "needs review" and right swipe marks it as "known", using `onSwipeLeft` and `onSwipeRight` callbacks to update state.
- **Photo selection.** A small batch of candidate images that a user accepts or rejects one at a time.
- **Survey or quiz questions.** Sequential question cards that advance on swipe instead of a next button.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `SwipeableStack` when:**

- The deck is small: 3 to 10 cards. The component renders all cards simultaneously as absolutely-positioned layers. A large number of cards means many concurrent DOM nodes.
- The user is on a touch device or the interaction is intended as a touch-first experience. The drag gesture works on both touch and mouse, but the swipe metaphor is native to mobile.
- Each decision is binary (accept/reject, like/skip). The two-direction gesture maps cleanly to `onSwipeRight` and `onSwipeLeft`.

**Do not use `SwipeableStack` when:**

- You need non-destructive browsing where the user scrolls back and forth through items. `SwipeableStack` removes cards from the visible stack on swipe; the "Reset" button restores from `children`, but there is no built-in undo for individual swipes. If users need to revisit specific cards, use a [Linear Carousel](/docs/animations/specials/linear-carousel) instead.
- The primary interface is desktop with keyboard-only users. There is no built-in keyboard alternative to the swipe gesture. Add keyboard handlers before using in production for desktop apps.
- You need to display metadata alongside the stack (a progress bar, a count, labels). The component provides no built-in UI for this; you must build it around the stack using the `onSwipeLeft`/`onSwipeRight` callbacks.
- The cards contain forms or interactive content that the user needs to interact with without accidentally triggering a swipe. Drag with `dragElastic={0.7}` is very sensitive. Input focus does not suppress drag in the current implementation.

## Accessibility notes

- **No keyboard swipe alternative.** The drag gesture is the only way to advance cards. Keyboard users cannot interact. Add Arrow Left/Arrow Right key handlers in a `useEffect` on the `SwipeableStack` wrapper:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === "ArrowRight") triggerSwipe("right")
    if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") triggerSwipe("left")
  }
  window.addEventListener("keydown", handler)
  return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handler)
}, [cards])
```

- **Screen reader announcements.** When a card is swiped, screen readers are not informed that the content has changed. Add a live region that announces the current card position:

```tsx
<div role="status" aria-live="polite" className="sr-only">
  Card {totalCards - cards.length + 1} of {totalCards}
</div>
```

- **Interactive content inside cards.** If cards contain buttons, links, or form elements, the outer `motion.div` with `drag="x"` may capture pointer events before they reach the child. Ensure interactive elements have `stopPropagation` on pointerdown or use `dragListener={false}` inside nested interactive areas.
- **"No more items" state.** The empty state renders a "Reset" button as a `<button>` element, which is keyboard-accessible. Confirm the button receives focus after the last card is removed so keyboard users can continue.
- **Reduced motion.** The rotate, scale, and fly-off animations should be suppressed:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"

function AccessibleSwipeableStack(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof SwipeableStack>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  // When reduced, a keyboard-driven advance replaces the animated swipe
  // Fork the component to conditionally skip x/rotate animations
  return <SwipeableStack {...props} />
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **All cards mounted simultaneously.** Every child is in the DOM as an absolutely-positioned `motion.div`. The top card has active drag listeners; background cards are static. For 5 cards this is fine. Avoid passing more than 20 children without virtualization.
- **`useMotionValue`, `useTransform`, `useAnimation` per card.** Each `Card` instance creates its own set of motion values and an animation controller. These are lightweight, but with many cards visible simultaneously the initial mount cost is proportional to the card count.
- **`dragElastic={0.7}`.** High elastic allows the card to move well beyond `dragConstraints: { left: 0, right: 0 }`. The elastic resistance runs on the main thread during drag. Lower values (0.3 to 0.5) reduce the overshoot distance and may feel snappier on lower-end devices.
- **`AnimatePresence` exit.** When `onRemove("right")` is called, `controls.start({ x: 500, opacity: 0 })` runs to completion, then the card is removed from state. `AnimatePresence` handles the exit of the removed element. The fly-off is compositor-friendly (transform + opacity only).
- **`array.pop()` mutation.** The `removeCard` function calls `cards.pop()` directly on the state-derived array before calling `setCards`. This mutates the array in place, which can cause subtle bugs if `cards` is referenced elsewhere before the state update flushes. Prefer `cards.slice(0, -1)` for a pure immutable update.

## Customization examples

### Flashcard deck with callbacks

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { SwipeableStack } from "@/components/animations/specials/swipeable-stack"

const flashcards = [
  { question: "What is a closure?", answer: "A function that retains access to its lexical scope." },
  { question: "What is a pure function?", answer: "A function with no side effects that returns the same output for the same input." },
  { question: "What is memoization?", answer: "Caching the result of a function call to avoid redundant computation." },
]

export function FlashcardDeck() {
  const [known, setKnown] = useState<string[]>([])
  const [review, setReview] = useState<string[]>([])

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-6">
      <p className="text-sm text-neutral-500">
        Swipe right to mark known, left to review.
      </p>
      <div className="h-64 w-56">
        <SwipeableStack
          onSwipeRight={(i) => setKnown((prev) => [...prev, flashcards[i]?.question ?? ""])}
          onSwipeLeft={(i) => setReview((prev) => [...prev, flashcards[i]?.question ?? ""])}
        >
          {flashcards.map((card, i) => (
            <div key={i} className="flex h-full w-full flex-col justify-center gap-3 rounded-2xl bg-white dark:bg-neutral-900 border border-neutral-200 dark:border-neutral-800 p-5 shadow-sm">
              <p className="text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-wide text-neutral-400">Question</p>

        <span>Known: {known.length}</span>
        <span>Review: {review.length}</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```
