# blur-in.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/blur-in.mdx

title: Blur In Text
description: Text that blurs in word by word or character by character.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextBlurIn } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/blur-in';

## Overview

The `TextBlurIn` creates a staggered blur-in effect for text.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextBlurIn } from "@/components/animations/text/blur-in"

<TextBlurIn className="text-3xl font-bold">
  This text blurs into focus
</TextBlurIn>`}
  <TextBlurIn className="text-3xl font-bold">This text blurs into focus</TextBlurIn>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-blur-in
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-blur-in
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-blur-in
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-blur-in
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/blur-in.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface TextBlurInProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"p">, "children"> {
  children: string;
  duration?: number;
  delay?: number;
  by?: "character" | "word";
  staggerDelay?: number;
}
export function TextBlurIn({
  children,
  className,
  duration = 0.8,
  delay = 0,
  by = "word",
  staggerDelay = 0.04,
  ...props
}: TextBlurInProps) {
  const units = by === "word" ? children.split(" ") : children.split("");
  return (
    <motion.p className={cn(className)} {...props}>
      {units.map((unit, index) => (
        <motion.span
          key={index}
          initial={{ opacity: 0, filter: "blur(10px)" }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
          transition={{
            duration,
            delay: delay + index * staggerDelay,
          }}
          style={{ display: "inline-block" }}
        >
          {unit}
          {by === "word" && index < units.length - 1 && "\u00A0"}
        </motion.span>
      ))}
    </motion.p>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextBlurIn } from "@/components/animations/text/blur-in"

<TextBlurIn>Hello World</TextBlurIn>
```

## Examples

### By Character

  <TextBlurIn by="character" className="text-xl">Character by character blur</TextBlurIn>

### Custom Stagger

  <Preview background="default" code={`<TextBlurIn staggerDelay={0.02}>Fast</TextBlurIn>`}>
    <TextBlurIn staggerDelay={0.02} className="text-lg">Fast blur effect</TextBlurIn>
  
  <Preview background="default" code={`<TextBlurIn staggerDelay={0.1}>Slow</TextBlurIn>`}>
    <TextBlurIn staggerDelay={0.1} className="text-lg">Slow blur effect</TextBlurIn>
</PreviewGrid>

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to animate |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.8` | Blur duration (seconds) |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Initial delay |
| `by` | `"word" \| "character"` | `"word"` | Animation unit |
| `staggerDelay` | `number` | `0.04` | Delay between units |

## Use cases

`TextBlurIn` animates each word (or character) from `opacity: 0, filter: blur(10px)` to fully visible, staggered by `staggerDelay` seconds per unit. Reach for it when:

- **Hero headings.** A short 3 to 6 word headline blurs into focus on page load, drawing the eye without jarring movement.
- **Section titles.** A `by="word"` stagger at the default 0.04 s delay feels cinematic for above-the-fold section reveals triggered by scroll.
- **Pull quotes.** A short emphasized sentence that appears as the user scrolls past a content break.
- **App splash / onboarding.** A product name or tagline that blurs in on first render before the rest of the UI populates.

The `by="word"` default (splitting on spaces) keeps DOM node count low: a 6-word headline produces 6 `<span>` elements. Switching to `by="character"` on the same string produces one span per character, so reserve character-level blur for very short strings (under ~20 characters).

## When to use / when not to use

**Use blur-in when:**

- The string is short enough that the stagger completes in under 1 second at the default 0.04 s delay (roughly 25 words or fewer).
- You want a softer, atmospheric reveal rather than a directional motion. Blur reads as "coming into focus" rather than "sliding in from below," which suits editorial and creative contexts.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Body copy or multi-sentence text.** A paragraph with 40+ words at `staggerDelay={0.04}` takes over 1.5 seconds to fully reveal. Users will start reading before the blur clears, which fights comprehension. Use [Fade In](/docs/animations/text/fade-in) with a single short duration or no animation at all.
- **Long strings with `by="character"`.** A 50-character string produces 50 motion spans, each running its own filter animation. On lower-end mobile devices this can drop frames. Switch to `by="word"` or [Slide Up](/docs/animations/text/slide-up) which uses only translate and opacity.
- **Content that must be immediately scannable** (navigation items, table headers, form labels). Delays hurt usability in interactive contexts.

## Accessibility notes

The component renders each word or character as a `<motion.span>` inside a `<motion.p>`. Because the text is split into individual spans, screen readers may read each span separately or announce the paragraph as fragmented. To guarantee the full string is announced as a single phrase:

```tsx
<TextBlurIn
  aria-label="This text blurs into focus"
  className="text-3xl font-bold"
>
  This text blurs into focus
</TextBlurIn>
```

Adding `aria-label` on the wrapping `<p>` provides the complete string to assistive technology. You can also add `aria-hidden` to the individual spans if you render them yourself, though the component does not expose that level of control directly.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not currently check `prefers-reduced-motion` internally. Add a wrapper to skip the blur when the user has opted out of motion:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextBlurIn } from "@/components/animations/text/blur-in"

function AccessibleBlurIn({ children, ...props }: { children: string; [key: string]: unknown }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <p {...props}>{children}</p>
  return <TextBlurIn {...props}>{children}</TextBlurIn>
}
```

Never hide the text behind the animation; the initial `opacity: 0` state means content is invisible until the animation fires. Ensure the page is usable if JavaScript or motion is blocked.

## Performance considerations

- **Filter animations are GPU-accelerated** on modern browsers when combined with an opacity change, but `filter: blur()` can be more expensive than a plain opacity or transform. On a short hero headline (under 10 words) the cost is negligible; on long strings with `by="character"`, each span runs its own blur, which multiplies compositor work.
- **Per-span DOM cost.** A 100-character string with `by="character"` creates 100 motion spans, each registered with the motion library. Keep character-mode strings under ~25 characters.
- **Static `staggerDelay`.** Total animation time is `delay + (units.length - 1) * staggerDelay + duration`. For `by="word"` with 10 words: `0 + 9 * 0.04 + 0.8 = 1.16 s`. Plan the total duration to not exceed 1 to 1.5 seconds for a comfortable page load experience.
- **Animate only on mount.** The component runs once on mount via `animate={{ opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)" }}` with no repeat, so there is no continuous compositor load after the animation completes.

# dia-text.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/dia-text.mdx

title: Dia Text
description: Scroll-driven text reveal with precision blur and spring physics.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';

## Overview

The `DiaText` component is a dynamic word rotator where each word enters with a fast, multi-color gradient trace that solidifies to black, before swiping away for the next word. Inspired by modern kinetic typography.

## Usage

```tsx
import { DiaText } from "@/registry/new-york/animations/text/dia-text";

export default function Hero() {
  return (
    <h1 className="text-4xl font-bold">
      <DiaText words={["Chat", "Build", "Ship"]} /> with your tabs
    </h1>
  );
}
```

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-dia-text
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-dia-text
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-dia-text
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-dia-text
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the component**

    ```tsx title="registry/new-york/animations/text/dia-text.tsx"
    "use client";

    import { useState, useEffect } from "react";
    import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

    export interface DiaTextProps extends React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement> {
        words: string[];
        duration?: number;
        className?: string;
    }

    export function DiaText({
        words,
        duration = 2000,
        className,
        ...props
    }: DiaTextProps) {
        const [index, setIndex] = useState(0);

        useEffect(() => {
            const interval = setInterval(() => {
                setIndex((prev) => (prev + 1) % words.length);
            }, duration);

            return () => clearInterval(interval);
        }, [words, duration]);

        return (
            <span
                className={cn("relative inline-block overflow-hidden min-w-[2ch] align-bottom text-black dark:text-white", className)} 
                style={{ verticalAlign: "bottom" }} 
                {...props}
            >
                <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
                    <motion.span
                        key={index}
                        initial={{ y: "100%", opacity: 0, filter: "blur(4px)" }}
                        animate={{ y: "0%", opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
                        exit={{ y: "-100%", opacity: 0, filter: "blur(4px)" }}
                        transition={{
                            y: { type: "spring", stiffness: 300, damping: 30 },
                            opacity: { duration: 0.2 },
                            filter: { duration: 0.2 },
                        }}
                        className="absolute inset-0 inline-block"
                    >
                        <motion.span
                            className="inline-block bg-clip-text pb-1"
                            style={{
                                WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent",
                                backgroundImage: "linear-gradient(90deg, currentColor 50%, #2563EB 50%, #EA580C, #DB2777, #9333EA)", 
                                backgroundSize: "250% 100%", 
                            }}
                            initial={{
                                backgroundPosition: "100% 0%",
                            }}
                            animate={{
                                backgroundPosition: "0% 0%", 
                            }}
                            transition={{
                                duration: 0.8,
                                ease: "easeInOut",
                                delay: 0.1,
                            }}
                        >
                            {words[index]}
                        </motion.span>
                    </motion.span>
                </AnimatePresence>
                
                {/* Spacer for layout stability */}
                <span className="invisible" aria-hidden="true">{words[index]}</span>
            </span>
        );
    }
    ```

## Props

| Prop        | Type                  | Default       | Description                                      |
| :---        | :---                  | :---          | :---                                             |
| words       | string[]              | Required      | Array of words to cycle through                  |
| duration    | number                | 2000          | Duration to display each word (ms)               |
| className   | string                | -             | Additional classes for the container wrapper     |

## Use cases

`DiaText` cycles through a `words` array using `setInterval` at `duration` milliseconds per word (default 2000 ms). Each word enters from below with a spring transition (`stiffness: 300, damping: 30`) and blurs out upward on exit. While sliding in, the word's text color sweeps left-to-right from a multi-color gradient (blue `#2563EB`, orange `#EA580C`, pink `#DB2777`, purple `#9333EA`) to the solid inherited `currentColor` via `background-position` animation. An invisible spacer span preserves layout width. Reach for it when:

- **Hero taglines.** Inline within an `<h1>` to convey a product's multiple value propositions without a full content switch: "Build [Chat / Ship / Deploy] products."
- **Feature rotation.** Cycling benefit keywords next to a static verb: "Code [faster / smarter / without friction]."
- **Brand voice statements.** Short, punchy adjectives that establish tone above the fold.
- **Pricing headline.** "The [simplest / most affordable / best-value] plan for your team."

The gradient trace is purely cosmetic and always resolves to the parent's text color, so the component drops into any heading without custom color configuration.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use DiaText when:**

- The rotating words are roughly similar in character length. The container uses an invisible spacer to hold width, so words that are much longer or shorter than the spacer word can cause minor layout shifts.
- You want a visually premium kinetic effect at the start of a page where grabbing attention is the goal.
- The list has 2 to 5 items. Longer lists mean users may never see all words, which wastes content.

**Reach for something else when:**

- You need more than word rotation, such as full phrase changes. [Word Carousel](/docs/animations/text/word-carousel) uses the same slide mechanic with a simpler, gradient-free implementation.
- The parent text is body copy or inside a paragraph users must read. The continuous cycling distraction hurts reading comprehension; reserve this effect for display text only.
- You want the user to control the rotation (e.g., a tabbed interface). The `setInterval` runs unconditionally; there is no pause or manual trigger prop.
- The page has multiple DiaText instances on screen at once. Competing simultaneous rotations split attention and dilute the effect of each.

## Accessibility notes

The currently visible word lives inside an `<AnimatePresence>` block inside a `<span>`. Screen readers may announce each word change as it cycles, which can be disruptive mid-sentence. Two mitigations to consider:

**Option 1: Mark the rotating span as `aria-hidden` and provide a static accessible label on the parent.**

```tsx
<h1 className="text-4xl font-bold">
  <span aria-label="Chat, Build, and Ship with your tabs">
    <span aria-hidden="true">
      <DiaText words={["Chat", "Build", "Ship"]} />
    </span>
    {" "}with your tabs
  </span>
</h1>
```

**Option 2: Use `aria-live="off"` to suppress announcements** if the rotating text is purely decorative and the static surrounding text already conveys the meaning.

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion`. Wrap it to show only the first word statically when motion is reduced:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { DiaText } from "@/components/animations/text/dia-text"

function AccessibleDiaText({ words, ...props }: { words: string[] }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <span {...props}>{words[0]}</span>
  return <DiaText words={words} {...props} />
}
```

**Color contrast.** The gradient trace uses `WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent"` during the sweep, which means the text is briefly visible only through the gradient colors. Ensure each gradient color meets the WCAG AA contrast ratio against your background. The animation resolves to `currentColor` within 0.8 s, so this is a transient concern rather than a static one.

## Performance considerations

- **`setInterval` runs indefinitely.** The interval is cleared on unmount via the effect cleanup, but if the component is mounted off-screen, it keeps cycling without any visual output. Pair with an in-view check to pause when not visible.
- **`background-position` animation.** The inner `motion.span` animates `backgroundPosition` on every cycle, which triggers a paint on the text layer. Because it uses `background-clip: text` and `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent`, it cannot be promoted to its own compositor layer; each cycle is a repaint. This is acceptable for a single instance in a hero, but avoid multiple simultaneous DiaText components.
- **Spring transition.** The `y` transition uses a spring (`stiffness: 300, damping: 30`), which runs on the compositor as a transform and costs nothing after the initial frame calculation.
- **Invisible spacer.** The spacer `<span aria-hidden="true">` always renders the current word invisibly to hold layout. If your words have wildly different widths, the container can appear to jump. Pre-size the container with a `min-w-[Xch]` class.

```tsx
  We build <DiaText words={["products", "experiences", "tools"]} duration={3000} /> people love
</h1>
```

```tsx
    <div className="text-2xl font-semibold text-center">
      Your team can now{" "}
      <DiaText
        words={["collaborate in real time", "review designs faster", "ship with confidence"]}
        duration={2500}
        className="font-semibold"
      />
```

# fade-in.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/fade-in.mdx

title: Fade In Text
description: Text that fades in word by word or character by character.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextFadeIn } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/fade-in';

## Overview

The `TextFadeIn` creates a staggered fade-in effect for text.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextFadeIn } from "@/components/animations/text/fade-in"

<TextFadeIn className="text-2xl font-bold">
  This text fades in word by word
</TextFadeIn>`}
  <TextFadeIn className="text-2xl font-bold">This text fades in word by word</TextFadeIn>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-fade-in
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-fade-in
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-fade-in
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-fade-in
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/fade-in.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface TextFadeInProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"p">, "children"> {
  children: string;
  duration?: number;
  delay?: number;
  by?: "character" | "word";
  staggerDelay?: number;
}
export function TextFadeIn({
  children,
  className,
  duration = 0.5,
  delay = 0,
  by = "word",
  staggerDelay = 0.03,
  ...props
}: TextFadeInProps) {
  const units = by === "word" ? children.split(" ") : children.split("");
  return (
    <motion.p className={cn(className)} {...props}>
      {units.map((unit, index) => (
        <motion.span
          key={index}
          initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
          transition={{
            duration,
            delay: delay + index * staggerDelay,
          }}
          style={{ display: "inline-block" }}
        >
          {unit}
          {by === "word" && index < units.length - 1 && "\u00A0"}
        </motion.span>
      ))}
    </motion.p>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextFadeIn } from "@/components/animations/text/fade-in"

<TextFadeIn>Hello World</TextFadeIn>
```

## Examples

### Custom Stagger

  <Preview background="default" code={`<TextFadeIn staggerDelay={0.01}>Fast</TextFadeIn>`}>
    <TextFadeIn staggerDelay={0.01} className="text-lg">Fast stagger effect</TextFadeIn>
  
  <Preview background="default" code={`<TextFadeIn staggerDelay={0.1}>Slow</TextFadeIn>`}>
    <TextFadeIn staggerDelay={0.1} className="text-lg">Slow stagger effect</TextFadeIn>
</PreviewGrid>

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to animate |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.5` | Fade duration (seconds) |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Initial delay |
| `by` | `"word" \| "character"` | `"word"` | Animation unit |
| `staggerDelay` | `number` | `0.03` | Delay between units |

## Use cases

`TextFadeIn` animates each word (or character) from `opacity: 0` to `opacity: 1` in staggered sequence. With a default `duration` of 0.5 s and `staggerDelay` of 0.03 s, a 10-word sentence completes in about 0.77 s total. Reach for it when:

- **Section titles and subheadings.** A word-by-word fade on a short heading establishes rhythm without distracting from what comes after.
- **Feature descriptions.** Triggered by scroll, the fade draws the eye through bullet points or card titles as they enter the viewport.
- **Onboarding copy.** Introductory sentences that appear step-by-step as the user progresses through a flow.
- **Captions and labels.** A quiet reveal for secondary text that complements a bolder animated headline.

Because `TextFadeIn` only animates opacity, it is the least visually aggressive of the staggered text components. It is a reliable default when you want motion without commitment to a strong directional statement.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use fade-in when:**

- You need a low-key reveal that does not compete with other animations on the same page.
- The text is short enough that the stagger resolves before the user reads it: roughly 20 words at the default 0.03 s delay finishes in under 1.1 s.
- You want a calmer alternative to [Blur In](/docs/animations/text/blur-in) or [Slide Up](/docs/animations/text/slide-up) for body-adjacent copy.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Long paragraphs or body copy.** A 60-word paragraph at 0.03 s stagger takes nearly 2 seconds to fully fade in. Users will read the fully faded words before the end of the paragraph appears. Either animate the whole block at once (no stagger) or skip animation entirely.
- **Frequently updated text.** Each `children` change resets the component state. If you feed it live data that updates every few seconds, the repeat fades become noise.
- **Per-character on long strings.** A 50-character string with `by="character"` creates 50 spans running in parallel. Prefer `by="word"` for strings over 20 characters, or use [Blur In](/docs/animations/text/blur-in) which handles per-character gracefully for short strings.

## Accessibility notes

The component splits text into per-word or per-character `<motion.span>` elements inside a `<motion.p>`. Screen readers may announce each span individually depending on the browser/AT combination, breaking the natural sentence rhythm.

Add `aria-label` on the `<p>` with the full string so assistive technology reads it as a single phrase:

```tsx
<TextFadeIn
  aria-label="Your ideas, brought to life"
  className="text-2xl font-bold"
>
  Your ideas, brought to life
</TextFadeIn>
```

**Reduced motion.** The component does not check `prefers-reduced-motion` internally. Wrap it to skip the animation for users who prefer reduced motion:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextFadeIn } from "@/components/animations/text/fade-in"

function AccessibleFadeIn({ children, ...props }: { children: string; [key: string]: unknown }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <p {...props}>{children}</p>
  return <TextFadeIn {...props}>{children}</TextFadeIn>
}
```

The initial `opacity: 0` state means text is invisible until the animation fires. If JavaScript is disabled or the component fails to hydrate, the text remains invisible. For critical content, consider starting visible and animating to a highlighted state instead.

## Performance considerations

- **Opacity-only animation.** `TextFadeIn` only animates `opacity`, which runs on the compositor thread with no layout or paint cost. It is the most performant of the staggered text components.
- **DOM node count.** Each unit produces one `<motion.span>`. A 20-word sentence with `by="word"` creates 20 spans; the same string with `by="character"` creates up to 100+ spans. Keep `by="character"` mode for strings under ~25 characters.
- **Single run.** The animation fires once on mount and does not loop. After it completes there is no ongoing compositor work.
- **Stagger math.** Total animation time equals `delay + (units.length - 1) * staggerDelay + duration`. For 15 words: `0 + 14 * 0.03 + 0.5 = 0.92 s`. Keep this sum under 1.2 s for a comfortable page-load experience.

# gradient.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/gradient.mdx

title: Gradient Text
description: Text with animated gradient colors.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextGradient } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/gradient';

## Overview

The `TextGradient` creates smooth animated gradient text effects.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextGradient } from "@/components/animations/text/gradient"

<TextGradient className="text-4xl font-bold">
  Beautiful Gradient Text
</TextGradient>`}
  <TextGradient className="text-4xl font-bold">Beautiful Gradient Text</TextGradient>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-gradient
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-gradient
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-gradient
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-gradient
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/gradient.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface TextGradientProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"p">, "children"> {
  children: string;
  gradient?: string;
  animate?: boolean;
  duration?: number;
}
export function TextGradient({
  children,
  className,
  gradient = "linear-gradient(90deg, #3b82f6, #8b5cf6, #ec4899)",
  animate: shouldAnimate = true,
  duration = 3,
  ...props
}: TextGradientProps) {
  return (
    <motion.p
      className={cn(className)}
      style={{
        backgroundImage: gradient,
        backgroundSize: shouldAnimate ? "200% auto" : "100% auto",
        WebkitBackgroundClip: "text",
        WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent",
        backgroundClip: "text",
      }}
      animate={
        shouldAnimate
          ? {
              backgroundPosition: ["0% center", "200% center"],
            }
          : undefined
      }
      transition={
        shouldAnimate
          ? {
              duration,
              ease: "linear",
              repeat: Infinity,
            }
          : undefined
      }
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.p>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextGradient } from "@/components/animations/text/gradient"

<TextGradient>Gradient Text</TextGradient>
```

## Examples

### Custom Gradients

<PreviewGrid cols={2}>
  <Preview background="dots" code={`<TextGradient gradient="linear-gradient(90deg, #ff0080, #ff8c00, #40e0d0)">Sunset</TextGradient>`}>
    <TextGradient gradient="linear-gradient(90deg, #ff0080, #ff8c00, #40e0d0)" className="text-2xl font-bold">Sunset Colors</TextGradient>
  
  <Preview background="dots" code={`<TextGradient gradient="linear-gradient(90deg, #667eea, #764ba2)">Purple</TextGradient>`}>
    <TextGradient gradient="linear-gradient(90deg, #667eea, #764ba2)" className="text-2xl font-bold">Purple Dream</TextGradient>

### Static Gradient

<Preview background="default" code={`<TextGradient animate={false}>Static</TextGradient>`}>
  <TextGradient animate={false} className="text-3xl font-bold">Static Gradient</TextGradient>

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to display |
| `gradient` | `string` | `"linear-gradient(90deg, #3b82f6, #8b5cf6, #ec4899)"` | CSS gradient |
| `animate` | `boolean` | `true` | Animate the gradient |
| `duration` | `number` | `3` | Animation duration (seconds) |

## Use cases

`TextGradient` applies a CSS gradient to a text element via `background-clip: text` and `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent`. When `animate={true}` (the default), it shifts `backgroundPosition` from `"0% center"` to `"200% center"` on a `repeat: Infinity` loop with `ease: "linear"`, creating a continuous flow across the text. When `animate={false}`, the gradient is static. Reach for it when:

- **Brand headlines.** A vibrant gradient across a 1 to 4 word product name or tagline creates visual identity without a full image or illustration.
- **Pricing or tier names.** A gradient on "Pro" or "Enterprise" draws the eye to a premium tier without overloading the card with decoration.
- **CTA labels.** A gradient inside a button or link text signals an interactive element in design systems that use color as affordance.
- **Decorative display text.** Section numerals, large statistics, or short testimonial pull-quotes where color emphasis is appropriate.

The `gradient` prop accepts any valid CSS `<image>` value, so radial gradients and multi-stop linear gradients work out of the box.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use gradient text when:**

- The string is short (1 to 6 words). Gradient text has lower contrast than a solid color. On long strings the per-letter contrast variation makes reading difficult.
- You are using it on display text at `text-3xl` or larger, where even slightly lower contrast remains legible.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Body copy or paragraph text.** Gradient text reliably fails WCAG contrast requirements at body sizes. Use solid color text for anything users must read continuously.
- **Small text below `text-xl`.** `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent` with a gradient background makes anti-aliasing artifacts more visible at small sizes, reducing legibility.
- **You need the animated shimmer look.** The `backgroundPosition` loop in this component sweeps the whole gradient across the text. For a narrow highlight sweep, use [Shimmer](/docs/animations/text/shimmer) instead, which moves a bright band across a base text color rather than replacing the entire color.
- **Dark backgrounds with light text.** The default gradient (`#3b82f6, #8b5cf6, #ec4899`) is designed for light backgrounds. On a dark background these mid-range colors may have adequate contrast, but test explicitly.

## Accessibility notes

Gradient text uses `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent` with a background image behind the text. This means:

- **The text is still real DOM text** and is readable by screen readers, selectable, and searchable. The gradient is purely visual.
- **Contrast concerns are real.** The gradient may pass contrast at its darkest stop and fail at its lightest. WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Check each stop against your background color. Provide a fallback solid color via `color` CSS:

```tsx
// The text inherits color as a fallback if background-clip is unsupported.
// Set a solid color on the parent that passes contrast on its own.
<TextGradient
  className="text-4xl font-bold text-blue-600"
  gradient="linear-gradient(90deg, #3b82f6, #8b5cf6)"
>
  Gradient Heading
</TextGradient>
```

- **Do not use gradient text alone to convey meaning.** If color is your only signal (e.g., "green = good, pink = warning"), users with color blindness will miss it. Pair with text or icons.
- **Reduced motion.** The continuous `backgroundPosition` loop runs regardless of user preference. Use `animate={false}` for users who have opted out of motion, or check `prefers-reduced-motion`:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextGradient } from "@/components/animations/text/gradient"

function AccessibleGradient({ children, ...props }: { children: string; [key: string]: unknown }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  return <TextGradient animate={!reduced} {...props}>{children}</TextGradient>
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **Continuous animation.** When `animate={true}`, `backgroundPosition` loops forever. This animation is GPU-composited on most browsers because only a property affecting paint (not layout) changes. However, it does require the browser to repaint the text layer on each frame. For a single hero headline this is unnoticeable; for many simultaneous animated gradient texts it accumulates.
- **Use `animate={false}` where motion is not needed.** Static gradient text (sidebar labels, card titles) should set `animate={false}` to eliminate the indefinite loop.
- **`backgroundSize: "200% auto"`.** When animated, the gradient is sized at 200% to allow the sweep. This means the first and last stops in your gradient are rendered off-screen at any given moment. If you only see one color, check that your gradient has enough stops to cover the visible range mid-sweep.

# scramble.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/scramble.mdx

title: Scramble Text
description: Text that decodes from random characters.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextScramble } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/scramble';

## Overview

The `TextScramble` creates a hacker-style text decoding effect.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextScramble } from "@/components/animations/text/scramble"

<TextScramble className="text-3xl font-bold">
  DECODING TEXT
</TextScramble>`}
  <TextScramble className="text-3xl font-bold">DECODING TEXT</TextScramble>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-scramble
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-scramble
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-scramble
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-scramble
        ```
    **Step 1: Copy the hook**

    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-scramble.ts"
    import * as React from "react"

    export interface UseScrambleOptions {
      text?: string
      duration?: number
      delay?: number
      scrambleChars?: string
    }

    export function useScramble(options: UseScrambleOptions): string {
      const {
        text = "",
        duration = 0.8,
        delay = 0,
        scrambleChars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789!@#$%^&*()",
      } = options

      const [displayText, setDisplayText] = React.useState(text)

      React.useEffect(() => {
        const iterations = Math.floor(duration * 60)
        let currentIteration = 0

        const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
          const interval = setInterval(() => {
            if (currentIteration >= iterations) {
              setDisplayText(text)
              clearInterval(interval)
              return
            }

            const progress = currentIteration / iterations
            const newText = text
              .split("")
              .map((char, index) => {
                if (char === " ") return " "
                if (index / text.length < progress) {
                  return char
                }
                return scrambleChars[Math.floor(Math.random() * scrambleChars.length)]
              })
              .join("")

            setDisplayText(newText)
            currentIteration++
          }, (duration * 1000) / iterations)

          return () => clearInterval(interval)
        }, delay * 1000)

        return () => clearTimeout(timeout)
      }, [text, duration, delay, scrambleChars])

      return displayText
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 3: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/scramble.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import { useScramble, type UseScrambleOptions } from "@/lib/use-scramble";
export interface TextScrambleProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"p">, "children">,
    UseScrambleOptions {
  children: string;
}
export function TextScramble({
  children,
  className,
  duration,
  delay,
  scrambleChars,
  ...props
}: TextScrambleProps) {
  const displayText = useScramble({
    text: children,
    duration,
    delay,
    scrambleChars,
  });
  return (
    <motion.p
      className={cn("font-mono", className)}
      initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
      transition={{ duration: 0.2, delay: delay || 0 }}
      {...props}
    >
      {displayText}
    </motion.p>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextScramble } from "@/components/animations/text/scramble"

<TextScramble>Decode Me</TextScramble>
```

## Examples

### Different Speeds

  <Preview background="dots" code={`<TextScramble duration={0.5}>Fast</TextScramble>`}>
    <TextScramble duration={0.5} className="text-xl font-mono">FAST DECODE</TextScramble>
  
  <Preview background="dots" code={`<TextScramble duration={2}>Slow</TextScramble>`}>
    <TextScramble duration={2} className="text-xl font-mono">SLOW DECODE</TextScramble>
</PreviewGrid>

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to decode |
| `duration` | `number` | `1` | Decode duration (seconds) |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Delay before animation |
| `scrambleChars` | `string` | `"!@#$%^&*"` | Characters to use for scrambling |

## Use cases

`TextScramble` uses the `useScramble` hook to run a decoding animation. Internally, the hook calculates `iterations = Math.floor(duration * 60)` frames and schedules them at `duration * 1000 / iterations` ms intervals (roughly 16 ms, or one frame at 60 fps). On each frame, characters to the left of the current progress ratio are already resolved; the rest are randomly replaced from `scrambleChars`. Spaces are preserved. The hook fires once on mount. Reach for it when:

- **Password or code reveal.** Simulating a system "cracking" a code works in hacker/terminal UIs.
- **Loading complete label.** After a process finishes (file upload, compilation), scramble-reveal the completion message for a satisfying effect.
- **Teaser text on hover.** Trigger the scramble on `onMouseEnter` to reveal a button label or product name dramatically.
- **Error code display.** In a dark-themed dashboard or log viewer, scramble-in an error code or ID to reinforce the terminal aesthetic.

The component renders a `<motion.p>` with `font-mono` applied by default, so the scramble resolves in a fixed-width font where substituted characters do not cause layout shifts.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use scramble when:**

- The effect matches the product's personality: technical, cyberpunk, security-focused, or terminal-inspired.
- The text is short. At 30 characters and `duration=0.8`, the animation resolves in about 0.8 s. Long strings take longer to resolve character by character and the readable content is delayed.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Essential information users must read immediately.** A scramble animation delays legibility by design. Error messages, alerts, and success confirmations should be readable the moment they appear. Use [Fade In](/docs/animations/text/fade-in) or a plain static element instead.
- **Body copy or any text longer than a short label.** Reading is impossible during the scramble phase. The effect is appropriate only when the content is revealed as a reward after the user waits.
- **Long strings.** A 60-character string resolves left-to-right, meaning the right half is unreadable for nearly the full duration. Prefer [Typewriter](/docs/animations/text/typewriter) if you need a character-by-character reveal that stays readable as it builds.
- **Frequent updates.** Each `children` change replays the full scramble from the start. If the text updates every few seconds (e.g., a live feed), the repeated scramble becomes noise.

## Accessibility notes

During the scramble phase the displayed text is random characters, not the intended message. Screen readers may announce the scrambled content if the `<p>` is in the normal document flow. To ensure assistive technology announces the final text rather than the scramble noise:

```tsx
<TextScramble
  aria-label="SYSTEM READY"
  className="text-2xl font-mono"
>
  SYSTEM READY
</TextScramble>
```

The `aria-label` is read immediately, while the visual scramble plays out. Never rely solely on the scrambled text to convey information.

**Reduced motion.** The hook runs a frame-by-frame interval regardless of user preference. Wrap the component to skip the scramble and show the final text directly:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextScramble } from "@/components/animations/text/scramble"

function AccessibleScramble({ children, ...props }: { children: string; [key: string]: unknown }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <p className="font-mono" {...props}>{children}</p>
  return <TextScramble {...props}>{children}</TextScramble>
}
```

**`aria-live` caution.** If you place `TextScramble` inside an `aria-live` region, every frame update will trigger an announcement in the live region. Avoid live regions around scrambling text; announce only the final resolved value.

## Performance considerations

- **Frame-rate interval.** The hook runs `setInterval` at approximately 16 ms (1000 ms / 60 iterations for a 1 s duration), producing up to 60 state updates per second via `setDisplayText`. Each update causes a React re-render of the component. This is by design but means the component is a continuous re-render source for its duration.
- **Duration scales iterations.** `iterations = Math.floor(duration * 60)`. A 2 s scramble runs 120 `setDisplayText` calls. Keep `duration` at 0.5 to 1.5 s to limit re-render count.
- **`font-mono` by default.** The component applies `font-mono` to prevent layout shifts as random characters replace each other. Do not remove this class unless your custom font is a monospace face.
- **Only one scramble at a time.** The hook uses a single `setInterval` and `clearInterval` cleanup. Multiple simultaneous `TextScramble` instances each run their own interval. Keep active instances to 1 or 2 on screen at a time.

# shimmer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/shimmer.mdx

title: Shimmer Text
description: Text with smooth gradient shimmer effect.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextShimmer } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/shimmer';

## Overview

The `TextShimmer` creates a smooth gradient shimmer effect using pure CSS for 60fps performance.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextShimmer } from "@/components/animations/text/shimmer"

<TextShimmer className="text-4xl font-bold">
  Shimmer Effect
</TextShimmer>`}
  <TextShimmer className="text-4xl font-bold">Shimmer Effect</TextShimmer>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-shimmer
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-shimmer
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-shimmer
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-shimmer
        ```
    **Step 1: Copy the hook**

    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-shimmer.ts"
    import { type CSSProperties } from "react"

    export interface UseShimmerOptions {
      duration?: number
      colors?: [string, string, string]
    }

    export function useShimmer(options: UseShimmerOptions = {}): CSSProperties {
      const {
        duration = 2.5,
        colors = ["transparent", "rgba(255,255,255,0.8)", "transparent"],
      } = options

      const gradient = `linear-gradient(90deg, ${colors[0]} 0%, ${colors[1]} 50%, ${colors[2]} 100%)`
      const animationName = 'shimmer'

      if (typeof document !== 'undefined') {
        const styleId = 'shimmer-keyframes'
        if (!document.getElementById(styleId)) {
          const style = document.createElement('style')
          style.id = styleId
          style.textContent = `
            @keyframes shimmer {
              0% { background-position: 200% center; }
              100% { background-position: -200% center; }
            }
          `
          document.head.appendChild(style)
        }
      }

      return {
        display: "inline-block",
        backgroundImage: gradient,
        backgroundSize: "200% auto",
        WebkitBackgroundClip: "text",
        WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent",
        backgroundClip: "text",
        animation: `${animationName} ${duration}s linear infinite`,
      }
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 3: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/shimmer.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
import { useShimmer, type UseShimmerOptions } from "@/lib/use-shimmer";
export interface TextShimmerProps
  extends React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLParagraphElement>,
    UseShimmerOptions {
  children: string;
  as?: "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "p" | "span" | "div";
}
export function TextShimmer({
  children,
  className,
  duration,
  colors,
  as: Component = "p",
  ...props
}: TextShimmerProps) {
  const shimmerStyle = useShimmer({
    duration,
    colors: colors || ["transparent", "#3b82f6", "transparent"],
  });
  return (
    <Component style={shimmerStyle} className={cn(className)} {...props}>
      {children}
    </Component>
  );
}

```

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to display |
| `duration` | `number` | `2` | Animation duration (seconds) |
| `colors` | `string[]` | `["transparent", "rgba(255,255,255,0.8)", "transparent"]` | Shimmer colors |
| `as` | `string` | `"p"` | HTML element to render |

## Use cases

`TextShimmer` uses the `useShimmer` hook to inject a CSS `@keyframes shimmer` rule into the document head (once, guarded by a `styleId` check) and applies it via inline `animation`. The shimmer sweeps a bright band defined by the `colors` tuple from `200% center` to `-200% center`, creating a traveling highlight. The default colors are `["transparent", "#3b82f6", "transparent"]` (a blue highlight on a transparent base). Reach for it when:

- **Processing or pending states.** A shimmer on a label like "Analyzing..." or "Generating..." communicates active work without a spinner, keeping the text visible.
- **Premium feature labels.** A shimmer on "Pro" or "AI Powered" adds polish to marketing tiers.
- **Loading skeleton text fallback.** Before real text resolves, shimmer placeholder lines communicate that content is on the way.
- **Decorative headings.** Short display-size headlines in dark themes where a bright traveling highlight suits the aesthetic.

The `as` prop lets you render the shimmer as any heading level (`h1` through `h6`) or inline (`span`) without extra wrapper markup.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use shimmer text when:**

- The animation adds meaning: it signals an ongoing process or a premium state rather than just looking animated.
- The text is short to medium (1 to 10 words). The sweep is most readable when the highlight visually completes a full pass in a perceivable time.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Essential, must-read text.** The `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent` approach renders the text color from the gradient alone. If the gradient colors lack contrast against the background, the text may be difficult or impossible to read during certain phases of the animation cycle. For information users must not miss, use static text.
- **Body copy.** Continuous shimmer on a paragraph is visually tiring and impairs reading. Reserve shimmer for short labels, headings, or decorative strings.
- **Multiple shimmer instances.** Each instance runs its own CSS animation indefinitely. A page with many simultaneous shimmer texts accumulates paint work. If you need a single shimmer across multiple elements, consider a shared CSS class approach instead.
- **Static gradient without motion.** If you want gradient text but not the sweeping animation, use [Gradient](/docs/animations/text/gradient) with `animate={false}`.

## Accessibility notes

The shimmer uses `WebkitTextFillColor: transparent` with `background-clip: text`. The text is real DOM content and screen readers can read it, but contrast is determined by the gradient colors at any given frame, not by a static color value.

**Provide a solid color fallback.** Set a `color` property on the wrapper that meets contrast requirements; it will show if `background-clip` is unsupported or overridden:

```tsx
<TextShimmer
  className="text-3xl font-bold text-blue-600"
  colors={["transparent", "#2563eb", "transparent"]}
>
  Analyzing...
</TextShimmer>
```

**Reduced motion.** The `useShimmer` hook does not check `prefers-reduced-motion`; the CSS `animation` property runs regardless. Detect the preference and skip the shimmer hook output:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextShimmer } from "@/components/animations/text/shimmer"

function AccessibleShimmer({ children, className }: { children: string; className?: string }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <p className={className}>{children}</p>
  return <TextShimmer className={className}>{children}</TextShimmer>
}
```

**`aria-live` considerations.** If the shimmer text is inside an `aria-live` region and the text content changes, the change will be announced. The animation itself is invisible to screen readers; only text changes matter.

**Color alone.** Do not rely on the shimmer highlight color alone to convey status. A shimmer on "Error" in red may be invisible to colorblind users; pair with an icon or label.

## Performance considerations

- **CSS animation, not JavaScript.** The `@keyframes shimmer` rule is injected once and the animation runs entirely in CSS. Unlike the motion-library-based components, this does not create JavaScript frame callbacks per instance. The browser handles the sweep natively.
- **`background-clip: text` repaint.** Despite being CSS-driven, `background-clip: text` requires the browser to repaint the text layer on each animation frame because the background must be composited against the glyph shapes. This is more expensive than a plain `opacity` or `transform` animation.
- **Indefinite loop.** The animation runs `infinite` with `linear` timing. Conditionally render the component (e.g., unmount it when the pending state resolves) rather than hiding it with CSS to stop the animation.
- **Style tag deduplication.** The hook checks for a `<style id="shimmer-keyframes">` element before inserting one. Multiple `TextShimmer` instances on the same page share one `@keyframes` rule.

# slide-up.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/slide-up.mdx

title: Slide Up Text
description: Text that slides up word by word or character by character.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextSlideUp } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/slide-up';

## Overview

The `TextSlideUp` creates a staggered slide-up effect for text.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextSlideUp } from "@/components/animations/text/slide-up"

<TextSlideUp className="text-2xl font-bold">
  This text slides up word by word
</TextSlideUp>`}
  <TextSlideUp className="text-2xl font-bold">This text slides up word by word</TextSlideUp>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-slide-up
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-slide-up
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-slide-up
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-slide-up
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/slide-up.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface TextSlideUpProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"p">, "children"> {
  children: string;
  duration?: number;
  delay?: number;
  by?: "character" | "word";
  staggerDelay?: number;
  distance?: number;
}
export function TextSlideUp({
  children,
  className,
  duration = 0.5,
  delay = 0,
  by = "word",
  staggerDelay = 0.03,
  distance = 20,
  ...props
}: TextSlideUpProps) {
  const units = by === "word" ? children.split(" ") : children.split("");
  return (
    <motion.p className={cn(className)} {...props}>
      {units.map((unit, index) => (
        <motion.span
          key={index}
          initial={{ opacity: 0, y: distance }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
          transition={{
            duration,
            delay: delay + index * staggerDelay,
          }}
          style={{ display: "inline-block" }}
        >
          {unit}
          {by === "word" && index < units.length - 1 && "\u00A0"}
        </motion.span>
      ))}
    </motion.p>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextSlideUp } from "@/components/animations/text/slide-up"

<TextSlideUp>Hello World</TextSlideUp>
```

## Examples

### By Character

<Preview background="dots" code={`<TextSlideUp by="character">Character animation</TextSlideUp>`}>
  <TextSlideUp by="character" className="text-xl">Character by character slide</TextSlideUp>

### Custom Distance

<PreviewGrid cols={2}>
  <Preview background="default" code={`<TextSlideUp distance={10}>Small</TextSlideUp>`}>
    <TextSlideUp distance={10} className="text-lg">Small slide distance</TextSlideUp>
  
  <Preview background="default" code={`<TextSlideUp distance={40}>Large</TextSlideUp>`}>
    <TextSlideUp distance={40} className="text-lg">Large slide distance</TextSlideUp>
</PreviewGrid>

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to animate |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation duration (seconds) |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Initial delay |
| `by` | `"word" \| "character"` | `"word"` | Animation unit |
| `staggerDelay` | `number` | `0.03` | Delay between units |
| `distance` | `number` | `20` | Slide distance (pixels) |

## Use cases

`TextSlideUp` animates each word or character from `opacity: 0, y: distance` (default `20` px) to `opacity: 1, y: 0` in a staggered sequence. The default `by="word"` splits on spaces; `by="character"` splits on every character. With the defaults, a 10-word headline completes in `0 + 9 * 0.03 + 0.5 = 0.77 s`. Reach for it when:

- **Hero section titles.** A word-by-word upward entry on a headline is one of the most legible text reveal patterns, because each word is fully visible once it completes.
- **Scroll-triggered section headings.** Entering from below on scroll is a conventional, expected motion pattern that does not surprise or disorient users.
- **Card or panel titles.** A subtle stagger on a short 2 to 4 word title adds hierarchy without heavy animation.
- **Animated statistics.** The slide-up pairs naturally with a number counter: the label slides up while the counter increments.

The `distance` prop lets you tune the entry from a subtle nudge (`distance={8}`) to a more theatrical entrance (`distance={40}`).

## When to use / when not to use

**Use slide-up when:**

- You want a directional entrance that feels natural on most content: text entering from below is a spatial metaphor for "coming up" into view.
- The string is short enough that the stagger completes before the user needs to act on the content.
- You want a slightly more directional alternative to [Fade In](/docs/animations/text/fade-in), which is purely opacity.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Long paragraphs.** Same rule as fade-in: a 50-word paragraph at 0.03 s stagger takes nearly 2 seconds to complete. Users will read the start before the end appears, creating a disjointed experience. Use no animation or a single uniform fade on the whole block.
- **Navigation or interactive elements.** Animating menu items or buttons on every page load adds latency to interaction. Reserve text animations for read-only display text.
- **Per-character on long strings.** A 40-character string with `by="character"` and `staggerDelay={0.03}` takes over 1.7 s to complete. Prefer `by="word"` for anything over ~15 characters.
- **You want a purely atmospheric entrance** without spatial movement. Use [Blur In](/docs/animations/text/blur-in) for a softer focus-in effect or [Fade In](/docs/animations/text/fade-in) for no direction at all.

## Accessibility notes

The component splits text into per-word or per-character `<motion.span>` elements inside a `<motion.p>`. Provide `aria-label` on the wrapper to ensure screen readers announce the full sentence as one unit rather than individual spans:

```tsx
<TextSlideUp
  aria-label="Ship products faster than ever"
  className="text-4xl font-bold"
>
  Ship products faster than ever
</TextSlideUp>
```

**Reduced motion.** The component animates both `opacity` and `y`, so it moves text across the screen. This is a translational motion and may trigger discomfort for users with vestibular sensitivities. Wrap to skip the animation:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextSlideUp } from "@/components/animations/text/slide-up"

function AccessibleSlideUp({ children, ...props }: { children: string; [key: string]: unknown }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <p {...props}>{children}</p>
  return <TextSlideUp {...props}>{children}</TextSlideUp>
}
```

**Invisible initial state.** `opacity: 0` on mount means text is hidden until JavaScript hydrates and runs the animation. For essential page content (headings, body copy), this is a risk: if the hydration is delayed or JavaScript fails, users see nothing. Consider progressive enhancement patterns where the initial server-rendered state is visible.

## Performance considerations

- **Translate + opacity.** `TextSlideUp` animates `y` (a CSS `transform`) and `opacity`. Both run on the compositor thread without layout or paint, making this the most GPU-friendly of the staggered text components alongside [Fade In](/docs/animations/text/fade-in).
- **Per-span nodes.** One `<motion.span>` per unit. Keep total span count under 30 to avoid registering too many motion observers simultaneously.
- **Single-shot.** The animation fires once on mount; `animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}` with no repeat. No ongoing compositor cost after completion.
- **`overflow-hidden` if needed.** The initial `y: distance` pushes text below its final position, which can cause a brief overflow flash on the parent element. Wrap in `overflow-hidden` if the text lives near a container edge.

## Customization examples

### Subtle nudge for a card title

```tsx
import { TextSlideUp } from "@/components/animations/text/slide-up"

<TextSlideUp
```

# split-reveal.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/split-reveal.mdx

title: Split Reveal Text
description: Text that reveals with a vertical split effect.

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { TextSplitReveal } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/split-reveal';

## Overview

The `TextSplitReveal` reveals text with a dramatic vertical split effect.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { TextSplitReveal } from "@/components/animations/text/split-reveal"

<TextSplitReveal className="text-4xl font-bold">
  SPLIT REVEAL
</TextSplitReveal>`}
  <TextSplitReveal className="text-4xl font-bold">SPLIT REVEAL</TextSplitReveal>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-split-reveal
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-split-reveal
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-split-reveal
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-split-reveal
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/split-reveal.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
export interface TextSplitRevealProps
  extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"p">, "children"> {
  children: string;
  duration?: number;
  delay?: number;
  staggerDelay?: number;
}
export function TextSplitReveal({
  children,
  className,
  duration = 0.6,
  delay = 0,
  staggerDelay = 0.1,
  ...props
}: TextSplitRevealProps) {
  const midpoint = Math.ceil(children.length / 2);
  const leftHalf = children.slice(0, midpoint);
  const rightHalf = children.slice(midpoint);
  return (
    <motion.p className={cn("overflow-hidden", className)} {...props}>
      <motion.span
        className="inline-block"
        initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20, clipPath: "inset(0 100% 0 0)" }}
        animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)" }}
        transition={{
          duration,
          delay,
          ease: "easeOut",
        }}
      >
        {leftHalf}
      </motion.span>
      <motion.span
        className="inline-block"
        initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20, clipPath: "inset(0 0 0 100%)" }}
        animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, clipPath: "inset(0 0 0 0%)" }}
        transition={{
          duration,
          delay: delay + staggerDelay,
          ease: "easeOut",
        }}
      >
        {rightHalf}
      </motion.span>
    </motion.p>
  );
}

```

## Usage

```tsx
import { TextSplitReveal } from "@/components/animations/text/split-reveal"

<TextSplitReveal>Split Text</TextSplitReveal>
```

## Examples

### Different Timings

<PreviewGrid cols={2}>
  <Preview background="dots" code={`<TextSplitReveal staggerDelay={0.05}>Fast</TextSplitReveal>`}>
    <TextSplitReveal staggerDelay={0.05} className="text-2xl font-bold">FAST SPLIT</TextSplitReveal>
  
  <Preview background="dots" code={`<TextSplitReveal staggerDelay={0.3}>Slow</TextSplitReveal>`}>
    <TextSplitReveal staggerDelay={0.3} className="text-2xl font-bold">SLOW SPLIT</TextSplitReveal>
</PreviewGrid>

### Hero Text

<Preview background="gradient" code={`<TextSplitReveal>HERO TITLE</TextSplitReveal>`}>
  <TextSplitReveal className="text-5xl font-black text-white">HERO TITLE</TextSplitReveal>

## Props

| `children` | `string` | Required | Text to reveal |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.6` | Animation duration (seconds) |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Initial delay |
| `staggerDelay` | `number` | `0.1` | Delay between halves |

## Use cases

`TextSplitReveal` splits the string at `Math.ceil(children.length / 2)` and animates each half independently. The left half enters from the left using `clipPath: "inset(0 100% 0 0)"` (fully clipped on the right) to `clipPath: "inset(0 0% 0 0)"`, while the right half mirrors this from the right. Both halves also fade in (`opacity: 0 to 1`) and slide up (`y: 20 to 0`). The right half is delayed by `staggerDelay` (default `0.1 s`). Reach for it when:

- **Short, bold hero headlines.** "SPLIT REVEAL" or "SHIP FASTER" benefit from the theatrical two-part entry, which gives the impression of the text assembling itself.
- **Full-screen splash screens.** The clean left-right split suits product name reveals in dark or full-bleed landing sections.
- **Section dividers with a single strong word.** A numbered section title like "01. DESIGN" can split dramatically to open the section.
- **Call-to-action phrases.** A punchy 2 to 4 word CTA label entering as two assembling halves draws attention without competing with the button it sits above.

Because only two spans are ever created (not one per character), `TextSplitReveal` is the cheapest of the character-level reveal effects in terms of DOM node count.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use split-reveal when:**

- The string length is even or odd: the `Math.ceil` split handles both gracefully, though the two halves may differ by one character.
- The text is a single short phrase (2 to 6 words). The effect reads as one unified reveal. Longer text produces longer halves that clip slowly and feel unfinished.
- You want maximum impact with minimum DOM overhead.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Sentences longer than 5 or 6 words.** At that length the two-half split becomes arbitrary and the clip animation takes too long to complete gracefully.
- **Text that wraps to multiple lines.** The split is calculated on the raw character string, not the visual rendering. A long headline that wraps may split mid-word across lines, producing a misaligned visual result.
- **You need word-by-word stagger.** This component always produces exactly two animated spans. For per-word timing, use [Slide Up](/docs/animations/text/slide-up) or [Fade In](/docs/animations/text/fade-in) with `by="word"`.
- **Lowercase or mixed-case editorial text.** The split-reveal aesthetic reads best on uppercase or title-case display text. On sentence-case body copy the two halves look like a rendering artifact rather than an intentional effect.

## Accessibility notes

The text is split into two `<motion.span>` elements rendered inside a `<motion.p>`. The split is at the character level of the raw string. Screen readers will read both spans in order, and the result is usually correct, but add `aria-label` on the `<p>` to guarantee the full string is announced as a single unit:

```tsx
<TextSplitReveal
  aria-label="HERO TITLE"
  className="text-5xl font-black"
>
  HERO TITLE
</TextSplitReveal>
```

**Reduced motion.** The animation combines `clipPath`, `opacity`, and `y`. The `clipPath` change is a paint operation and may not be appropriate for users with vestibular sensitivity. Wrap to skip it:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { TextSplitReveal } from "@/components/animations/text/split-reveal"

function AccessibleSplitReveal({ children, ...props }: { children: string; [key: string]: unknown }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) return <p {...props}>{children}</p>
  return <TextSplitReveal {...props}>{children}</TextSplitReveal>
}
```

**`overflow-hidden` on the parent.** The `<motion.p>` has `overflow-hidden` applied by default (via `cn("overflow-hidden", className)`). This clips the translating halves during entry. If you apply the component inside a container that also clips, verify that the clipping does not truncate the final state.

## Performance considerations

- **Two spans total.** Unlike per-word or per-character components, `TextSplitReveal` creates exactly two `<motion.span>` elements regardless of text length. This is the lowest DOM overhead of any staggered text component.
- **`clipPath` animation cost.** `clipPath: "inset()"` transitions require a paint on each frame because the browser must re-clip the text layer. This is more expensive than a pure transform/opacity change. On a single hero element the cost is imperceptible. Do not use on many simultaneously animating instances.
- **Combined `opacity + y + clipPath`.** All three properties change at once. The `y` translation is GPU-composited, but the `clipPath` forces a paint. This is acceptable for a one-shot entry animation.
- **Single-shot.** Like all the staggered text components, the animation fires once on mount and does not loop.

# svg-text-draw.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/animations/text/svg-text-draw.mdx

title: SVG Text Draw
description: SVG path drawing animation that reveals text letter by letter with stroke animation.
secondary: "#60A5FA"

import { Preview, PreviewGrid } from '@/components/preview';
import { SvgTextDraw } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/text/svg-text-draw';

## Overview

The `SvgTextDraw` component creates a smooth SVG drawing animation where each letter is drawn stroke-by-stroke using SVG path animations, similar to handwriting or signature effects.

## Preview

  background="default"
  code={`import { SvgTextDraw } from "@/components/animations/text/svg-text-draw"

<SvgTextDraw className="text-4xl font-semibold">
  hello world
</SvgTextDraw>`}
  <SvgTextDraw className="text-4xl font-semibold">hello world</SvgTextDraw>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-svg-text-draw
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-svg-text-draw
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-svg-text-draw
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/text-svg-text-draw
        ```
    **Step 1: Add the utility**

    ```tsx title="lib/utils.ts"
    import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx"
    import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

    export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
      return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
    }
    ```

    **Step 2: Copy the component**

    ```tsx title="components/animations/text/svg-text-draw.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
import { motion, SVGMotionProps } from "motion/react";
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

export interface SvgTextDrawProps extends Omit<SVGMotionProps<SVGSVGElement>, "children"> {
  children: string;
  delay?: number;
  speed?: number;
  className?: string;
}

// Simple letter path definitions (lowercase letters)
const letterPaths: Record<string, string> = {
  a: "M 10 30 Q 10 10, 25 10 Q 40 10, 40 25 Q 40 40, 25 40 Q 15 40, 10 35 M 40 10 L 40 40",
  b: "M 10 0 L 10 40 M 10 20 Q 10 10, 20 10 Q 30 10, 30 25 Q 30 40, 20 40 Q 10 40, 10 35",
  c: "M 35 15 Q 30 10, 20 10 Q 10 10, 10 25 Q 10 40, 20 40 Q 30 40, 35 35",
  d: "M 40 0 L 40 40 M 40 10 Q 40 10, 25 10 Q 10 10, 10 25 Q 10 40, 25 40 Q 40 40, 40 35",
  e: "M 35 25 L 10 25 Q 10 10, 25 10 Q 40 10, 40 25 Q 40 40, 25 40 Q 10 40, 10 35",
  f: "M 30 5 Q 25 0, 20 0 M 20 0 L 20 40 M 10 15 L 30 15",
  g: "M 40 10 Q 40 10, 25 10 Q 10 10, 10 25 Q 10 40, 25 40 Q 40 40, 40 30 L 40 45 Q 40 50, 25 50",
  h: "M 10 0 L 10 40 M 10 20 Q 10 10, 20 10 Q 30 10, 30 20 L 30 40",
  i: "M 20 5 L 20 8 M 20 15 L 20 40",
  j: "M 25 5 L 25 8 M 25 15 L 25 40 Q 25 50, 15 50",
  k: "M 10 0 L 10 40 M 30 15 L 10 25 L 30 40",
  l: "M 20 0 L 20 40",
  m: "M 10 40 L 10 10 Q 10 10, 17 10 Q 24 10, 24 17 L 24 40 M 24 10 Q 24 10, 31 10 Q 38 10, 38 17 L 38 40",
  n: "M 10 40 L 10 10 Q 10 10, 20 10 Q 30 10, 30 20 L 30 40",
  o: "M 25 10 Q 10 10, 10 25 Q 10 40, 25 40 Q 40 40, 40 25 Q 40 10, 25 10",
  p: "M 10 50 L 10 10 Q 10 10, 20 10 Q 30 10, 30 25 Q 30 40, 20 40 Q 10 40, 10 35",
  q: "M 40 10 Q 40 10, 25 10 Q 10 10, 10 25 Q 10 40, 25 40 Q 40 40, 40 35 L 40 50",
  r: "M 10 40 L 10 10 Q 10 10, 20 10 Q 30 10, 30 15",
  s: "M 35 15 Q 30 10, 20 10 Q 10 10, 10 17 Q 10 25, 30 25 Q 40 25, 40 33 Q 40 40, 20 40 Q 10 40, 10 35",
  t: "M 20 5 L 20 35 Q 20 40, 25 40 M 10 15 L 30 15",
  u: "M 10 10 L 10 30 Q 10 40, 20 40 Q 30 40, 30 30 L 30 10",
  v: "M 10 10 L 20 40 L 30 10",
  w: "M 10 10 L 15 40 L 25 10 L 30 40 L 35 10",
  x: "M 10 10 L 30 40 M 30 10 L 10 40",
  y: "M 10 10 L 20 30 L 30 10 M 20 30 L 20 45 Q 20 50, 10 50",
  z: "M 10 10 L 30 10 L 10 40 L 30 40",
  " ": "",
};

const letterWidth = 50; // Width allocated for each letter

export function SvgTextDraw({
  children,
  className,
  delay = 0,
  speed = 1,
  ...props
}: SvgTextDrawProps) {
  // Convert children to string and lowercase
  const text = String(children).toLowerCase();
  const totalWidth = text.length * letterWidth;

  const calc = (x: number) => x * speed;

  return (
    <motion.svg
      className={cn("h-12", className)}
      xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
      viewBox={`0 0 ${totalWidth} 60`}
      fill="none"
      stroke="currentColor"
      strokeWidth="3"
      strokeLinecap="round"
      strokeLinejoin="round"
      initial={{ opacity: 1 }}
      animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
      {...props}
    >
      <title>{children}</title>
      {text.split("").map((char, index) => {
        const path = letterPaths[char] || "";
        if (!path) return null;

        const xOffset = index * letterWidth;
        const charDelay = delay + index * 0.15 * speed;

        return (
          <motion.path
            key={`${char}-${index}`}
            d={path}
            transform={`translate(${xOffset}, 0)`}
            initial={{ pathLength: 0, opacity: 0 }}
            animate={{ pathLength: 1, opacity: 1 }}
            transition={{
              pathLength: {
                duration: calc(0.5),
                ease: "easeInOut",
                delay: calc(charDelay),
              },
              opacity: {
                duration: calc(0.3),
                delay: calc(charDelay),
              },
            }}
          />
        );
      })}
    </motion.svg>
  );
}

```


## Props

## Styling Tips

Adjust the height to scale the text:

```tsx
<SvgTextDraw className="h-16">
  larger text
</SvgTextDraw>
```

Change stroke color:

```tsx
<SvgTextDraw className="h-12 text-blue-500">
  colored text
</SvgTextDraw>
```

Use with gradients:

