# press.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/press.mdx

title: usePress
description: Press-down feedback animation for interactive elements providing tactile feedback.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `usePress` hook adds a press-down effect when clicking or tapping elements, providing tactile feedback. Perfect for buttons, cards, and any interactive element that needs visual confirmation of user interaction.

<Callout type="info">
  **Tactile Feedback:** This hook uses `whileTap` to provide immediate visual feedback, making your UI feel more responsive and interactive.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-press
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-press
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-press
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-press
        ```
    Copy and paste the hook code into your project:

    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-press.ts"
import { type MotionProps, type Easing } from "motion/react";

export interface UsePressOptions {
  pressScale?: number;

  duration?: number;

  ease?: Easing | Easing[];

  addRotation?: boolean;

  rotationAmount?: number;
}

export function usePress(options: UsePressOptions = {}): MotionProps {
  const {
    pressScale = 0.95,
    duration = 0.1,
    ease = "easeInOut",
    addRotation = false,
    rotationAmount = 2,
  } = options;

  return {
    whileTap: {
      scale: pressScale,
      rotate: addRotation ? rotationAmount : 0,
    },
    transition: {
      duration,
      ease,
    },
  };
}

```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"

      className="inline-flex h-11 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-6 text-sm font-semibold text-white"
    >
      Click me
    </motion.button>
  )
}
```

- `transition` - Animation transition config

## Composing with Other Hooks

Combine with hover effects for rich interactions:

```tsx
import { usePress } from "@/lib/hooks/use-press"
import { useHoverLift } from "@/lib/hooks/use-hover-lift"

export function RichButton() {
  const press = usePress({ pressScale: 0.92 })
  const lift = useHoverLift({ liftDistance: 6 })
  
  // Merge the animations
  const combined = {
    ...lift,
    ...press,
  }
  
  return (
    <motion.button {...combined} className="btn">
      Hover + Press
    </motion.button>
  )
}
```

## Use cases

`usePress` returns `MotionProps` with a `whileTap` object (containing `scale` and `rotate`) and a `transition` object. Spread the props onto any `motion.*` element and the element will compress when clicked or tapped, then spring back.

- **Primary and secondary action buttons.** Every click deserves a physical response. A `motion.button` with `usePress()` at the default `pressScale: 0.95` gives every submit, confirm, or cancel button a tactile click feel.
- **Icon-only toolbar buttons.** Tight icon buttons (share, like, bookmark) benefit from `pressScale: 0.9` so the scale change is noticeable on a small target.
- **Clickable cards.** A card that navigates on click can use `pressScale: 0.98` for a barely-there press that signals interactivity without making the card feel fragile.
- **Image thumbnails in a gallery.** A `motion.img` or `motion.button` wrapping a thumbnail with `usePress({ pressScale: 0.96 })` lets the user know the image responds to their tap before a lightbox opens.
- **Chip and tag filters.** Toggle chips with `usePress({ pressScale: 0.92, addRotation: true, rotationAmount: 2 })` make filter selection feel playful.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `usePress` directly when:**

- You need the press effect on a custom element, not a prebuilt component.
- You want to compose the press with [useHoverLift](/docs/hooks/hover-lift): since both return plain `MotionProps`, you can spread them both onto the same `motion.button` and the `whileHover` and `whileTap` props do not conflict.
- You need `addRotation: true` for a playful icon button where a tiny twist on press adds personality.

**Reach for the prebuilt component when:**

- You just need a standard styled button with a press effect and no custom host element.

**Avoid `usePress` when:**

- The element is a text input, textarea, or select. Users hold these down to select text, and a scale-down during the hold will distort the text cursor position.
- The element is a drag handle. `whileTap` fires immediately on pointer down, and scaling the handle while dragging can shift the drag origin.
- The press scale would be applied to a layout container that holds many children; scaling the container changes all children's apparent positions and can cause visual glitches.

## Accessibility notes

`usePress` uses `whileTap`, which fires on `pointerdown` and ends on `pointerup` or `pointercancel`. This works for mouse clicks, touch taps, and stylus presses. It does not fire on keyboard Enter or Space.

- **Keyboard users.** Pressing Enter or Space on a `<button>` triggers the button's `click` event but does not trigger `whileTap`. The visual press animation is absent for keyboard users. This is acceptable as long as the button has a visible `:focus-visible` ring that communicates focus.
- **Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.** A fast scale change (default `0.1s`) is unlikely to cause vestibular issues, but best practice is to honor the setting:

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { usePress } from "@/lib/use-press"

export function ActionButton({ children, onClick }: { children: React.ReactNode; onClick: () => void }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const pressProps = usePress({ pressScale: 0.95 })

  return (
    <motion.button
      onClick={onClick}
      {...(reduced ? {} : pressProps)}
      className="rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-6 py-2.5 text-sm font-semibold text-white focus-visible:outline focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-blue-500"
    >
      {children}
    </motion.button>
  )
}
```

- If using `addRotation: true`, keep `rotationAmount` small (1 to 3 degrees). Larger rotations on buttons can make them appear broken to users who are not expecting the effect.

## Performance considerations

- `usePress` uses `whileTap` and animates only `scale` (and optionally `rotate`). Both are transforms and run on the compositor with no layout or paint.
- The default `duration: 0.1s` means the animation completes in 6 frames at 60fps. The total compositor cost is minimal.
- Because the hook returns a plain `MotionProps` object, it is reconstructed on every render of the calling component. If the parent re-renders often, pass a stable options object (or call `usePress` outside of frequently-rendered components).
- For elements that receive very rapid clicks (double-click actions, spam-clicking), Framer Motion interrupts and reverses the current animation immediately when a new press starts. This is handled gracefully and does not cause visual glitches.

## Real-world examples

### Submit button that disables while loading

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { usePress } from "@/lib/use-press"

export function SubmitButton() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  const pressProps = usePress({ pressScale: 0.95 })

  async function handleSubmit() {
    setLoading(true)
    try {
      await submitForm()
    } finally {
      setLoading(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <motion.button
      onClick={handleSubmit}
      disabled={loading}
      {...(loading ? {} : pressProps)}
      className="flex h-11 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-xl bg-blue-600 px-8 text-sm font-semibold text-white disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60"
    >
      {loading ? "Saving..." : "Save changes"}
    </motion.button>
  )
}
```

### Keyboard shortcut chip with press feedback

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { usePress } from "@/lib/use-press"

export function ShortcutChip({ keys, label, onActivate }: { keys: string; label: string; onActivate: () => void }) {

  return (
    <motion.button
      onClick={onActivate}
      {...pressProps}
      aria-label={label}
      className="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-md border border-neutral-200 bg-neutral-50 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-mono text-neutral-600 dark:border-neutral-700 dark:bg-neutral-800 dark:text-neutral-400"
    >
      {keys}
    </motion.button>
  )
}
```

# pulse.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/pulse.mdx

title: usePulse
description: Continuous pulsing animation for attention-grabbing elements like notifications and badges.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `usePulse` hook creates a continuous pulsing animation, perfect for notifications, badges, or drawing attention to important elements. The animation loops infinitely with smooth easing.

<Callout type="info">
  **Attention-grabbing:** Use pulse animations sparingly for truly important elements to avoid overwhelming users.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-pulse
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-pulse
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-pulse
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-pulse
        ```
    Copy and paste the hook code into your project:

    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-pulse.ts"
import { type MotionProps, type Easing } from "motion/react";

export interface UsePulseOptions {
  scaleFrom?: number;

  scaleTo?: number;

  duration?: number;

  ease?: Easing | Easing[];

  repeat?: number;

  delay?: number;
}

export function usePulse(options: UsePulseOptions = {}): MotionProps {
  const {
    scaleFrom = 1,
    scaleTo = 1.05,
    duration = 1,
    ease = "easeInOut",
    repeat = Infinity,
    delay = 0,
  } = options;

  return {
    animate: {
      scale: [scaleFrom, scaleTo, scaleFrom],
    },
    transition: {
      duration,
      ease,
      repeat,
      delay,
    },
  };
}

```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx
  )
}
```

    ```tsx
        <motion.div 
          {...pulseProps}
          className={`w-3 h-3 rounded-full ${
            status === 'online' ? 'bg-green-500' : 'bg-gray-400'
          }`}
        />
      )
    }
    ```

## API Reference

### Options

<div className="overflow-x-auto">
  <table className="w-full">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th>Option</th>
        <th>Type</th>
        <th>Default</th>
        <th>Description</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td>`scaleFrom`</td>
        <td>`number`</td>
        <td>`1`</td>
        <td>Minimum scale (starting point)</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>`scaleTo`</td>
        <td>`number`</td>
        <td>`1.05`</td>
        <td>Maximum scale (peak of pulse)</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>`duration`</td>
        <td>`number`</td>
        <td>`1`</td>
        <td>Duration for one complete pulse cycle in seconds</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>`ease`</td>
        <td>`string \| number[]`</td>
        <td>`"easeInOut"`</td>
        <td>Animation easing function</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>`repeat`</td>
        <td>`number`</td>
        <td>`Infinity`</td>
        <td>Number of times to repeat (Infinity for continuous)</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
        <td>`delay`</td>
        <td>`number`</td>
        <td>`0`</td>
        <td>Delay before animation starts in seconds</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>

### Returns

Returns `MotionProps` object containing:
- `animate` - Animation keyframes for continuous pulsing
- `transition` - Animation transition config with repeat

### Subtle Pulse

```tsx
  duration: 2,
})
```

### Strong Pulse

```tsx

  duration: 0.6,
})
```

### Slow Breathing

```tsx

  duration: 3,
})
```

### Limited Pulses

```tsx

  scaleTo: 1.1,
  duration: 1,
  repeat: 3,  // Pulse only 3 times
})
```

### Delayed Start

```tsx
const pulseProps = usePulse({
  scaleTo: 1.08,
  duration: 1.5,
  delay: 1,  // Wait 1 second before starting
})
```

## Use cases

`usePulse` returns `MotionProps` with an `animate` object that cycles `scale` through `[scaleFrom, scaleTo, scaleFrom]` (defaults: `[1, 1.05, 1]`) and a `transition` with `repeat: Infinity`. Spread the props onto any `motion.*` element.

- **Notification badges and unread counters.** A small `motion.span` badge that pulses at `scaleTo: 1.12` and `duration: 1` draws the eye to new activity without flashing or changing color.
- **Online / live status dots.** A green dot with `scaleTo: 1.3` and `duration: 1.2` communicates "active now" the same way a blinking cursor communicates typing.
- **CTA buttons awaiting user action.** A hero button that has not been clicked can pulse gently at `scaleTo: 1.03` and `duration: 2` to invite interaction without being aggressive.
- **Alert and warning icons.** A warning icon that pulses at `scaleTo: 1.15` during an error state amplifies urgency beyond static color alone.
- **Recording or live broadcast indicators.** A red circle with a slow `duration: 0.8` pulse communicates "currently recording" in video or audio interfaces.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `usePulse` directly when:**

- You need the pulse effect on a custom element that is not a standard badge or button.
- You want `repeat: N` for a finite pulse (for example, three pulses after a successful action) rather than an infinite loop.
- You want to `delay` the pulse to start after another animation completes (for example, a `useFadeIn` entrance followed by a pulse).

**Avoid `usePulse` when:**

- More than two or three elements on the same view pulse simultaneously. Multiple concurrent pulses compete for attention and diminish the effect of all of them.
- The element is large, such as a full-width banner or hero section. A scale change on a large element causes significant layout reflow for nearby content unless the element is positioned absolutely.
- The information communicated by the pulse is critical. A pulse is easy to miss. Pair it with text ("3 unread"), color, or ARIA live regions to ensure the information reaches all users.

## Accessibility notes

`usePulse` animates `scale` via `animate` with `repeat: Infinity`. The animation starts immediately on mount and runs until the element unmounts.

- Continuous scale animation is among the motion patterns most likely to be distracting or to cause symptoms for users with vestibular or attention disorders. Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` by returning no animation props:

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { usePulse } from "@/lib/use-pulse"

export function LiveDot() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const pulseProps = usePulse({ scaleTo: 1.3, duration: 1 })

  return (
    <motion.span
      {...(reduced ? {} : pulseProps)}
      className="inline-block h-2.5 w-2.5 rounded-full bg-green-500"
      aria-label="Online"
    />
  )
}
```

- Do not convey meaning through the pulse animation alone. Pair it with text, a color, or an accessible label so screen reader users and reduced-motion users receive the same information.
- If you mount the element conditionally based on a state change (for example, only when unread count > 0), the `animate` loop starts fresh on mount. Unmounting the component when the state clears is cleaner than setting `repeat: 0` after mount.

## Performance considerations

- `usePulse` animates only `scale`, which is a transform. The animation runs on the compositor thread with no layout or paint cost.
- `repeat: Infinity` keeps the compositor busy indefinitely. Conditionally mount the element (e.g., `{unread > 0 && <motion.span {...pulseProps}>...}`) so the compositor is freed when the state clears, rather than hiding it with `opacity: 0` while the animation continues.
- `scaleFrom` and `scaleTo` are close to `1` by default (`1` and `1.05`). This keeps the composited layer small. Larger `scaleTo` values (above `1.2`) expand the composited layer's bounding box and may clip neighboring elements if the container has `overflow: hidden`.
- For staggered badge pulses, use the `delay` option rather than mounting multiple instances of the hook to avoid all badges scaling in lockstep.

# scale-in.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/scale-in.mdx

title: useScaleIn
description: Scale up entrance animation with fade for smooth element reveals.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `useScaleIn` hook creates a scale-up entrance animation with optional fade. Elements start small and scale to full size, perfect for modals, cards, and attention-grabbing entrances.

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scale-in
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scale-in
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scale-in
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scale-in
        ```
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-scale-in.ts"
import { type MotionProps, type Easing } from "motion/react";

export interface UseScaleInOptions {
  duration?: number;

  delay?: number;

  from?: number;

  to?: number;

  initialOpacity?: number;

  ease?: Easing | Easing[];

  viewport?: "once" | "always";
}

export function useScaleIn(options: UseScaleInOptions = {}): MotionProps {
  const {
    duration = 0.5,
    delay = 0,
    from = 0.8,
    to = 1,
    initialOpacity = 0,
    ease = "easeOut",
    viewport = "once",
  } = options;

  return {
    initial: {
      scale: from,
      opacity: initialOpacity,
    },
    whileInView: {
      scale: to,
      opacity: 1,
    },
    viewport: {
      once: viewport === "once",
    },
    transition: {
      duration,
      delay,
      ease,
    },
  };
}

```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useScaleIn } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scale-in"

export function Card() {
  const scaleProps = useScaleIn()
  
  return (
    <motion.div {...scaleProps} className="card">
      <h3>Scales in on view</h3>
      <p>Content appears smoothly</p>
    </motion.div>
  )
}
```

### Modal Entrance

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useScaleIn } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scale-in"

export function Modal({ isOpen }: { isOpen: boolean }) {
  const scaleProps = useScaleIn({ 
    from: 0.5,
    duration: 0.3 
  })
  
  if (!isOpen) return null
  
  return (
    <motion.div {...scaleProps} className="modal">
      <h2>Modal Title</h2>
      <p>Modal content</p>
    </motion.div>
  )
}
```

### Staggered Grid

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useScaleIn } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scale-in"

export function ProductGrid({ products }) {
  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
      {products.map((product, index) => {
        const scaleProps = useScaleIn({ 
          delay: index * 0.1  // Stagger effect
        })
        
        return (
          <motion.div key={product.id} {...scaleProps}>
            <img src={product.image} alt={product.name} />
            <h3>{product.name}</h3>
          </motion.div>
        )
      })}
    </div>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `duration` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation duration in seconds |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Delay before animation starts |
| `from` | `number` | `0.8` | Initial scale (0 = invisible, 1 = normal) |
| `to` | `number` | `1` | Final scale |
| `initialOpacity` | `number` | `0` | Initial opacity (0-1) |
| `ease` | `string \| number[]` | `"easeOut"` | Animation easing |
| `viewport` | `"once" \| "always"` | `"once"` | Animate once or every time in view |

## Examples

### Dramatic Entrance

```tsx
const scaleProps = useScaleIn({
  from: 0,
  duration: 0.6,
})
```

### Subtle Scale

```tsx
const scaleProps = useScaleIn({
  from: 0.95,
  duration: 0.3,
})
```

### Pop Effect

```tsx
const scaleProps = useScaleIn({
  from: 0.5,
  to: 1.05,  // Slightly overshoot
  duration: 0.4,
  ease: [0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55],  // Bounce easing
})
```

## Use cases

`useScaleIn` returns `MotionProps` with `initial` (containing `scale: from` and `opacity: initialOpacity`), `whileInView` (containing `scale: to` and `opacity: 1`), `viewport`, and `transition`. Spread the props onto any `motion.*` element to reveal it as it enters the viewport.

- **Modal and dialog entrances.** Mount a `motion.div` with `useScaleIn({ from: 0.6, duration: 0.3 })` to make a dialog appear to grow from the center of the screen.
- **Product cards in a grid.** Stagger each card with `delay: index * 0.08` so the grid populates from top-left to bottom-right as the user scrolls.
- **Feature tiles on a landing page.** Cards at `from: 0.85` with `ease: "easeOut"` scale up just enough to feel like they "land" into place without a dramatic pop.
- **Avatars and icon badges.** Small circular avatars with `from: 0.4` and a bouncy ease give social or collaboration features a lively feel.
- **Toast notifications.** Combine with `useSlideIn` to make a toast slide in from a corner and scale up simultaneously.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `useScaleIn` directly when:**

- You need the scale entrance on a custom element not covered by a prebuilt component.
- You want to compose it with [useFadeIn](/docs/hooks/fade-in) or [useSlideIn](/docs/hooks/slide-in) by merging their `initial` and `whileInView` objects.
- You need `viewport: "always"` so the element scales in every time it re-enters the viewport.

**Avoid `useScaleIn` when:**

- The element is a block-level section that spans the full viewport width. Scaling the entire section causes surrounding layout to shift, which feels chaotic. Prefer [useFadeIn](/docs/hooks/fade-in) for large sections.
- The scale start value `from` is 0. Starting at zero makes the element appear to appear from nothing, which can disorient users who are sensitive to sudden size changes. Use `from: 0.7` or higher for smoother reveals.
- Multiple overlapping elements scale in at the same time without stagger. The overlapping motions compete and can cause perceived jank. Apply sequential `delay` values.

## Accessibility notes

`useScaleIn` uses `whileInView` and sets `initial.opacity: 0`. The element is in the DOM from mount but hidden visually. Screen readers can still find it.

Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by returning props with `opacity` animation only, dropping the scale change:

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { useScaleIn } from "@/lib/use-scale-in"
import { useFadeIn } from "@/lib/use-fade-in"

export function FeatureTile({ title, icon }: { title: string; icon: React.ReactNode }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const scaleProps = useScaleIn({ from: 0.85, duration: 0.4 })
  const fadeProps = useFadeIn({ duration: 0.4 })

  return (
    <motion.div
      {...(reduced ? fadeProps : scaleProps)}
      className="rounded-xl border border-neutral-200 p-6"
    >
      <div className="mb-3 text-blue-500">{icon}</div>
      <h3 className="font-semibold">{title}</h3>
    </motion.div>
  )
}
```

- When `initialOpacity: 0` is the default, ensure any content that must be immediately readable (for example, navigation labels) is not wrapped in a `useScaleIn` without a near-zero delay. Use `delay: 0` and a very short `duration` for content that must be visible immediately.

## Performance considerations

- `useScaleIn` animates `scale` (a transform, compositor-only) and `opacity` (also compositor-only). No layout or paint is triggered during the animation.
- `whileInView` uses an `IntersectionObserver` internally. With `viewport: "once"` (default), the observer disconnects after the first intersection, incurring no ongoing cost.
- For grids of more than 20 items, consider using Framer Motion's `staggerChildren` variant system instead of calling `useScaleIn` inside a `.map()`, as many simultaneous `IntersectionObserver` instances can add up.
- The `initialOpacity: 0` default means the element is transparent until it enters the viewport. If the page is scrolled past the element's position on first load, the element will never animate in unless `viewport: "always"` is set.

"use client"

export function ConfirmDialog({

}

# scramble.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/scramble.mdx

title: useScramble
description: Matrix-style text scramble/decode animation that reveals text character by character.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `useScramble` hook creates a "decoding" text animation where random characters scramble before revealing the final text. Perfect for tech-themed interfaces, loading states, or dramatic text reveals.

<Callout type="info">
  **Pure React:** No motion library required - uses React state and intervals for the animation.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scramble
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scramble
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scramble
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-scramble
        ```
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-scramble.ts"
import * as React from "react";

export interface UseScrambleOptions {
  text?: string;
  duration?: number;
  delay?: number;
  scrambleChars?: string;
}

export function useScramble(options: UseScrambleOptions): string {
  const {
    text = "",
    duration = 0.8,
    delay = 0,
    scrambleChars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789!@#$%^&*()",
  } = options;

  const [displayText, setDisplayText] = React.useState(text);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    const iterations = Math.floor(duration * 60); // 60fps
    let currentIteration = 0;

    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
      const interval = setInterval(
        () => {
          if (currentIteration >= iterations) {
            setDisplayText(text);
            clearInterval(interval);
            return;
          }

          const progress = currentIteration / iterations;
          const newText = text
            .split("")
            .map((char, index) => {
              if (char === " ") return " ";
              if (index / text.length < progress) {
                return char;
              }
              return scrambleChars[
                Math.floor(Math.random() * scrambleChars.length)
              ];
            })
            .join("");

          setDisplayText(newText);
          currentIteration++;
        },
        (duration * 1000) / iterations,
      );

      return () => clearInterval(interval);
    }, delay * 1000);

    return () => clearTimeout(timeout);
  }, [text, duration, delay, scrambleChars]);

  return displayText;
}

```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx
import { useScramble } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scramble"

export function ScrambleHeading() {
  const displayText = useScramble({ text: "Hello World" })
  
  return (
    <h1 className="font-mono text-4xl">
      {displayText}
    </h1>
  )
}
```

### With Custom Duration

```tsx
import { useScramble } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scramble"

export function SlowScramble() {
  const displayText = useScramble({ 
    text: "Decoding...",
    duration: 2,
  })
  
  return (
    <div className="font-mono text-green-500">
      {displayText}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### With Delay

```tsx
import { useScramble } from "@/lib/hooks/use-scramble"

export function DelayedScramble() {
  const displayText = useScramble({ 
    text: "Welcome Back",
    duration: 1,
    delay: 0.5, // Wait 0.5s before starting
  })
  
  return <h2 className="font-mono">{displayText}</h2>
}
```

### Custom Scramble Characters

<Tabs items={['Numbers Only', 'Binary', 'Symbols', 'Custom']}>
  <Tab value="Numbers Only">

## Styling Tips

Works best with monospace fonts:

```tsx
<div className="font-mono">
  {displayText}
</div>
```

Add a cursor effect:

```tsx
<div className="font-mono">
  {displayText}<span className="animate-pulse">_</span>
</div>
```

## Use cases

`useScramble` returns a `string` (the current animated text). It does not return `MotionProps`; there is no `motion.*` element involved. Instead, render the returned string inside any element. The hook runs a `setInterval` internally, firing approximately 60 times per second for `duration * 60` iterations, replacing un-decoded characters with random ones from `scrambleChars`.

- **Hero headlines on a tech or developer-focused site.** A heading like "Build faster" that scrambles before resolving on page load establishes a code-like aesthetic immediately.
- **Loading state labels in terminal-style UIs.** Showing `"CONNECTING..."` scrambled while a WebSocket connects, then resolving to `"CONNECTED"`, communicates progress without a traditional spinner.
- **Hover-activated text reveals on portfolio items.** Trigger a new `text` value on hover to re-run the scramble effect over a project title or role label.
- **Staggered intro sequences.** Call the hook three times with increasing `delay` values to reveal a tagline word by word in a terminal boot sequence style.
- **Interactive command palette labels.** A label that scrambles briefly before showing the matched command adds a sci-fi character to a keyboard-first interface.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `useScramble` when:**

- You want a pure-React text animation with no `motion.*` element required.
- The aesthetic is explicitly technical, terminal, cyberpunk, or matrix-themed.
- The text is short (under 40 characters). Longer text scrambles slowly and can look noisy.

**Avoid `useScramble` when:**

- The content is user-generated text that the user typed themselves. Scrambling their own input would be confusing.
- The text is inside a form or an interactive input. Screen readers re-read text nodes when their content changes, so a 60fps interval firing `setDisplayText` will cause screen readers to read dozens of random characters.
- The text changes frequently based on external data. Each change of the `text` option restarts the animation. Rapid re-renders with changing `text` props can cause the animation to never fully resolve.

## Accessibility notes

`useScramble` updates a string state at ~60fps for the duration of the animation. During scrambling, the displayed string is meaningless to screen readers.

- Wrap the animated element in an `aria-label` or `aria-live="off"` to suppress screen reader announcements during the scramble, and use `aria-label` to provide the final text upfront:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useScramble } from "@/lib/use-scramble"

export function AccessibleScramble({ finalText }: { finalText: string }) {
  const displayText = useScramble({ text: finalText, duration: 0.8 })

  return (
    <h1 aria-label={finalText} className="font-mono text-4xl font-bold">
      {displayText}
    </h1>
  )
}
```

- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by returning the final text immediately instead of scrambling it:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { useScramble } from "@/lib/use-scramble"

export function ReducedScramble({ text }: { text: string }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const displayText = useScramble({ text, duration: reduced ? 0 : 0.8 })

  return (
    <span className="font-mono" aria-label={text}>
      {displayText}
    </span>
  )
}
```

Setting `duration: 0` makes `iterations = 0`, so `setDisplayText(text)` is called on the first interval tick and the scramble resolves immediately.

## Performance considerations

- `useScramble` uses `setInterval` at a rate of `(duration * 1000) / (duration * 60)` ms per tick, which equals approximately 16.7ms (60fps). This is a JavaScript-main-thread interval that calls `setDisplayText` and triggers one React state update per frame.
- Each state update schedules a React render and a DOM text node update. For a single element this is negligible, but avoid running multiple `useScramble` instances simultaneously on a page if the interval is rapid (duration under 0.5s).
- The `setTimeout` wrapper respects the `delay` option and does not start the interval until after the delay elapses. The timeout is cleaned up in the effect's return function, preventing memory leaks on unmount.
- The interval fires for exactly `Math.floor(duration * 60)` iterations and then clears itself. There is no ongoing cost after the animation completes unless `text` changes, which restarts the effect.
- Prefer monospace fonts (`font-mono`) to prevent text-width jitter during scrambling. Variable-width fonts cause the layout to shift on every character change.

# shimmer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/shimmer.mdx

title: useShimmer
description: Shimmer/shine text effect using pure CSS for smooth, performant animations.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `useShimmer` hook creates a smooth shimmer/shine effect on text using pure CSS animations. Perfect for loading states, premium branding, or eye-catching headings.

<Callout type="info">
  **Pure CSS:** No JavaScript animation - uses CSS gradients and keyframes for maximum performance.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-shimmer
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-shimmer
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-shimmer
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-shimmer
        ```
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-shimmer.ts"
import { type CSSProperties } from "react";

export interface UseShimmerOptions {
  duration?: number;
  colors?: [string, string, string];
}

export function useShimmer(options: UseShimmerOptions = {}): CSSProperties {
  const {
    duration = 2.5,
    colors = ["transparent", "rgba(255,255,255,0.8)", "transparent"],
  } = options;

  const gradient = `linear-gradient(90deg, ${colors[0]} 0%, ${colors[1]} 50%, ${colors[2]} 100%)`;

  const animationName = "shimmer";

  if (typeof document !== "undefined") {
    const styleId = "shimmer-keyframes";
    if (!document.getElementById(styleId)) {
      const style = document.createElement("style");
      style.id = styleId;
      style.textContent = `
        @keyframes shimmer {
          0% { background-position: 200% center; }
          100% { background-position: -200% center; }
        }
      `;
      document.head.appendChild(style);
    }
  }

  return {
    display: "inline-block",
    backgroundImage: gradient,
    backgroundSize: "200% auto",
    WebkitBackgroundClip: "text",
    WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent",
    backgroundClip: "text",
    animation: `${animationName} ${duration}s linear infinite`,
  };
}

```

## Use cases

`useShimmer` returns a `CSSProperties` object, not `MotionProps`. Spread it onto a regular HTML element or a React component that accepts a `style` prop. The returned object sets `backgroundImage`, `backgroundSize: "200% auto"`, `WebkitBackgroundClip: "text"`, `WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent"`, and `animation` with the injected `@keyframes shimmer` definition.

- **Premium tier labels and plan badges.** A "PRO" or "ENTERPRISE" badge with a gold shimmer (`colors: ["transparent", "rgba(255,215,0,0.9)", "transparent"]`) signals exclusivity without an icon.
- **Hero headings on dark landing pages.** A white shimmer sweep across a dark hero title creates a spotlight-sweeping-across-stage effect that is impossible with static gradients.
- **Loading placeholder text.** Replace content areas with shimmer-animated placeholder headings while data loads, giving a branded loading skeleton for text content.
- **Feature announcement ribbons.** A "NEW" tag or "BETA" ribbon with a shimmer communicates recency and draws the eye.
- **Countdown or launch page headlines.** A slow shimmer (`duration: 4`) on a large countdown heading adds movement to a page that is otherwise static.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `useShimmer` when:**

- The target is a text element (heading, span, label) where `WebkitBackgroundClip: "text"` applies correctly.
- You want a CSS-only animation with no Framer Motion dependency. `useShimmer` injects a `@keyframes shimmer` rule into the document `<head>` once and reuses it for all subsequent calls.
- You need to control the exact shimmer colors via the `colors` tuple.

**Avoid `useShimmer` when:**

- The element is a non-text block (a card background, an image overlay). The hook uses `WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent"`, which only affects text rendering. For shimmer on non-text elements, build a separate CSS animation with a `::before` pseudo-element overlay.
- The text must be selectable and copyable in a way that matches its visual color. `WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent"` makes the text visually transparent while the background gradient shows through; some browsers may render copied text as empty or invisible in certain clipboard contexts.
- Server-side rendering with strict hydration. The `useShimmer` hook calls `document.getElementById` and `document.createElement` inside the render path. It guards with `typeof document !== "undefined"`, but the injected `<style>` tag will not exist on the server, causing a hydration mismatch if the style affects layout.

## Accessibility notes

`useShimmer` produces a continuously moving animation (infinite loop). The text content itself is unchanged; only the visual gradient and animation are applied.

- Screen readers read the text content, not the visual gradient, so the text remains fully accessible.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. The shimmer sweep moves across the element indefinitely. When the preference is set, return an empty style object so the text renders normally without the gradient:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { useShimmer } from "@/lib/use-shimmer"

export function AccessibleShimmer({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const shimmerStyle = useShimmer({ duration: 2.5 })

  return (
    <span style={reduced ? undefined : shimmerStyle} className="text-4xl font-bold">
      {children}
    </span>
  )
}
```

- Because `WebkitTextFillColor: "transparent"` makes the text itself invisible (only the background gradient is visible), ensure the gradient colors provide sufficient contrast against the page background for users with color vision deficiencies.

## Performance considerations

- `useShimmer` uses a pure CSS animation via `background-position` changes on a `linear-gradient`. This does not trigger layout or paint on each frame because background-position is composited by the browser's rendering engine in most cases.
- The `@keyframes shimmer` style block is injected into `document.head` only once per page load (guarded by `document.getElementById("shimmer-keyframes")`). Multiple components using `useShimmer` share the same keyframes.
- `backgroundSize: "200% auto"` doubles the gradient's virtual width. The animation moves the position from `200% center` to `-200% center`. This is equivalent to a translate of 400% of the element width, which is handled in the browser's compositing layer and does not cause repaints.
- The hook reconstructs the `CSSProperties` object on every render. Memoize the options if the parent component re-renders frequently.

```tsx
    colors: ["transparent", "rgba(255,255,255,0.85)", "transparent"],
    duration: 4,
  })

  return (
    <div className="bg-neutral-950 py-20 text-center">
      <p className="text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-widest text-neutral-500">Launching in</p>
      <h1
        style={shimmerStyle}
        className="mt-4 text-8xl font-black text-white"
        aria-label={`${days} days`}
      >
        {days}
      </h1>
      <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-neutral-400">days</p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

<Callout>
  **Tip:** Works best on bold, large text for maximum visual impact.
</Callout>

# slide-in.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/slide-in.mdx

title: useSlideIn
description: Slide in entrance animation from any direction with fade effect.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `useSlideIn` hook creates a slide-in entrance animation from any direction (left, right, up, down) with optional fade. Perfect for sidebars, drawers, notifications, and sequential content reveals.

<Callout type="info">
  **Directional flexibility:** Choose the slide direction that best matches your layout and user flow.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-slide-in
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-slide-in
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-slide-in
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-slide-in
        ```
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-slide-in.ts"
import { type MotionProps, type Easing } from "motion/react";

export type SlideDirection = "left" | "right" | "up" | "down";

export interface UseSlideInOptions {
  direction?: SlideDirection;

  distance?: number;

  duration?: number;

  delay?: number;

  initialOpacity?: number;

  ease?: Easing | Easing[];

  viewport?: "once" | "always";
}

export function useSlideIn(options: UseSlideInOptions = {}): MotionProps {
  const {
    direction = "left",
    distance = 50,
    duration = 0.5,
    delay = 0,
    initialOpacity = 0,
    ease = "easeOut",
    viewport = "once",
  } = options;

  const getInitialPosition = () => {
    switch (direction) {
      case "left":
        return { x: -distance, y: 0 };
      case "right":
        return { x: distance, y: 0 };
      case "up":
        return { x: 0, y: -distance };
      case "down":
        return { x: 0, y: distance };
      default:
        return { x: -distance, y: 0 };
    }
  };

  const initialPosition = getInitialPosition();

  return {
    initial: {
      ...initialPosition,
      opacity: initialOpacity,
    },
    whileInView: {
      x: 0,
      y: 0,
      opacity: 1,
    },
    viewport: {
      once: viewport === "once",
    },
    transition: {
      duration,
      delay,
      ease,
    },
  };
}

```

```tsx

export function Card() {

  return (
    <motion.div {...slideProps} className="card">
      <h3>Slides in from left</h3>
      <p>Content appears smoothly</p>
    </motion.div>
  )
}
```

## API Reference

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `direction` | `"left" \| "right" \| "up" \| "down"` | `"left"` | Direction to slide from |
| `distance` | `number` | `50` | Distance to slide in pixels |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation duration in seconds |
| `delay` | `number` | `0` | Delay before animation starts |
| `initialOpacity` | `number` | `0` | Initial opacity (0-1) |
| `ease` | `string \| number[]` | `"easeOut"` | Animation easing |
| `viewport` | `"once" \| "always"` | `"once"` | Animate once or every time in view |

## Common Use Cases

```tsx
<motion.div {...useSlideIn({ direction: "down", distance: 100 })}>
```

## Use cases

`useSlideIn` returns `MotionProps` with `initial` (containing the starting x or y offset plus `opacity: initialOpacity`), `whileInView` (setting `x: 0`, `y: 0`, `opacity: 1`), `viewport`, and `transition`. Spread the props onto any `motion.*` element.

- **Section-level text blocks.** A `motion.div` containing a headline and body copy with `direction: "left"` and `distance: 60` gives each section a clean lateral entrance as the user scrolls.
- **Alternating two-column layouts.** Left column with `direction: "left"`, right column with `direction: "right"`, staggered by `delay: 0.1` creates a symmetrical pincer entrance.
- **Sidebars and drawer panels.** A `motion.aside` with `direction: "left"` and `distance: 300` slides in from off-screen when toggled. Pair with `AnimatePresence` for the exit.
- **Toast and notification banners.** A `motion.div` with `direction: "down"` and `distance: 80` drops in from the top of the viewport. A bounce ease (`[0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55]`) makes it feel lively.
- **Staggered feature lists.** Each list item slides in from the left with a `delay: index * 0.07` to produce a cascading reveal as the section enters the viewport.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `useSlideIn` directly when:**

- You need the slide effect on a custom element, such as a `motion.section`, `motion.article`, or a custom sidebar component.
- You want to compose `useSlideIn` with [useFadeIn](/docs/hooks/fade-in) to produce a slide-plus-fade by merging their `initial` and `whileInView` objects.
- You need `direction: "up"` or `direction: "down"` (vertical slides), which is specific to `useSlideIn`.

**Avoid `useSlideIn` when:**

- The element is very large (full-viewport width or height). A large `distance` on a full-screen element creates a dramatic layout jump. Use `distance: 20` to 30 for section-level elements.
- The slide direction conflicts with the page's reading flow. A right-to-left slide on a left-to-right reading layout can feel counter-intuitive. Match the direction to the user's expected reading path.
- You need a one-shot entrance on a modal or dialog. Modals are not in the viewport scroll flow, so `whileInView` may not fire as expected. Use `animate` directly or `AnimatePresence` with `useScaleIn` instead.

## Accessibility notes

`useSlideIn` uses `whileInView` and sets `initial.opacity: 0`. The element exists in the DOM from mount but is hidden.

Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` by returning only the fade (opacity) change, dropping the translate:

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { useSlideIn } from "@/lib/use-slide-in"
import { useFadeIn } from "@/lib/use-fade-in"

export function SectionBlock({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const slideProps = useSlideIn({ direction: "left", distance: 50, duration: 0.5 })
  const fadeProps = useFadeIn({ duration: 0.5 })

  return (
    <motion.section
      {...(reduced ? fadeProps : slideProps)}
      className="py-16"
    >
      {children}
    </motion.section>
  )
}
```

Additional guidance:

- Content that starts off-screen (`x: -distance`) is technically in the DOM but painted outside the viewport. Screen readers access it normally. Ensure that `initialOpacity: 0` does not cause content to be skipped by assistive technology that tests visibility by opacity.
- For drawer-style slides that conditionally render (mount/unmount), use `AnimatePresence` so the exit animation plays before the element is removed from the DOM and keyboard focus is not lost abruptly.

## Performance considerations

- `useSlideIn` animates `x` or `y` (transforms) and `opacity`. Both are compositor properties. No layout or paint is triggered.
- `whileInView` uses an `IntersectionObserver`. With `viewport: "once"` (default), the observer disconnects after the first intersection.
- For large scroll pages with dozens of slide-in elements, each element has its own `IntersectionObserver` instance. Framer Motion batches intersection callbacks efficiently, but for very long pages (100 or more elements), consider using the Framer Motion `variants` system with `staggerChildren` on a parent, which uses a single observer for the whole list.
- The `distance` option determines the initial translated position. Large `distance` values (above 200) on many elements mean more content is rendered off-screen. This does not affect performance directly but can affect how scroll restoration behaves on page reload.

## Customization examples

### Feature section with left-right alternating slides

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useSlideIn } from "@/lib/use-slide-in"

interface Feature {
  title: string
  description: string
  image: string
}

export function AlternatingFeature({ feature, index }: { feature: Feature; index: number }) {
  const isEven = index % 2 === 0
  const textSlide = useSlideIn({ direction: isEven ? "left" : "right", distance: 60, duration: 0.55 })
  const imageSlide = useSlideIn({ direction: isEven ? "right" : "left", distance: 60, duration: 0.55, delay: 0.1 })

  return (
    <div className={`flex gap-12 items-center ${isEven ? "" : "flex-row-reverse"}`}>
      <motion.div {...textSlide} className="flex-1">
        <h3 className="text-2xl font-bold">{feature.title}</h3>
        <p className="mt-3 text-neutral-500">{feature.description}</p>
      </motion.div>
      <motion.img {...imageSlide} src={feature.image} alt={feature.title} className="flex-1 rounded-2xl object-cover" />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Toast notification that slides down

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react"
import { useSlideIn } from "@/lib/use-slide-in"

export function Toast({ message, visible }: { message: string; visible: boolean }) {
  const slideProps = useSlideIn({
    direction: "down",
    distance: 80,
    duration: 0.4,
    ease: [0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55],
  })

  return (
    <AnimatePresence>
      {visible && (
        <motion.div
          {...slideProps}
          role="status"
          className="fixed right-4 top-4 z-50 rounded-xl bg-neutral-900 px-5 py-3 text-sm text-white shadow-lg"
        >
          {message}
        </motion.div>
      )}
    </AnimatePresence>
  )
}
```

# stroke-draw.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/stroke-draw.mdx

title: useStrokeDraw
description: SVG path drawing animation that reveals strokes progressively.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `useStrokeDraw` hook animates SVG paths with a drawing effect, perfect for logos, icons, signatures, or decorative elements.

<Callout type="info">
  **SVG Only:** This hook is specifically designed for SVG `<path>` elements using Framer Motion.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-stroke-draw
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-stroke-draw
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-stroke-draw
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-stroke-draw
        ```
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-stroke-draw.ts"
import { type MotionProps, type Easing } from "motion/react";

export interface UseStrokeDrawOptions {
  duration?: number;
  delay?: number;
  repeat?: boolean;
  ease?: Easing | Easing[];
}

export function useStrokeDraw(options: UseStrokeDrawOptions = {}): MotionProps {
  const {
    duration = 1.5,
    delay = 0,
    repeat = false,
    ease = "easeInOut",
  } = options;

  return {
    initial: { pathLength: 0, opacity: 0 },
    animate: { pathLength: 1, opacity: 1 },
    transition: {
      pathLength: { duration, delay, ease },
      opacity: { duration: 0.2, delay },
      repeat: repeat ? Infinity : 0,
      repeatDelay: 1,
    },
  };
}

```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useStrokeDraw } from "@/lib/hooks/use-stroke-draw"

export function DrawingLogo() {
  const strokeProps = useStrokeDraw()
  
  return (
    <svg width="200" height="200" viewBox="0 0 200 200">
      <motion.path
        d="M 50 100 Q 100 50 150 100 T 250 100"
        stroke="currentColor"
        strokeWidth="3"
        fill="none"
        {...strokeProps}
      />
    </svg>
  )
}
```

```tsx
  })
```

## Tips

### Use with strokeDasharray

```tsx
<motion.path
  {...strokeProps}
  strokeDasharray="5 5" // Dashed line
/>
```

### Custom Easing

```tsx
const strokeProps = useStrokeDraw({
  ease: [0.6, 0.01, 0.05, 0.95], // Custom cubic bezier
})
```

<Callout type="warn">
  **SVG Required:** This hook only works with SVG path elements. For other animations, use different hooks.
</Callout>

## Use cases

The hook animates the SVG `pathLength` property from 0 to 1, so a stroke appears to draw itself. Framer Motion normalizes `pathLength` to a 0 to 1 range, which means you never have to measure the path or compute `strokeDasharray` by hand. Reach for it when:

- **Logo and wordmark reveals** that draw in on first paint.
- **Success and status marks**, like a checkmark stroking in after a form submits.
- **Signature effects** for contracts, certificates, or playful hero art.
- **Decorative accents**, such as an underline or divider that draws under a heading.
- **Line-art icons** that reveal their outline on mount, hover, or scroll into view.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use this hook when:**

- You have real vector line art (`<path>`, `<circle>`, `<line>`, `<polyline>`) and want a one-shot draw-on reveal.
- The stroke itself is the visual, so `fill="none"` with a visible `stroke` and `strokeWidth`.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **Your shape is filled, not stroked.** `pathLength` only animates the outline. A solid icon with no stroke will appear to animate nothing. Give it `fill="none"` and a `stroke`, or animate `opacity`/`scale` instead.
- **You need an indeterminate loading spinner.** Setting `repeat: true` here loops the draw, but a continuous draw reads slower than a real spinner. Use the [Spinner](/docs/animations/loaders/spinner) or [Spin icon](/docs/animations/icons/spin).
- **You are revealing text or block content.** Use [useFadeIn](/docs/hooks/fade-in) or [useSlideIn](/docs/hooks/slide-in) for that.

## Accessibility notes

An SVG carries no meaning to assistive tech unless you give it some, and a drawing animation can be a problem for motion-sensitive users.

- **Label or hide the graphic.** If the SVG conveys meaning, add `role="img"` plus a `<title>` (or `aria-label`). If it is purely decorative, mark it `aria-hidden="true"` so screen readers skip it.
- **Never put state only in the motion.** A checkmark that draws in to signal success must also be backed by text such as "Saved" so users who do not see the animation still get the result.
- **Respect reduced motion.** Render the finished path immediately for users who ask for less motion:

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion, useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { useStrokeDraw } from "@/lib/hooks/use-stroke-draw"

function AccessibleCheck() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const strokeProps = useStrokeDraw({ duration: 0.5 })
  // Skip the draw and show the final stroke instantly.
  const props = reduced ? { initial: { pathLength: 1, opacity: 1 } } : strokeProps

  return (
    <svg width="100" height="100" viewBox="0 0 100 100" role="img" aria-label="Success">
      <motion.path
        d="M 20 50 L 40 70 L 80 30"
        stroke="#10b981"
        strokeWidth="6"
        strokeLinecap="round"
        fill="none"
        {...props}
      />
    </svg>
  )
}
```

- **Avoid `repeat: true` for anything informational.** A looping draw is continuous motion; gate it behind the reduced-motion check above.

## Performance considerations

- **This is a paint animation, not a compositor transform.** Animating `pathLength` repaints the stroke each frame, unlike `transform`/`opacity` which run on the GPU. For a handful of small paths this is smooth, but cost grows with path complexity.
- **Keep `d` data simple.** A very long, highly detailed path string costs more to repaint every frame. Simplify curves where you can.
- **Stagger instead of firing everything at once.** Animating many paths simultaneously multiplies the per-frame paint. Use the `delay` option to spread them out.
- **Unmount looping draws.** `repeat: true` runs forever. Conditionally render the SVG (`{visible && <Logo />}`) so the animation stops when it leaves the screen.

## Customization examples

### Dashed stroke

Combine with `strokeDasharray` for a dashed line that still draws on:

```tsx
<motion.path {...strokeProps} strokeDasharray="6 6" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" />
```

### Custom easing

```tsx
const strokeProps = useStrokeDraw({
  duration: 2,
  ease: [0.6, 0.01, 0.05, 0.95], // hand-drawn feel
})
```

### Sequential multi-path draw

Use `delay` to draw shapes one after another:

```tsx
const first = useStrokeDraw({ duration: 0.8, delay: 0 })
const second = useStrokeDraw({ duration: 0.8, delay: 0.8 })
```

# word-carousel.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/hooks/word-carousel.mdx

title: useWordCarousel
description: Rotating word carousel that cycles through words with smooth transitions.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Overview

The `useWordCarousel` hook cycles through an array of words at a specified interval. Perfect for dynamic hero titles, feature highlights, or rotating testimonials.

<Callout type="info">
  **Works with AnimatePresence:** Pair with Framer Motion's `AnimatePresence` for smooth transitions between words.
</Callout>

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-word-carousel
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-word-carousel
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-word-carousel
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/hooks-use-word-carousel
        ```
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-word-carousel.ts"
import * as React from "react";

export interface UseWordCarouselOptions {
  words: string[];
  interval?: number;
}

export function useWordCarousel(options: UseWordCarouselOptions) {
  const { words, interval = 2 } = options;
  const [currentIndex, setCurrentIndex] = React.useState(0);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      setCurrentIndex((prev) => (prev + 1) % words.length);
    }, interval * 1000);

    return () => clearInterval(timer);
  }, [words.length, interval]);

  return {
    currentWord: words[currentIndex],
    currentIndex,
    key: currentIndex, // For AnimatePresence
  };
}

```

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react"
import { useWordCarousel } from "@/lib/hooks/use-word-carousel"

export function RotatingWords() {
  const { currentWord, key } = useWordCarousel({ 
    words: ["Fast", "Modern", "Beautiful"] 
  })
  
  return (
    <div className="text-4xl font-bold">
      Build{" "}
      <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
        <motion.span
          key={key}
          initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
          exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -20 }}
          transition={{ duration: 0.3 }}
          className="text-blue-500"
        >
          {currentWord}
        </motion.span>
      </AnimatePresence>
      {" "}Apps
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Tips

### Always Use AnimatePresence

For smooth transitions, wrap the animated element in `AnimatePresence`:

```tsx
<AnimatePresence mode="wait">
  <motion.span key={key}>
    {currentWord}
  </motion.span>
</AnimatePresence>
```

### Use `mode="wait"`

This ensures the exit animation completes before the enter animation starts.

### Inline Display

For inline text, use `display: inline-block`:

```tsx
<motion.span
  key={key}
  className="inline-block"
  // ... animations
>
  {currentWord}
</motion.span>
```

<Callout>
  **Accessibility:** Ensure rotating text doesn't convey critical information that users might miss. Consider adding pause controls for accessibility.
</Callout>

## Use cases

The hook keeps a `currentIndex` in state and advances it on a `setInterval`, cycling through your `words` array and returning a `key` you spread onto an `AnimatePresence` child. Reach for it when:

- **Hero headlines** that cycle an adjective, like "Build Fast / Modern / Beautiful apps".
- **Rotating value props** where one slot swaps through a few benefits.
- **Audience or persona lines**, such as "Built for Developers / Designers / Creators".
- **Short rotating quotes** in a compact testimonial slot.

The surrounding sentence should carry the meaning. The rotating word is emphasis, not the whole message.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use this hook when:**

- You are cycling short words or phrases as decoration around a stable sentence.
- The complete meaning still reads even if a user never sees a particular word.

**Reach for something else when:**

- **The rotating text is essential information.** Auto-advancing content can be missed entirely, and it works against [WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html). Put critical content in static text.
- **The items are full sentences.** A fixed interval cannot match every reader's pace, so long strings get cut off mid-read. Show them as a static list.
- **You want a prebuilt component.** If you do not need hook-level control, the [Word Carousel](/docs/animations/text/word-carousel) component wraps this for you. For a one-time reveal rather than a loop, use [useFadeIn](/docs/hooks/fade-in).

## Accessibility notes

Auto-rotating text is one of the easier ways to create an accessibility problem, so handle it deliberately.

- **Provide a way to pause.** The shipped hook runs continuously with no pause control. If the rotation lasts longer than 5 seconds, WCAG 2.2.2 requires a pause, stop, or hide mechanism. The simplest fix is a small extension that accepts a `paused` flag (see Real-world examples below) wired to hover and focus.
- **Control what screen readers announce.** Letting `AnimatePresence` swap text on a live region every couple of seconds either spams announcements or gets skipped. Mark the rotating word `aria-hidden="true"` and give the parent a stable `aria-label` that states the full message:

```tsx
<h1 aria-label="Built for developers, designers, and creators">
  Built for{" "}
  <span aria-hidden="true">
    <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
      <motion.span key={key} /* ... */>{currentWord}</motion.span>
    </AnimatePresence>
  </span>
</h1>
```

- **Respect reduced motion.** For users who ask for less motion, drop the enter/exit transforms and show a single word:

```tsx
"use client"
import { motion, AnimatePresence, useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { useWordCarousel } from "@/lib/hooks/use-word-carousel"

function AccessibleRotator() {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  const words = ["Fast", "Secure", "Reliable"]
  const { currentWord, key } = useWordCarousel({ words })

  if (reduced) {
    return <span className="font-bold text-blue-600">{words[0]}</span>
  }

  return (
    <span aria-hidden="true">
      <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
        <motion.span
          key={key}
          initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
          exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -10 }}
          className="inline-block font-bold text-blue-600"
        >
          {currentWord}
        </motion.span>
      </AnimatePresence>
    </span>
  )
}
```

## Performance considerations

- **It re-renders on every tick.** `setCurrentIndex` fires each interval, re-rendering the component that calls the hook. Keep that component small and low in the tree so the re-render stays cheap, rather than rotating a word from a large page-level component.
- **The interval resets when `words.length` or `interval` changes.** The effect depends on those two values, so changing the number of words restarts the cycle at index 0. A new array identity with the same length is fine.
- **`mode="wait"` doubles the transition time.** The exit animation finishes before the enter begins, so keep durations short (0.2 to 0.4 seconds) to avoid a sluggish swap.
- **Prefer transform and opacity.** The Slide and Scale variants animate compositor-friendly properties. The Blur variant animates a `filter`, which triggers repaint and is heavier, so reserve it for a single hero instance.

## Customization examples

### Reserve width to stop layout shift

Words have different widths, so the text after them jumps on each swap. Stack an invisible copy of the longest word to lock the width:

```tsx
<span className="relative inline-grid">
  <span aria-hidden="true" className="invisible col-start-1 row-start-1 font-bold">
    Innovators
  </span>
  <span className="col-start-1 row-start-1">
    <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
      <motion.span key={key} className="inline-block font-bold text-blue-600">
        {currentWord}
      </motion.span>
    </AnimatePresence>
  </span>
</span>
```

### Faster or slower cadence

```tsx

const slow = useWordCarousel({ words, interval: 5 })   // calm
```

```tsx
    >

        <span className="invisible col-start-1 row-start-1">Innovators</span>

              exit={{ opacity: 0, y: -20 }}
```

### Pause on hover and focus (WCAG-friendly)

The shipped hook has no pause option, so extend it with a `paused` flag and wire it to pointer and keyboard:

```tsx
"use client"
import * as React from "react"
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react"

// A pausable variant of useWordCarousel.
function usePausableWordCarousel({ words, interval = 2, paused = false }: {
  words: string[]
  interval?: number
  paused?: boolean
}) {
  const [index, setIndex] = React.useState(0)

  React.useEffect(() => {
    if (paused) return
    const id = setInterval(() => setIndex((p) => (p + 1) % words.length), interval * 1000)
    return () => clearInterval(id)
  }, [words.length, interval, paused])

  return { currentWord: words[index], currentIndex: index, key: index }
}

export function PausableRotator() {
  const [paused, setPaused] = React.useState(false)
  const words = ["Fast", "Secure", "Reliable"]
  const { currentWord, key } = usePausableWordCarousel({ words, interval: 2.5, paused })

  return (
    <span
      onMouseEnter={() => setPaused(true)}
      onMouseLeave={() => setPaused(false)}
      onFocus={() => setPaused(true)}
      onBlur={() => setPaused(false)}
      tabIndex={0}
      className="text-2xl font-bold text-blue-600 outline-none"
    >
      <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
        <motion.span
          key={key}
          initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
          animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
          exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
          className="inline-block"
        >
          {currentWord}
        </motion.span>
      </AnimatePresence>
    </span>
  )
}
```

## What is AnimBits?

AnimBits is a collection of **copy-paste animation components** and **primitive hooks** built on Framer Motion. Unlike traditional animation libraries, AnimBits gives you the source code. Customize everything to match your design system.

<Callout type="info">
  **Not a component library.** AnimBits is a collection of re-usable components and hooks that you can copy and paste into your apps. Built with React, TypeScript, and Framer Motion.
</Callout>

## Key Features

<div className="not-prose mt-8 grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2">
  <div className="rounded-lg border bg-card p-6">
    <h3 className="mb-2 font-semibold">Component-Agnostic</h3>
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground block">
      Use any animation on any element. Not locked into categories like "button animations" or "card animations".
    </span>
  
  <div className="rounded-lg border bg-card p-6">
    <h3 className="mb-2 font-semibold">Primitive Hooks</h3>
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground block">
      Low-level hooks that return Framer Motion props. Maximum flexibility to compose and combine animations.
    </span>
  
  <div className="rounded-lg border bg-card p-6">
    <h3 className="mb-2 font-semibold">Copy & Paste</h3>
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground block">
      No npm dependencies. Copy the source code directly into your project and customize to your heart's content.
    </span>
  
  <div className="rounded-lg border bg-card p-6">
    <h3 className="mb-2 font-semibold">Composable</h3>
    <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground block">
      Mix and match animations. Combine lift + glow, fade + scale, or any other combination you can imagine.
    </span>

## Quick Start

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Install dependencies
    
    AnimBits requires Framer Motion and React. Install them if you haven't already:
    
    ```bash
    npm install framer-motion
    ```
  </Step>
  
  <Step>
    ### Copy a component or hook
    
    Browse the [components](/docs/components/buttons) or [hooks](/docs/hooks/hover-lift) and copy the code you need:
    
    <Tabs items={['Component', 'Hook']}>
      <Tab value="Component">
        ```tsx
        // Copy from registry/buttons/lift.tsx
        import { LiftButton } from '@/components/animations/buttons/lift'
        
        export function MyComponent() {
          return (
            <LiftButton className="inline-flex h-11 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-6 text-sm font-semibold text-white">
              Hover Me
            </LiftButton>
          )
        }
        ```
      
      <Tab value="Hook">
        ```tsx
        // Copy from lib/hooks/use-hover-lift.ts
        import { motion } from "motion/react"
        import { useHoverLift } from '@/lib/hooks/use-hover-lift'
        
        export function MyComponent() {
          const liftProps = useHoverLift({ liftDistance: 12 })
          
          return (
            <motion.div {...liftProps} className="p-6 bg-white rounded-lg">
              This card lifts on hover!
            </motion.div>
          )
        }
        ```
  </Step>
  
  <Step>
    ### Customize to your needs
    
    Modify the animations, change the styling, add your own features. It's your code now!
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Choose Your Layer

<Tabs items={['Semantic Components', 'Primitive Hooks', 'Generic Wrappers']}>
  <Tab value="Semantic Components">
    **Best for:** Quick prototyping, consistent patterns
    
    ```tsx
    import { LiftButton } from '@/components/animations/buttons/lift'
    
    <LiftButton>Click me</LiftButton>
    ```
    
    - Fastest to implement
    - Opinionated styling included
    - Less flexible for custom use cases
  
  <Tab value="Primitive Hooks">
    **Best for:** Custom implementations, maximum flexibility
    
    ```tsx
    import { motion } from "motion/react"
    import { useHoverLift } from '@/lib/hooks/use-hover-lift'
    
    const liftProps = useHoverLift({ liftDistance: 16 })
    <motion.article {...liftProps}>
      Custom article with lift!
    </motion.article>
    ```
    
    - Works with ANY element
    - Easy to compose multiple animations
    - Component-agnostic
    - Requires more setup
  
  <Tab value="Generic Wrappers">
    **Best for:** Consistent animation patterns across elements
    
    ```tsx
    import { Animated } from '@/lib/components/animated'
    import { useHoverLift } from '@/lib/hooks/use-hover-lift'
    
    const lift = useHoverLift()
    <Animated animation={lift} as="article">
      Convenient wrapper!
    </Animated>
    ```
    
    - Cleaner than raw motion components
    - Still fully flexible
    - Extra abstraction layer

## Philosophy

<Callout>
  **You own the code.** AnimBits is not a package you install. It's a collection of components and hooks you copy into your project. This means:
  
  - No version conflicts or breaking changes
  - Full control over implementation
  - Customize without fighting the library
  - Learn by reading the source
</Callout>

## What's Included

- **8+ Primitive Hooks:** `useHoverLift`, `useHoverGlow`, `useFadeIn`, `useScaleIn`, `useSlideIn`, `usePulse`, `usePress`, `useBounce`
- **40+ Semantic Components:** Buttons, cards, icons, lists, pages, text, loaders, and transitions
- **TypeScript:** Fully typed with intelligent autocomplete
- **Composable:** Mix and match animations freely
- **Accessible:** Built with accessibility in mind

# installation.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/installation.mdx

title: Installation
description: AnimBits is not a traditional npm package. You can download using shadcn cli or copy the components and hooks directly into your project. This gives you full control over the code and allows you to customize everything.

import { Step, Steps } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';
import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';

## Prerequisites

Before you begin, make sure you have:

- React 18.0 or later
- TypeScript 4.9 or later (recommended)
- Node.js 16.0 or later

## Pick Your Framework

Start by selecting your framework of choice. Then follow the instructions to install the dependencies and structure your app. AnimBits is built to work with all React frameworks.
