## Quick Start

<Steps>
  <Step>
    ### Install Framer Motion
    
    AnimBits is built on top of Framer Motion. Install it in your project:
    
        ```bash
        npm install framer-motion
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm add framer-motion
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn add framer-motion
        ```
        ```bash
        bun add framer-motion
        ```
  </Step>
  
  <Step>
    ### Install Tailwind CSS (Optional)
    
    While not required, AnimBits components use Tailwind CSS for styling. If you haven't set it up:
    
        ```bash
        npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
        npx tailwindcss init -p
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
        pnpm dlx tailwindcss init -p
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
        yarn dlx tailwindcss init -p
        ```
        ```bash
        bun add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
        bunx tailwindcss init -p
        ```
    
    Configure your `tailwind.config.js`:
    
    ```js title="tailwind.config.js"
    /** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
    module.exports = {
      content: [
        './pages/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}',
        './components/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}',
        './app/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx,mdx}',
      ],
      theme: {
        extend: {},
      },
      plugins: [],
    }
    ```
    
    Add Tailwind directives to your CSS:
    
    ```css title="app/globals.css"
    @tailwind base;
    @tailwind components;
    @tailwind utilities;
    ```
  </Step>
  
       <Step>
    ### Create Directory Structure
    
    Create the necessary folders in your project:
    
    ```bash
    mkdir -p lib
    mkdir -p components
    ```
    
    Your structure should look like:
    
    ```
    your-project/
    ├── lib/
    │   ├── use-hover-lift.ts    # Animation primitive hooks
    │   ├── use-press.ts
    │   └── utils.ts
    └── components/
        ├── buttons-lift
        ├── cards-hover-glow     # components goes here
        ├── cards-tilt
        └── ...
    ```
  </Step>
  
  <Step>
    ### Copy Your First Component
    
    Browse the [components](/docs/animations/buttons/lift) or [hooks](/docs/hooks/hover-lift) documentation and copy the code you need.
    
    For example, to use the hover lift animation:
    
    **Option 1: Copy the hook (recommended for flexibility)**
    
    ```tsx title="lib/hooks/use-hover-lift.ts"
    import { type MotionProps } from "motion/react"

    export interface UseHoverLiftOptions {
      liftDistance?: number
      addShadow?: boolean
      duration?: number
      shadowStyle?: string
    }

    export function useHoverLift(options: UseHoverLiftOptions = {}): MotionProps {
      const {
        liftDistance = 8,
        addShadow = true,
        duration = 0.2,
        shadowStyle = "0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.15)",
      } = options

      return {
        initial: {
          y: 0,
          boxShadow: addShadow ? "0 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0)" : undefined,
        },
        whileHover: {
          y: -liftDistance,
          boxShadow: addShadow ? shadowStyle : undefined,
        },
        transition: { duration },
      }
    }
    ```
    
    **Option 2: Copy the component (quick start)**
    
    ```tsx title="components/animations/buttons/lift.tsx"
    "use client"

    import { motion, type HTMLMotionProps } from "motion/react"
    import { useHoverLift } from "@/lib/use-hover-lift"

    export interface LiftButtonProps extends Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"button">, "animate"> {
      children: React.ReactNode
      liftHeight?: number
      shadow?: boolean
    }

    export function LiftButton({
      children,
      liftHeight = 8,
      shadow = true,
      ...props
    }: LiftButtonProps) {
      const liftAnimation = useHoverLift({
        liftDistance: liftHeight,
        addShadow: shadow,
      })

      return (
        <motion.button
          {...liftAnimation}
          {...props}
        >
          {children}
        </motion.button>
      )
    }
    ```
  </Step>
  
  <Step>
    ### Use in Your Project
    
    Import and use the component or hook in your application:
    
    <Tabs items={['Using Component', 'Using Hook']}>
      <Tab value="Using Component">
        ```tsx title="app/page.tsx"
        import { LiftButton } from '@/components/animations/buttons/lift'

        export default function Home() {
          return (
            <LiftButton className="inline-flex h-11 items-center gap-2 rounded-lg bg-blue-600 px-6 text-sm font-semibold text-white">
              Hover Me
            </LiftButton>
          )
        }
        ```
      <Tab value="Using Hook">
        ```tsx title="app/page.tsx"
        import { motion } from "motion/react"
        import { useHoverLift } from '@/lib/use-hover-lift'

        export default function Home() {
          const liftProps = useHoverLift({ liftDistance: 12 })
          
          return (
            <motion.div 
              {...liftProps} 
              className="p-6 bg-white rounded-lg shadow"
            >
              This card lifts on hover!
            </motion.div>
          )
        }
        ```
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Framework-Specific Setup

### Next.js

AnimBits works seamlessly with Next.js 13+ (App Router).

#### Create project

Start by creating a new Next.js project. You will be asked if you want to use TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and ESLint - we recommend selecting **Yes** for all.

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'npm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>
    ```bash
    pnpm create next-app@latest my-app
    cd my-app
    ```
    ```bash
    npx create-next-app@latest my-app
    cd my-app
    ```
    ```bash
    yarn create next-app my-app
    cd my-app
    ```
    ```bash
    bun create next-app my-app
    cd my-app
    ```

#### Install dependencies

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'npm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>
    ```bash
    pnpm add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    npm install framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    yarn add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    bun add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```

#### Add utility function

Create a `lib/utils.ts` file for class merging:

```ts title="lib/utils.ts"
import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
}
```

#### Use in your components

Add the `"use client"` directive to any component that uses animations.

```tsx title="components/animations/buttons/lift.tsx"
"use client"

import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useHoverLift } from "@/lib/hooks/use-hover-lift"

export function LiftButton({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const liftProps = useHoverLift()
  return <motion.button {...liftProps}>{children}</motion.button>
}
```

```tsx title="app/page.tsx"
import { LiftButton } from "@/components/animations/buttons/lift"

export default function Home() {
  return <LiftButton>Hover me!</LiftButton>
}
```

AnimBits works seamlessly with Vite. Follow these steps to set up a new Vite project.

#### Create project

Start by creating a new React project using `vite`. Select the React + TypeScript template:

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'npm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>
    ```bash
    pnpm create vite@latest my-app --template react-ts
    cd my-app
    ```
    ```bash
    npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
    cd my-app
    ```
    ```bash
    yarn create vite my-app --template react-ts
    cd my-app
    ```
    ```bash
    bun create vite my-app --template react-ts
    cd my-app
    ```

#### Install dependencies

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'npm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>
    ```bash
    pnpm install
    pnpm add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    npm install
    npm install framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    yarn
    yarn add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    bun install
    bun add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```

#### Add Tailwind CSS

<Tabs items={['pnpm', 'npm', 'yarn', 'bun']}>
    ```bash
    pnpm add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
    pnpm dlx tailwindcss init -p
    ```
    ```bash
    npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
    npx tailwindcss init -p
    ```
    ```bash
    yarn add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
    yarn dlx tailwindcss init -p
    ```
    ```bash
    bun add -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer
    bunx tailwindcss init -p
    ```

Configure your `tailwind.config.js`:

```js title="tailwind.config.js"
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
export default {
  content: [
    "./index.html",
    "./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}",
  ],
  theme: {
    extend: {},
  },
  plugins: [],
}
```

Replace everything in `src/index.css` with the following:

```css title="src/index.css"
@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;
```

#### Set up path aliases

Update your `vite.config.ts` to use path aliases:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import path from 'path'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      '@': path.resolve(__dirname, './src'),
    },
  },
})
```

Update your `tsconfig.json` (or `tsconfig.app.json`) to support path aliases:

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./src/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Add utility function

Create a `src/lib/utils.ts` file:

```ts title="src/lib/utils.ts"
import { type ClassValue, clsx } from "clsx"
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge"

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs))
}
```

### Manual Installation

For any other React framework (Remix, Gatsby, Astro with React, etc.) or custom setup.

**Step 1: Install Dependencies**

    ```bash
    npm install framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    pnpm add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    yarn add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```
    ```bash
    bun add framer-motion clsx tailwind-merge
    ```

**Step 2: Create folder structure**

Create these folders in your project (adjust paths based on your framework):

```bash
mkdir -p lib/
mkdir -p components/
```

**Step 3: Copy animation primitives**

Browse the [hooks documentation](/docs/hooks/hover-lift) and copy the hooks you need into `lib/`.

**Step 4: Use in your components**

```tsx
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useHoverLift } from "./lib/use-hover-lift"

function MyComponent() {
  const liftProps = useHoverLift({ liftDistance: 12 })
  return (
    <motion.div {...liftProps} className="card">
      Content that lifts on hover
    </motion.div>
  )
}
```

Configure your `tailwind.config.js`:

```js title="tailwind.config.js"
/** @type {import('tailwindcss').Config} */
export default {

    "./index.html",
    "./src/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}",
  ],
```

#### Set up routing

Update your `src/main.tsx` to include React Router:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { StrictMode } from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom'
import App from './App.tsx'
import './index.css'

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <BrowserRouter>
      <App />
    </BrowserRouter>
  </StrictMode>,
)
```

Create a basic router structure in `src/App.tsx`:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { Routes, Route, Link } from 'react-router-dom'
import { motion } from "motion/react"
import { useHoverLift } from './lib/use-hover-lift'

function Home() {
  const liftProps = useHoverLift()
  
  return (
    <div className="p-8">
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold mb-4">Home</h1>
      <motion.button 
        {...liftProps} 
        className="px-6 py-3 bg-blue-600 text-white rounded-lg"
      >
        Hover me!
      </motion.button>
    </div>
  )
}

function About() {
  return (
    <div className="p-8">
      <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold">About</h1>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  return (
    <div>
      <nav className="p-4 bg-gray-100">
        <Link to="/" className="mr-4 text-blue-600 hover:underline">Home</Link>
        <Link to="/about" className="text-blue-600 hover:underline">About</Link>
      </nav>
      
      <Routes>
        <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
        <Route path="/about" element={<About />} />
      </Routes>
    </div>
  )
}

export default App
```

## TypeScript Configuration

For better type support, ensure your `tsconfig.json` includes:

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "lib": ["ES2020", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "jsx": "react-jsx",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "allowJs": true,
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "paths": {
      "@/*": ["./*"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

### "Module not found" errors

Make sure your path aliases are set up correctly. Check your `tsconfig.json` or bundler configuration.

### Animations not working

Ensure Framer Motion is properly installed and you're using `motion` components from `framer-motion`.

### "use client" directive missing

If using Next.js 13+ App Router, add `"use client"` at the top of any component that uses animations.

### TypeScript errors

Make sure you're using TypeScript 4.9 or later and have proper type definitions installed.

# expanding-card.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/transitions/expanding-card.mdx

title: Expanding Card
description: Smoothly expand a card into a detail view with multiple animation styles.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { ExpandingCard } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/expanding-card';

## Overview

The `ExpandingCard` component creates a seamless transition from a compact grid view to an immersive detail view. Choose from multiple animation variants to control how cards expand.

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/expanding-card
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/expanding-card
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/expanding-card
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/expanding-card
        ```
    Copy and paste the following code into your project.

    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/expanding-card.tsx"
    "use client";

    import React, { useState, useId } from "react";
    import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
    import { X } from "lucide-react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

    export interface CardItem {
      id: number | string;
      title: string;
      description: string;
      longDescription: string;
      image: string;
    }

    interface ExpandingCardProps {
      items: CardItem[];
      className?: string;
      columns?: 2 | 3 | 4;
      variant?: "scale-center" | "slide-up" | "rotate-scale" | "elastic" | "fade-scale";
    }

    export function ExpandingCard({ items, className, columns = 3, variant = "scale-center" }: ExpandingCardProps) {
      const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<number | string | null>(null);
      const id = useId();

      const gridCols = {
        2: "md:grid-cols-2",
        3: "md:grid-cols-3",
        4: "md:grid-cols-4"
      }[columns];

      const getExpandTransition = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "scale-center":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 };
          case "slide-up":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.5 };
          case "rotate-scale":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.25, duration: 0.7 };
          case "elastic":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.4, duration: 0.8 };
          case "fade-scale":
            return { type: "tween" as const, duration: 0.3, ease: "easeOut" as const };
          default:
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 };
        }
      };

      const getExpandInitial = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "slide-up":
            return { opacity: 0, y: 50 };
          case "rotate-scale":
            return { opacity: 0, scale: 0.8, rotate: -5 };
          case "fade-scale":
            return { opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 };
          default:
            return {};
        }
      };

      const getExpandAnimate = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "slide-up":
            return { opacity: 1, y: 0 };
          case "rotate-scale":
            return { opacity: 1, scale: 1, rotate: 0 };
          case "fade-scale":
            return { opacity: 1, scale: 1 };
          default:
            return {};
        }
      };

      return (
        <div className={cn("flex flex-col items-center justify-center min-h-[600px] w-full p-8 bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-xl overflow-hidden relative", className)}>
          <div className={cn("grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 w-full max-w-6xl relative z-10", gridCols)}>
            {items.map((card) => (
              <motion.div
                key={card.id}
                layoutId={`${id}-card-${card.id}`}
                onClick={() => setSelectedId(card.id)}
                className={cn(
                  "relative overflow-hidden rounded-xl cursor-pointer shadow-lg hover:shadow-xl transition-shadow bg-white dark:bg-zinc-800",
                  "flex flex-col h-64 group"
                )}
                whileHover={{ scale: 1.02 }}
                whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }}
              >
                <motion.div
                  layoutId={`${id}-image-${card.id}`}
                  className="h-40 w-full overflow-hidden"
                >
                  <img
                    src={card.image}
                    alt={card.title}
                    className="w-full h-full object-cover transition-transform duration-500 group-hover:scale-110"
                  />
                </motion.div>
                <div className="p-4">
                  <motion.h3
                    layoutId={`${id}-title-${card.id}`}
                    className="text-lg font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100"
                  >
                    {card.title}
                  </motion.h3>
                  <motion.p
                    layoutId={`${id}-desc-${card.id}`}
                    className="text-sm text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 mt-1"
                  >
                    {card.description}
                  </motion.p>
                </div>
              </motion.div>
            ))}
          </div>

          <AnimatePresence>
            {selectedId && (
              <>
                <motion.div
                  initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
                  animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
                  exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
                  onClick={() => setSelectedId(null)}
                  className="absolute inset-0 bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-sm z-20"
                />
                <div className="absolute inset-0 flex items-center justify-center z-30 pointer-events-none p-4">
                  {items
                    .filter((c) => c.id === selectedId)
                    .map((card) => (
                      <motion.div
                        key={card.id}
                        layoutId={`${id}-card-${card.id}`}
                        className="w-full max-w-lg bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-2xl overflow-hidden shadow-2xl pointer-events-auto relative max-h-[85vh] flex flex-col"
                        transition={getExpandTransition()}
                        initial={getExpandInitial()}
                        animate={getExpandAnimate()}
                      >
                        <motion.button
                          className="absolute top-4 right-4 p-2 bg-black/10 dark:bg-white/10 rounded-full text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 z-50 hover:bg-black/20 dark:hover:bg-white/20 transition-colors"
                          onClick={(e) => {
                            e.stopPropagation();
                            setSelectedId(null);
                          }}
                          initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
                          animate={{ opacity: 1, transition: { delay: 0.2 } }}
                          exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
                        >
                          <X size={20} />
                        </motion.button>

                        <motion.div
                          layoutId={`${id}-image-${card.id}`}
                          className="h-64 w-full overflow-hidden flex-shrink-0"
                        >
                          <img
                            src={card.image}
                            alt={card.title}
                            className="w-full h-full object-cover"
                          />
                        </motion.div>

                        <div className="p-6 overflow-y-auto">
                          <motion.h3
                            layoutId={`${id}-title-${card.id}`}
                            className="text-2xl font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 mb-2"
                          >
                            {card.title}
                          </motion.h3>
                          <motion.p
                            layoutId={`${id}-desc-${card.id}`}
                            className="text-base text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400 mb-4"
                          >
                            {card.description}
                          </motion.p>

                          <motion.div
                            initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 20 }}
                            animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
                            exit={{ opacity: 0, y: 10 }}
                            transition={{ delay: 0.1 }}
                            className="text-sm text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 leading-relaxed"
                          >
                            <p>{card.longDescription}</p>
                          </motion.div>
                        </div>
                      </motion.div>
                    ))}
                </div>
              </>
            )}
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

## Props

| `items` | `CardItem[]` | - | Array of card data objects. |
| `columns` | `2 \| 3 \| 4` | `3` | Number of columns in grid layout. |
| `variant` | `"scale-center" \| "slide-up" \| "rotate-scale" \| "elastic" \| "fade-scale"` | `"scale-center"` | Animation style for card expansion. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |

## Use cases

`ExpandingCard` is built around Framer Motion's shared-layout system: the grid card and the expanded detail view share four `layoutId` values each (`card-{id}`, `image-{id}`, `title-{id}`, `desc-{id}`), so the browser morphs between them rather than cutting or fading. Use it when visual continuity between a thumbnail and its full-size detail view matters:

- **Photo and portfolio galleries.** A grid of cropped thumbnails that each expand into a hero image with a caption. The shared image `layoutId` keeps the photo in place while the card grows.
- **E-commerce product grids.** A compact product card expands to show a longer description, size options, or specs without navigating away.
- **Pricing or FAQ accordions.** A collapsed feature card (title + one-liner) expands into a full benefit explanation. `variant="fade-scale"` suits text-heavy content where the tween easing (0.3s easeOut) avoids spring overshoot on text.
- **Portfolio case studies.** A thumbnail with a project title expands into a full case-study panel. `variant="elastic"` (bounce 0.4) adds energy appropriate for creative work; drop it to `variant="scale-center"` (bounce 0.2) for professional or finance contexts.
- **Content cards in a CMS dashboard.** Editors click a post card in a grid to expand it and edit metadata inline.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ExpandingCard` when:**

- The user needs visual continuity between a compact representation and its detail view. The shared `layoutId` morph communicates "you are looking at the same item, expanded", which a simple modal fade cannot.
- Your data is already structured as a flat list of `CardItem` objects with a `longDescription` field distinct from `description`. The component renders both in the detail view.
- You have 3 to 12 cards. Fewer than three makes the grid feel empty; many more means users will be scrolling past unmounted `AnimatePresence` trees.

**Do not use `ExpandingCard` when:**

- You need deep interactivity inside the expanded view (forms with multiple steps, nested navigations). The expanded panel sits inside a `motion.div` with no focus trap or scroll lock, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot safely interact with it.
- The primary action is to navigate to a separate page. Reach for a standard `<Link>` card instead; shared-layout morphing feels misleading when the URL changes without continuity.
- Cards contain wildly different aspect-ratio images. The shared `layoutId` on the image container forces it to scale, which can distort tall portrait images during the tween.
- You want a plain dialog without the layout-morph effect. The [Shared Modal](/docs/transitions/shared-modal) component gives you the same `AnimatePresence` wrapper without coupling the trigger and dialog via shared `layoutId`.

## Accessibility notes

The current implementation uses plain `motion.div` elements for both the grid card and the overlay. There are several gaps to address before deploying in a production app:

- **Dialog semantics.** The expanded overlay is visually a dialog but carries no `role="dialog"` or `aria-modal="true"`. Add both to the expanded `motion.div` so screen readers announce it as a dialog and suppress background content.
- **Focus trap.** When the overlay opens, focus should move into the expanded card and be trapped there. Libraries like `focus-trap-react` work alongside Framer Motion without conflict.
- **Escape to close.** Handle `keydown` for `Escape` to call `setSelectedId(null)`. Without it, keyboard users cannot dismiss the overlay.
- **Return focus.** When the overlay closes, return focus to the card that triggered the expansion. Store a `ref` to the trigger before opening and call `.focus()` inside the `onAnimationComplete` callback on exit.
- **Close button label.** The `<X size={20} />` button has no visible text. Add `aria-label="Close"` to it.
- **Backdrop click.** The backdrop `motion.div` calls `setSelectedId(null)` on click, but it should also be keyboard-reachable (`role="button"` or a hidden button element).
- **Scroll lock.** Add `overflow: hidden` to `document.body` while the overlay is open so background content does not scroll behind the backdrop.

## Performance considerations

- **Shared layout measurement.** Framer Motion measures and animates layout for every element sharing a `layoutId`. Each card holds four shared elements (`card`, `image`, `title`, `desc`). With twelve cards in the grid, that is 48 layout measurements on each expand or collapse. Keep the grid to a reasonable size and avoid nesting many other `layout`-animated elements inside the same render tree.
- **`AnimatePresence` and mount cost.** The overlay is conditionally rendered inside `AnimatePresence`. It is fully mounted on open and unmounted on close, so you pay a render cost each time. This is fine for the use case but means heavy content (e.g., `<video>` elements) inside `longDescription` will remount and restart on every open.
- **Spring settling.** The `elastic` variant uses `bounce: 0.4` with a `duration: 0.8s` spring. Springs do not have a strict end time; with high bounce they can settle over 1 to 1.5 seconds. Use `bounce: 0.2` (the `scale-center` default) if users complain the animation feels slow.
- **Backdrop `backdrop-blur-sm`.** CSS `backdrop-filter` forces the GPU to composite the blurred layer separately. On mobile devices with many layers, this can cause jank. Test on low-end targets and remove the blur if frame rate drops.
- **`useId()` prefix.** The component calls `useId()` to namespace all `layoutId` values, preventing collisions if you mount multiple `ExpandingCard` instances on the same page. Do not replace these with static strings.

# shared-modal.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/transitions/shared-modal.mdx

title: Shared Modal
description: A trigger that morphs into a modal with multiple animation styles.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { SharedModal } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/shared-modal';

## Overview

The `SharedModal` uses shared layout animations to morph a trigger element into a modal dialog. Choose from multiple animation variants to match your design aesthetic.

## Preview

  code={`import { SharedModal } from "@/components/animations/transitions/shared-modal"

<SharedModal variant="scale" />`}
  <SharedModal variant="scale" />

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/shared-modal
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/shared-modal
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/shared-modal
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/shared-modal
        ```
    Copy and paste the following code into your project.

    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/shared-modal.tsx"
    "use client";

    import React, { useState, useId } from "react";
    import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
    import { Plus } from "lucide-react";

    interface SharedModalProps {
      variant?: "scale" | "slide-bottom" | "slide-right" | "fade-in" | "scale-up";
    }

    export function SharedModal({ variant = "scale" }: SharedModalProps = {}) {
      const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
      const id = useId();

      const getModalTransition = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "scale":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 };
          case "slide-bottom":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.5 };
          case "slide-right":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.5 };
          case "fade-in":
            return { type: "tween" as const, duration: 0.3, ease: "easeOut" as const };
          case "scale-up":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.5, duration: 0.8 };
          default:
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 };
        }
      };

      const getModalInitial = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "slide-bottom":
            return { opacity: 0, y: "100%" };
          case "slide-right":
            return { opacity: 0, x: "100%" };
          case "fade-in":
            return { opacity: 0, scale: 1.1 };
          case "scale-up":
            return { opacity: 0, scale: 0.5 };
          default:
            return {};
        }
      };

      const getModalAnimate = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "slide-bottom":
            return { opacity: 1, y: 0 };
          case "slide-right":
            return { opacity: 1, x: 0 };
          case "fade-in":
            return { opacity: 1, scale: 1 };
          case "scale-up":
            return { opacity: 1, scale: 1 };
          default:
            return {};
        }
      };

      return (
        <div className="flex items-center justify-center p-8 bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-xl min-h-[400px] w-full">
          <AnimatePresence>
            {!isOpen ? (
              <motion.div
                layoutId={`${id}-modal`}
                onClick={() => setIsOpen(true)}
                className="h-16 w-16 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-800 rounded-full shadow-lg cursor-pointer flex items-center justify-center border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-700"
                whileHover={{ scale: 1.05 }}
                whileTap={{ scale: 0.95 }}
              >
                <motion.div layoutId={`${id}-icon`}>
                  <Plus className="text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400" />
                </motion.div>
              </motion.div>
            ) : (
              <div className={cn(
                "fixed inset-0 z-[100] px-4 pointer-events-none",
                (variant === "slide-bottom" || variant === "slide-right") ? "flex" : "grid place-items-center",
                variant === "slide-bottom" && "items-end justify-center pb-4",
                variant === "slide-right" && "items-center justify-end pr-4"
              )}>
                <motion.div
                  initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
                  animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
                  exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
                  onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
                  className="absolute inset-0 bg-black/20 backdrop-blur-sm pointer-events-auto"
                />
                <motion.div
                  {...(variant === "scale" ? { layoutId: `${id}-modal` } : {})}
                  className="w-full max-w-sm bg-white dark:bg-zinc-800 rounded-2xl shadow-2xl overflow-hidden z-20 relative pointer-events-auto"
                  transition={getModalTransition()}
                  initial={getModalInitial()}
                  animate={getModalAnimate()}
                  exit={getModalInitial()}
                  style={{ transformPerspective: 1000 }}
                >
                  <motion.div layoutId={`${id}-icon`} className="absolute top-4 right-4 z-10">
                    <button
                      onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); setIsOpen(false); }}
                      className="p-1 rounded-full bg-black/10 dark:bg-white/10 hover:bg-black/20 dark:hover:bg-white/20 transition-colors"
                    >
                      <Plus className="rotate-45 text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400" />
                    </button>
                  </motion.div>

                  <img 
                    src="https://picsum.photos/seed/modal1/400/200" 
                    alt="Project header"
                    className="h-32 w-full object-cover"
                  />
                  <div className="p-6">
                    <h3 className="text-xl font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 mb-2">New Project</h3>
                    <p className="text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 mb-6">Create a new project to get started with your ideas.</p>
                    <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
                      <button
                        onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); setIsOpen(false); }}
                        className="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-300 hover:bg-zinc-100 dark:hover:bg-zinc-700 rounded-lg transition-colors"
                      >
                        Cancel
                      </button>
                      <button
                        onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); setIsOpen(false); }}
                        className="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium bg-zinc-900 dark:bg-zinc-100 text-white dark:text-zinc-900 rounded-lg hover:opacity-90 transition-opacity"
                      >
                        Create
                      </button>
                    </div>
                  </div>
                </motion.div>
              </div>
            )}
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

## Props

| `variant` | `"scale" \| "slide-bottom" \| "slide-right" \| "fade-in" \| "scale-up"` | `"scale"` | Animation style for modal opening. |

## Use cases

`SharedModal` wraps both the trigger element and the modal in a single `AnimatePresence`, toggling between them based on the `isOpen` boolean. In the `"scale"` variant, the trigger `motion.div` and the modal `motion.div` share the same `layoutId` (`modal`), so Framer Motion morphs one into the other. The close icon also uses a shared `layoutId` (`icon`) so the Plus icon seamlessly rotates into the dismiss button. Use this component when the visual connection between a compact trigger and the resulting dialog adds meaning:

- **"Add item" actions.** A small circular plus button morphs into a "New Project" form. The morph communicates that the form is the expansion of that button, not a separate page.
- **Image lightboxes.** A thumbnail trigger expands into a full-size preview dialog. Pair with `variant="scale"` to preserve the spatial relationship between the thumbnail and the overlay.
- **Confirmation dialogs.** A delete icon expands into a confirmation panel. `variant="fade-in"` (tween 0.3s easeOut) is calmer than a bouncy spring for destructive actions.
- **Quick forms.** Contact, feedback, or subscribe forms that should feel embedded in the page rather than navigated to. `variant="slide-bottom"` (initial `y: "100%"`) suits mobile-first layouts where bottom sheets are familiar.
- **Side panel details.** Clicking a table row triggers a `variant="slide-right"` panel (initial `x: "100%"`) that reveals the row's full record without a page change.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `SharedModal` when:**

- There is one trigger and one corresponding modal, and the visual morph between them is meaningful to the user.
- The modal content is relatively simple: a form with two or three fields, a confirmation message, or a detail preview. The component renders a fixed-height panel with a scrollable body; deeply nested UIs are awkward here.
- The trigger is small and centered on screen, so the `"scale"` morph has room to expand without jumping off-screen.

**Do not use `SharedModal` when:**

- You need to open the same modal from multiple, differently-shaped triggers. Framer Motion's `layoutId` ties the morph to a single trigger element; shared IDs across multiple triggers cause the animation to jump between them.
- The dialog needs to be fully accessible immediately (a screen reader or keyboard-only workflow). The current implementation has no focus trap, no `role="dialog"`, and no Escape key handler. Use a headless dialog primitive (Radix UI `Dialog`, Headless UI `Dialog`) with a custom `AnimatePresence` wrapper instead.
- You want a slide-over drawer that persists across navigations. A drawer component with `position: fixed` and controlled open state is a better fit.
- The morph effect is not worth the complexity. For a plain centered modal without a trigger-to-dialog animation, the overhead of shared `layoutId` is unnecessary. A simple `AnimatePresence` fade is cleaner.

Compare with [Expanding Card](/docs/transitions/expanding-card): `ExpandingCard` morphs one item out of a grid into a detail panel; `SharedModal` morphs a single floating trigger into a dialog. If you have a grid of triggers, use `ExpandingCard`.

## Accessibility notes

The current implementation needs these additions before it is safe for keyboard and screen-reader users:

- **Role and label.** Add `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="true"` to the expanded `motion.div`. Add `aria-labelledby` pointing to the modal's `<h3>` id so screen readers announce the dialog title when it opens.
- **Focus trap.** On open, move focus to the first interactive element inside the modal (the Cancel button or the close button). Use `focus-trap-react` or manually call `.focus()` inside the `animate` callback. Without this, keyboard users remain focused on the backdrop.
- **Escape to close.** Add a `keydown` listener on `document` for `Escape` that calls `setIsOpen(false)`. Remove the listener on unmount.
- **Return focus.** Store a ref to the trigger element before opening and restore focus to it when the dialog closes. This is especially important when the trigger is re-rendered after the `AnimatePresence` exit because the trigger `motion.div` only exists when `!isOpen`.
- **Scroll lock.** While the modal is open, set `document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"` to prevent background scroll. Restore it on close.
- **Close button label.** The rotated Plus icon used as a close button has no accessible text. Add `aria-label="Close dialog"` to that `<button>`.

## Performance considerations

- **Single `layoutId` constraint.** The `"scale"` variant connects the trigger and modal via a shared `layoutId`. Framer Motion measures both elements before and after the state change to compute the layout delta. This is a single measurement, but it takes a synchronous read of the DOM. Keep the trigger and modal subtrees shallow.
- **`AnimatePresence` mount and unmount.** The trigger and the modal are mutually exclusive inside `AnimatePresence`. When opening, the trigger exits (unmounts) and the modal enters (mounts). On close, the reverse happens. This means the modal's children re-render from scratch on every open. Avoid putting expensive computations directly in the modal's render; memoize or fetch data before mounting.
- **`backdrop-blur-sm` backdrop.** The `bg-black/20 backdrop-blur-sm` overlay is GPU-composited. On mobile browsers and devices with many stacking contexts, blur compositing is expensive. Test on real hardware and remove the blur if needed.
- **`transformPerspective: 1000` style.** This is set directly on the modal `motion.div`. It creates a stacking context and can prevent certain CSS optimizations. Only relevant if you are layering many 3D-transformed elements.
- **Variants `"slide-bottom"` and `"slide-right"`.** These do not use `layoutId`; they use plain `initial`/`animate`/`exit` values (`y: "100%"` or `x: "100%"`). This is cheaper than shared layout because no measurement is needed, just a transform animation.

## Real-world examples

### Image lightbox

A thumbnail expands into a full-size overlay. The `"scale"` variant keeps the image's position in space while it grows.

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState, useId } from "react"
import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react"

export function ImageLightbox({ src, alt }: { src: string; alt: string }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const id = useId()

  return (
    <>
      <AnimatePresence>
        {!open && (
          <motion.img
            layoutId={`${id}-img`}
            src={src}
            alt={alt}
            onClick={() => setOpen(true)}
            className="w-48 h-32 object-cover rounded-lg cursor-pointer shadow-md"
          />
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>
      <AnimatePresence>
        {open && (
          <>
            <motion.div
              initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
              animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
              exit={{ opacity: 0 }}
              onClick={() => setOpen(false)}
              className="fixed inset-0 z-40 bg-black/70"
            />
            <motion.img
              layoutId={`${id}-img`}
              src={src}
              alt={alt}
              className="fixed inset-0 m-auto z-50 max-w-3xl max-h-[80vh] object-contain rounded-xl shadow-2xl"
              transition={{ type: "spring", bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.5 }}
            />
          </>
        )}
      </AnimatePresence>
    </>
  )
}
```

### "New task" button that expands into a form

The floating action button morphs into a task creation form. After submit the form dismisses and the button reappears in place.

```tsx
"use client"
import { SharedModal } from "@/components/animations/transitions/shared-modal"

export function TaskPage() {
  return (
    <div className="relative min-h-screen bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-950 p-8">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 mb-6">My Tasks</h1>
      {/* task list here */}
      <div className="fixed bottom-6 right-6">
        <SharedModal variant="scale" />
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/tab-switcher
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/tab-switcher
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/tab-switcher
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/tab-switcher
        ```
    Copy and paste the following code into your project.

    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/tab-switcher.tsx"
    "use client";

    import React, { useState, useId } from "react";
    import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

    interface Tab {
      id: string;
      label: string;
      content: React.ReactNode;
      icon?: React.ReactNode;
    }

    interface TabSwitcherProps {
      tabs: Tab[];
      defaultTab?: string;
      className?: string;
      variant?: "pill" | "underline" | "segmented";
    }

    export function TabSwitcher({ tabs, defaultTab, className, variant = "pill" }: TabSwitcherProps) {
      const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState(defaultTab || tabs[0].id);
      const id = useId();

      return (
        <div className={cn("flex flex-col items-center justify-start p-8 bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-xl min-h-[400px] w-full", className)}>
          <div className={cn(
            "flex items-center",
            variant === "pill" && "space-x-1 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-950 p-1.5 rounded-full shadow-sm border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800",
            variant === "underline" && "border-b border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 w-full justify-center gap-8",
            variant === "segmented" && "bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-800 p-1 rounded-lg w-full max-w-md"
          )}>
            {tabs.map((tab) => (
              <button
                key={tab.id}
                onClick={() => setActiveTab(tab.id)}
                className={cn(
                  "relative px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold outline-none transition-colors duration-200 z-10 flex items-center gap-2",
                  variant === "pill" && "rounded-full",
                  variant === "underline" && "rounded-t-md pb-3",
                  variant === "segmented" && "rounded-md flex-1",
                  activeTab === tab.id
                    ? "text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100"
                    : "text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-700 dark:hover:text-zinc-200"
                )}
                style={{ WebkitTapHighlightColor: "transparent" }}
              >
                {activeTab === tab.id && variant === "pill" && (
                  <motion.div
                    layoutId={`${id}-bubble`}
                    className="absolute inset-0 bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-800 rounded-full -z-10 shadow-sm border border-zinc-200/50 dark:border-zinc-700/50"
                    transition={{ type: "spring", bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 }}
                  />
                )}
                {activeTab === tab.id && variant === "underline" && (
                  <motion.div
                    layoutId={`${id}-underline`}
                    className="absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 h-0.5 bg-zinc-900 dark:bg-zinc-100"
                    transition={{ type: "spring", bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 }}
                  />
                )}
                {activeTab === tab.id && variant === "segmented" && (
                  <motion.div
                    layoutId={`${id}-segmented`}
                    className="absolute inset-0 bg-white dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-md -z-10 shadow-sm"
                    transition={{ type: "spring", bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 }}
                  />
                )}
                {tab.icon && <span className="w-4 h-4">{tab.icon}</span>}
                {tab.label}
              </button>
            ))}
          </div>

          <motion.div
            layout
            className="mt-8 w-full max-w-md bg-white dark:bg-zinc-950 rounded-2xl p-6 shadow-sm border border-zinc-100 dark:border-zinc-800 overflow-hidden"
            transition={{ duration: 0.3 }}
          >
            <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
              {tabs.map((tab) =>
                tab.id === activeTab ? (
                  <motion.div
                    key={tab.id}
                    initial={{ opacity: 0, x: -10 }}
                    animate={{ opacity: 1, x: 0 }}
                    exit={{ opacity: 0, x: 10 }}
                    transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}
                    className="text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400 text-sm"
                  >
                    {tab.content}
                  </motion.div>
                ) : null
              )}
            </AnimatePresence>
          </motion.div>
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

        icon: <Bell size={16} />,

          <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 mb-2">Notifications</h3>
          <p>3 new notifications</p>
      },
      { 
        id: "settings", 
        label: "Settings", 
        icon: <Settings size={16} />,
        content: <div className="p-6 text-center text-zinc-600 dark:text-zinc-400">
          <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 mb-2">Settings</h3>
          <p>Configure your preferences</p>
      },
    ]} 
  />

## Props

| `tabs` | `Tab[]` | - | Array of tab objects with id, label, content, and optional icon. |
| `defaultTab` | `string` | `tabs[0].id` | ID of the initially active tab. |
| `variant` | `"pill" \| "underline" \| "segmented"` | `"pill"` | Visual style of the tab indicator. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |

## Use cases

`TabSwitcher` drives its active indicator with a single `layoutId` per variant: `bubble` for pill, `underline` for underline, and `segmented` for the segmented control. Switching tabs moves that `motion.div` to the new button using a spring (`bounce: 0.2`, `duration: 0.6`). Content transitions use `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` with a short fade-and-slide (`opacity`, `x: -10/10`, `duration: 0.2`). Use it when:

- **Dashboard sections.** Overview, Analytics, and Reports are parallel content panels for the same entity. The `"underline"` variant reads as a formal navigation row above a data table.
- **Settings pages.** General, Security, Notifications, and Billing are mutually exclusive panels. The `"segmented"` variant (full-width, iOS-style) signals "pick exactly one" clearly.
- **Product detail pages.** Description, Specifications, and Reviews are all about the same product. The `"pill"` variant is compact enough to sit near the product title without dominating the layout.
- **Time-range pickers.** Daily, Weekly, Monthly controls that update a chart below them. Use `"segmented"` because the three options are equal-width and semantically a choice among three mutually exclusive values.
- **Feature comparison tabs.** Features, Pricing, and Testimonials on a marketing page. `"underline"` suits long labels; the indicator glides smoothly between them.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `TabSwitcher` when:**

- Content panels are mutually exclusive and roughly equal in importance. Tabs are the right pattern when the user should look at one section at a time.
- You have 2 to 6 tabs. Fewer than two gives you a toggle; more than six and the labels overflow or become unreadable on mobile.
- The tab labels fit on one line. The indicator animation relies on each tab button having a stable position; wrapping to a second line breaks the `layoutId` morph.

**Do not use `TabSwitcher` when:**

- You need to **switch the layout of the same data** (grid vs. list of the same items). That is a view mode toggle, not a tab navigation. Use [View Toggle](/docs/transitions/view-toggle) instead.
- The content panels are independent pages with their own URLs. Use real navigation with `<Link>` elements and URL-driven routing; client-side tabs that should be linkable are an antipattern.
- One of the panels is significantly more important than the others and should always be visible. Use progressive disclosure or a details/summary element instead.
- You have only two options and one is "on" or "off". A labeled toggle switch is more appropriate.

## Accessibility notes

The source uses plain `<button>` elements inside a flex container. This is functional for mouse users but fails several ARIA tab requirements. Before shipping in production, wire up the roles so each button and panel are linked:

```tsx
<div role="tablist" aria-label="Section navigation">
  <button
    role="tab"
    aria-selected={activeTab === tab.id}
    aria-controls={`panel-${tab.id}`}
  >
    {tab.label}
  </button>
</div>

<div role="tabpanel" id={`panel-${tab.id}`}>
  {tab.content}
</div>
```

- **Tab list and tab roles.** Wrap the button row in `role="tablist"` with an `aria-label`, and give each button `role="tab"`.
- **Tab panel role.** The content container for each tab needs `role="tabpanel"` and an `id` that matches the button's `aria-controls`, so the link resolves.
- **Arrow-key navigation.** The ARIA tabs pattern requires `ArrowLeft` and `ArrowRight` to move focus between tabs, with `Home` and `End` for first and last. Mouse-only `onClick` is insufficient. Implement a roving tabindex: set `tabIndex={0}` on the active tab and `tabIndex={-1}` on all others, then update it in a `keydown` handler.
- **`aria-selected`.** Currently the active tab is distinguished only by visual styling. Screen readers need `aria-selected="true"` on the active tab and `aria-selected="false"` on all others.
- **Keyboard activation.** The ARIA tabs pattern uses automatic activation on focus (focus moves + content updates) or manual activation (focus moves, user presses Enter or Space to activate). Pick one and be consistent.
- **Icon-only tabs.** If you pass icons without labels, add `aria-label` to each button.

## Performance considerations

- **Single `layoutId` indicator.** Each variant tracks one `motion.div` (the indicator) across tabs. This is a lightweight shared layout: Framer Motion measures only that element's bounding rect before and after the active tab changes. The spring animation runs on the compositor.
- **`AnimatePresence mode="wait"`.** The content panel uses `mode="wait"`, which means the old content exits completely before the new content enters. This prevents two panels from being in the DOM simultaneously, keeping memory usage low. The tradeoff is a brief gap (equal to the exit duration, 0.2s) before new content appears.
- **Content size changes.** The content wrapper has `layout` set, so Framer Motion will re-measure and animate the wrapper's height when the active panel changes height. If your tabs have very different content heights, this layout animation adds to the per-switch cost. Set a fixed `min-h` on the wrapper to avoid height jumping.
- **`useId()` prefix.** The component namespaces `layoutId` values with `useId()`. Mounting multiple `TabSwitcher` instances on the same page is safe; the indicators will not cross-animate.

## Customization examples

### Controlled tab with external state

Read and set the active tab from outside the component using `defaultTab` and an `onChange` pattern. Currently the component is uncontrolled (no `onChange` prop), so you would need to either lift state or copy the component and add a controlled prop:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useState } from "react"

  { id: "settings", label: "Settings", content: <div className="p-6">Settings panel</div> },
]

  return (
    <TabSwitcher
      tabs={tabs}
      defaultTab="settings"
      variant="underline"
    />
  )
}
```

# theme-toggle-circular.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular.mdx

title: Theme Toggle Circular
description: Circular ripple animation for theme toggle using View Transitions API.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';
import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { TransitionDemo } from '@/components/transition-demo';
import { ThemeToggleCircular } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-circular';

## Overview

The `ThemeToggleCircular` component creates an expanding circle effect from the click position when toggling themes. The new theme always expands from the click point, creating a natural ripple effect. Uses the native View Transitions API for smooth, hardware-accelerated animations with customizable speed and blur.

<Callout type="info">
  **Browser Support:** View Transitions API is supported in Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, and Opera 97+. Falls back to instant theme changes in unsupported browsers.
</Callout>

## Interactive Demo

Try it live! Adjust the speed and blur sliders, then click the button to see the transition effect.

<Preview background="grid">
  <TransitionDemo TransitionComponent={ThemeToggleCircular} />

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-circular
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-circular
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-circular
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-circular
        ```
    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-circular.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
export interface ThemeToggleCircularProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  onToggle?: () => void;
  theme?: "light" | "dark";
  className?: string;
  speed?: number;
  blur?: number;
}
export function ThemeToggleCircular({
  children,
  onToggle,
  theme,
  className,
  speed = 0.5,
  blur = 0,
}: ThemeToggleCircularProps) {
  const [isTransitioning, setIsTransitioning] = React.useState(false);
  const handleClick = async (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    if (isTransitioning) return;
    if (!document.startViewTransition) {
      onToggle?.();
      return;
    }
    setIsTransitioning(true);
    const x = e.clientX;
    const y = e.clientY;
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark");
    const targetTheme = isDark ? "to-light" : "to-dark";
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--x", `${x}px`);
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty("--y", `${y}px`);
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--transition-speed",
      `${speed}s`,
    );
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--transition-blur",
      `${blur}px`,
    );
    document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme-transition", targetTheme);
    try {
      const transition = document.startViewTransition(() => {
        onToggle?.();
      });
      await transition.finished;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error("Theme transition error:", error);
    } finally {
      document.documentElement.removeAttribute("data-theme-transition");
      setIsTransitioning(false);
    }
  };
  return (
    <div
      onClick={handleClick}
      className={className}
      style={{ pointerEvents: isTransitioning ? "none" : "auto" }}
    >
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

```

    **Required CSS** (add to `globals.css`):
    ```css
    /* Circular ripple animation origin variables */
    :root {
      --transition-speed: 0.5s;
      --transition-blur: 0px;
      --x: 50%;
      --y: 50%;
    }

    /* Base View Transition Configuration */
    ::view-transition-group(root) {
      animation: none;
      isolation: isolate;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    ::view-transition-image-pair(root) {
      isolation: isolate;
      overflow: hidden;
    }

    /* Apply blur if specified */
    ::view-transition-old(root),
    ::view-transition-new(root) {
      filter: blur(var(--transition-blur));
      overflow: hidden;
      backface-visibility: hidden;
      contain: paint;
    }

    /* Light → Dark: Dark theme expands from click position */
    [data-theme-transition="to-dark"]::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: none;
      z-index: -1;
      mix-blend-mode: normal;
    }

    [data-theme-transition="to-dark"]::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: circle var(--transition-speed) ease-in-out;
      will-change: clip-path;
      mix-blend-mode: normal;
      z-index: 1;
      transform: translateZ(0);
    }

    /* Dark → Light: Dark shrinks away, revealing light underneath */
    [data-theme-transition="to-light"]::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: circle-reverse var(--transition-speed) ease-in-out;
      will-change: clip-path;
      z-index: 1;
      transform: translateZ(0);
    }

    [data-theme-transition="to-light"]::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: none;
      mix-blend-mode: normal;
      z-index: -1;
    }

    /* Circle expand animation */
    @keyframes circle {
      from {
        clip-path: circle(0% at var(--x) var(--y));
      }
      to {
        clip-path: circle(150% at var(--x) var(--y));
      }
    }

    /* Circle shrink animation */
    @keyframes circle-reverse {
      from {
        clip-path: circle(150% at var(--x) var(--y));
      }
      to {
        clip-path: circle(0% at var(--x) var(--y));
      }
    }

    /* Disable animations for reduced motion preference */
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      ::view-transition-group(*),
      ::view-transition-old(*),
      ::view-transition-new(*) {
        animation: none !important;
      }
    }
    ```

## Usage

### With next-themes

```tsx
"use client"

import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleCircular } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-circular"
import { Moon, Sun } from "lucide-react"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { setTheme } = useTheme()
  
  const toggleTheme = () => {
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
    if (isDark) {
      document.documentElement.classList.remove("dark")
      setTheme("light")
    } else {
      document.documentElement.classList.add("dark")
      setTheme("dark")
    }
  }
  
  return (
    <ThemeToggleCircular onToggle={toggleTheme}>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="icon">
        <Sun className="h-5 w-5 rotate-0 scale-100 transition-all dark:-rotate-90 dark:scale-0" />
        <Moon className="absolute h-5 w-5 rotate-90 scale-0 transition-all dark:rotate-0 dark:scale-100" />
      </Button>
    </ThemeToggleCircular>
  )
}
```

### With Custom State

```tsx
"use client"

import { useState } from "react"
import { ThemeToggleCircular } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-circular"

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState<"light" | "dark">("light")
  
  const toggleTheme = () => {
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
    const newTheme = isDark ? "light" : "dark"
    
    setTheme(newTheme)
    
    if (isDark) {
      document.documentElement.classList.remove("dark")
    } else {
      document.documentElement.classList.add("dark")
    }
  }
  
  return (
    <ThemeToggleCircular theme={theme} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
      <button className="p-2 rounded-md hover:bg-accent">
        {theme === 'dark' ? '🌞' : '🌙'}
      </button>
    </ThemeToggleCircular>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger element (button, icon, etc.) |
| `onToggle` | `() => void` | - | Callback when theme should toggle |
| `theme` | `"light"` \| `"dark"` | - | Current theme (optional) |
| `speed` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation speed in seconds |
| `blur` | `number` | `0` | Blur amount in pixels |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`ThemeToggleCircular` reads the click coordinates (`e.clientX`, `e.clientY`) and stores them as `--x` and `--y` CSS custom properties on `<html>`. The CSS then drives a `clip-path: circle(0% at var(--x) var(--y))` to `circle(150% at ...)` keyframe animation on the `::view-transition-new(root)` pseudo-element when going to dark, and the reverse (`circle-reverse`) when going to light. The result is a radial reveal that originates from the exact point where the user clicked, which feels intentional and spatial.

Use it when:

- Your navbar or header has a Sun/Moon toggle button and you want the theme change to feel tied to that specific button rather than emanating from an edge of the screen.
- The toggle can appear anywhere on the page (floating action button, inline settings toggle, command palette shortcut). Because the origin is the click point, it works regardless of button position.
- You want the ripple to feel "organic": `speed=0.3` to `0.5` with `blur=0` gives a crisp, fast reveal; `speed=0.8` with `blur=8` gives a softer, dreamlike wash.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use circular when:**

- The toggle button can be anywhere on the screen and the radial origin naturally follows it. This variant reads as the most spatially grounded of the five.
- You want a single, direction-agnostic reveal. The circular keyframe works well at any button position without looking awkward.

**Consider a different variant when:**

- Your layout has a natural horizontal or vertical axis and you want the transition to reinforce it. A sidebar-based toggle that slides the page from left to right is more meaningful with [Slide Left](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left) or [Slide Right](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right).
- The toggle is always at the top of the page (in a sticky nav). [Slide Top](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top) (new theme slides down from the top) or [Slide Bottom](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom) (new theme slides up from the bottom) aligns the animation direction with the button's screen position.
- You want zero-configuration without needing to track `clientX`/`clientY`. The four slide variants (`slide-top`, `slide-bottom`, `slide-left`, `slide-right`) do not need click coordinates; they are simpler to drop in.

**Do not use any theme toggle when:**

- The transition animation is purely cosmetic and your users are on devices or browsers that do not support the View Transitions API (Firefox as of mid-2025, Safari before 18). All five variants fall back to an instant theme change via the `!document.startViewTransition` guard, which is safe.

## Accessibility notes

- **Accessible name on the trigger.** `ThemeToggleCircular` renders a wrapper `<div>` and delegates the click. Your `children` must be a button or include an accessible label. Use `<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Toggle theme">` so screen readers announce the action.
- **`aria-pressed` or role switch.** The toggle button should communicate its current state. Either use `aria-pressed={isDark}` on an icon button, or a `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`. Without it, screen reader users hear "Toggle theme button" with no indication of the current value.
- **The clip-path animation is decorative.** The theme change itself (class toggling on `<html>`) must happen synchronously inside the `startViewTransition` callback, which it does via `onToggle?.()`. Users who switch themes rapidly or interrupt the transition still get the correct theme because the DOM change is not gated on the animation finishing.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`.** The CSS already includes `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { ::view-transition-group(*), ::view-transition-old(*), ::view-transition-new(*) { animation: none !important; } }`. For users who prefer reduced motion, the theme switches instantly with no circle animation. This is correct behavior and requires no extra JavaScript.
- **`isTransitioning` guard.** The component sets `pointerEvents: none` during the transition and bails out early if a transition is already in progress. This prevents double-firing but also means the button is briefly unreachable. Ensure the `speed` is short enough (0.3 to 0.8s) that users do not notice the brief unresponsiveness.

## Performance considerations

- **View Transitions API is hardware-accelerated.** `document.startViewTransition` takes a snapshot of the current page, applies the DOM change, then cross-fades using `::view-transition-old` and `::view-transition-new` pseudo-elements. The browser composites these as GPU layers, so the circular `clip-path` animation avoids layout and paint.
- **`clip-path: circle(...)` is GPU-friendly** when painted on a compositor layer. The `will-change: clip-path` declaration in the CSS primes the layer in advance, but keep the viewport pixel count in mind: a full-screen clip-path on a 4K display still moves many pixels per frame. Keep `speed` at or below 0.6s for large displays.
- **`blur` prop performance.** Setting `blur` to any value greater than 0 applies `filter: blur()` via the `--transition-blur` CSS variable to both `::view-transition-old` and `::view-transition-new`. CSS blur is expensive on large surfaces; use it sparingly (4 to 8px maximum) and only on desktop-class hardware.
- **One transition at a time.** The `isTransitioning` boolean prevents overlapping `startViewTransition` calls. Rapid theme toggling without this guard can leave stale `data-theme-transition` attributes on `<html>`, breaking subsequent animations. The `finally` block in `handleClick` cleans up the attribute reliably.
- **No Framer Motion cost.** This component does not use `motion` or `AnimatePresence`; it relies entirely on the native View Transitions API. There is no Framer Motion overhead at runtime.

## Customization examples

### Bouncy circular reveal

Override the easing with a cubic-bezier that overshoots:

```css
[data-theme-transition="to-dark"]::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: circle var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.27, 1.55);
}
[data-theme-transition="to-light"]::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: circle-reverse var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.27, 1.55);
}
```

### Asymmetric speeds

Go to dark quickly, return to light slowly:

```css
[data-theme-transition="to-dark"]::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: circle 0.3s ease-out;
}
[data-theme-transition="to-light"]::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: circle-reverse 0.8s ease-in;
}
```

### Blurred dream transition

Add a blur for an impressionistic feel on desktop:

```tsx
<ThemeToggleCircular speed={0.7} blur={12} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
  <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Toggle theme">
    <Sun className="h-5 w-5 dark:hidden" />
    <Moon className="h-5 w-5 hidden dark:block" />
  </Button>
</ThemeToggleCircular>
```

## Real-world examples

### Navbar theme toggle (next-themes)

The most common integration: a Sun/Moon button in the top navigation bar that triggers a radial reveal from the button's click position.

```tsx
"use client"
import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleCircular } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-circular"
import { Moon, Sun } from "lucide-react"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function NavbarThemeToggle() {
  const { setTheme } = useTheme()

  const toggleTheme = () => {
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", !isDark)
    setTheme(isDark ? "light" : "dark")
  }

  return (
    <nav className="flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4 border-b border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800">
      <span className="font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100">Acme</span>
      <ThemeToggleCircular onToggle={toggleTheme} speed={0.5}>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Toggle theme">
          <Sun className="h-5 w-5 rotate-0 scale-100 dark:-rotate-90 dark:scale-0 transition-all" />
          <Moon className="absolute h-5 w-5 rotate-90 scale-0 dark:rotate-0 dark:scale-100 transition-all" />
        </Button>
      </ThemeToggleCircular>
    </nav>
  )
}
```

### Settings page toggle with label

A labeled row in a settings panel, where the circular reveal clarifies which side of the screen is "activating" the change:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleCircular } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-circular"
import { Switch } from "@/components/ui/switch"
import { Label } from "@/components/ui/label"

export function AppearanceRow() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()
  const isDark = theme === "dark"

  const toggleTheme = () => {
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", !isDark)
    setTheme(isDark ? "light" : "dark")
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center justify-between py-4 border-b border-zinc-100 dark:border-zinc-800">
      <Label htmlFor="theme-toggle" className="text-sm font-medium text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100">
        Dark mode
      </Label>
      <ThemeToggleCircular onToggle={toggleTheme} speed={0.4}>
        <Switch id="theme-toggle" checked={isDark} aria-label="Toggle dark mode" />
      </ThemeToggleCircular>
    </div>
  )
}
```

## Customization

### Custom Easing

You can customize the easing function for different animation feels:

```css
/* Bouncy effect */
[data-theme-transition="to-dark"]::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: circle var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55);
}

[data-theme-transition="to-light"]::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: circle-reverse var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55);
}
```

### Different Speeds Per Direction

```css
/* Faster when going to dark */
[data-theme-transition="to-dark"]::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: circle 0.3s ease-out;
}

/* Slower when going to light */
[data-theme-transition="to-light"]::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: circle-reverse 0.7s ease-in;
}
```
