# theme-toggle-slide-bottom.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom.mdx

title: Theme Toggle Slide Bottom
description: Bottom to top slide animation for theme toggle using View Transitions API.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';
import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { TransitionDemo } from '@/components/transition-demo';
import { ThemeToggleSlideBottom } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom';

## Overview

The `ThemeToggleSlideBottom` component creates a slide-up effect from the bottom when toggling themes. Uses the native View Transitions API with customizable speed and blur.

<Callout type="info">
  **Browser Support:** View Transitions API is supported in Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, and Opera 97+. Falls back to instant theme changes in unsupported browsers.
</Callout>

## Interactive Demo

Try it live! Adjust the speed and blur sliders, then click the button to see the transition effect.

<Preview background="grid">
  <TransitionDemo TransitionComponent={ThemeToggleSlideBottom} />

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-bottom
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-bottom
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-bottom
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-bottom
        ```
    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
export interface ThemeToggleSlideBottomProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  onToggle?: () => void;
  theme?: "light" | "dark";
  className?: string;
  speed?: number;
  blur?: number;
}
export function ThemeToggleSlideBottom({
  children,
  onToggle,
  theme,
  className,
  speed = 0.5,
  blur = 0,
}: ThemeToggleSlideBottomProps) {
  const [isTransitioning, setIsTransitioning] = React.useState(false);
  const handleClick = async () => {
    if (isTransitioning) return;
    if (!document.startViewTransition) {
      onToggle?.();
      return;
    }
    setIsTransitioning(true);
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--transition-speed",
      `${speed}s`,
    );
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--transition-blur",
      `${blur}px`,
    );
    document.documentElement.classList.add("theme-slide-bottom");
    const transition = document.startViewTransition(() => {
      onToggle?.();
    });
    try {
      await transition.finished;
    } catch (error) {
      console.warn("Theme transition interrupted:", error);
    } finally {
      document.documentElement.classList.remove("theme-slide-bottom");
      setIsTransitioning(false);
    }
  };
  return (
    <div
      onClick={handleClick}
      className={className}
      style={{ pointerEvents: isTransitioning ? "none" : "auto" }}
    >
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

```

    **Required CSS** (add to `globals.css`):
    ```css
    :root {
      --transition-speed: 0.5s;
      --transition-blur: 0px;
    }

    .theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: slide-out-bottom var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
      filter: blur(var(--transition-blur));
    }

    .theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: slide-in-bottom var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
      filter: blur(var(--transition-blur));
    }

    @keyframes slide-out-bottom {
      to {
        transform: translateY(100%);
      }
    }

    @keyframes slide-in-bottom {
      from {
        transform: translateY(100%);
      }
    }

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-group(*),
      .theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-old(*),
      .theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-new(*) {
        animation: none !important;
      }
    }
    ```

## Usage

### With next-themes

```tsx
"use client"

import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideBottom } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()
  
  return (
    <ThemeToggleSlideBottom 
      onToggle={() => setTheme(theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')}
      speed={0.5}
      blur={0}
    >
      <Button>Toggle Theme</Button>
    </ThemeToggleSlideBottom>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger element (button, icon, etc.) |
| `onToggle` | `() => void` | - | Callback when theme should toggle |
| `theme` | `"light"` \| `"dark"` | - | Current theme (optional) |
| `speed` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation speed in seconds |
| `blur` | `number` | `0` | Blur amount in pixels |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`ThemeToggleSlideBottom` adds the class `theme-slide-bottom` to `<html>` before calling `document.startViewTransition`, then removes it in the `finally` block. The CSS pairs `slide-out-bottom` (`translateY(100%)` exit) and `slide-in-bottom` (`translateY(100%)` enter) on the `::view-transition-old` and `::view-transition-new` layers respectively, both using `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`. The current page slides down and off, and the new theme slides up from the bottom to replace it.

Use it when:

- Your theme toggle is in a bottom navigation bar, a footer, or a mobile bottom sheet. The upward direction of the reveal reinforces the idea that the change is "coming from" the area near the control.
- You are designing a mobile-first app where upward swipes and bottom sheets are familiar interaction patterns. The slide-up aligns with that vocabulary.
- You want the simplest directional slide with a single, clear axis. `slide-bottom` is the most "uplifting" feeling of the four slide variants and reads positively for switching to a lighter theme.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use slide-bottom when:**

- The toggle button lives near the bottom of the viewport (mobile nav, floating footer button). The upward reveal originates from the same region as the control, creating spatial coherence.
- Your app has a bottom tab bar and switching themes feels like "refreshing from the ground up."

**Consider a different variant when:**

- The toggle is in a top navigation bar. [Slide Top](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top) (new theme cascades down from the top) or [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular) (ripple from the exact click point) better matches a top-bar button.
- Your layout is horizontal (side-by-side panels) and you want the transition to respect that axis. [Slide Left](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left) or [Slide Right](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right) are more appropriate.
- You want the origin point to follow the cursor. [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular) does this and is more spatially expressive.

**Do not use any theme toggle when:**

- The browser does not support `document.startViewTransition`. All five variants fall back to an instant theme change, which is correct behavior.

## Accessibility notes

- **Trigger must be a real button.** `ThemeToggleSlideBottom` wraps `children` in a `<div onClick={...}>`. Your `children` must include a semantic `<button>` or `<input type="checkbox">` so the toggle is keyboard-focusable and announced correctly by screen readers.
- **`aria-pressed` or `role="switch"`.** Add `aria-pressed={isDark}` to the button child, or use a `<Switch>` component with `aria-checked`. Without a pressed/checked state, screen reader users cannot tell the current theme.
- **Accessible name.** Provide `aria-label="Toggle theme"` (or similar) on the inner button, especially if the visible content is an icon only.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`.** The CSS already handles this: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` sets `animation: none !important` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements when the `.theme-slide-bottom` class is present. Users who prefer reduced motion get an instant theme swap.
- **Animation duration.** Keep `speed` between 0.3 and 0.8 seconds. Longer durations block user input (`pointerEvents: none` is set during the transition) and may frustrate users who toggle themes frequently.

## Performance considerations

- **Transform-only animation.** `slide-out-bottom` and `slide-in-bottom` animate only `translateY`, which runs on the compositor with no layout or paint. The animation is as cheap as a CSS transition on `transform`.
- **No click-coordinate tracking.** Unlike [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular), this variant does not read `clientX`/`clientY`. There is no synchronous DOM read on click, making the handler slightly lighter.
- **`cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`.** This is Material Design's standard easing (`ease-in-out` family). It has a gentle ease-in and a soft ease-out, which looks polished at `speed=0.5`. At `speed=0.2` it can look abrupt because there is not enough duration for the curve to register; keep `speed` at or above 0.3 for this easing.
- **`blur` prop.** `filter: blur()` on the `::view-transition-old` and `::view-transition-new` layers is applied to the full-viewport snapshot. On mobile GPUs, full-screen blur is expensive. Only use `blur` on desktop-class hardware, and keep values at or below 8px.
- **One active transition at a time.** The `isTransitioning` flag prevents overlapping `startViewTransition` calls. The `theme-slide-bottom` class is cleaned up in `finally`, so it is always removed even if the transition is interrupted.

## Customization examples

### Snappier slide with ease-out

Override the easing in your globals.css to emphasize the arrival rather than the departure:

```css
.theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: slide-out-bottom var(--transition-speed) ease-in;
}
.theme-slide-bottom::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: slide-in-bottom var(--transition-speed) ease-out;
}
```

### Faster bottom toggle for mobile

The default 0.5s can feel long on mobile where users expect snappy feedback:

```tsx
<ThemeToggleSlideBottom speed={0.3} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
  <button aria-label="Toggle theme" className="p-3 rounded-full bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-800">
    <Sun className="h-5 w-5 dark:hidden" />
    <Moon className="h-5 w-5 hidden dark:block" />
  </button>
</ThemeToggleSlideBottom>
```

## Usage

### With next-themes

```tsx
"use client"

import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideLeft } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()
  
  return (
    <ThemeToggleSlideLeft 
      onToggle={() => setTheme(theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')}
      speed={0.5}
      blur={0}
    >
      <Button>Toggle Theme</Button>
    </ThemeToggleSlideLeft>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger element (button, icon, etc.) |
| `onToggle` | `() => void` | - | Callback when theme should toggle |
| `theme` | `"light"` \| `"dark"` | - | Current theme (optional) |
| `speed` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation speed in seconds |
| `blur` | `number` | `0` | Blur amount in pixels |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`ThemeToggleSlideLeft` adds `theme-slide-left` to `<html>` before the `startViewTransition` call. The CSS animates `slide-out-left` (`translateX(-100%)` on the old snapshot) and `slide-in-left` (`translateX(-100%)` start on the new snapshot) using `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`. The current page slides out to the left while the new theme arrives from the same direction, creating a left-to-right page-flip.

Use it when:

- Your layout reads left to right and the theme toggle is part of a horizontal control (e.g., a left sidebar toggle button, a left-aligned navbar item). The slide direction reinforces the spatial origin.
- You want the transition to feel like "going forward" in a left-to-right context, for example a multi-step wizard where dark mode is presented as a "next" option.
- Your app uses a left drawer or left sidebar and you want theme changes to visually originate from the same side.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use slide-left when:**

- The toggle is in a left sidebar or left-anchored nav. The leftward departure and leftward arrival creates a sense that the theme "comes from" the sidebar.
- You want a horizontal transition and the new theme should feel like it is arriving from the left side of the screen.

**Consider a different variant when:**

- The toggle button is in a top navbar. [Slide Top](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top) is more spatially coherent for a top control.
- The toggle is in a bottom nav bar. [Slide Bottom](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom) aligns better.
- You want the reveal to originate from the exact click point regardless of button position. [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular) handles that case.
- Your layout is right-to-left (RTL). The leftward slide may feel like "going backward" in RTL contexts. Consider [Slide Right](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right) instead.

## Accessibility notes

- **Trigger semantics.** The wrapper `<div onClick={...}>` is not focusable or announced by screen readers. Always pass a real `<button>` as `children` with an `aria-label` such as `"Toggle theme"`.
- **State communication.** Add `aria-pressed={isDark}` to the inner button (or use `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`) so screen readers report the current mode. The visual icon swap is not enough.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`.** The CSS includes `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` which sets `animation: none !important` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements when `.theme-slide-left` is present. Users with reduced motion preferences get an instant, animation-free theme swap.
- **Input blocking during transition.** `pointerEvents: none` is applied to the wrapper while `isTransitioning` is true. Keep `speed` short (0.3 to 0.6s) to minimize the window where the toggle is unresponsive.

## Performance considerations

- **Transform-only.** Both `slide-out-left` and `slide-in-left` animate only `translateX`, which runs on the GPU compositor without triggering layout or paint. The animation cost is equivalent to a CSS `transition: transform`.
- **No coordinate reads.** Unlike [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular), this variant does not call `e.clientX`/`e.clientY`. The click handler is a simple async function with no synchronous DOM measurements.
- **`cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`.** The Material Design standard easing registers well at `speed=0.4` to `0.5`. At very short durations (0.15s or less), the ease-in portion of the curve compresses to near-linearity, so consider switching to `ease-out` for `speed` values below 0.25.
- **`blur` prop.** Full-viewport blur on `::view-transition-old` and `::view-transition-new` is compositor-heavy. Avoid it on mobile or keep values at or below 6px.
- **Class cleanup.** `theme-slide-left` is removed in the `finally` block, so interrupted transitions (e.g., rapid tab switching) do not leave the class on `<html>` permanently.

## Customization examples

### Directional ease: emphasize arrival

Ease-out on the incoming layer makes the new theme feel like it "snaps into" place:

```css
.theme-slide-left::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: slide-out-left var(--transition-speed) ease-in;
}
.theme-slide-left::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: slide-in-left var(--transition-speed) ease-out;
}
```

### Faster slide for a sidebar toggle

```tsx
<ThemeToggleSlideLeft speed={0.3} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
  <button aria-label="Toggle theme" className="w-full flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-2 rounded-lg hover:bg-zinc-100 dark:hover:bg-zinc-800 text-sm">
    <Sun className="h-4 w-4 dark:hidden" />
    <Moon className="h-4 w-4 hidden dark:block" />
    <span>Toggle theme</span>
  </button>
</ThemeToggleSlideLeft>
```

### Horizontal onboarding step

In a multi-step wizard where dark mode is step 3, the leftward page flip matches the forward-progression direction:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideLeft } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function AppearanceStep({ onNext }: { onNext: () => void }) {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()

  const applyAndProceed = () => {
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", !isDark)
    setTheme(isDark ? "light" : "dark")
    onNext()
  }

  return (
    <div className="space-y-6 max-w-sm">
      <h2 className="text-xl font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100">Choose your theme</h2>
      <ThemeToggleSlideLeft speed={0.4} onToggle={applyAndProceed}>
        <Button variant="outline" className="w-full justify-start gap-2">
          Switch to {theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark"} mode and continue
        </Button>
      </ThemeToggleSlideLeft>
    </div>
  )
}
```

# theme-toggle-slide-right.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right.mdx

title: Theme Toggle Slide Right
description: Right to left slide animation for theme toggle using View Transitions API.

import { Callout } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/callout';
import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { TransitionDemo } from '@/components/transition-demo';
import { ThemeToggleSlideRight } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right';

## Overview

The `ThemeToggleSlideRight` component creates a slide-left effect from the right when toggling themes. Uses the native View Transitions API with customizable speed and blur.

<Callout type="info">
  **Browser Support:** View Transitions API is supported in Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, and Opera 97+. Falls back to instant theme changes in unsupported browsers.
</Callout>

## Interactive Demo

Try it live! Adjust the speed and blur sliders, then click the button to see the transition effect.

<Preview background="grid">
  <TransitionDemo TransitionComponent={ThemeToggleSlideRight} />

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-right
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-right
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-right
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/theme-toggle-slide-right
        ```
    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right.tsx"
"use client";
import * as React from "react";
export interface ThemeToggleSlideRightProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  onToggle?: () => void;
  theme?: "light" | "dark";
  className?: string;
  speed?: number;
  blur?: number;
}
export function ThemeToggleSlideRight({
  children,
  onToggle,
  theme,
  className,
  speed = 0.5,
  blur = 0,
}: ThemeToggleSlideRightProps) {
  const [isTransitioning, setIsTransitioning] = React.useState(false);
  const handleClick = async () => {
    if (isTransitioning) return;
    if (!document.startViewTransition) {
      onToggle?.();
      return;
    }
    setIsTransitioning(true);
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--transition-speed",
      `${speed}s`,
    );
    document.documentElement.style.setProperty(
      "--transition-blur",
      `${blur}px`,
    );
    document.documentElement.classList.add("theme-slide-right");
    const transition = document.startViewTransition(() => {
      onToggle?.();
    });
    try {
      await transition.finished;
    } catch (error) {
      console.warn("Theme transition interrupted:", error);
    } finally {
      document.documentElement.classList.remove("theme-slide-right");
      setIsTransitioning(false);
    }
  };
  return (
    <div
      onClick={handleClick}
      className={className}
      style={{ pointerEvents: isTransitioning ? "none" : "auto" }}
    >
      {children}
    </div>
  );
}

```

    **Required CSS** (add to `globals.css`):
    ```css
    :root {
      --transition-speed: 0.5s;
      --transition-blur: 0px;
    }

    .theme-slide-right::view-transition-old(root) {
      animation: slide-out-right var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
      filter: blur(var(--transition-blur));
    }

    .theme-slide-right::view-transition-new(root) {
      animation: slide-in-right var(--transition-speed) cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
      filter: blur(var(--transition-blur));
    }

    @keyframes slide-out-right {
      to {
        transform: translateX(100%);
      }
    }

    @keyframes slide-in-right {
      from {
        transform: translateX(100%);
      }
    }

    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      .theme-slide-right::view-transition-group(*),
      .theme-slide-right::view-transition-old(*),
      .theme-slide-right::view-transition-new(*) {
        animation: none !important;
      }
    }
    ```

## Usage

### With next-themes

```tsx
"use client"

import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideRight } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()
  
  return (
    <ThemeToggleSlideRight 
      onToggle={() => setTheme(theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')}
      speed={0.5}
      blur={0}
    >
      <Button>Toggle Theme</Button>
    </ThemeToggleSlideRight>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger element (button, icon, etc.) |
| `onToggle` | `() => void` | - | Callback when theme should toggle |
| `theme` | `"light"` \| `"dark"` | - | Current theme (optional) |
| `speed` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation speed in seconds |
| `blur` | `number` | `0` | Blur amount in pixels |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`ThemeToggleSlideRight` adds `theme-slide-right` to `<html>` and drives `slide-out-right` (`translateX(100%)` exit) and `slide-in-right` (`translateX(100%)` enter) via the View Transitions API. The current theme slides out to the right and the new theme arrives from the right, creating a right-to-left page-flip that reads as "going back" or "returning."

Use it when:

- Your toggle is in a right sidebar, a right-anchored panel, or a right-aligned element. The rightward departure and arrival creates continuity with that side of the screen.
- Your app supports RTL (right-to-left) languages and "forward" navigation slides from right to left. The slide-right matches the RTL forward direction.
- You want to create an asymmetric pair: use [Slide Left](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left) for "enabling dark mode" (going forward) and `slide-right` for "disabling dark mode" (going back). You would need a custom implementation to swap variants based on direction, but the visual metaphor is coherent.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use slide-right when:**

- The toggle lives in a right sidebar or a right-aligned control bar. The rightward slide feels connected to the control's position.
- Your app uses RTL layout conventions and a right-to-left slide is the "forward" direction.

**Consider a different variant when:**

- The toggle is in a left sidebar. [Slide Left](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left) is more spatially coherent.
- The toggle is in a top or bottom bar. [Slide Top](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top) or [Slide Bottom](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom) match those positions.
- You want the ripple to follow the cursor. [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular) is better for that.

## Accessibility notes

- **Button semantics.** The `children` must include a keyboard-accessible `<button>`. The wrapper `<div>` receives the click handler but is not focusable. Screen readers and keyboard users need the inner button.
- **State.** Use `aria-pressed={isDark}` or `role="switch" aria-checked={isDark}` on the button so screen readers report the current theme. An icon-only button is ambiguous without this.
- **`aria-label`.** Provide a descriptive label: `aria-label="Toggle theme"` or `aria-label="Enable dark mode"` depending on which state the button toggles to.
- **Reduced motion.** The CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block sets `animation: none !important` on all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements when `.theme-slide-right` is present. No additional JavaScript is needed.
- **Transition lock duration.** `speed` defaults to 0.5s. During this window `pointerEvents: none` is set. Keep `speed` short to avoid frustrating users who toggle themes in rapid succession.

## Performance considerations

- **Transform-only animation.** `slide-out-right` and `slide-in-right` animate only `translateX(100%)`. This runs on the compositor without layout or paint.
- **No click-coordinate reads.** The handler is a parameter-less async function; there are no synchronous DOM reads on click.
- **Class lifecycle.** `theme-slide-right` is added before `startViewTransition` and removed in `finally`. Interrupted transitions cannot leave stale class state on `<html>`.
- **`cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` at short durations.** Below 0.25s, this easing's ease-in portion compresses to near-linearity. If you set `speed=0.2`, consider overriding to a simpler `ease-out` in CSS.
- **Full-screen `filter: blur()`.** Non-zero `blur` values apply to the full-viewport View Transition snapshots. Keep at or below 8px and test on mobile hardware before shipping.

### RTL-aware theme toggle


```css
.theme-slide-right::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: slide-out-right var(--transition-speed) ease-in;
}
.theme-slide-right::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: slide-in-right var(--transition-speed) ease-out;
}
```

## Usage

### With next-themes

```tsx
"use client"

import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideTop } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()
  
  return (
    <ThemeToggleSlideTop 
      onToggle={() => setTheme(theme === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark')}
      speed={0.5}
      blur={0}
    >
      <Button>Toggle Theme</Button>
    </ThemeToggleSlideTop>
  )
}
```

## Props

| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | The trigger element (button, icon, etc.) |
| `onToggle` | `() => void` | - | Callback when theme should toggle |
| `theme` | `"light"` \| `"dark"` | - | Current theme (optional) |
| `speed` | `number` | `0.5` | Animation speed in seconds |
| `blur` | `number` | `0` | Blur amount in pixels |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Use cases

`ThemeToggleSlideTop` adds `theme-slide-top` to `<html>`, then calls `document.startViewTransition`. The CSS animates `slide-out-top` (`translateY(-100%)` exit) and `slide-in-top` (`translateY(-100%)` enter) using `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`. The current page slides upward and off; the new theme slides down from the top to fill it.

Use it when:

- Your theme toggle is in a top navigation bar or a sticky header. The new theme cascading down from the top reads as "coming from" the header where the toggle lives.
- The interface has a vertical information hierarchy (hero at top, content below) and the top-down wipe reinforces that hierarchy.
- You want a "curtain drop" feel: the new theme descends like a curtain from the navbar, which is a familiar metaphor for a mode change.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use slide-top when:**

- The toggle is in a sticky top navbar, a desktop app's top menu bar, or a header announcement bar. The downward reveal connects spatially to the control.
- You want a "closing curtain" metaphor where the new theme is revealed as the old one rises out of view.

**Consider a different variant when:**

- The toggle is in a bottom nav bar. [Slide Bottom](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-bottom) (upward reveal) is more spatially coherent.
- The toggle is in a left or right sidebar. [Slide Left](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-left) or [Slide Right](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-right) respect the horizontal origin.
- You want the ripple to track the cursor position. [Circular](/docs/transitions/theme-toggle-circular) follows the exact click point regardless of where the button is.

**Do not use any theme toggle when:**

- `document.startViewTransition` is not available. All variants fall back to an instant theme swap via the `!document.startViewTransition` guard, which is the correct behavior.

## Accessibility notes

- **Keyboard accessibility.** The outer `<div onClick={...}>` is not keyboard-reachable. Always pass a focusable `<button>` element as `children`.
- **State communication.** Add `aria-pressed={isDark}` to the inner button (or `role="switch" aria-checked={isDark}`) so screen readers announce the current mode. The visual Sun/Moon icon swap is invisible to assistive technology.
- **Label.** An icon-only button must have `aria-label="Toggle theme"` or equivalent. Without it, screen readers may say "button" with no context.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`.** The bundled CSS includes `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` which sets `animation: none !important` for all `::view-transition-*` pseudo-elements when `.theme-slide-top` is present. No extra JavaScript is required; the theme change still fires, just without the slide animation.
- **`pointerEvents: none` window.** The wrapper is unclickable while `isTransitioning` is true. Keep `speed` at or below 0.6s to minimize this window.

## Performance considerations

- **Transform-only animation.** `slide-out-top` and `slide-in-top` animate only `translateY(-100%)`. This runs on the GPU compositor; no layout or paint is triggered.
- **No DOM reads on click.** The handler does not read `clientX`/`clientY`. It only writes CSS custom properties and adds a class, which are cheap DOM write operations.
- **`cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` suitability.** This easing has a gentle ease-in followed by a pronounced ease-out. At `speed=0.5` it feels polished for a full-screen slide. At `speed=0.2` the ease-in portion compresses; consider overriding to plain `ease-out` for sub-0.3s transitions.
- **`blur` prop.** Applying `filter: blur()` to the full-viewport `::view-transition-old` and `::view-transition-new` layers is GPU-intensive. Restrict to desktop-class contexts and keep values at or below 8px.
- **Class lifecycle.** `theme-slide-top` is always removed in the `finally` block, so interrupted transitions do not leave stale state.

## Customization examples

### Top-to-bottom with faster ease

A crisper slide-down that emphasizes the new theme arriving:

```css
.theme-slide-top::view-transition-old(root) {
  animation: slide-out-top var(--transition-speed) ease-in;
}
.theme-slide-top::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation: slide-in-top var(--transition-speed) ease-out;
}
```

### Slow curtain with subtle blur

A cinematic top-down wipe for a portfolio or showcase site:

```tsx
<ThemeToggleSlideTop speed={0.9} blur={6} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
  <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Toggle theme">
    <Sun className="h-5 w-5 dark:hidden" />
    <Moon className="h-5 w-5 hidden dark:block" />
  </Button>
</ThemeToggleSlideTop>
```

## Real-world examples

### Top navbar theme toggle

The most common placement: a Sun/Moon icon button in a sticky header, with the new theme sliding down from where the button lives.

```tsx
"use client"
import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideTop } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top"
import { Moon, Sun } from "lucide-react"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"

export function TopNavThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()

  const toggleTheme = () => {
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", !isDark)
    setTheme(isDark ? "light" : "dark")
  }

  return (
    <header className="sticky top-0 z-40 flex items-center justify-between px-6 h-14 border-b border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 bg-white/80 dark:bg-zinc-950/80 backdrop-blur">
      <span className="font-bold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100">Acme</span>
      <ThemeToggleSlideTop speed={0.5} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
        <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label="Toggle theme" aria-pressed={theme === "dark"}>
          <Sun className="h-5 w-5 rotate-0 scale-100 transition-all dark:-rotate-90 dark:scale-0" />
          <Moon className="absolute h-5 w-5 rotate-90 scale-0 transition-all dark:rotate-0 dark:scale-100" />
        </Button>
      </ThemeToggleSlideTop>
    </header>
  )
}
```

### App menu bar toggle (desktop-class)

For a desktop-style app with a top menu bar, a slower speed with light blur gives a more "weighty" feel:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useTheme } from "next-themes"
import { ThemeToggleSlideTop } from "@/components/animations/transitions/theme-toggle-slide-top"

export function MenuBarTheme() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme()

  const toggleTheme = () => {
    const isDark = document.documentElement.classList.contains("dark")
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", !isDark)
    setTheme(isDark ? "light" : "dark")
  }

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center h-8 bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-900 border-b border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-800 px-4 gap-4">
      <span className="text-xs font-medium text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300">File</span>
      <span className="text-xs font-medium text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300">Edit</span>
      <span className="text-xs font-medium text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300">View</span>
      <ThemeToggleSlideTop speed={0.55} blur={4} onToggle={toggleTheme}>
        <button
          aria-pressed={theme === "dark"}
          aria-label="Toggle theme"
          className="text-xs font-medium text-zinc-700 dark:text-zinc-300 hover:text-zinc-900 dark:hover:text-zinc-100"
        >
          Theme
        </button>
      </ThemeToggleSlideTop>
    </div>
  )
}
```

# view-toggle.mdx

title: View Toggle
description: Smoothly rearrange items with multiple animation styles when switching views.

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { ListGrid } from '@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/list-grid';

## Overview

The `ViewToggle` component demonstrates layout animations to smoothly rearrange items when switching between grid and list views. Choose from multiple animation variants to control the transition style.

    Copy and paste the following code into your project.

    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/list-grid.tsx"
    "use client";

    import React, { useState, useId } from "react";
    import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
    import { Grid, List } from "lucide-react";

    export interface ListGridItem {
      id: string | number;
      title: string;
      subtitle: string;
      status: string;
      avatar?: string;
    }

    interface ListGridProps {
      items: ListGridItem[];
      className?: string;
      views?: Array<"grid" | "list" | "compact" | "card">;
      variant?: "smooth" | "stagger" | "scale-fade" | "crossfade";
    }

    export function ListGrid({ items, className, views = ["grid", "list"], variant = "smooth" }: ListGridProps) {
      const [view, setView] = useState<"grid" | "list" | "compact" | "card">(views[0]);
      const id = useId();

      const getItemTransition = (index: number) => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "smooth":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 };
          case "stagger":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6, delay: index * 0.05 };
          case "scale-fade":
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.15, duration: 0.5 };
          case "crossfade":
            return { type: "tween" as const, duration: 0.3 };
          default:
            return { type: "spring" as const, bounce: 0.2, duration: 0.6 };
        }
      };

      const getItemInitial = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "scale-fade":
            return { opacity: 0, scale: 0.9 };
          case "crossfade":
            return { opacity: 0 };
          default:
            return { opacity: 0, scale: 0.9 };
        }
      };

      const getItemAnimate = () => {
        switch (variant) {
          case "scale-fade":
            return { opacity: 1, scale: 1 };
          case "crossfade":
            return { opacity: 1 };
          default:
            return { opacity: 1, scale: 1 };
        }
      };

      return (
        <div className={cn("flex flex-col items-center justify-center p-8 bg-zinc-50 dark:bg-zinc-900 rounded-xl min-h-[400px] w-full", className)}>
          <div className="w-full max-w-md">
            <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-6">
              <h3 className="text-sm font-semibold text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400 uppercase tracking-wider">
                Items
              </h3>
              <div className="flex bg-white dark:bg-zinc-800 rounded-lg p-1 border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-700">
                <button
                  onClick={() => setView("grid")}
                  className={cn(
                    "p-2 rounded-md transition-colors relative",
                    view === "grid"
                      ? "text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100"
                      : "text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-600"
                  )}
                >
                  {view === "grid" && (
                    <motion.div
                      layoutId={`${id}-bg`}
                      className="absolute inset-0 bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-700 rounded-md -z-10 shadow-sm"
                      transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}
                    />
                  )}
                  <Grid size={16} />
                </button>
                <button
                  onClick={() => setView("list")}
                  className={cn(
                    "p-2 rounded-md transition-colors relative",
                    view === "list"
                      ? "text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100"
                      : "text-zinc-400 hover:text-zinc-600"
                  )}
                >
                  {view === "list" && (
                    <motion.div
                      layoutId={`${id}-bg`}
                      className="absolute inset-0 bg-zinc-100 dark:bg-zinc-700 rounded-md -z-10 shadow-sm"
                      transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}
                    />
                  )}
                  <List size={16} />
                </button>
              </div>
            </div>

            <motion.div
              layout
              className={cn(
                "grid gap-4",
                view === "grid" ? "grid-cols-2" : "grid-cols-1"
              )}
            >
              <AnimatePresence>
                {items.map((item, index) => (
                  <motion.div
                    key={item.id}
                    layout
                    initial={getItemInitial()}
                    animate={getItemAnimate()}
                    exit={getItemInitial()}
                    transition={getItemTransition(index)}
                    className={cn(
                      "bg-white dark:bg-zinc-800 p-4 rounded-xl border border-zinc-200 dark:border-zinc-700 shadow-sm hover:shadow-md transition-shadow cursor-default",
                      view === "list" && "flex items-center justify-between"
                    )}
                  >
                    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
                      {item.avatar ? (
                        <img
                          src={item.avatar}
                          alt={item.title}
                          className="w-10 h-10 rounded-full object-cover"
                        />
                      ) : (
                        <div className="w-10 h-10 rounded-full bg-gradient-to-br from-zinc-100 to-zinc-200 dark:from-zinc-700 dark:to-zinc-800 flex items-center justify-center text-xs font-bold text-zinc-500">
                          {item.title.substring(0, 2).toUpperCase()}
                        </div>
                      )}
                      <div>
                        <h4 className="font-semibold text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 text-sm">
                          {item.title}
                        </h4>
                        <p className="text-xs text-zinc-500 dark:text-zinc-400">
                          {item.subtitle}
                        </p>
                      </div>
                    </div>

                    {view === "list" && (
                      <span
                        className={cn(
                          "px-2 py-1 rounded-full text-xs font-medium",
                          item.status === "Active" &&
                          "bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-700 dark:bg-emerald-900/30 dark:text-emerald-400",
                          item.status === "Pending" &&
                          "bg-amber-100 text-amber-700 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-400",
                          item.status === "Archived" &&
                          "bg-zinc-100 text-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-800 dark:text-zinc-400"
                        )}
                      >
                        {item.status}
                      </span>
                    )}

                    {view === "grid" && (
                      <div className="mt-4 flex justify-between items-center">
                        <span
                          className={cn(
                            "px-2 py-1 rounded-full text-xs font-medium",
                            item.status === "Active" &&
                            "bg-emerald-100 text-emerald-700 dark:bg-emerald-900/30 dark:text-emerald-400",
                            item.status === "Pending" &&
                            "bg-amber-100 text-amber-700 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-400",
                            item.status === "Archived" &&
                            "bg-zinc-100 text-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-800 dark:text-zinc-400"
                          )}
                        >
                          {item.status}
                        </span>
                      </div>
                    )}
                  </motion.div>
                ))}
              </AnimatePresence>
            </motion.div>
          </div>
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

## Props

| `items` | `ListGridItem[]` | - | Array of items with id, title, subtitle, status, and optional avatar. |
| `views` | `Array<"grid" \| "list" \| "compact" \| "card">` | `["grid", "list"]` | Available view modes. |
| `variant` | `"smooth" \| "stagger" \| "scale-fade" \| "crossfade"` | `"smooth"` | Animation style for view transitions. |
| `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes. |

## Use cases

`ListGrid` (exported as `ViewToggle` in the docs) renders the same `items` array in two mutually exclusive layouts (default: `"grid"` and `"list"`). Each item is a `motion.div` with `layout` set, so Framer Motion measures and animates the transition from one grid position to another as the `view` state changes. The active view indicator uses a shared `layoutId` (`bg`) on the toggle buttons. Items enter/exit via `AnimatePresence` with `scale` + `opacity`.

Use it when the same data can be meaningfully presented in more than one layout density and the user should be able to choose:

- **Team member or contact directory.** Grid view shows avatar-focused cards; list view shows a denser row with name, role, and status badge. Users on large screens prefer grid; users scanning quickly prefer list.
- **File explorer or media library.** Grid view shows large thumbnails; list view shows file name, size, and date in a table-like row. The `"stagger"` variant (0.05s delay per item) adds a pleasing cascade when switching.
- **Product catalog.** Grid for visual browsing, list for comparing specs. The `"crossfade"` variant (tween, no scale) is most appropriate when items contain complex UI that would distort under scale transforms.
- **Project or task board.** Grid view shows cards with progress indicators; list view shows a compact row per task. `"smooth"` (spring, bounce 0.2) feels natural for task management tools.
- **Search results.** Let users choose between image-heavy grid results and text-dense list results.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ListGrid` (ViewToggle) when:**

- The same data makes sense in two or more layout densities and users have a preference. Both layouts show identical records; only the visual arrangement changes.
- You have 4 to 24 items. Fewer than four makes the layout toggle feel pointless; many more and the `layout` animation (which measures every item) becomes expensive.

**Do not use `ListGrid` when:**

- You are switching between different content panels (Overview, Analytics, Reports). That is a tab navigation pattern. Use [Tab Switcher](/docs/transitions/tab-switcher) instead. The difference: ViewToggle switches the layout of the same data; TabSwitcher switches the content to entirely different data.
- Items have very different sizes across views. Framer Motion's `layout` animation interpolates bounding rects; if an item shrinks dramatically between grid and list, the spring can overshoot and look like a glitch. Use `"crossfade"` (no spring) in that case.
- You need more than two view modes with complex transitions between all pairs. The component supports `compact` and `card` as view values in the type but only renders `grid` and `list` layout classes in the source. Adding more modes requires modifying the component.

## Accessibility notes

- **Toggle button labels.** The grid and list toggle buttons render `<Grid size={16} />` and `<List size={16} />` icons with no visible text. Add `aria-label="Grid view"` and `aria-label="List view"` to each button so screen readers announce the action.
- **Active view announcement.** When the view changes, screen readers should be informed. Wrap the toggle group in a `<div role="group" aria-label="View options">`. The active button can carry `aria-pressed="true"` or `aria-current="true"` so the current layout is communicated.
- **Item content.** Each `motion.div` item is purely presentational. If items contain interactive elements (buttons, links), ensure focus order is logical in both grid and list views. The reflow from grid to list can move DOM elements visually but not in the DOM order, which can confuse screen readers if the source order is not preserved.
- **`AnimatePresence` remounting.** Items are entered and exited by `AnimatePresence`. If an item had focus when the view switched, focus is lost because the element unmounts and remounts. Restore focus to the previously focused item after the switch, or avoid putting interactive controls inside items.
- **Reduced motion.** The `layout` animation and the `scale`/`opacity` enter/exit will still run under `prefers-reduced-motion` because the component does not check for it. Add a `useReducedMotion` check from `motion/react` and set `transition={{ duration: 0 }}` on the `motion.div` items if reduced motion is preferred.

## Performance considerations

- **`layout` on every item.** Each `motion.div` item has the `layout` prop, which means Framer Motion measures its bounding rect before and after every view switch. With 24 items, that is 48 synchronous DOM reads per switch. This is fine for typical item counts but becomes expensive beyond 30 to 40 items. For large datasets, consider virtualization (e.g., `@tanstack/react-virtual`) and disable `layout` animation in favor of a simpler fade.
- **`AnimatePresence` inside a `layout` parent.** The outer `motion.div` has `layout` set, so its height animates when items change height. Nested `AnimatePresence` inside a `layout` container is a known Framer Motion complexity; keep the tree shallow to avoid unexpected layout cascades.
- **`"stagger"` variant.** The stagger adds `index * 0.05` seconds of delay per item. With 20 items, the last item starts its animation 1 second after the view switch. If the animation feels laggy, reduce the multiplier or switch to `"smooth"`.
- **`"crossfade"` variant.** Uses `type: "tween", duration: 0.3` with no scale. This is the cheapest variant because there is no spring settling. Use it for large item counts or items with complex internal layouts.
- **Toggle button shared `layoutId`.** The active background indicator uses `layoutId="bg"` (namespaced with `useId()`). This is a single lightweight shared layout. Mounting multiple `ListGrid` instances on the same page is safe because each uses its own `useId()`.

```tsx
  { id: "f3", title: "backup-2024.tar.gz", subtitle: "892 MB", status: "Archived" },

}
```

# zoom-hollow.mdx

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/content/docs/transitions/zoom-hollow.mdx

title: Zoom Hollow Text
description: A beautiful text transition that zooms in with a hollow outline effect, perfect for theme toggles

import { Preview } from '@/components/preview';
import { ZoomHollowText } from "@/registry/new-york/animations/transitions/zoom-hollow";

## Overview

The `ZoomHollowText` component creates a stunning text transition with zoom-in animation and hollow outline effect. Perfect for hero sections, theme toggles, and attention-grabbing headlines. Works seamlessly with light and dark modes.

export default function Example() {

      className="text-7xl font-black"
    />
  );
}`}

## Installation

        ```bash
        npx shadcn@latest add @animbits/zoom-hollow
        ```
        ```bash
        pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/zoom-hollow
        ```
        ```bash
        yarn dlx shadcn@latest add @animbits/zoom-hollow
        ```
        ```bash
        bunx shadcn@latest add @animbits/zoom-hollow
        ```
    Copy and paste the following code into your project.

    ```tsx title="components/animations/transitions/zoom-hollow.tsx"
    "use client";

    import React, { useState, useEffect } from "react";
    import { motion, AnimatePresence } from "motion/react";
    import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

    interface ZoomHollowTextProps {
      words: string[];
      className?: string;
      duration?: number;
      interval?: number;
      strokeWidth?: number;
      fillColor?: string;
      strokeColor?: string;
    }

    export function ZoomHollowText({
      words,
      className = "",
      duration = 0.8,
      interval = 2500,
      strokeWidth = 2,
      fillColor = "transparent",
      strokeColor = "currentColor",
    }: ZoomHollowTextProps) {
      const [index, setIndex] = useState(0);

      useEffect(() => {
        const timer = setInterval(() => {
          setIndex((prev) => (prev + 1) % words.length);
        }, interval);
        return () => clearInterval(timer);
      }, [words.length, interval]);

      return (
        <div className={cn("relative inline-block", className)}>
          <AnimatePresence mode="wait">
            <motion.span
              key={words[index]}
              initial={{ scale: 0.5, opacity: 0, filter: "blur(10px)" }}
              animate={{ scale: 1, opacity: 1, filter: "blur(0px)" }}
              exit={{ scale: 1.5, opacity: 0, filter: "blur(10px)" }}
              transition={{
                duration,
                ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1],
              }}
              style={{
                WebkitTextStroke: `${strokeWidth}px ${strokeColor}`,
                WebkitTextFillColor: fillColor,
                paintOrder: "stroke fill",
              }}
              className="block"
            >
              {words[index]}
            </motion.span>
          </AnimatePresence>
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```

## CSS Customization

The hollow effect is created using webkit text stroke. You can customize it with CSS:

```css
.custom-hollow {
  -webkit-text-stroke: 3px currentColor;
  -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent;
  paint-order: stroke fill;
}
```

For dark mode support, use CSS variables:

```css
.theme-aware-hollow {
  -webkit-text-stroke: 2px hsl(var(--foreground));
  -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent;
}

```

## Props

| `words` | `string[]` | Required | Array of words to cycle through |
| `className` | `string` | `""` | Additional CSS classes |
| `duration` | `number` | `0.8` | Animation duration in seconds |
| `interval` | `number` | `2500` | Time between word changes in ms |
| `strokeWidth` | `number` | `2` | Width of the text outline |
| `fillColor` | `string` | `"transparent"` | Fill color of the text |
| `strokeColor` | `string` | `"currentColor"` | Color of the text outline |

## Use cases

`ZoomHollowText` cycles through `words` on a `setInterval` every `interval` milliseconds (default 2500ms). Each word change uses `AnimatePresence mode="wait"`: the current word exits (`scale: 1.5`, `opacity: 0`, `filter: blur(10px)`), then the next word enters (`scale: 0.5` to `scale: 1`, `opacity: 0` to `1`, blur clears). The custom easing `[0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]` (a fast ease-out curve) makes the entry feel snappy and the exit feel like the word explodes outward. The hollow outline is CSS-only via `-webkit-text-stroke` and `-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent`.

Use it when:

- **Hero sections.** A headline like "We help you [Design / Build / Ship / Scale]" where the cycling word reinforces the brand message. The hollow outline at large sizes (`text-7xl` or above) has high visual impact.
- **Value proposition cycling.** A landing page that cycles through product benefits. `interval=3000` with `duration=0.8` gives enough reading time between transitions.
- **Loading or splash screens.** While a heavy page loads, a cycling word display entertains the user. `interval=1500` with `duration=0.5` keeps energy high.
- **Theme-aware decorative text.** With `strokeColor="currentColor"` and `fillColor="transparent"`, the outline color automatically matches the current text color in both light and dark mode, requiring no custom CSS.

## When to use / when not to use

**Use `ZoomHollowText` when:**

- The words are short (1 to 2 words, ideally under 12 characters). Long words at `text-7xl` will overflow their container on mobile.
- The context is decorative, not informational. Cycling text is not readable for users who need to parse it to understand the page.
- You control when the component is visible. Running `setInterval` continuously when the element is off-screen wastes CPU. Use an `IntersectionObserver` to pause cycling when scrolled away.

**Do not use `ZoomHollowText` when:**

- The cycling message is essential for the user to read before taking an action. `AnimatePresence mode="wait"` means only one word is in the DOM at a time; users who look away will miss words.
- The words have very different lengths. `motion.span` has `display: block`, so its bounding box changes with each word. The parent container must have a fixed height to prevent layout shift.
- You need the animation to stop at a specific word (e.g., after user interaction). The component has no `pause` or `index` prop; pausing requires lifting the `index` state out of the component.

## Accessibility notes

- **Decorative content.** The cycling text conveys no critical information. Wrap it in a container with `aria-hidden="true"` and provide the primary message in a static, always-visible sibling element. This is the safest approach.
- **If the text is meaningful.** If the cycling words communicate important product benefits, add a visually-hidden list of all words so screen readers read the complete message without the animation. Example: `<ul className="sr-only"><li>Design</li><li>Create</li><li>Innovate</li></ul>`.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`.** The component does not currently check `useReducedMotion`. Add it to skip the enter/exit animation and display words statically, just updating the text without the zoom-blur transition:

```tsx
"use client"
import { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react"
import { ZoomHollowText } from "@/components/animations/transitions/zoom-hollow"

// Static fallback when the user prefers reduced motion.
function AccessibleZoomHollow(props: React.ComponentProps<typeof ZoomHollowText>) {
  const reduced = useReducedMotion()
  if (reduced) {
    return (
      <span style={{ WebkitTextStroke: `${props.strokeWidth ?? 2}px ${props.strokeColor ?? "currentColor"}`, WebkitTextFillColor: props.fillColor ?? "transparent" }}>
        {props.words[0]}
      </span>
    )
  }
  return <ZoomHollowText {...props} />
}
```

- **`-webkit-text-stroke` support.** `-webkit-text-stroke` and `-webkit-text-fill-color` are supported in all modern browsers but are technically prefixed. They have no standard fallback in Firefox for very old versions. Test and provide a `fillColor="currentColor"` fallback if full-text support is required.

## Performance considerations

- **`AnimatePresence mode="wait"`.** Only one `motion.span` is in the DOM at a time. The exiting word unmounts before the entering word mounts. This keeps the DOM clean but means two full enter/exit animations fire on each cycle. The combined animation cost is `duration * 2` per cycle (the exit overlaps with the enter by `mode="wait"` semantics, actually it is sequential, so cost is the exit duration plus the enter duration).
- **Blur in `filter`.** The component animates `filter: blur(10px)` on enter and exit. CSS `filter` creates a new stacking context. For a small inline text span this is cheap, but if the span is very large (e.g., a massive `text-9xl` hero headline), the blur area is large and can cause GPU overdraw. Test on mobile and reduce `blur` if needed by using `duration=0.5` with no blur in the transition config (currently hardcoded at 10px; to change it you would need to modify the component).
- **`setInterval` + `setIndex`.** Each interval tick calls `setIndex`, which re-renders the component. This is a minimal re-render (only the `motion.span` changes), but keep the component's parent tree shallow to avoid triggering expensive ancestor re-renders.
- **Custom easing `[0.22, 1, 0.36, 1]`.** This is a fast cubic-bezier with an overshooting feel at the end of the `scale` animation on enter. It is specified as an array, which Framer Motion evaluates as a cubic-bezier. There is no spring settling involved, so the animation ends at exactly `duration` seconds.

# Contributing to Animbits

Source: https://github.com/garvit1000/animbits/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to Animbits

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Animbits! This guide will help you add new animations to the registry.

## Project Structure

```
animbits/
├── registry/
│   └── new-york/
│       └── animations/
│           ├── icons/          # Icon animations
│           ├── buttons/        # Button animations
│           ├── cards/          # Card animations
│           ├── lists/          # List animations
│           └── pages/          # Page transition animations
├── lib/
│   └── animation-presets.ts   # Shared animation variants
├── registry.json              # Registry configuration
└── README.md
```

## Adding a New Animation

### 1. Create the Animation Component

Create a new file in the appropriate namespace folder:

```tsx
// registry/new-york/animations/[namespace]/[animation-name].tsx
"use client"

import { motion, type Variants } from "framer-motion"
import { type ComponentProps } from "react"

const variants: Variants = {
  // Define your animation variants
}

interface AnimatedComponentProps extends ComponentProps<typeof motion.div> {
  children: React.ReactNode
  // Add custom props
}

export function YourAnimation({ children, ...props }: AnimatedComponentProps) {
  return (
    <motion.div
      variants={variants}
      initial="initial"
      animate="animate"
      {...props}
    >
      {children}
    </motion.div>
  )
}
```

### 2. Register in registry.json

Add your animation to the `items` array:

```json
{
  "name": "namespace/animation-name",
  "type": "registry:component",
  "title": "Animation Title",
  "description": "Brief description of the animation",
  "dependencies": ["framer-motion"],
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "registry/new-york/animations/namespace/animation-name.tsx",
      "type": "registry:component"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 3. Build and Test

```bash
# Build the registry
pnpm registry:build

# Test installation
npx shadcn@latest add http://localhost:3000/r/namespace/animation-name
```

## Animation Guidelines

### Best Practices

1. **Use "use client" directive**: All animation components must be client components
2. **Export named components**: Use descriptive PascalCase names
3. **Extend motion props**: Allow users to pass additional Framer Motion props
4. **Provide sensible defaults**: Make animations work out of the box
5. **Keep it simple**: Focus on one animation pattern per component
6. **Type everything**: Use TypeScript for all props and variants

### Performance

- Prefer `transform` and `opacity` for animations (GPU-accelerated)
- Avoid animating `width`, `height`, or `top/left` when possible
- Use `will-change` sparingly
- Test on lower-end devices

### Naming Conventions

- **Files**: kebab-case (e.g., `fade-in.tsx`)
- **Components**: PascalCase (e.g., `FadeInCard`)
- **Props**: camelCase (e.g., `trigger`, `delay`)
- **Namespaces**: lowercase (e.g., `icons`, `buttons`)

## Namespaces

### Current Namespaces

- `icons/` - Animations for icon elements
- `buttons/` - Button interaction animations
- `cards/` - Card component animations
- `lists/` - List and list item animations
- `pages/` - Page transition animations

### Adding a New Namespace

1. Create the folder: `registry/new-york/animations/[namespace]/`
2. Add at least 2-3 animations to the namespace
3. Update README.md with the new namespace
4. Add examples to the documentation

## Common Patterns

### Trigger-based Animations

```tsx
interface Props {
  trigger?: "hover" | "tap" | "mount"
}

const animationProps = {
  initial: "initial",
  ...(trigger === "mount" && { animate: "animate" }),
  ...(trigger === "hover" && { whileHover: "animate" }),
  ...(trigger === "tap" && { whileTap: "animate" }),
}
```

### Staggered List Animations

```tsx
const containerVariants = {
  hidden: { opacity: 0 },
  visible: {
    opacity: 1,
    transition: { staggerChildren: 0.1 },
  },
}

const itemVariants = {
  hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 20 },
  visible: { opacity: 1, y: 0 },
}
```

### Delay Support

```tsx
interface Props {
  delay?: number
}

<motion.div
  initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
  animate={{ opacity: 1 }}
  transition={{ duration: 0.5, delay }}
/>
```

## Testing Checklist

Before submitting a PR:

- [ ] Animation works in both light and dark mode
- [ ] Component is properly typed
- [ ] Props are documented with JSDoc comments
- [ ] Animation is smooth (60fps)
- [ ] Works on mobile devices
- [ ] Registered in registry.json
- [ ] README updated if adding new namespace
- [ ] Example usage provided
